  30-minute heartbeat and in-memory findings could not host timers
  (`jarvis_schedule.py`'s header says why); the digest lives in
  `jarvis_arbiter.py`, which this repository **does** hold
  (`backend/jarvis_arbiter.py`, and its `jarvis-backend/` twin - the routes
  are §123.4). The scheduler is
  the one clock; briefings, sleep mode and the overnight tidy are to plug in
  as new kinds (`register_kind`), not as schedulers of their own. Sleep mode
  now has, as the standby schedule (21.8), and so has the morning briefing
  (section 22).
- **A routine (21.15) has its own gaps, all of them small and all of them
  stated there**: the Windows toast names the part only in words (it has no
  per-part buttons), the phone shows a part only while connected, and a part
  whose question is never answered is never announced as lost — once every
  part has fired, the next occurrence starts without it, and an untimed part
  that never fired keeps the routine silent until it is answered.

### 21.10 "Also on my phone" (added 2026-09-26, the phone only)

The owner's decision of 2026-09-26 (the cutting-edge "Quick wins"; the
feasibility audit's I93). In the phone's Brain -> Coming up, an **alarm**
or a **reminder** has a button, "Also on my phone", that hands a copy to the
phone's own apps - **by the owner's tap only, never on its own**:

- an alarm -> the phone's Clock app (`AlarmClock.ACTION_SET_ALARM`): the
  hour, the minute and the owner's words, and for a repeat the days (every
  day, weekdays, or the chosen days). The Clock app shows its own screen
  (`EXTRA_SKIP_UI` false) and the owner saves it there. A one-off alarm is
  offered only when it is due within 24 hours - the Clock app sets an alarm
  by time of day only - and further ahead the row says "offered from the day
  before". One that repeats every few hours is not offered.
- a reminder -> the phone's calendar (`Intent.ACTION_INSERT` on
  `CalendarContract.Events`): an event at its next time, 15 minutes long,
  titled with the owner's words, repeating the same way (`RRULE`
  `FREQ=DAILY` or `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=...`). The calendar app shows its own
  editing screen.

Nothing is sent to the PC and nothing changes there, so there is **no
approval card** (the tap, and saving in the phone's own app, are the
owner's decision) and the button is not held on a stale link. It reads the
job's `rule` (`every`, `at`, `days`) and `due` from `GET /api/schedule` -
the same answer Coming up already reads; no new route. Not offered while
the private lists are hidden (the words are hidden), nor for a paused one,
a timer, a to-do item, a briefing, a "tell me when" or the standby
schedule. One line under the list says what it does and warns plainly:
"Keep both and both will ring; the phone's calendar may copy the event to
your Google account." The phone asks for one install-time permission,
`com.android.alarm.permission.SET_ALARM`, and still no exact-alarm
permission. Jarvis's own late-alarm rule (21.1, a job heard of more than 10
minutes late is a silent "Missed at") stays on Jarvis's own alarms; a copy
in the Clock app is the Clock app's. A repeat's time is the PC's wall-clock
time ("07:00"); on a phone set to another time zone it rings at 07:00 there.

The desktop has no such button, on purpose (ARCHITECTURE section 8, "On the
phone, kept off the desktop").

### 21.9 Snooze, "cancel that" and named lists (added 2026-09-25)

The creativity audit's everyday quick wins (`docs/CREATIVITY-AUDIT-2026-09-25.md`
item 6, `docs/creativity-2026-09-25/usefulness.md` idea 1). No new route, no
new patch: `jarvis_schedule.py` and `jarvis_quick.py` only, and both apps.
Nothing here needs a card: a snooze is a one-off, and the owner's rule is no
card for a one-off.

**Snooze.** A timer, alarm or reminder that WENT OFF can be snoozed:
`POST /api/schedule/act {"id", "do": "snooze", "seconds"?}` (10
minutes when not said; 1 minute to 24 hours). **The route reaches back a day**
- a job that has gone off is kept for `FIRED_KEEP` (24 hours) so an app that
was out of reach can still act on it - while **the "Just went off" list and
the spoken phrase reach back one hour** (`WENT_OFF_SHOWN`, 3600, and
`jarvis_quick.py`'s own words are "Nothing went off in the last hour, so there
is nothing to snooze."). **`delete` uses that same day-long reach-back** (the
owner's decision of 2026-10-14, DEF-008): a job that has gone off is one the
"Just went off" list SHOWS, so it must be one the apps can clear, and `delete`
is routed before the scheduler's own state gate exactly as `snooze` is. It is
the only other verb that acts on such a job - `pause`, `resume`, `done` and
`add_time` on one answer 409 "It has already gone off.", where they used to
answer 404 "That is not on the list any more." about an entry both apps were
still showing. Snooze makes a **new one-off copy**
of the job (same kind, same words, `"snoozed": true`, `source` `"snooze"`),
due after the snooze. A repeating job's own rule and next time are not
touched, so only that one occurrence moves. Snoozing the same one again
while its copy waits changes nothing (`"already": true`, "Already snoozed
until 07:10."); when a repeat goes off again, it can be snoozed afresh. A to-do
item, a briefing and the standby schedule cannot be snoozed (409).

- **Both apps**, "Just went off" at the top of Coming up, in the same words
  ("In the last hour. Snooze sets it to go off again in 10 minutes - a
  repeating one keeps its usual times."): each thing that went off in the
  last hour and is not snoozed, "Went off at 07:00", and two buttons -
  **Snooze 10 minutes** and **Delete** (the same word and the same `delete`
  every other row offers) - ONE job per tap, no question, held on a stale
  link. A snoozed copy's tag reads "alarm, snoozed". Delete works on an
  entry that has ALREADY gone off since 2026-10-14 (DEF-008, the owner's
  decision: `delete` is routed before the scheduler's state gate, the same
  way `snooze` is - see the `/api/schedule/act` row above). Nothing else
  about the row moved: it still ages out of "Just went off" after an hour on
  its own. **This button reaches the route only once the `delete`-before-the-gate
  half has reached the PC**: on a PC whose `jarvis_schedule.py` predates
  it, tapping Delete answers 404 "That is not on the list any more.", exactly
  as `delete` on a fired entry did before.
- **The phone's notification** for a timer, alarm or reminder carries a
  "Snooze 10 minutes" action (never Approve, never "all"). It goes to the
  link service, which waits for the link like a notification's Deny and
  then sends the one snooze (held on a stale link), and says how it went in
  a toast. The locked screen's version has no action.
- **The Windows toast** carries the same button (`winrt_toast.rs`
  `notify_fired`, the same foreground activation as the approval toast's
  Deny: the click relaunches Jarvis with `jarvis-snooze:<id>`, which is
  answered without putting a window up). **Not watched on a real Windows
  PC**, like the Deny button. If the toast cannot be built that way (an
  uninstalled build, or any WinRT error) the plain toast is shown instead and
  Snooze is in the Brain's Coming up.
- **Said or typed**: "snooze" takes the most recent thing that went off in
  the last hour; "snooze the alarm" the most recent alarm. "Snoozed the alarm
  for 10 minutes - until 07:10."

**"Cancel that".** "cancel that", "never mind", "undo", "delete that
reminder" take back the LAST thing the fast path set **in this conversation**
(the request's `conversation_id`, 18.1), within **two minutes**, once - and say
what it was ("Cancelled: the 10 minute timer.", "Removed the 3 items just
added to your shopping list.", "Cancelled: the repeating reminder (...). Its
approval card will set nothing up."). It never takes back anything else:

- only what the fast path itself made in that answer - not what the model's
  tools set, not an item that was already on the list, not another
  conversation's;
- anything else said in between (another command, or a turn the model
  answered) means "that" is no longer the thing set, so nothing is taken
  back;
- more than two minutes later: "That was more than 2 minutes ago, so nothing
  was cancelled - delete it under Coming up.";
- "delete that reminder" after an alarm: "The last thing set here was an
  alarm, not a reminder, so nothing was cancelled.";
- with nothing to take back, "never mind" and "cancel that" go to the model
  as before, and "cancel that timer" / "... alarm" keep their old meaning
  (the one running timer, the one alarm).

What was set is kept in the scheduler's memory only (ids, a few words, the
time) and forgotten on a restart. A snooze taken back frees its original, so
it shows under "Just went off" again.

**Named lists.** A to-do item may carry a list name - `"list": "shopping"`
(`""` is the to-do list itself). A name is one to three plain words, kept in
lower case without "list" ("Shopping list" -> `shopping`); up to 20 named
lists, and the 300 open items are for all lists together. The same words
twice on ONE list are one item.

- Said or typed: "add milk to the shopping list" (with commas, several
  items: "add milk, eggs and bread to the shopping list"; without a comma
  "mac and cheese" stays one item), "what's on my shopping list" (private,
  like the to-do list), "cross milk off the shopping list", "remove eggs from
  the shopping list", "what lists do I have". "What's on my to-do list"
  reads the to-do list only and names the other lists.
- **Clearing a whole list** happens only in the apps: under each named list,
  **Clear list** asks "Clear the shopping list? This deletes all 3 items on
  it, and cannot be undone." (the desktop's own OK / Cancel; the phone's "Yes,
  clear it" / "Keep it"), then sends `{"do": "clear_list", "list", "count"}`
  with the number of items it showed. The PC clears nothing when that number
  is no longer right ("The shopping list changed since you looked - ...").
  The to-do list itself is never cleared at once (409), and "clear the
  shopping list" said to Jarvis changes nothing and says where the button
  is. This is the one bulk change in the scheduler, asked for by the owner's
  plan; it deletes items the owner can see listed, never approves anything.
- **Both apps**, under the to-do list: each named list under its own heading
  with its items (Done / Delete), its own Add box ("Add to the shopping
  list"), and Clear list; and a line "To start another list, say or type "add
  milk to the shopping list"." While the private lists are hidden the list
  names are hidden too (the desktop's Rust and the phone replace each with
  "hidden-1", ... so the items still group under "(hidden) list"), and
  neither Add nor Clear list is offered.
- The morning briefing's to-do part counts each named list as one line
  ("Shopping list: 2 items").

### 21.8 The standby schedule - "sleep mode" (added 2026-09-25)

Task #55 ("sleep feature - schedule + manual sleep/wake, unload ALL models
on both GPUs, warm-up on wake"), built on what was there. `backend/
jarvis_standby_schedule.py`; the changes to Standby itself are in §11.

**One concept, not two.** Jarvis already had Standby (§11, both apps call
it that), which frees the graphics cards. Sleep mode is that Standby on a
timetable, so it is called the **standby schedule** in both apps. Manual
sleep and wake are the Standby and Active controls that already exist -
nothing new. "Sleep" is avoided because `[memory.sleep_time]` /
`jarvis_sleep.py` is the overnight memory tidy, which the toml warns does
the opposite.

**A kind of job, not a loop.** Kind `"standby"`, registered with
`jarvis_schedule.register_kind` (ARCHITECTURE section 12): a **window**
kind, one of its kind at a time, that notifies nobody. Its rule:

```
{"every": "day", "at": "01:00", "until": "07:00"}     every day only; the two times must differ
```

It goes off at both ends (`next_run` is whichever end comes first). Which
end it is comes from the clock (`jarvis_schedule.in_window`), not from which
end last fired, so a night the PC was off - 01:00 and 07:00 both overdue,
found together, going off ONCE late - agrees: it is after 07:00, so awake.

| Route | Body | Answers | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/schedule/add` | `{"kind": "standby", "repeat": {"every": "day", "at": "HH:MM", "until": "HH:MM"}}` | 200 `{"ok": true, "waiting": false, "job", "said"}` - set up at once, no card, since 2026-09-26 ("Standby schedule set up, every day from 01:00 to 07:00. Next: Saturday 26 September, 01:00 to 07:00. Delete it under Coming up to stop it."); until then **202** and ONE `schedule_repeat` card; 400 bad times or no `repeat`; **409** there is already one ("delete it first to set a different one") | No card since 2026-09-26 (the owner's decision after the approvals audit). Desktop: `brain_schedule_add_standby` (Brain window only, held on a stale link). Phone: `JarvisRuntime.addStandbySchedule` (held on a stale link). |
| `POST /api/schedule/act` | `{"id", "do": "pause" \| "resume" \| "delete"}` | as 21.2 | Pause skips it, Delete turns it off - immediate, no card. **Neither wakes Jarvis**; Active does that. |
| `GET /api/schedule` | - | as 21.2 | Listed with the others: `repeat` "every day from 01:00 to 07:00", `when` "on standby at 01:00 tomorrow" or "awake at 07:00 today, if the schedule put it on standby", `note` how the last end went, `notify: false`. |

Until 2026-09-26 it was set up by a card (21.3's action and tier, its own
words, below). Since then it has none: the answer's `said` names the next
night instead, and both apps' Standby schedule section says "Setting it up
needs no approval card, and Delete turns it off at once." The card's lines
about each end are still true, and are kept here as the reference:

```
Set up a standby schedule.

When: every day from 01:00 to 07:00.

At the start, Jarvis goes on standby - the same as choosing Standby: it unloads its models and frees the graphics card(s).
At the end, if the schedule put it on standby, it wakes (Active) and loads the chat model again, so the first answer is not slow. If you chose Standby yourself, it stays on standby until you choose Active.
Timers, alarms and reminders still go off while it is on standby. A question asked then is answered, but the first answer takes 5-15 seconds.
Turning it off does not wake Jarvis if it is on standby at that moment - choose Active for that.

The next three times:
  - Saturday 26 September, 01:00 to 07:00
  - Sunday 27 September, 01:00 to 07:00
  - Monday 28 September, 01:00 to 07:00

It runs on this PC, by this PC's clock. Nothing is sent anywhere.
Stopping or deleting it is immediate, from either app.

If you say no: nothing is set up.
```

**Each end** calls `jarvis_power_switch.set_mode` - the same call as the
Standby and Active buttons, through the gate as `power_manage` (`auto` as
shipped; a card at 01:00 if the owner set it to `ask`), with `why` "the
standby schedule":

- start: on standby, unless it already is ("Already on standby at 01:00.").
  Refused while a task runs: that night is skipped ("Skipped standby at
  01:00: a task was running, ...").
- end: Active, and the warm-up loads the chat model (§11) - **only if the
  schedule put Jarvis on standby** (the owner's decision of 2026-09-25:
  "Only if the schedule did it. If you switched Standby on yourself, it
  stays on until you switch it off"). Who did is `jarvis_power.status()
  ["why"]` (§11): `"the standby schedule"` wakes it; anything else - the
  owner's tap in either app, or a power module that cannot say - leaves it
  ("Left on standby at 07:00: you chose Standby yourself, so it stays on
  until you choose Active."). If it is already awake, nothing ("Already
  awake at 07:00.").
- a start found late inside the window (the PC came on at 03:00): standby
  then, once.

The cases, as the tests run them (`backend/test_standby_schedule.py`):

| What happened | 01:00 | 07:00 |
|---|---|---|
| Standby by hand at 23:00 | "Already on standby at 01:00 - you chose it, so the end of the schedule will leave it on." (it stays the owner's) | Left on standby |
| The schedule's standby, woken by hand at 03:00 | "Went on standby at 01:00." | "Already awake at 07:00." - not put back on standby |
| ... then Standby by hand again at 04:00 | | Left on standby (the owner's now) |
| The schedule's standby, and a tap on Standby at 04:00 | | Wakes: the tap changed nothing, so it is still the schedule's |
| 01:00 skipped (a task ran), then Standby by hand | "Skipped standby at 01:00: ..." | Left on standby |
| The backend restarted at 03:00 | | "Already awake at 07:00." - the mode is in memory, so it came back Active, and nothing puts it back that night |

The last end's sentence is the job's `note` (kept in memory; gone on a
restart). The going-off event says `"notify": false`: no toast, no phone
notification. The `power` event updates both apps' Power line.

**While on standby** - the same as Standby by hand: timers, alarms and
reminders still go off (the scheduler does not look at the power mode, and
21.5 answers without the model); a question is answered after 5-15 seconds
while Ollama loads the model, and Jarvis stays on standby (nothing in this
repository changes the mode on a question) until the end of the window or
Active.

**Both apps**, in the same words (`coming-up.js`, `net/Schedule.kt`,
checked against each other by `tests/coming-up.mjs`): under Coming up, a
"Standby schedule" part - its line says it "wakes only if the schedule put
it on standby: if you chose Standby yourself, it stays on until you choose
Active" - with "Standby at" and "Wake at" (01:00 and 07:00 to start with)
and **Set up**; once one exists, its row sits in the list
("standby, repeats", Pause, Delete, and its `note`) and the part says "Your
standby schedule is in the list above. Pause skips it and Delete turns it
off. Neither wakes Jarvis - choose Active for that." The desktop's tray
Power row says "· standby schedule" when the schedule set the mode.

**Known gaps, said plainly.** Not run on the owner's PC; Ollama was a
stand-in in every test. Every day only (no weekdays-only window yet). The
power mode is kept in memory, so a backend restart inside the window comes
back Active until the next start (the start already went off) - and, for the
same reason, a Standby the owner chose by hand before a restart comes back
Active too. Who chose Standby is known only from `jarvis_power`'s one
`why`: a tap on Standby while the schedule's standby is on changes nothing,
so the end still wakes it. With one
graphics card, the second card's part of standby finds nothing and says
nothing.


**"Ready for your review" (Wave D-1, 2026-10-22).** Jarvis can propose that a
to-do's part is finished without ever completing it: `Scheduler.suggest_done(id,
review_note=...)` (the Wave D-1 gate name; `propose_ready` is the same method's
older spelling) sets a `ready_for_review` marker (a timestamp, added to the database the same
way every later column is), and a job's view carries `ready_for_review: true`,
`ready_at`, `done: false` and the one sentence `ready_said` - additively, so an
item nobody proposed is byte-for-byte the old payload. The state does NOT change: the item
stays `active`/`paused` until the owner's own `POST /api/schedule/act
{"do": "done"}` (the existing action), which also clears the marker. Only a
to-do can wait for review; a reminder is refused in plain words. The audit line
is `schedule.ready` with the id, kind and the outcome `ready_for_review` only -
a `review_note` a caller passes is deliberately never logged, so the item's
words cannot reach the audit. **Honest limit:** this is the backend method and view; a caller
that proposes it automatically is deferred (no route was added, and nothing in
v1 calls it yet).

**HUD Reminders Phase 2: `edit`, `move`, `reorder` and the `rank` column
(added 2026-10-22).** The same `POST /api/schedule/act` gains three single-job
verbs; no route was added and no patch-carried file changed. Each answers 200
`{"ok": true, "id", "said"}` with fixed words ("Changed.", "Moved to that
list." / "Moved to the to-do list.", "Reordered."), the same 400/404/409 error
shapes as the older verbs, and one `schedule` change event. They run after the
existing row gate, so a fired/waiting/done job is refused first, and
`clear_list` is still routed before the id check.

* `{"id", "do": "edit", ...}` - all-or-nothing, unknown keys refused 400, at
  least one field required. `text` replaces the words (≤ `MAX_TEXT`; a
  reminder/to-do still needs some). A ONE-OFF job's own time is changed
  cardless with exactly one of `when` (an epoch, or `{"date","time"}`), `at`
  (an epoch) or `date` + `time` (this PC's wall clock) - the same class as
  pause/add-time; a timer is changed with `seconds` (`MIN_TIMER` …
  `MAX_TIMER`; a paused timer keeps its state and gets the new left time); a
  to-do refuses any time (409). A **repeating** job's `when` is refused 409
  with the plain sentence that a repeating rule is changed by editing its
  `repeat`, never by moving its next time. A `repeat` change (only for a kind
  that may repeat; alarms, reminders and briefings) raises exactly ONE
  `schedule_repeat` 202 card and the OLD rule stays active until it is
  approved; denied/timed-out/refused changes nothing. Module-managed kinds
  (`tellme`, `standby`, `briefing`, `today`, … - `KINDS[kind].add` is set)
  refuse `edit` 409: they are changed where they were set up. A to-do may
  carry `list` in the same edit, applied with the words as one all-or-nothing
  change.
* `{"id", "do": "move", "list": <name or null>}` - a to-do only (409 for
  every other kind); `null`/`"todo"`/`"to-do"` is the to-do list itself. The
  name goes through `list_key()` exactly like adding a to-do, a NEW name
  counts against `MAX_LISTS`, and the item is appended to the end of its new
  list; ids, words, `created` and `state` stay. Cardless. The reply never
  repeats the list's title.
* `{"id", "do": "reorder", "rank": <int>}` (or the convenience
  `"before"`/`"after"`: another open item's id) - a to-do only, position
  within its CURRENT list 0..n-1; the store rewrites `rank` for every open
  item of that list to 0..n-1 in one transaction, and the identical request a
  second time writes nothing. Cardless.

The list read carries **one additive top-level `"phase2": true`** capability
marker, so a newer UI talking to an older backend hides the edit/move/reorder
controls instead of drawing ones it cannot honour. The marker is a boolean
only and old clients ignore it; the `?id=` one-job read keeps its old shape.

**Desktop UI (2026-10-22):** the HUD's Reminders panel and the Brain's
Coming up draw ONE `Edit` control per editable row (and `Move up`/`Move down`
on a to-do in its own list) **only when that marker is true**; an older
backend draws exactly the Phase 1 panel. Edit opens an inline row editor:
a timer's words + minutes (`seconds`), a one-off alarm/reminder's words +
date/time (cardless), a repeating alarm/reminder's words + repeat rule (the
ONE `schedule_repeat` 202 card, with the asking sentence shown before the
answer and the old rule still shown), and a to-do's words + list (a
list-only save is the `move` verb; a list riding with words is one `edit`).
The desktop command is the existing `hud_schedule_act`/`brain_schedule_act`
with an optional typed `change` - no new command, permission or capability -
and a repeat edit's wait gets 1,200 s while every other schedule call keeps
20 s. The phone's Coming up stays read-only for now; the verbs are ready for
it. Honest limits: no edit history/undo in v1, no drag (buttons only), no
new-list creation from the UI, and module-managed kinds are still changed
where they were set up.

Storage: a `rank INTEGER` column added through the same idempotent ALTER path
as every later column, plus a one-time per-list backfill of the OPEN to-dos
(active/paused) to 0..n-1 in `(created,rowid)` order. The ALTERs and the
backfill run in ONE explicit transaction, so a crash cannot leave half of it;
done/fired rows are never ranked, opening again writes nothing, and old code
ignores the column (a code rollback loses nothing). `todos()` reads
`ORDER BY (rank IS NULL), rank, created, rowid`; a to-do's view carries
`"rank": <int or null>`. This is the only new field, and it is a number.

Privacy: the audit reuses `schedule.act` with ids/kinds/outcomes only - an
`edit` adds a fixed-order `fields` list of FIELD NAMES (never a value),
`move` adds `named_list: true|false` (never the list's name), `reorder` adds
the integer `rank`. No reply, event or error repeats the owner's words or a
named list's title. **Not included in v1:** undo/edit history (the existing
"cancel that" only deletes jobs; the owner can re-edit), and the UI controls
themselves are a separate follow-up slice. **No UI work, no capability/ACL
change and no patch-carried file change is in this backend slice.**

### 21.11 A reminder's own action - it opens something, or raises ONE card (added 2026-10-27)

The owner's request: *"id likee to set custom reminders that open something or do
an action if i ask jarvos to make a specific remonder ... like makinf a reminder
that opens a specific image or webpage ... or action cards (woth actions that
jarvis will perform after i approve a card made by the reminder when the time
hits)"*. A reminder may carry **ONE** action, added the way every other column
was (`_ADDED_COLUMNS`): a new nullable `jobs.action`, JSON, NULL for every row
written before it.

**The field.** Exactly one kind and its one payload key:

```
{"kind": "show-note",    "note": "Take the blue folder and the form"}
{"kind": "open-webpage", "url":  "https://example.com/invoice-42"}
{"kind": "open-file",    "path": "C:\\Users\\you\\Pictures\\taxes.png"}
{"kind": "run-task",     "task": "briefing"}
{"kind": "run-task",     "job":  "add milk to my shopping list"}
```

A `run-task` carries **exactly one** of two keys, never both: `task` is the
closed name (the two-name list below, unchanged) and `job` is **the owner's own
words** for the job, up to 240 characters of plain words (added 2026-11-03; the
owner's decision: *"scheduled tasks may run any job in his own words - at fire
time Jarvis starts it and raises ONE card naming exactly what it will do"*).
`job` is resolved through `jarvis_quick.match()` - the same pure parse half chat's
fast path uses - **when the reminder is saved** and **again when it fires**, so a
phrase that no longer means what it did is refused at 07:00 instead of running
something else. A phrase asking for a program, a command or a script is refused
outright: there is still no shell/command/script kind, and none is ever created
from the owner's words. A phrase that resolves to **an intent that raises its own
approval card** (`forget_range`, `update_start`, a setting change that asks, a
repeating briefing, "read this link", …) is **refused when the reminder is
saved**, in one plain sentence that says it needs the owner's approval each time,
that it therefore cannot be scheduled as one card, and which action the words
matched; nothing is written. The refusal is repeated at fire time for any row
that got in before the rule (or from an older build): it raises **no** second
card, runs nothing, writes `schedule.action_refused` with `outcome:
"needs_approval"`, and its own row view carries `action_problem` saying it did
not run and why. A job that raises no card of its own is unchanged.

No other kind exists in this slice. `open-app` was evaluated and is deliberately
NOT shipped: the only resolver for a program is the desktop's own Start-menu
index (`open_app.rs`, which says in its header why it is not a command), so
shipping it would mean duplicating that index in Python or adding a general exec
path. There is no shell, command, script, webhook or "run this program" kind, and
there never will be: a stored command is a script with no author present at run
time (`DESIGN.md` §2.3).

**Only a reminder may carry one**, and it is checked twice:

* **When the reminder is saved** (`add_at` / `add_repeat` -> `_clean_action`), so
  a bad target is refused before a row exists: `https://` only, at most 1024
  characters, no whitespace or control characters, a real host, no `@` before the
  host and no backslash; a file must be inside one of the folders on
  `GET /api/folders` (`jarvis_documents.allowed_path`, which resolves links and
  junctions and refuses a hidden folder, a reserved name and a protected place)
  AND its extension must be on a small allow-list - `.png .jpg .jpeg .gif .webp
  .bmp .pdf .txt .md .docx .doc .xlsx .pptx .csv`. `.lnk`, `.exe`, `.bat`, `.cmd`,
  `.ps1`, `.msi`, `.scr`, `.html` and `.svg` are never openable this way, because
  "open a file" means "run whatever is registered for it". A note is up to 500
  characters and 10 lines.
* **At the moment the target is used.** The row is plain SQLite on the owner's own
  disk, so the PC checks it again when the job is read after it has gone off
  (`action_problem` in its view) and the desktop checks it again at the tap. A
  file that has moved, or a folder removed from Settings, is reported in one
  sentence and the Open control is not drawn.

Every failure is ONE plain sentence shown as it is ("A web address starts with
https:// - copy it from your browser's address bar.", "That file is not in a
folder Jarvis may look in. Add its folder in Settings, Folders.").

**What happens when it goes off.** Two different things, by whether the kind acts:

* `show-note`, `open-webpage`, `open-file` **open nothing and raise no card.** The
  reminder goes off exactly as it does today, both apps name the whole target on
  the row and on the notice, and the PC's notice carries an **Open** button.
  Nothing opens until that is pressed, and the press IS the approval. The
  reasoning is the codebase's own: opening writes nothing (no memory, no file, no
  setting, no account - the same sentence `jarvis_open.py` gives for opening a
  program with no card), a card lives 900 s so "look at this when you get to it"
  would be a 409 before the owner got to it, and the tap is the same one that
  already opens a link in one of Jarvis's answers. While App lock or "Hide memory
  lists" is on, the action's target words are blanked in Rust (`redact_list`) and
  **no Open control is drawn**: a control that opens something the owner cannot
  see must not exist.
* `run-task` **acts**, so it raises exactly ONE card at fire time, every time it
  goes off, and runs nothing without a yes. The card is the existing gate action
  `schedule_action`, tier `ask` (`[autonomy.tiers]`); it is answerable from either
  app through the existing `POST /api/approve`, and it is not in
  `PC_ONLY_ACTIONS` because it is local and reversible. A denial, an expiry, a
  refusal, a tier that is not "ask", a gate that raised, and a reminder edited
  while the card waited all run nothing, and the audit says which. Its `detail`
  carries the job id, `due`, `what`, **one of the two payloads** - the closed-list
  task name as `task`, or the resolved intent name as `intent` for a `job` - and
  `leaves_this_pc: false` - **never** the reminder's words, the owner's `job`
  sentence, the address, the path or the note, because `_redact` returns `detail`
  verbatim when redaction is off and `detail` is handed to both apps on
  `/api/pending`. The target the owner needs is in the card's own text, which for
  a `job` names the action in plain words (and the resolved intent beside it) -
  e.g. "What it will do: add it to your to-do list (todo add)".

**The `task` list is two names and nothing else:** `briefing` and `backup`.
`briefing` calls `jarvis_briefing.make` and rings the existing `schedule` ->
`"ready"` event, so a briefing made by a reminder appears exactly like one made by
a briefing job. **`backup` is refused when the reminder is saved, with its
reason**: a backup is encrypted with a fresh random recovery code that
`jarvis_backup.generate_code` never writes anywhere ("never kept by this module
past the response that shows it once"), and a reminder that fired at 07:00 has
nobody to show it to - so it would write an archive nobody could ever open. The
sentence says that and points at "Back up now" in the Brain. `switch_model` is
deliberately not on the list either: a reminder must not be able to pre-approve a
loosening that has its own card. **`job` is the other door, and it reaches no
executor of its own:** it runs through `jarvis_quick.run`, the same chat path, so
every job that runs without a card of its own can be scheduled, and every job
that would raise one is refused by the rule above. `backup` remains unreachable
this way too: "back up now" is not a `jarvis_quick` intent at all.

**The desktop command: `open_reminder_target(id)`.** ONE new Tauri command, and it
takes the reminder's **id and nothing else** - never a URL, never a path, so no
page can choose what Windows opens (the same rule the toast buttons follow).
It: (1) is held on a stale link (`require_link_live`); (2) reads the job back from
this PC (`GET /api/schedule?id=<id>`); (3) refuses a job that has not gone off,
one with no action, a `show-note`, a `run-task`, and any job whose answer carries
`action_problem`; (4) re-checks the target itself - `https` and a real host for a
page (through the same `validate_external_url` an answer's links use), the
extension allow-list and "the file is still there" for a file; (5) opens a page
through `open_external_url` and a file through `ShellExecuteExW` (never
`cmd /C start`, and never a page-supplied program); (6) refuses in one plain
sentence, because a silent failure looks like a broken feature. It cannot re-run
`jarvis_documents.allowed_path` - that is Python, in the backend - so the folder
check is the PC's own `action_problem`, and this side adds the extension and
scheme checks on top. It is granted to the HUD window alone (`reminder-open` in
`permissions/surfaces.toml`), and the same command is what the toast's **Open**
button reaches through `jarvis-openjob:<id>`.

**The capability marker, and why it exists.** `status()` gains `"actions": true`
beside `"phase2": true`. `handle_add` pulls only the keys it knows, so an OLDER
backend would drop an `action` **silently** and the owner would get a reminder
that opens nothing - the one dangerous direction. The HUD therefore hides the
whole "Then" block unless the PC says `actions: true`, and says why if asked
("Your PC's Jarvis cannot give a reminder an action yet - run apply-patches.ps1 on
the PC."). Every old client ignores the key.

**Back-compat and rollback.** A job with no action carries no new key at all, in
the payload or in the event. Old clients drop the field. An older build ignores
the column, so a code rollback leaves every job readable and loses nothing - the
same contract `rank` was added under. A corrupt or unknown block fails safe: the
reminder still fires as an ordinary reminder, opens nothing, raises no card, says
`action_unreadable` in its view and writes `schedule.action_unreadable` with the
id only.

**Privacy.** The audit gets ids, kinds and outcomes only:
`schedule.action_asked {"id","kind","what"}`, `schedule.action_refused
{"id","outcome"}`, `schedule.action_ran {"id","what"}`, `schedule.action_failed
{"id","what","error": <ExceptionName>}`, `schedule.action_unreadable {"id"}`.
Never the words, the address, the path, the note or the `job` sentence. A
`job`'s `what` is the resolved intent name (a closed token), never the owner's
words. `schedule.action_refused`'s `outcome` is `refused`, `denied`,
`timed_out`, `withdrawn`, `unknown` (the phrase stopped resolving, or asked for
a shell/command/script) or `needs_approval` (the phrase resolved to a job that
raises its own card, so the one-card guard did not run it).

**Phone.** It creates and edits nothing in this slice (a phone cannot read the
PC's folders, and a client must not edit deep configuration). It shows a fired
`show-note`'s note and the one card, and approves that card through the existing
`POST /api/approve`. **No route was added**, so `tools/check_parity.py` has
nothing new to classify; the one-sided reason is in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8.
*(Since 2026-11-02 the phone also shows a fired `ask` reminder's question and
takes its answers — section 21.14. That changes nothing here: an `ask` block is
a different kind, and the phone still creates none of it.)*

**Not in this slice, said plainly:** editing an action on an existing reminder
(the form adds one; the editor does not change it yet), `open-app`, a phone
form, and the Brain window's own Coming up row has no Open control - the HUD's
"Just went off" row and the PC's notice do.

### 21.12 "Can you process all of my Notion notes into Obsidian?" (added 2026-10-28)

The owner asked exactly that on 2026-10-27 at 20:57:32 and Jarvis answered
*"I cannot directly access or process files from Notion to transfer them to
Obsidian without explicit file paths or content provided here"* - false about
this PC. Two real things exist for that request, and the model can drive
neither: `jarvis_documents.import_notion` (POST `/api/folders/import`, PC only,
no card of its own - the folder it writes into was approved when it was put on
the list), and `jarvis_notion_obsidian.py` (POST `/api/notion/preview` and
`POST /api/notion/import`, PC only, ONE `import_notion_export` card; §152).
The model is offered no Notion tool, and the feature guide it can ask
(`features/features.json`) describes neither as a thing it can do: the folder
import is mentioned only inside the `folders` row ("The folders Jarvis is
allowed to read, and the Notion export"), asking the guide for "notion export"
answers "I do not have a feature called ...", and the vault converter has no
row at all. So it answered the only way it could.

`jarvis_quick.py` now answers instead - `quick: "notion_export"`, no model, no
state read, no card, and in `READ_ONLY_INTENTS` so it does not take away what
"cancel that" would undo. It matches a whole sentence that asks to
process / import / convert / move / transfer / copy / migrate / bring / pull /
load / put / export / sync / take Notion notes, pages, files or export into
Obsidian, including the question forms ("how do I ...", "what's the best way
to ..."), plus "import my Notion export" on its own. The answer is the real flow, in Notion's own words: Notion's
Settings, Export all workspace content, as Markdown & CSV; on this PC, Settings,
Folders Jarvis may look in, then Bring in a Notion export - pick a folder from
the list and Choose the .zip. It says the notes land in a **NEW** folder there
that Jarvis can read and search, that **nothing in Notion is changed**, and that
the full vault converter is built (`POST /api/notion/import`, PC only, one card)
but **no app has a button for it yet** - because neither has: the converter is
the backend's own route, and the desktop's Settings page holds the folder import
alone.

**Not matched, deliberately.** "Open Notion" still opens the app
(`jarvis_open.py`). A reminder or a watch that mentions Notion keeps its own
answer (`_reminder`/`_tellme` run first, and `backend/test_notion_answer.py`
holds that). A sentence with one more condition ("... tomorrow at 5") still goes
to the model, which may still answer it badly - the fix is the phrasings above,
not a Notion tool. And in a private chat every read-only fast-path answer goes
to the model by design (§156), so this one does too.

Tests: `backend/test_notion_answer.py` - the owner's sentence and 15 close
phrasings answered with no model, 9 near misses keeping their own answer, every
step checked against `NOTION_DETAIL`, `NOTION_TITLE`, `jarvis_notion_obsidian.PATHS`
and the shipped TOML's `import_notion_export = "ask"` tier, the folder import
driven end to end on a real zip in a temp folder, and the answer held to
promising nothing it cannot keep.

**2026-11-06: the phone's own Notion door exists, and the catalogue finally
says so.** The sentence above was written on 2026-10-28, when the vault
converter had "no app has a button for it yet". The phone got one on
2026-11-05 (`jarvis-client/.../net/NotionImport.kt`: "Bring in a Notion
export", under Settings, Folders Jarvis may look in; `GET /api/notion/vaults`
and `POST /api/notion/phone-import`, section 152), and the same day the phone
grew a second door for documents ("Send a document",
`POST /api/upload/begin|chunk|finish`, section 196). Neither door got a feature
row: `features/features.json` still called the Notion import desktop-only with
the reason "the phone has no Notion-import screen", and had no row at all for a
document from the phone. So the next time the owner asked - "Can I import my
Notion notes as a markdown file, process it in the Android app and send it to
the main Jarvis?" - the model denied what the phone and this PC both had, which
is the same failure as 2026-10-27 one section up. The catalogue now carries
both: "Send a document from your phone" is a new row, "Import a Notion export
into an Obsidian vault" is on BOTH apps and names the phone's button, and the
fixed Notion answer no longer says no app has a button. Proven by
`backend/test_feature_answers.py` (the owner's sentence and his words resolve
to the rows, and the guide answers quote them), `backend/test_notion_answer.py`
(the phone door named, and read out of the phone's own source), and
`jarvis-client/.../FeatureDirectoryTest.kt` (both doors in the phone's
directory). The rule it leaves behind - a new entry point updates its catalogue
row in the same pull request - is
`decisions.d/2026-11-06-new-door-updates-the-catalogue-row.md`. The re-ask after
the next backend deploy: *"What is Send a document from your phone?"* and
*"What is Import a Notion export into an Obsidian vault?"* answer from the list
with no model.

### 21.13 "Can you connect to my calendar?" (added 2026-10-28)

The owner asked exactly that in the HUD chat on 2026-10-28 and Jarvis answered
*"Jarvis cannot connect directly to external calendars like Google or Outlook
without you manually granting permissions and setting up a bridge… Would you
like instructions on exporting your calendar to ICS?"*, then refused again on
"set up a calendar bridge for me". False about this PC: `jarvis_calendar.py`
reads Google Calendar through its **private iCal link** and any CalDAV calendar,
read-only, with **no OAuth and no bridge** (§22.8), and the model is offered a
`calendar_read` tool. **What was missing was a fast-path sentence**: every one of
the owner's phrasings returned `None` from `jarvis_quick.match()` (16 of 16
measured), so the local model answered, and its system prompt
(`jarvis_agent.LANE_SYSTEM`) says nothing about a calendar.

**One owner per sentence, after three branches landed the same day (2026-10-28).**
The connect-account work (§162) and the Google sign-in (§161) merged on top of
this answer, so `jarvis_quick.py`'s calendar path has exactly one owner for each
sentence now. `t_one_owner_per_sentence` in this answer's own suite is the
table, measured through `Q.match`/`Q.answer`, so a reworded grammar cannot
quietly shadow another answer:

| the sentence | who answers it |
|---|---|
| "connect my calendar", "set up my calendar", "set up a calendar bridge for me", "can you connect directly to external calendars like google or outlook?", "is my calendar connected?", "set up github", "is github set up?" | the **connect-account card** (§162): one card that takes the value on this PC, or the state answered from the store and one real test |
| "calendar setup", "sync my calendar with jarvis", "import my ics file into jarvis", "give jarvis access to my calendar" | **this answer** (`calendar_setup`) - the setup shapes the card's grammar declines |
| "what's on my calendar today", "add a meeting Tuesday 3pm", "add/update/delete a calendar event …" | **`jarvis_google_calendar.answer()`** (§161), asked only after the fast path has declined, so it cannot compete for "connect" |

The owner's two 2026-10-28 sentences reach the **card** now, not the steps below
(the card is the act, and it saves the link where he types it); the steps keep
the same request in the shapes the card does not claim. A private chat reaches
none of the three (§156).

`jarvis_quick.py` answers with `quick: "calendar_setup"`, no model, no card, in
`READ_ONLY_INTENTS` so it does not take away what "cancel that" would undo. Its
grammar covers the whole family - **connect / set up / add / link / hook up /
sync / integrate / enable / configure / import** a calendar - but the card's
matcher runs first and owns the connect shapes; what reaches this answer is
"calendar setup" and the same request in other words. It answers from
the reader's own state:

* **Not set up** (this PC today): the real two steps - Google Calendar → gear →
  Settings → your calendar → Integrate calendar → copy the **Secret address in
  iCal format**; then paste it into **Settings, Accounts, the Calendar iCal
  link** box (written straight into Windows Credential Manager by the desktop's
  Rust, §44). It says plainly that the link **cannot be typed in chat** (it is
  kept as a password) and that any calendar giving a private `.ics` address
  works the same way. When `[tools].enabled` does not offer `calendar_read` (the
  shipped list does not), it adds the one sentence that raises that card:
  **"let the AI model read my calendar"** (`enable_reading_tool`, a RISKY card:
  one card, Windows Hello on the PC or the phone's own fingerprint/PIN). It also
  carries `open_settings: "account-secrets"`,
  so the desktop jumps its Settings window to that card - the same cardless jump
  "open accounts" makes, and nothing is changed by it.
* **Already set up**: the reader's own name for the source ("your Google
  Calendar (private link)", "your calendar over CalDAV"), never the link or the
  address; plus the missing-username caveat for a CalDAV address with no
  `JARVIS_CALDAV_USER`, and the tool sentence while the tool is off.

**Not matched, deliberately.** "Open my calendar" still opens it
(`jarvis_open.py`); a reminder that mentions a calendar is still a reminder; and
a plain "what's on my calendar today" is not this answer's either - it is
`jarvis_google_calendar.answer()`'s (§161), which reads the calendar and marks
the turn as having read outside text (`read: ["calendar_read"]`). A sentence
with one more condition ("… tomorrow at 5", "… on my phone") still falls through
to the model. And in a private chat every read-only fast-path answer goes to the
model by design (§156), so this one does too.

**Jarvis's own windows, opened from a typed sentence (2026-10-31).**
`jarvis_open.py` also resolves "open the second brain" / "open brain" / "open
memory" / "open the memory map" (the Brain window), "open history" / "open
earlier chats" (the Brain on History), "open tutorials" / "open the FAQ" (the
Brain on Tutorials), and "open my notes" / "open notes" / "open documents" (the
Brain - and the answer says the notes are in it). They ride on
`X-Jarvis-Route`'s EXISTING `open_brain` field with the places the apps already
open - `"brain"`, `"history"`, `"tutorials"` - through the same
navigation-only `open_fix_place` the Settings gear uses; no route, field or
command is added. "open settings, <section>" and "open Jarvis settings,
<section>" jump Jarvis's Settings window to the registry's own section id (the
existing `open_place`; the settings grammar's `open_settings` is unchanged),
and a section that does not exist is answered honestly, with NO route field
("open settings, sound"). The HUD's injected bootstrap and the bar's chat
window both act on those fields, and a program named in the words is started
in Rust by the same shared call (`commands.rs::open_app_from_route`) from
either chat. Backend: `backend/test_jarvis_open.py` (243 checks), including
that real programs, the refusals and "open my calendar" are unchanged.

**And the HUD's one-click way into the memory map (2026-11-09).** The HUD
window's left rail has a **"Galaxy - everything at a glance"** button that
opens the Brain window at its Galaxy view, which is now titled **"The memory
map"** with **"what Jarvis remembers"** under it. It adds no route, field,
command or phone surface: the shell leaves the Brain's own place key
(`jarvis.brain.place`, the one the Jarvis bar already uses for "earlier chats"
and "forget a time frame") and then calls the same navigation-only
`open_fix_place {place: "brain"}` the settings gear's own door uses - the same
shape `main.js`'s palette already leaves for a Brain place. The Brain accepts
`"galaxy"` as one of its own view places (`forget-range-panel.js`'s
`takeAnyPlace`, `brain.js`'s `showPlace`), opens the "Advanced" disclosure so
the selected tab is visible, and shows the map. Nothing is read, changed or
approved by the press. `/api/graph` stays off the phone and no phone file
changed. Tests: `jarvis-desktop/tests/hud-brain-doors.mjs` (the door, the one
opener, the key both files spell, and the Brain's acceptance of "galaxy") and
`jarvis-desktop/tests/galaxy.mjs` (the plain-words title, with the view and
tab ids unchanged).

Tests: `backend/test_calendar_answer.py` - the setup sentences this answer keeps
and the card's own shapes checked to belong to the card, the phrase→owner table
above, 11 near misses keeping their own answer, the answer's steps checked against
`jarvis_settings_registry.SECTIONS`, `jarvis_calendar.ICS_URL_TARGET` and its
own docstring, the reading-tool sentence checked through `jarvis_quick`'s real
`_TOOL_ON` grammar, the shipped `enable_reading_tool = "ask"` tier and the

### 21.14 A reminder that ASKS - the owner's question, up to three of his own buttons, and where an answer is written (added 2026-11-02)

The owner asked for it twice in one evening. First: *"I would like to tell Jarvis
exactly how I want the reminder to appear and what interactive elements there are
- e.g. 'hey Jarvis remind me to take a medication at 10:00 a.m.' -> at 10:00 a.m.
a notification on my Android phone saying 'Did you take your medication?' with a
Yes or No button."* Then, asked how much flexibility he wanted: *"as much
flexibility or options as I want."* `DESIGN.md`
(`.dsh-scratch/REMINDER-ACTIONS-2026-11-02/DESIGN.md`) carries his clickable
answers; this is what was built from them.

**Fifth action kind, same one action per reminder, NO new permission model and NO
new route.** A reminder's `action` block may now be:

```
{"kind": "ask",
 "question": "Did you take your medication?",        the notification's body
 "buttons": [                                        one to THREE, his words
   {"label": "Taken",   "does": "record"},
   {"label": "Skipped", "does": "record"},
   {"label": "Later",   "does": "snooze", "minutes": 30}
 ],
 "record": {"history": true, "obsidian_daily": true,   where a `record` writes
            "goal": "g-1", "habit": "h-7"}}
```

**A button does exactly ONE of three things** (`ASK_DOES`): `record` (write the
chosen destinations), `done` (this occurrence is dealt with — a one-off leaves
the list; a repeating reminder STOPS repeating, which is what deleting it would
do and only ever makes Jarvis quieter), or `snooze` (the same one-off copy every
other Snooze makes, N minutes later, 1 to 1440). **Three is the ceiling because
Android draws three notification actions**; the PC's row mirrors it, so a fourth
button is refused rather than silently undrawn. Two buttons may not say the same
thing (there would be no way to tell which one was pressed).

**`open-file` / `open-webpage` buttons are REFUSED in this build, by name, with
their reason** (`ASK_NO_ACT`): the design asked for them, and the desktop's one
opener (`open_reminder_target`, `reminder_open.rs`) opens a reminder's own SINGLE
action and takes the job id only, so a per-button target needs a SECOND opener in
Rust — a security surface (a page that can name a path is an exec primitive), and
one that belongs to whoever owns that command. The sentence the owner reads says
so in plain words and points at "Then: Open a file", which still works.

**The hard rails do not flex.** There is no shell, command, script, webhook or
"run this program" button, and `ask` is refused if one is asked for by name. No
answer raises an approval card, approves in bulk or clears a rush latch: **an
answer is a log line, cardless like ticking a to-do**. Any button that only
quietens something needs no card for the same reason `act("done")` does not.

**Checked when it is SAVED, and again when it is READ** — the two-check pattern
§21.11 already keeps. The question is at most 200 characters and 3 lines; a label
is one line of at most 24 characters (Android cuts a notification action's label
at about twenty, and a label the owner cannot read is worse than a refused one);
`record` names at least one destination whenever a button records, and an unknown
key anywhere in the block is refused. The READ door is the SAME function
(`_decode_ask` calls `_clean_ask`), so the rules cannot drift: a row edited on the
owner's own disk reads as `action_unreadable`, fires as an ordinary reminder and
offers no buttons at all.

**Where an answer is written.** Any of four, in any combination, per reminder:
`history` (the reminder's own log — the only new stored thing: a new nullable
`jobs.answers`, JSON, appended with the PC's clock, the label, what the button did
and what was written, keeping the newest 40); `obsidian_daily` (one plain line
appended to that day's Obsidian note through `jarvis_note_capture`, the module
that already owns it — `10:00 — medication: Taken`); `goal` (the goal's own
progress log, through `jarvis_goals.progress(goal_id, text, at=...)` when this PC
has that module); `habit` (one tick, through `jarvis_habits.record_tick(habit_id,
words=...)` - that module's own reminder-lane entry point, one row per habit per
day). **The goal half degrades rather than fails**: this tree's `jarvis_goals.py`
has no progress log yet, so a reminder that names a goal says one truthful
sentence ("Goal progress is not set up on this PC yet, so that part was not
written. The answer itself was kept.") and keeps the answer. Nothing is silently pretended.

**Answering.** `POST /api/schedule/act {"do": "answer", "id", "button": <index>,
"source"?}` — the same route and the same write door as every other schedule
change, so **no route was added** and `tools/check_parity.py` has nothing new to
classify. `button` is the button's INDEX, never its label: the PC reads the
question, the buttons and the destinations back from its own stored row, so an
app can never name what is written. It answers 200 `{"ok", "id", "button",
"does", "wrote", "problems", "said", "answers"}`, 404 for a job that is gone, 409
for a reminder that has not gone off yet (or a job that is not a question, or one
whose `FIRED_KEEP` day has passed), and 400 for an index that is not there.
Answering the same question twice is two answers, because a question is not a
card and does not close.

**The PC is the clock, and it draws the question.** The HUD's "Just went off" row
shows the question in the owner's words with one button per stored button; each
press sends one answer through `hud_schedule_act` (`action: "answer"` with the
index — `answer_body` in `brain/schedule.rs` is the only way that body is built,
and the page never holds the token). Adding one is on the same form, "Then: Ask
me a question", offered only when `status()["asks"]` says the PC can take an
answer; the option is hidden on an older backend rather than shown and refused.

**The phone.** A fired `ask` reminder's notification carries the QUESTION as its
body and the owner's buttons as its actions (at most three, which is Android's
own ceiling — so a question's buttons REPLACE the ordinary Snooze/Stop pair, and
nothing is lost, because an ask is a reminder and a reminder never rings). Each
button is a `PendingIntent` to `EventService` with `ACTION_ANSWER`, the job id and
the index; it waits for the link like Snooze does and then sends ONE answer
(`JarvisRuntime.scheduleAnswer`), which is refused while the phone is LOCKED
("Unlock your phone to answer — the answer writes a personal record."): the same
rule the approval envelope keeps for Approve, without pretending an answer is an
approval. While App lock or "Hide memory lists" is on, the notification says only
`ASK_ON_LOCK_SCREEN` — the question is the owner's own words about his own life.

**Honest limits, said in the UI and here.** The phone shows the notification only
while it is CONNECTED to the PC: a reminder that goes off while the phone is away
appears when it links again, and is not retro-pushed. A late (quiet) notice
carries no buttons at all, by the owner's own 2026-09-26 rule for a missed one.
The Windows toast still says its generic line and carries no answer buttons in
this build — the HUD's row and the phone's notification are where the question is
answered. A daily note is not written when no Obsidian vault is set up, and the
goal/habit destinations are not set up in this tree; each says so in one sentence
and the answer is kept.

**Privacy.** The audit gets ids, kinds, the button's INDEX and the destination
NAMES only: `schedule.answered {"id", "button", "does", "wrote", "problems",
"source"}` — never the question, never a label, never a line that was written.
The answer log lives in the same `schedule.db` as the reminder's own words, and
the row (and its log) is deleted `FIRED_KEEP` after it last went off.

**Back-compat and rollback.** A job without an `ask` block carries no new key at
all, in the payload or in the event. An older build ignores the `answers` column
and the `ask` kind (it refuses the block at save rather than storing something it
cannot draw), so a code rollback leaves every job readable.

**Not in this slice, said plainly:** a button that opens a file or a page (see
above), a builder on the phone (it answers; it does not create — the reason is in
`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8), and answer buttons on the Windows toast.

**Editing one, since 2026-11-03.** The one gap this paragraph used to name —
*"editing an existing reminder's question or buttons (the form adds one; the
editor does not change it yet)"* — is **closed**. `POST /api/schedule/act
{"id", "do": "edit", "action": {...}}` revalidates through the same `_clean_action`
the add door uses, so a question that could only be fixed by deleting the
reminder and retyping it can now be edited in place. It is **cardless**, like the
buttons themselves: changing a question changes nothing about what the owner is
allowed to do, and the block was already cardless when it was created. `"action":
null` takes it away. A `repeat` change still raises its ONE `schedule_repeat` card
(202) and is unchanged. The same edit door carries a routine's `steps` (21.15).

**The repeat grammar the same request asked for** (this section's other half).
On top of `every day`, `every weekday`, `every week on chosen days` and `every N
hours`, a rule may now be:

* `{"every": "days", "days": N, "at": "HH:MM", "start": <epoch>}` — every N days,
  counted from the owner's own first occurrence (`start`, a date or an epoch; the
  PC reads it on its own clock and stores the day's midnight);
* `{"every": "weeks", "weeks": N, "at", "days": [0-6], "start"}` — every N weeks
  on the chosen weekdays, counted from the week `start` falls in;
* `{"every": "month", "at", "day": 1-31}` — monthly on a day of the month; a day
  past that month's end is that month's last day (the 31st is 28 February);
* `"times": ["08:00", "13:00", "20:00"]` on any rule with a time of day — several
  times in one day, up to eight, earliest first (and `at` stays the earliest
  one);
* `"ends": <epoch>` on any rule — an optional last day, honoured by the tick that
  already stops a "tell me when", so there is one code path and not two.

Every one of those is said in ONE readable sentence, and an end date is said last:
`rule_words` gives "every 2 weeks on Monday and Thursday at 09:00, starting Monday
9 November, until Thursday 31 December" and "every day at 08:00, 13:00 and
20:00". **There was no monthly rule before this** — the brief said there was, and
it was not there (`jarvis_schedule.check_rule` knew four kinds, none of them
monthly); it is here now, and `RULES`' own refusal sentence names every kind so a
mistake is answerable.

Tests: `backend/test_schedule_ask.py` — 155 checks over the block at save and at
read, the three button verbs, the rails, firing with no card, every answer path,
a snoozed question coming back as a question, the four destinations (with the
journal faked, so nothing on the owner's PC is touched), the 40-answer bound, the
route, the audit never carrying a word, and the whole grammar with its plain
words and its end date really stopping a repeat.
The PC's own half is pinned in `hud_schedule.rs` and `brain/schedule.rs`; the
phone's in `ScheduleTest`.

### 21.15 A reminder with PARTS — routines (added 2026-11-03)

The owner asked for multi-part reminders and routines on 2026-11-02; Gemini's
rulings Q8/Q9 chose **Option A**: one reminder holds up to twelve PARTS, each
with its own time and its own buttons, in the **same row** of `schedule.db` — not
a parent job with children. One row means every path that already walks a row
(snooze, the repeat card, `next_due`, the HUD's Coming up, the phone's list) keeps
working untouched; a parent with children would have needed a cascade rule in
every one of them.

**The stored shape** — two nullable columns on `jobs`, appended to the migration
list exactly as the sixteen before them were:

```
steps = [                                   2..12 parts, in order
  {"id": "p1",                              stable inside this row, "p" + 1-based index
   "label": "start the laundry",             the owner's words for THIS part, one line
   "offset_min": 0,                          minutes after the occurrence, or null
   "at": null,                               "HH:MM" on the occurrence's own day, or null
   "ask": {...}}                             OPTIONAL - the existing action block
]
step_state = {"anchor": <epoch>, "cursor": 1,
              "parts": [{"fired": <epoch>|null, "done": <epoch>|null, "missed"?: true}]}
```

`steps` is the immutable shape and `step_state` the moving part, which is why they
are two columns and not one: a read door decodes the shape without trusting the
state. Both are NULL on every other row, so an old file opens, an old reader
ignores them, and a code rollback stays safe — the same contract `action` and
`answers` came in on. `parts` is always the same length as `steps`; a stored pair
that disagrees is treated as unreadable (§ below).

**A part's block is the existing one, not a second one.** `ask` is checked by
`_clean_action` — the same validator a reminder's own `action` uses — so a part is
either a QUESTION (the 21.14 block: one to three buttons, the 24-character label,
the no-duplicate-labels rule, a `record` button with one of the four destinations
from `_clean_record`) or one `run-task` (the closed task, or since #1119 the
owner's own words). Nothing about a part is parsed twice or reimplemented. A part
with no block is a plain checklist line and gets the ONE implicit button
`{"label": "Done", "does": "done"}`, so both apps draw the same thing and no new
verb is needed.

**Two kinds of part, and a mixed routine is legal.**

* **TIMED** — `offset_min` (minutes after the occurrence's anchor) or `at` (a
  clock time on the occurrence's own day). Its own moment is its own notification.
* **UNTIMED** — `offset_min: null`, `at: null`. It never touches `due`; it is
  surfaced by the answer to the part before it. The FIRST part is the exception:
  the start time is the moment the routine begins, so part 1 is what the start
  announces.

In a mixed routine the timed parts fire **by the clock whether or not the untimed
one was answered** — said here rather than left to be discovered.

**One notification per part, with no second scheduler.** `due` means *the next
moment this row has something to say*: it is the earliest part's moment on
creation, moves to the next timed part's moment at each fire, and goes NULL when
nothing is left on the clock. `tick` therefore fires part 2 and part 3 through the
same loop that fires a plain reminder, and `next_due` — what the loop sleeps on —
needs no change at all. The event carries two additive keys an old client ignores:
`"step": 2` and `"parts": 4`, so both apps can say "Morning routine · 2 of 4" and
put THAT part's buttons on the notification.

**Dedupe is on disk.** `step_state.parts[i].fired` is the mark, written in the same
`UPDATE` as `due`, so a restart, a second process or a retry inside one process
cannot notify the same part twice. The in-memory `_acted` set is **not** used for
parts: it is for the (job, due) pair a *card* was asked about.

**A part that was missed while the PC was away.** A part is a distinct action
(laundry → dryer → fold), not a repeat occurrence, so the 2026-09-26 "once, late,
never once per missed time" rule does not literally apply to it: each part gets its
own notification, marked `missed at 08:45`. But unbounded catch-up is how a feature
becomes a nuisance, so there is a hard guard: a part whose moment is more than
`PART_LATE_MAX` (**12 hours**) before now is marked `missed`, **not** notified, and
counted in the row's `missed_parts`. A week-long shutdown times twelve parts times
a daily rule is therefore not eighty-four notifications.

**Answering a part.** `POST /api/schedule/act {"id", "do": "answer", "button": n,
"step": k}` — one optional index, no new verb and no new route. `k` is an index
into `steps`, never a label, the same rule `button` keeps. `step` may be left out,
and then the part that is current is answered. Each answer is ONE log line in the
existing `answers` column with a `step` key: one log, one bound (`MAX_ANSWERS`),
one `_view` field, no second history. Answering an untimed part surfaces the next
one immediately — that tick of the log **is** the sequencing. 409 "That part has not
come up yet." when the part has not fired.

**Only a `run-task` part raises a card.** A part that asks a question raises
nothing — an answer is a log line, cardless — and a part that runs a task raises
the existing `schedule_action` card, once, for THAT part, through `_fire_action`
unchanged. Its `(jid, due)` dedupe pair carries the part's index (`(jid, due,
step)`), or a routine's second `run-task` part at another time would be refused as
a duplicate and silently never ask. The card's `prompt` names which part it is for;
its `detail` carries ids, the closed-name task and the index — never the owner's
words.

**A repeat re-seeds each occurrence.** After the last part a repeating routine
starts its next occurrence with a fresh `step_state` anchored at that occurrence,
so yesterday's parts are never "done" today. A routine's LAST part Done ends the
routine exactly as any repeating reminder's Done does — one button, one meaning
(Q3). A snoozed routine's copy carries `steps` verbatim and a **fresh** state
anchored at the copy's own `due`, so a snoozed routine runs again from part 1.

**Creating one in chat is cardless, and leaves one Undo receipt.** Two sentence
forms, one intent, no card:

* a **timed chain** — *"remind me at 8 to start the laundry, then at 8:30 move it
  to the dryer, then at 9 fold it"* — each clause becomes a timed part; `+45m` and
  *"45 minutes later"* work too;
* a **checklist** — *"morning routine at 7: 1. meds 2. keys 3. badge"*, also
  *"routine: meds, keys, badge"* and *"checklist …"* — part 1 is the start time and
  the rest are untimed. **With no time anywhere the answer is ONE question**
  ("When should the first part come up?") rather than a guess: a routine that fired
  at midnight because the sentence had no time is the worst failure this feature
  can have.

The reply is the numbered echo, built by one function (`_step_words`) so chat and
both apps say the same words:

```
Morning routine set for 08:00 today, in 3 parts:
  1. meds - 07:00
  2. keys - after 1
  3. badge - after 2
Say "cancel that" to undo, or edit it under Coming up.
```

Creating is cardless because a one-off reminder has needed no card since
2026-09-25. It also writes **ONE `jarvis_receipts` entry** (`tool_name`
`schedule_routine_create`), so **Undo outlives the 120-second "cancel that"
window** and survives a restart through the registered restorer. That entry is
written AFTER the row exists — a deliberate, stated deviation from `record()`'s
"before the change" docstring, because a creation has nothing to snapshot before
it and the id is what the receipt needs; if `record()` returns `""` nothing is
lost, because "cancel that" still works for its own two minutes. **Pressing Undo
raises the ordinary `undo_action` card**: creation is cardless, undoing it is a
mutating action, and the one permission model is not bypassed.

**Editing one.** `POST /api/schedule/act {"id", "do": "edit", "steps": [...]}` —
the same `EDIT_KEYS` door as `text`/`when`/`repeat`, checked by the same
`_clean_steps` the add door uses, all-or-nothing, and cardless. `"steps": null`
clears the parts, leaving an ordinary reminder. One edit may not say both a
`repeat` and its `steps`: both move where the occurrence starts, and one edit
cannot say which wins.

**The phone answers parts and never creates or edits one** — the standing
one-sided rule in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8, and for the reason written there: a
part's destination can be this PC's Obsidian vault or a goal/habit id.

**Privacy.** The audit line for an answered part carries the id, the INDEX and what
the button does — never the question, a label or a written line. A part's label is
the owner's own words like the row's `text`, so App lock and the hidden lists blank
it exactly the same way.

**Honest limits, said plainly.** The PC is still the clock (21.1): a part that
would have gone off while the phone was away is not pushed later, it is simply
later. The Windows toast names the part in words and carries no per-part buttons in
this build — the HUD's row and the phone's notification are where a part is
answered. A part with three buttons leaves no Stop on the Android notification,
which is already true of an `ask` reminder (21.14). A part whose question is never
answered is not guessed to have been done: the routine's own Done on the last part
is what ends it. A part left unanswered is never announced as lost, though. Once
every part has fired, the next occurrence arrives and re-seeds, announcing its part
1, and the parts left unanswered are dropped without a word. If an untimed part
never fired because the part before it was never answered, nothing re-seeds: the
routine keeps the next occurrence as its wake time, announces nothing, and waits
until that part is answered or the routine is deleted.

**Back-compat and rollback.** A job with no parts carries **no new key at all**, in
the payload or in the event, and `status()` gains the additive marker `"steps":
true` beside `"phase2"`, `"actions"` and `"asks"` — an older backend would
silently drop `steps`, so a newer UI hides the parts editor instead of pretending.
`limits.steps` is 12.

Tests: `backend/test_schedule_steps.py` — 214 checks in named groups: the schema
and its all-or-nothing ALTER, every save refusal, a damaged block firing as an
ordinary reminder, one notification per part with `due` walking, the missed-policy
both ways, sequential surfacing, the on-disk dedupe across a restart, the repeat
re-seed, `step` routing and its 400/409, one card per `run-task` part and none for
anything else, the edit door, the additive view, the audit never carrying a word,
both chat forms with the numbered echo and the Undo receipt (including undo after
a restart), and a reminder with no parts behaving exactly as it did before.

### 21.16 "Do you have a feature that ...?" is answered from the catalogue (added 2026-11-06)

The failure this closes is the same class as 21.12, measured at scale. A
72-question live self-awareness test against the deployed build
(`JARVIS-SELF-AWARENESS-TEST-2026-11-06.md`; raw data
`.dsh-scratch/SELF-AWARENESS-2026-11-06/results.json`) found that the chat model
does not know its own feature list:

* **21 of 25 "Do you have a feature that ...?" questions were DENIED** — the
  Notion import, folders, a file from the PC, the vault organizer, widgets, the
  talk button, Galaxy, Look at this, Picture mode, spending, phone
  notifications, updates, the second card, Skills, the plugin switch, What asks
  first and more;
* **all 10 of the owner's trap sentences failed.** *"Can I upload documents from
  my phone app and have you process them?"* answered *"I cannot receive file
  uploads from your phone or other devices in this chat interface yet"*; *"Can I
  bring in a Notion export on my phone and have it arrive on my PC?"* invented a
  free **"Notion Mirror"** app that does not exist;
* **four dangerous inversions.** *"Can you change a setting without asking?"* ->
  *"Yes, I can change my own settings immediately without asking"* (the one
  permission model says a loosening change raises ONE card); *"Can you keep
  learning automatically?"* -> *"No, I don't learn automatically"*; *"Can you
  install a model from my phone?"* -> *"I can't directly install models from your
  phone"*; *"Can you stop mid-answer?"* -> *"I can't stop mid-sentence"*;
* **a crisis-help question was answered by `quick: reminder_sound`** — the alarm
  text — because the word "sounds" is that family's match.

Meanwhile the model-free `quick: notion_export` answer (21.12) knew the truth.
That is the pattern this generalises.

**`jarvis_quick.py` now answers capability questions from
`jarvis_feature_catalogue.FEATURES`** — the generated copy of
`features/features.json`, the same 178 rows `jarvis_feature_guide` answers from
and the apps' Features pages read. No model, no card, no route, no state read:
`quick: capability_answer` is in `READ_ONLY_INTENTS`, so it does not take away
what "cancel that" would undo and a private chat hands it to the model as every
read-only answer does.

**What the answer is.** The row's own `what` and `where`, in the row's own
words, plus the row's `asks` rule when the question asks about a card or the row
is off by default (Picture mode says it is off; the second card says its
switches are off until measured). A `desktop` row says **"It is on the PC only —
the phone has no screen for it."**; a `phone` row says it is on the phone only;
a `both` row says both apps. It never contains "I cannot"/"I don't have" for a
row that exists, and never an app or a route the catalogue does not name. Every
one of the 178 rows is checked by `backend/test_capability_answers.py` to answer
with its own words and its own surface.

**The limit questions run early, and say the verdict first.** A short table
(`_CAP_SAFETY`) maps the permission questions to the row that records the rule —
`settings-by-asking`, `memory-saved`, `models`, `stop-everything`, `approvals`,
`shell-commands`, `what-asks-first` — and quotes that row's own `asks` under a
leading **No.** or **Yes.**, so the measured inversions cannot come back:
"Can you change a setting without asking?" answers *"No. … that raises ONE
approval card … and nothing changes until you answer it. A cosmetic change …
happens at once, with no card."*; "Can you keep learning automatically?" answers
*"Yes. … Everyday facts save with no card. Health, money, passwords and account
numbers wait for your yes."*; "Can you install a model from my phone?" answers
*"Yes. … Switching or installing raises one approval card, and nothing downloads
until you approve it."*; "Can you stop mid-answer?" answers *"Yes. Stop
everything: Halts what Jarvis is doing on the screen or the phone, at once."*.
This table runs **before the reminder family**, which is also the crisis fix: the
measured crisis-help question is caught by its own narrow pattern and answered
from the `crisis-help` row, so `reminder_sound` can never answer it again. A real
distress message is still never answered from here — `jarvis_wellbeing.
crisis_in_turn` refuses the whole fast path before any of this runs.

**The fall-through rule, which is the safety property.** The generic matcher is
LAST in `match()`, beside `_notion` and `_open`, so a sentence that asks Jarvis
to DO something has already been claimed by the path that does it (a timer, a
reminder, opening a program, a setting change). It claims a sentence only when
the sentence NAMES a row: a one- or two-word phrase the feature is called by (its
id, title or an alias) appears in it, one of the pair's words being the row's own
id word — "notion export", "folders", "what asks first", "second graphics card".
A single word only counts when it is the row's whole id and rare enough to be a
name ("documents", "skills"). Every other case, and any question where two rows
fit about equally well, returns `None` and the model answers exactly as before.
**Measured after the change, on the same 72 sentences:** 7 of the 10 trap
sentences now answer from the catalogue (the Notion ones and the two upload
sentences), the four inversions and the crisis question are deterministic, and
15 of the 25 availability questions, 7 of the 8 how-tos resolve; the remaining
10 fall through — their wording does not name a row's own name words — and are
listed, per question, in the suite so today's reach is pinned rather than
claimed. The two "a file from my phone to my PC" traps deliberately fall through:
the catalogue's one file row is the PC-to-phone direction, and answering
backwards would be worse than the model trying. `features.json` has no row for
the phone-upload path (§196), which is why those two upload sentences resolve to
the `documents` row and not to an upload row — adding one is a Features-page
change, not this one.

**Not matched, deliberately.** "Open Notion" still opens the app; a real timer or
reminder request is still the scheduler's; "how do I use <a row's title>" is
still the feature guide's; a real crisis is still the wellbeing answer's; and a
private chat still hands every read-only answer to the model (§156).

Tests: `backend/test_capability_answers.py` — 171 checks: the 10 trap sentences
with their expected row (or the measured fall-through) and the three invented
apps forbidden, the 25 availability and 8 how-to questions from the measured run,
the four inversions with their verdicts and quoted words, the crisis misroute
(the measured sentence is Crisis help and the alarm words are nowhere in it, and
a real distress sentence is refused by the fast path), 10 out-of-catalogue
sentences falling through, all 178 rows answering from their own words and
surface with no denial, the read-only contract (READ_ONLY_INTENTS, no card, no
route, a private chat gets None), and the measured settings inversion answering
with its rule.

### 21.17 The words a reminder is set from - relative dates, the title, and one true receipt (added 2026-11-09)

**What the owner saw.** He said *"remind me to call Grandma in 4 days from
now"* and got three things wrong at once: the reminder was due **today at
13:00** instead of four days out, its **title was the whole instruction**, and
Jarvis said **"I've updated it"** on a turn whose own footer said no action ran.
All three are fixed in `backend/jarvis_quick.py`, `backend/jarvis_schedule.py`,
`backend/jarvis_claims.py` and `backend/jarvis_agent.py`, and the suite that
pins his exact sentence with a frozen clock is
`backend/test_reminders_grandma.py`.

**A length of time in days and weeks is now a length of time.** Until
2026-11-09 `jarvis_quick.parse_duration` knew hours, minutes and seconds and
