  the list hides behind the same Show the phone's other history surfaces use -
  the screen's heading and its way in from the Inbox stay, because they say
  nothing about what was decided.

### 42.3 Known gaps, said plainly

- **The exact field names on a `history` row are assumed, not confirmed** -
  see §42.1. This is the one gap the audit itself anticipated ("first,
  check on your PC what the gate's `history` rows hold") and the one this
  section could not close from inside this repository.
- **No skipped-row notice.** `pending()`'s reader tells the owner when a row
  could not be read, because a decision is still waiting on it; a *past*
  card carries no such urgency, so a history row this phone cannot parse is
  silently dropped from the list rather than reported - unlike the live
  queue's own skipped-row count.
- **No paging.** The list shows whatever `history` sends in one read; there
  is no "load older" here, unlike Chat history's (§18) `before=`.
## 43. In-app switches for tools the AI may use (unlocked, 2026-11-04)

The owner asked for in-app switches instead of hand-editing `[tools].enabled`.
Gemini's 2026-10-31 ruling made it **tiered, not indiscriminate** - only Tier A
and Tier B were offered in the app, and Tier C and the unlisted tools stayed
settings-file choices. **The owner reversed the ON half on 2026-11-04:** "few
restrictions on its tools beyond the core values of jarvis that have already
been established, particularly reverse engineer anything among other things",
and, asked what the app should allow, they chose **"Switch any of them on in
the app"**. So every tool the AI model can be offered is switchable ON from the
Tools page, one approval card each. The only limits left are the five
non-negotiable rules (`CLAUDE.md`) and the shape below.

**The 60 switches** (2026-11-05; 48 at 2026-11-04, plus the six on-demand
  GitHub tools, hands-free's `send_text_message`, the approval-policy tool's
  own row and the four pack tools `pack_list`, `pack_inspect`, `pack_install`
  and `pack_remove`, below), in the page's own groups:

- **Notes and reading:** `calendar_read`, `notes_search`,
  `append_obsidian_daily`, `create_joplin_note`, `append_logseq_journal`.
- **Timers, lists and plans:** `set_timer`, `set_reminder`, `todo_add`,
  `todo_done`, `coming_up`.
- **Connected accounts & home:** `email_check`, `send_email`, `draft_email`,
  `tidy_inbox`, `home_read`, `home_control`, `my_spending`,
  `retirement_whatif`.
- **Safety and sharing:** `protect_from_jarvis`, `github_search`,
  `send_file_to_phone`.
- **Raw and powerful:** `shell_exec`, `control_computer`, `control_phone`,
  `browser_control`, `read_web_page`, `connect_account`, `rea_investigate` -
  the raw Tier C set, switchable since 2026-11-04. REA also needs its own
  `[rea] enabled = true`; browser control also needs its own switch (the
  second card's browser lane, or the headless browser); `web_search` also needs
  Settings, Web search on. Each card says which.
- **Everyday helpers:** `calculator`, `memory_search`, `file_read`,
  `web_search`, `my_files`, `propose_plan`, `change_setting`, `feature_guide` -
  the tools the earlier slice left out.
- **Jarvis's own tools (35):** `goals_list`, `goal_add`, `goal_progress`,
  `goal_done`, `conversation_find`, `conversation_open`, `phone_apps`,
  `plugin_list`, `plugin_switch`, `pack_list`, `pack_inspect`, `pack_install`,
  `pack_remove`, `send_text_message`, `refresh_abilities`,
  `self_portrait`, `setup_quiz`, `approval_policy` - the switch that offers
  the approval-policy TOOL at all (it never changes a policy by itself;
  §193 is the changing, and every loosening still needs its own card) - and,
  since 2026-11-05, the seventeen on-demand GitHub tools `github_list`,
  `github_read_file`, `github_ci_status`, `github_pr_scan`, `github_pr_detail`,
  `github_comment`, `github_open_issue`, `github_rerun_workflow`,
  `github_create_repo`, `github_merge_pr`, `github_fix_and_push`,
  `github_open_pr`, `github_workflow`, `github_issue_labels`, `github_edit_pr`,
  `github_pr_review` and `github_issue_state` (the five reads share the
  `github_inspect` action, the twelve writes their own; every use still raises
  its own card). The non-GitHub names above shipped ON and had no
  switch row at all before 2026-11-04; `send_text_message` came with
  hands-free the same day as the GitHub six.
**Four known tools are NOT switches of their own**, because the turn ignores
their line in `[tools].enabled` - a switch whose state the turn ignored would
be a lie (the rule that removed the web-search grant's two switches on
2026-11-02). They are named in `tools.not_switchable`, with the PC's own
sentence, and the route refuses ON for them with that sentence rather than
"does not know that name":

- `run_data_script` - the data and maths sandbox has its OWN switch (Settings,
  Data sandbox; `POST /api/sandbox/enabled`). With it on the model is offered
  the tool whether or not the file names it; with it off the file cannot offer
  it.
- `product_check` - the product check has its OWN switch too (`[product_check]
  enabled` in the settings file, off by default; §192). With it on the model is
  offered the tool whether or not `[tools].enabled` names it; with it off a
  `[tools].enabled` line alone offers nothing.
- `approve_web_search_for_conversation` and `stop_web_search_approval` - they
  ride with `web_search` (`jarvis_agent.GRANT_ASK_TOOLS`).

Every switch keeps the shape: ONE card plus Windows Hello, PC only, one tool at
a time; OFF is instant from either app; the phone is read-only. Per-use action
cards are unchanged - the card says each use still asks, the send-file card says
it stays off by default because the deterministic chat request is the normal
door, and the card names any other switch that must also be on.

Built into `backend/jarvis_asks_first.py` (shipped whole, no new module), the
RISKY shape (the owner's ruling of 2026-11-10): the PC asks Windows Hello and
the phone asks for its own fingerprint or PIN, so an approval cannot be given
without a person. It is NOT in `jarvis_owner_check.PC_ONLY_ACTIONS`.
**Desktop only for changing** (`CLAUDE.md`: no deep config
editing on the phone): the phone reads the same list but `can_enable` is false.

### 43.1 Route

| Route | Body | Answers | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/asks_first/tools` | `{"tool", "enabled": true}` | **202** `{"ok", "waiting": true, "message", "tools"}` while its card waits; 200 `changed: false` if already offered; **403** `{"error", "pc_only": true}` from any device but this PC; **403** with the PC's own sentence naming the real switch for one of the four `not_switchable` tools, and "does not know that name" for an unknown one; **503** the backend cannot ask Windows Hello itself, or `enable_reading_tool` is not tier `ask` | **ON**: requested from the PC only, held on a stale link. ONE approval card, action **`enable_reading_tool`** (§43.2), and that card may be approved on the PC (Windows Hello) or on the phone (its own fingerprint or PIN); a phone with no approval key is refused with `no_approval_key` so it can offer to turn signing on. Only a person's "approved" adds the tool to `[tools].enabled`. **Since 2026-11-04 this accepts EVERY tool the AI model can be offered** (60), not just Tier A/B. |
| (both) | **A row may name a legacy row id.** The row id and the tool name are the same now except `email_read` -> `email_check`; an old `"email_read"` entry in the file is read as `email_check` and removed when that switch is turned off (`jarvis_asks_first.TOOL_NAME`). | | |
| `POST /api/asks_first/tools` | `{"tool", "enabled": false}` | 200 `{"ok": true, "changed", "message", "tools"}` | **OFF**: at once, from either app, never held: it only narrows what the model may be offered. **Since D4 (the owner, 2026-11-04) this works for EVERY tool that is on**, including one enabled in `[tools].enabled` that has no in-app switch row, or a name this PC does not know at all (a drop-in module's own tool). The settings line is removed. For a name the PC does not know, the answer names `jarvis-framework.toml` so the owner can put it back by hand; for `run_data_script` it says the Data sandbox switch still offers it, and for the two grant tools that they ride with Web search - never "not offered any more", which would be false. An OFF for a name with no switch of its own that is **not** on changes nothing and keeps the old **403**. |

Its state rides on `GET /api/asks_first` (§32.2), which now carries:

```
"tools": {"label": "Let the AI use this",
          "detail": <the sentence above the switches>,
          "can_enable": bool,        true only for a request from this PC
          "items": [{"id", "title", "group", "on", "waiting",
                     "last": {"outcome", "tool", "message", "why", "at"}|null}, ...],
          "groups": [{"title", "ids"}],          # the page's order
          "vault": {"id": "vault_organizer", "kind": "switch", "title",
                    "group", "on", "waiting", "can_enable", "action", "what"},
          "extra": [{"id", "title", "group", "on", "waiting",
                     "switchable": false, "why",
                     "last": {"outcome", "message", "at"}|null}, ...],
          "not_switchable": {"ids": [...], "labels": {...},
                             "why": <the plain note>},
          "new_off": {"label": "New — currently off",
                      "why": <the plain reason>,
                      "items": [{"id", "title"}, ...]}}
```

`items` lists all 60 switches at 2026-11-05 (48 at 2026-11-04, plus the six
GitHub tools, hands-free's `send_text_message`, the approval-policy tool's own
row and the four pack tools - every tool the AI model can be offered except the
four below), grouped; `vault` is the vault organizer's
separate switch; `not_switchable` names the four tools whose own switch decides
them, with the PC's own sentence, so the page points at the real switch instead
of drawing one that would do nothing. `extra` is D4 (the owner, 2026-11-04):
every name in `[tools].enabled` that has no row in `items` - a name this PC does
not know, or one of the four when the file happens to name it - with its state
read from the file (`on`) and the PC's own plain `why`; `switchable: false` says
plainly that the page offers it no ON switch. A tool turned OFF through this
route stays in `extra` with `on: false` and the line the owner just saw (until
Jarvis restarts), so the page can say OFF truthfully instead of the row
vanishing; a tool the settings file lists again is shown as ON from the file.
The phone reads the same `GET /api/asks_first` and simply does not toggle
anything (`can_enable` false); it reads `extra` not at all, so the phone's page
is unchanged.

**`new_off`** (the owner's ruling of 2026-11-06, Q7). The tools the SHIPPED
template offers (`[tools].enabled` in `backend/rebuilt/jarvis-framework.toml`,
19 names) or this build added (the five: `approval_policy`, `pack_list`,
`pack_inspect`, `pack_install`, `pack_remove`), minus whatever the owner's own
`[tools].enabled` already names. Both apps draw `label` as one subtle pill at
the top of the tools card - "New — currently off" - with the titles beside it.
It is a signpost ONLY: nothing pops up, no chat card is raised, nothing starts
a notification, and turning one on is still `POST /api/asks_first/tools`
(§43.1), which is one Windows Hello card on the PC. The payload writes nothing:
`backend/test_asks_first_new_off.py` proves two reads leave the settings file
byte for byte as it was, and that the 19-name constant is the template's own
list, parsed from the template.

### 43.2 The card

One example, the raw one the owner named - `shell_exec`:

```
Offer this ability to the AI model: "Running commands on this PC"?

From now on the AI model may use this ability when it decides to. In plain
words: Running commands on this PC. This changes one line in your settings file
on this PC; nothing else changes.

This is separate from whether it asks you first: that is set above, in "Ask me
first", and is unchanged by this card.

It does not approve any use of the ability: each time the AI uses it, "Ask me
first" still decides whether you are asked.

Approving it needs Windows Hello on this PC. You can turn it off again at any
time from either app, and that is instant.

If you did not just do this, say no.

If you say no: nothing changes - the AI model is still not offered this
ability.
```

The first line and "in plain words" are the tool's own one-line description
(`jarvis_reach.TOOL_NAMES`), so the person is told what they are switching on,
never just a name. Where that description is a NAME rather than an action -
`control_computer`, `control_phone`, `browser_control` - the card adds one line
saying what using it means ("it can tap and type on your phone over the cable,
one approved plan at a time"), so nobody is asked to switch on a phrase they
cannot picture (`jarvis_asks_first.CARD_USES`). Where another switch must also
be on, the card adds a paragraph naming it - `rea_investigate` its
`[rea] enabled = true`, `web_search` its Settings, Web search switch,
`browser_control` its second-card browser lane or the headless browser - because
otherwise "offered" would be a promise the card cannot keep.
`send_file_to_phone` keeps its own paragraph: off by default on purpose, asking
in chat is the normal door.

Its title: "Jarvis wants to offer \"<the tool's own label>\" to the AI model"
(`jarvis_gate.notice_for` names the tool from the card's own `detail.setting`,
validated as a plain tool id and mapped through `jarvis_reach.TOOL_NAMES`; the
generic `jarvis_card_words.TITLES["enable_reading_tool"]` phrase is the fallback
for a malformed row). Tier `ask` in the shipped
`jarvis-framework.toml`, in `jarvis_asks_first.HARD_LIMITS` and `MUST_ASK`: it
always asks, and it is never itself on the switchable list.

### 43.3 Writing `[tools].enabled`

`jarvis_asks_first.rewrite_tools()`/`set_tools_enabled()`: only the single
`enabled = [...]` line under `[tools]` changes - one tool added or removed
from the array, every other entry and every other byte of the file kept
(comments, spacing, CRLF, a byte-order mark). The new text is parsed and
must match the old settings with only that one entry changed, or nothing is
written; an unusual file (no `[tools]` header, or two of them, or the array
split across several lines) is refused with a sentence saying to edit it by
hand - the same discipline as `set_tier` (§32.4).

### 43.4 What every other tool's row says

`backend/jarvis_reach.py`'s "What Jarvis can reach" (§24) already told the
owner when a tool was off because it was not in `[tools].enabled`. Since
2026-11-04 its wording (`_enable_line`, `_off_line`) names Settings, "What asks
first" for every tool that has a switch there - which is every tool the model
can be offered except the three: `run_data_script`'s row says the Data sandbox
switch decides it, the two grant tools' rows say they ride with Web search, and
a name this PC does not know says adding it to the file would offer nothing.

### 43.5 Known gaps, said plainly

- **Not run on Windows.** The Windows Hello prompt for this card is the
  same approval-gap machinery §32.5 already says is untested on Windows.
- **A program already on the PC** that holds the token can turn a tool OFF
  (harmless) and can raise the ON card; approving it still needs Windows
  Hello at the backend. Step 1's known limits (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`
  section 3) apply.
- **`run_data_script`'s file line is inert.** `[tools].enabled` naming it
  changes nothing either way - the data sandbox's switch decides it. That is
  why it has no switch here; the page says so rather than drawing one that
  would do nothing.

## 44. Accounts: email, calendar and Home Assistant secrets into Credential Manager (added 2026-09-27)

The ease-of-use audit's "Then" table, row 15 ("Security G3"): "Email,
calendar and Home Assistant secrets into Credential Manager, entered in a
PC-only box like the web search keys. Today they are Windows user
environment variables, which Windows stores as plain text." Four secrets
moved: the IMAP username and password (`backend/jarvis_email.py`, read by
both `jarvis_email_send.py` and `jarvis_email_draft.py`), the private
calendar link (`backend/jarvis_calendar.py`), and the Home Assistant
long-lived access token (`backend/jarvis_home.py`). **Desktop only**
(`CLAUDE.md`: no deep config editing on the phone) - see
`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8.

**The ADDRESSES those secrets authenticate against are a different shape and
a different section.** A secret goes into Credential Manager and never over
HTTP; an address is not a secret, so it takes §23's SearXNG-address shape - a
backend route over a plain JSON file - and it is in section 116.

**The mechanism** is `backend/jarvis_token_store.resolve_secret(env_name,
target)` - the general form of §23.4's Exa/Tavily/Brave/DeepSeek key pattern, added
to the same module that already keeps the pairing token in Credential
Manager (`jarvis_token_store.WindowsStore`, parametrized by `target` rather
than hard-coded to the pairing token's own name). For each of the four:

1. The environment variable, if the owner already set one - unchanged, and
   still wins: `resolve_secret`'s rule 2, "someone who set it meant it".
   **Backward compatibility**: an installation that already relies on the
   variable keeps working exactly as before, and Credential Manager is
   never even asked.
2. Otherwise Windows Credential Manager, under the secret's own named
   target (below).
3. Otherwise `""` - simply not configured. Unlike the pairing token, none
   of these four is required for the backend to run at all, so nothing is
   ever made up and there is no "this run only" state.

A store that cannot be reached, refuses, or is not there at all (any
platform but Windows) is treated as empty, never raises. A value read from
Credential Manager is registered with `jarvis_scrub` (there is no
environment-variable NAME there for its usual name-based scan to catch); a
value read from the environment is left to that existing scan, unchanged.

| Secret | Module | Environment variable | Credential Manager target |
|---|---|---|---|
| IMAP username | `jarvis_email.imap_user()` | `JARVIS_IMAP_USER` | `Jarvis Backend/IMAP username` |
| IMAP password | `jarvis_email.imap_password()` | `JARVIS_IMAP_PASSWORD` | `Jarvis Backend/IMAP password` |
| Private calendar link | `jarvis_calendar._feed_url()` | `JARVIS_CALENDAR_ICS_SECRET_URL` | `Jarvis Backend/Calendar iCal link` |
| Home Assistant token | `jarvis_home._token()` | `JARVIS_HOME_TOKEN` | `Jarvis Backend/Home Assistant token` |

`jarvis_email_send.py` and `jarvis_email_draft.py` call
`jarvis_email.imap_user()` / `imap_password()` rather than reading
`JARVIS_IMAP_USER` / `JARVIS_IMAP_PASSWORD` themselves, so all three modules
agree on where the account's credentials come from.

### 44.1 Entering a secret: the desktop, PC only

Settings, "Accounts" (`account-secrets-settings.js`;
`src-tauri/src/account_secrets.rs`, `token_store.rs`
`ACCOUNT_SECRET_TARGETS`) - one box per secret, the same shape as the web
search keys' own boxes (§23.4): typed once, saved straight into Windows
Credential Manager on this PC, and never shown again - only whether one is
saved. **No backend route is involved**: both the write and the "is one
already set" check happen entirely on this PC, exactly as the Exa/Tavily/
Brave keys never touch the backend's HTTP API either.

Three Tauri commands, Settings window only:

| Command | Args | Answers | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `get_account_secrets` | - | `{"secrets": [{"name", "env_set": bool, "saved": bool\|null}, ...]}`, all four, in the table's order | A read. `env_set` is checked fresh on this PC (`std::env::var`) - never the value. `saved` is Credential Manager's own answer, asked only when `env_set` is false (matching what the backend actually does - the variable, if set, is never overridden by anything saved here). |
| `save_account_secret` | `{"name", "value"}` | `{"ok": true, "said"}`; refused (a plain sentence) for an unknown `name`, an empty value, one with a control character, or (the calendar link only) anything not starting with `https://` | Written straight into Credential Manager (`token_store::write_account_secret`, read back to confirm it landed - the same check `write_search_key` makes). Never returns the value. |
| `forget_account_secret` | `{"name"}` | `{"ok": true, "said"}` | Removes it from Credential Manager. Never touches an environment variable of the same name - there is no way to unset another program's environment variable from here, and the page says so plainly (a box stays disabled while the variable is set). |

The page disables a secret's box while `env_set` is true (saving there would
do nothing until the variable is removed, so the page does not pretend
otherwise) and shows Remove only once `saved` is true. `save_account_secret`
and `forget_account_secret` are **not** held on a stale link - a value goes
into this PC's Credential Manager, not over the connection to the backend,
exactly like the web search keys.

### 44.2 What every secret's box says, and never says

Never shown again once saved: the box empties itself the instant it is
sent, whatever the answer. No card - unlike a setting that changes what
Jarvis does or asks, saving an account's own credentials is the owner
configuring their own accounts, the same judgement call §23.4 already makes
for the web search keys. Every existing "not set" refusal in
`jarvis_email.py`, `jarvis_email_send.py`, `jarvis_email_draft.py` and
`jarvis_calendar.py` now says plainly when NEITHER the environment variable
NOR Credential Manager holds a value, rather than naming only the
environment variable as before.

**Every other place that already asked "is this account set up?" was found
and fixed to match**, so a secret saved only in Credential Manager is never
wrongly reported as "not set up": `jarvis_reach.py`'s "What Jarvis can
reach" (§24, `_env`) now asks the owning module
(`jarvis_email.imap_user()`/`imap_password()`, `jarvis_calendar._feed_url()`,
`jarvis_home._token()`) for these four names instead of reading the
environment variable directly; the morning briefing's "what it includes"
(`jarvis_briefing.sources()`) now checks `jarvis_calendar.source()` for the
calendar row instead of the two environment-variable names; and
`jarvis_tellme.py`'s "tell me when" IMAP connections (§30) now call
`jarvis_email.imap_user()`/`imap_password()` instead of reading
`JARVIS_IMAP_USER`/`JARVIS_IMAP_PASSWORD` themselves.

### 44.3 Known gaps, said plainly

- **Not run on Windows.** Every Credential Manager write, read-back and
  delete for these four secrets is proven against a stand-in store
  (`backend/test_account_secrets.py`, `token_store.rs`'s own unit tests);
  the real ctypes/Win32 calls run live only in CI's `credential-manager`
  job, on a throwaway target name, same as the pairing token.
  `resolve_secret`'s env-wins / store-fallback / unconfigured branches are
  all exercised against that stand-in too.
- **A CalDAV username and password** (`JARVIS_CALDAV_USER`,
  `JARVIS_CALDAV_PASSWORD`) are a fifth and sixth calendar secret this row
  does not cover: the audit and `CLAUDE.md` rule 3 both call out the private
  iCal link by name, so only that one moved for calendar. CalDAV's own
  username and password stay environment-variable-only for now - a
  follow-up, not a silent gap, since `backend/README.md`'s own table still
  lists them as plain environment variables.
- **A backup taken before this feature ran** still has these four (if set)
  as plain environment variables in the owner's own Windows profile, which
  this feature does not touch or clean up - only new reads move to
  Credential Manager first.
## 45. Backups (added 2026-09-27)

The owner's decision (`CLAUDE.md`, 2026-09-27, the answers to
`docs/OWNER-QUESTIONS-2026-09-27.md`): "one locked backup file into a
folder the owner picks, a NordLocker (or other cloud-synced) folder
included. Locked with a recovery code only the owner has (shown once);
Jarvis keeps only the last few. This bends rule 1 for that one locked file
only, and the app must say plainly that a lost code means a useless
backup and that erased facts stay in older backups until they age out."
The design is `docs/CUTTING-EDGE-2026-09-26-round2-trust.md`, "2. Encrypted
backup and plain restore".

Built as a new module, `backend/jarvis_backup.py` (shipped whole,
`backup.patch`). **Desktop only**, apart from one read-only status line on
the phone - see `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8.

### 45.1 What is backed up, and what is not

One `.jbak` file: a zip archive, encrypted, holding -

- The real SQLite databases this backend has, snapshotted with
  SQLite's own online backup API (safe while Jarvis keeps them open):
  `memory.db`, `chat-history.db`, `schedule.db`, `feedback.db`,
  `projects.db` (projects and every number logged; added 2026-09-28 by
  the Projects feature audit), `goals.db`, and `study.db` (the review
  decks, section 102; added 2026-09-30, the owner's decision).
- Every `*.json` file directly in the Jarvis settings folder (never a
  subfolder), `jarvis-framework.toml`, and the `notes/` and `voice/`
  folders (the owner's own voice-print - not `voice-models/`, downloaded
  engine files, or `voices/`, the custom-voice bank).
- The chat-history encryption key, read from Windows Credential Manager
  and kept, base64, inside the archive - which is encrypted before it ever
  touches a disk.
- The review decks' own encryption key (`Jarvis Backend/study decks key`),
  the same way (`secrets/study-decks-key.b64`), **only when `study.db`
  exists and the key can be read**: sealed deck words are useless without
  their key, so a `study.db` is never carried without it (and a backup
  never makes a key for decks nobody has). A restore writes the file and
  the key back together and the running store reopens with them.
- **The backend's own program files** (added 2026-10-05): every `*.py` file
  directly in the folder `jarvis_backup.py` is running from - the live
  backend folder, the one holding `jarvis_hud.py` - kept as
  `source/<name>.py`. Five of them (`jarvis_hud.py`, the whole control
  plane; `jarvis_gate.py`, the approval gate; `jarvis_extract.py`,
  `jarvis_models.py`, `jarvis_skills.py`) were found to exist in exactly
  ONE place on Earth, with nothing reading a `.py` file: not this module,
  not `apply-patches.ps1`, not git (`backend/.gitignore` keeps the live
  sources out on purpose, with a written exception only for the ten under
  `backend/rebuilt/`). **Top level only, never the tree:** `__pycache__/`
  is bytecode that rebuilds itself, and the patcher's own
  `_jarvis-backup-*` folders already hold older copies of the same
  sources, so recursing would nest the whole source inside every new
  backup. Top level is 188 files, 10.1 MB, about 3.6 MB once deflated,
  inside the same encrypted archive - so the code is never in the clear
  either. A restore writes them back into the folder the module runs from
  (`flat=True`, one name per file, the same second lock `db/` and
  `settings/` have), which means **restoring an older backup also puts
  back the older program**; the restore card says so in plain words and
  points at `apply-patches.ps1` for getting later updates back.

**Never backed up**, on purpose (rule 3): the pairing token and every API
key (Exa, Tavily, Brave, DeepSeek, GitHub, ...) - all of them live in Windows
Credential Manager under their own target names, never in a settings
file, and this module reads exactly two Credential Manager entries, the
chat-history key and the review decks' key. Also never: model files (large; Ollama keeps its own
copy) and logs. Also never: any backend file that is not a top-level
`*.py` - the subfolders (`__pycache__/`, `_jarvis-logs/`, the patcher's
`_jarvis-backup-*` folders), other file types beside the sources, and
`*.py` nested deeper than one level. Also never: `approvals.db`/`holds.db` (pending-approval
state, not memory - restoring a stale row would be misleading, not a
security hole, since the in-memory approval stamp is gone the moment the
backend restarts). Also never: **`documents-index.db`** (a derived ranking
rebuilt from the folders) and **`media-index.db`** (the readable words kept
from recordings and videos - F5 S2, §149). The second one is the newer and
more important exclusion: a backup made before a Delete would still hold the
words afterwards, so deleting the index would not really delete them. Both
names are in `jarvis_backup.py`'s own `NOT_BACKED_UP` table with their
reasons, and `backend/test_media_index.py` drives that table's own decision
function.

### 45.2 The lock

AES-256-GCM with a key stretched from a recovery code by Argon2id
(`cryptography`, already a dependency here for chat history). The
recovery code is 20 characters from a 32-symbol alphabet with no
0/O/1/I/L (about 100 bits), shown four groups of five, ONCE - never
written to a file, a log, or the audit trail. **A lost recovery code
means a useless backup: there is no way in without it**, said in those
words wherever the code is shown and on the restore card. Restoring can
bring back an erased fact's original words if an older backup still has
them, until that backup ages out of the newest 5 kept - said in those
words too (`"Erase the words" cannot reach into an older backup ...`).

### 45.3 Routes

| Route | Notes |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/backup` | From this PC: the folder, whether a card is waiting, the last backup and the last restore's outcome (a one-time recovery code included exactly once, then gone on the next read). **Since 2026-10-20 (Gemini ruling 8.1, §45.4b) the last restore's outcome is PERSISTED** in `last-restore.json` in the settings folder: it stays readable until `POST /api/backup/restore/dismiss`, so a poll can no longer swallow it, and it survives a backend restart. The one-time recovery code keeps its old rule - shown exactly once, never stored on disk (the persisted record carries `recovery_code_hint` instead). From anywhere else: `{"available", "last_backup_at", "last_restore"}` - the phone's "Last backup: ...", plus the last restore's outcome WITHOUT the recovery code and without the technical `why`; reading it consumes nothing. Never held. The answer also carries `recovery_code_pending` (both depths): true while this PC still holds the safety backup's one-time code, which nobody has read out yet - a paired device's dismiss is refused while it is true (§45.4b point 4). If the full record could not be written to disk (a full disk), a short fallback marker is persisted instead and `last_restore.persist_failed: true` is set, so a restart never reports an older restore as the current one. **From this PC the answer also carries `prepared`** (2026-10-24, the owner's decision): `null`, or `{"at", "expires_at"}` for a phone-started run that is still waiting - the two times and NOTHING else, so Settings, Backups can offer to finish it ("A backup was started from your phone") while no read ever carries the recovery code or the run's `id`. Both reads build it through one `_pending_for_reader()` helper, so an EXPIRED run reads as `null` on the PC's `GET /api/backup` and on the phone's `GET /api/backup/status` alike, and a caller that is not this PC is not sent the key at all. |
| `GET /api/backup/list` | The kept backup files in the folder, newest first. This PC only (**403** otherwise). |
| `POST /api/backup/folder` `{"path"}` | Sets where backups are written. This PC only. **202** while ONE approval card waits (action `change_own_config`, the same action "Folders Jarvis may look in" uses to add a folder, and refused the same places - `jarvis_documents.check_folder`, imported not copied). |
| `POST /api/backup/now` `{}` | Makes one backup into the folder already set. This PC only, **no card** - the folder was already approved. **409** with no folder set. 200 `{"ok", "name", "at", "counts", "recovery_code", "message"}` - the code shown once. **`message` is built from the manifest and never a bare "Backed up." over an archive something is missing from** (data-integrity audit F1/F4, 2026-10-28): a database this PC has and the archive does not is named, with its reason, in `counts.excluded_dbs` (e.g. `"chat-history.db (encryption key missing or mismatched in Windows Credential Manager)"`, `"study.db (encryption key missing or unreadable in Windows Credential Manager)"`, `"health.db (encryption key missing or unreadable in Windows Credential Manager)"`, `"memory.db (could not be read)"`), and the sentence reads **"Backed up N databases, except &lt;names&gt;, left out to prevent an unreadable backup."** `counts.chat_history_key` is true only when a key that was PROVED against the archived history is inside the archive; a chat history whose key cannot be proved is **left out**, never carried unreadable, and a backup never mints a key. `POST /api/backup/commit` answers with the same message. |
| `GET /api/backup/status` | **What the FOLDER holds** (2026-10-14), for the phone. Read-only, **any paired device** - not PC-only. Returns `{"available", "folder", "keep", "kept", "last_backup_at", "last_backup_name", "verify", "last_attempt", "prepared"}`. `folder` is the folder's **LAST segment only** ("Jarvis Backups"), never the whole path: a full path names the owner's Windows account, which is what §8 already keeps off a phone for the memory store's own path. `keep` is `KEEP` (5); `kept` counts the files that are COMPLETE (the same rule retention uses). `last_backup_at` is read from the newest kept file's own name, so it is TRUE after the backend restarts - the older `last_backup_at` on `GET /api/backup` is the PC's memory only and answered null with four backups sitting in the folder. `verify` is `{"ok", "why", "words", "proves_open", "limit"}` for that newest file: `why` is `complete`/`missing`/`too_small`/`not_a_backup`/`unreadable`/`no_folder`/`empty`, checked against the file's own bytes (magic, header shape, minimum length). **`proves_open` is always false and is sent so a client never has to assume it**: only the recovery code opens a backup and codes are only typed on the PC. `last_attempt` is the last run THIS backend made, in memory - `{"ok", "at", "error"}` - and is where a **failure** is visible, so a failed backup is never read as a success. Carries no recovery code and never can. |
| `POST /api/backup/prepare` `{}` | **The phone asks for a backup** (2026-10-14). **Any paired device.** Mints this run's one-time recovery code and **WRITES NOTHING AT ALL** - the folder is byte-for-byte unchanged. 200 `{"ok", "pending", "id", "recovery_code", "at", "expires_at", "folder", "keep", "message"}`. **409** with no folder set (`NO_FOLDER`), because a code minted with nowhere to write is a code the owner would be told to keep for nothing. The code is held in the PC's memory only, for `PENDING_TTL_S` (15 minutes), and is never written to a file, a log or the audit trail. A second ask replaces the first. |
| `POST /api/backup/commit` `{"id", "code"}` | **The owner says he has kept the code, and the PC writes the file** (2026-10-14; **rule changed 2026-10-24**). **TWO callers may finish a run** (2026-10-24): (a) **the device that MINTED it** - `prepare` records the caller's `handler._jarvis_device` identity in the live run ("pc", "shared", or a paired device's id: the same identity `jarvis_devices` stamps on every request and `jarvis_chatbot_limits` reads, never a new header), and a `commit` whose identity matches is the phone's own finish press (ONE TAP after the tick, with no step on the PC); or (b) **this PC** typing the same code (`finish_phone_backup`, the fallback for a run left waiting). **Any OTHER paired device that holds or has learned the code is refused 403** `{"ok": false, "other_device": true, "error": "That backup was started on another device, so nothing was written and your folder is unchanged. Finish it on the phone that started it, or on your PC (Settings, Backups)."}` - it writes **NOTHING**, leaves the folder byte-for-byte unchanged, and does **NOT spend the run**, so its real finisher can still use it. The device is checked BEFORE the code, so a device that may not finish a run cannot use 400-vs-403 as a code oracle. **The fallback that must stay, said plainly:** a run whose asker identity was never recorded - a direct in-process call (the tests), or a backend with no `jarvis_devices`, where the token wrapper that stamps `_jarvis_device` never ran - cannot be bound, so possession of the live code still decides for it (`jarvis_backup.request_commit`'s own docstring). The old **403** `{"ok": false, "pc_only": true, "error": "The backup is written on your PC, ..."}` stays GONE: the phone that minted the run is not refused. What does not change is where the write happens - on the PC's disk, by the PC's backend, into the folder the owner chose on the PC. The code must be the one `prepare` minted and must still be inside `PENDING_TTL_S`; the comparison is cleaned the way the owner would type it (uppercase, hyphens and spaces dropped), so the four-groups-of-five form and the bare 20 characters are the same code. A **wrong or missing** code: **400**, the run stays open so a typo can be corrected, **nothing written**. An **expired or never-started** run: **409**, the run is dropped, **nothing written**. On success: 200 `{"ok", "name", "at", "counts", "size", "folder", "keep", "recovery_code", "message"}`, the file being made with **that same code** (`backup_now(code=...)`) - so the code the owner kept is the code that opens what landed. Any failure (a full disk, a refusal by the module, or no folder at commit - **409** `NO_FOLDER`) records `last_attempt.ok: false` and writes nothing. The run is **CLAIMED under the module's lock BEFORE the file is written**: two presses - from one app or from both, or the phone and the PC's fallback at once - write ONE file (the second is the 409 above), where before both could pass the check and write two files with the same code, the second one's retention pass pushing an older, still-openable backup out of the five kept. The `id` is sent but **never compared**, so the PC's fallback needs nothing from the phone but the code the owner wrote down. **The phone's half** (§45.5): after `prepare` showed the code and the owner ticked "I have written this code down somewhere safe", its finish button is this call; the screen says "Nothing has been written yet" until the answer says a file landed, and only then "Your PC wrote the backup". **What the guard does NOT close:** a caller holding a paired token can `prepare` (as itself) and then `commit` as the device that minted that same run, so it can still churn the kept backups (§45.6) - the guard stops a DIFFERENT device finishing a run it did not mint, not a token holder making its own. **Residual risk, accepted by the owner on 2026-10-24:** the tick is a client-side promise inside the phone app, not a check by the PC, so a modified or misused paired phone could commit without the code ever being kept - which writes a backup nobody can open and pushes the oldest of the five kept out. **What stays PC-only:** choosing the folder, restoring, listing files and deleting older copies (§45.5; `tools/check_parity.py` has this route as `ported`). |
| `POST /api/backup/restore/preview` `{"name", "code"}` | Decrypts to read the backup's own `manifest.json` - counts and its date, never any other content. Changes nothing. **400** `{"wrong_code": true}` for a code that does not open it. This PC only. |
| `POST /api/backup/delete-older` `{}` | **"Delete older backups now"**, offered by both apps after an "Erase the words" (2026-09-30): erased words can still be readable in a backup made before the erase. This PC only (**403** otherwise). **202** while ONE approval card waits (action `change_own_config`, the folder card's own; the card says how many files go and that it cannot be undone). Approved: one FRESH backup is made first (a new recovery code, returned once in `last_delete_older.fresh_backup`), then every other backup file in the folder is deleted; if the fresh one cannot be made, nothing is deleted. **409** with no folder or no backups. The outcome is in `GET /api/backup` as `last_delete_older` (`outcome` `deleted`\|`denied`\|`timed_out`\|`withdrawn`\|`refused`\|`failed`, `deleted`, `message`, `fresh_backup`) and `pending_delete_older_card`. |
| `POST /api/backup/restore` `{"name", "code"}` | **202** while ONE approval card waits, action **`restore_backup`** - in `jarvis_owner_check.PC_ONLY_ACTIONS`, so it ALWAYS needs Windows Hello and is ALWAYS refused from any device but this PC, whatever the gate's own risk table says (the same mechanism `loosen_what_asks_first` uses;
`enable_reading_tool` LEFT that list on 2026-11-10 and is a RISKY card instead). From anything but this PC it is refused **up front, before the body is read** - **403** `{"ok": false, "pc_only": true, "error": "Restoring has to be done in Jarvis on your PC, so nothing was restored. Open Jarvis there, then Settings, Backups."}` - and never with the 202 above, which promises a Windows Hello card that such a caller can never approve (2026-10-10; the same words are on `/api/backup/restore/preview`). **Its card must not NAME a file `jarvis_gate.py` protects** (`jarvis_hud.py` among them): the card is what the gate is handed as its prompt, and a prompt naming one is refused at tier `never` before any card exists, so nobody is ever asked - the card says "the .py files in the folder Jarvis runs from", not the file's name, and `backend/test_backup.py` holds it against the gate's own `_PROTECTED` list. A refusal is recorded in `last_restore` with `outcome: "refused"`, the next step in plain words in `message` (the desktop's Settings, Backups shows that), and the technical reason - which tier, and the gate's own sentence - in `why`, for a bug report. On approval: Jarvis backs up the CURRENT state first, automatically, with a FRESH one-time recovery code (returned in the outcome exactly once), so the restore itself can be undone - then writes the backup's files back. Restore only adds and overwrites; it never deletes a file that is not in the backup. From 2026-10-05 it also writes the archive's `source/*.py` back into the folder the module runs from, so the CODE comes back with the data - and the card says plainly that restoring an OLDER backup therefore puts back the older program and undoes updates applied since, naming `apply-patches.ps1`. **Since 2026-10-20 (ruling 8.1, §45.4b): the safety backup must be VERIFIED ON DISK before one live file is touched** - present, not empty, its own `JBAK1` shape, the size that was written, it opens with its code, and its manifest reads back; anything else refuses the restore with nothing changed, `reason: "safety_unverified"` in `last_restore` and in the audit's `backup.restore.card`, and the plain sentence "the safety backup could not be made first, so nothing was restored". The outcome's `restored` block names the EXACT files put back (`databases`, `settings_files`, `notes_files`, `voice_files`, `source_files`, `framework_toml`, `keys`), not just counts. |

| `POST /api/backup/restore/dismiss` `{}` | **Clears the last restore's outcome** (2026-10-20, Gemini ruling 8.1, §45.4b) - the ONLY thing that clears it, because reading `last_restore` now never consumes it. **Any paired device** may ask, EXCEPT while this PC has not yet shown the restore's one-time recovery code: the code exists only in the PC's memory, so a device clearing the notice first would destroy the only way to open the safety backup (audit 2026-10-21, M2). That request is **409** `{"ok": false, "code_pending": true, "error": "<plain words: read it on the PC first; the code is shown once>"}`, and **nothing is cleared**; the PC itself may always clear it (the owner can read the code in the same panel first), and once the PC has read it any paired device can. 200 `{"ok": true, "dismissed": <true when there was something to clear>}`; **idempotent** - dismissing an empty record is a 200 with `"dismissed": false`, not an error. Removes `last-restore.json` from the settings folder and clears the in-memory copy; the disk write of a finishing restore and a dismiss cannot interleave to resurrect a cleared record (audit 2026-10-21, LOW-1). Audited as `backup.restore.dismissed {had, from}`, and a refusal as `backup.restore.dismiss_refused`. **No app draws the button yet** (named follow-up in §45.5): the route is the explicit action the persistent record requires. |

`[autonomy.tiers]` carries `restore_backup = "ask"` (must stay `ask`, like
every other PC-only-with-Windows-Hello action); `jarvis_card_words.TITLES`
has its plain-words title; "What asks first" (§32) lists it under
"Jarvis's own settings, memory and voice".

### 45.4 Retention

The newest 5 backup files in the folder are kept; making a new one
deletes the rest - **never the one just written**, whatever its name says. A
name is trusted for its date, except one dated more than 5 minutes in the
future (the PC's clock was wrong): that file is dated by its real modified time
instead. A same-second `-2` file counts as newer than the first. A file too
small to be a backup (a copy or sync that was cut short) is listed with
`"complete": false`, is not counted among the kept, and is not deleted. Chosen, not measured: a card is shown for each restore
either way, so keeping more costs disk, not safety, and a synced folder
should not grow without bound. Two backups made in the same second get
distinct names (`-2`, `-3`, ...) rather than overwrite each other.

### 45.4a Restore is all-or-nothing, as far as files allow (2026-09-30)

Every file is first written beside its place as a hidden temp file (a full disk
fails here, before anything real is touched); then each real file is copied
aside and replaced in one step, and a restored database's old `-wal` and `-shm`
files are moved aside too (they belong to the OLD database); on any failure
everything already replaced is put back and every temp file removed. The
outcome words are true: "failed" says everything was put back;
"failed_partial" says putting back failed too and points to the safety backup;
a safety backup that could not be made says nothing was restored. A chat-history
key that cannot be put back in Credential Manager is a plain `warning` on the
restored outcome, not silence. The restore card says it "REPLACES your memory
and chat files, settings and notes with that day's copies" - what was added
or changed since is lost unless it is in the safety backup. Nothing can pause
the programs that hold these files open (there is no such hook), so restart
Jarvis afterwards, as the outcome says.

### 45.4b Restore fails closed without a verifiable safety backup; the outcome is PERSISTED; every restored file is named (2026-10-20; audit fixes 2026-10-21)

From the owner's accepted ruling on Gemini's late review, Part I §2 ruling
8.1, plus the independent 2026-10-21 audit's findings on that slice. All in
`jarvis_backup.py` (shipped whole; no patch):

1. **Fail closed before ANY overwrite.** The safety backup made at the start
   of an approved restore is now VERIFIED ON DISK before one live database,
   key or `jarvis-framework.toml`/settings/notes file is touched:
   the file exists; it is bigger than nothing; it has the `JBAK1` magic and
   the header shape (`check_file`); its size is the size that was just
   written; it OPENS with the recovery code it was written with; and its
   `manifest.json` reads back whole. `backup_now` also tries to flush and
   `os.fsync` the file before the rename - **best effort**: a file system that
   refuses fsync (some network shares) is tolerated, and the read-back check
   above is what decides (audit 2026-10-21, LOW-6). Anything but all-clear
   **refuses the restore with nothing changed**, records
   `reason: "safety_unverified"` in the audit event `backup.restore.card` and
   in `last_restore.reason`, and tells the owner in the plain `failed_before`
   words ("the safety backup could not be made or verified first, so nothing
   was restored and your data was not changed"). A safety backup that cannot
   even be made is refused the same way, as before. An unexpected exception
   from the check itself is refused in those same words instead of killing the
   card's thread (audit 2026-10-21, LOW-3). A safety backup that FAILED
   verification is removed from the folder - its one-time code was never
   shown, so it can never be opened, and left there it would eat one of the
   five kept slots; if it cannot be removed the refusal says which file it is
   (LOW-4).
2. **The last restore's outcome is PERSISTED** in `last-restore.json` in the
   settings folder (`_config_dir()`), written atomically and fsynced: outcome,
   when, the plain `message`, `warning`, the safety backup's NAME, time and size,
   the exact restored files (below), and - when it was a refusal -
   `reason`. `GET /api/backup` reads it on every poll and a restart keeps it;
   reading it consumes nothing (before this, the outcome lived in memory only
   and the first read took the one-time code with it, so a poll could swallow
   the recovery information). Both apps can read it: the phone's answer now
   carries `last_restore` without the recovery code and without `why`.
   **The one-time recovery-code rule is unchanged and deliberate**: the code
   is still shown exactly once, read out of memory once, and NEVER written to
   disk - a stored code would open the safety backup for anyone who read the
   file, which is the opposite of the design. The persisted record says so in
   `recovery_code_hint` rather than looking silently incomplete. The ONLY way
   the record is cleared is `POST /api/backup/restore/dismiss` (idempotent,
   audited `backup.restore.dismissed`); a read never clears it. **A failed
   write cannot leave an older restore looking current** (audit 2026-10-21,
   M3): a full disk writes a short fallback marker (`persist_failed: true`,
   the outcome this run knew, no file names), and if even that cannot be
   written the stale older record is removed - a restart then says "no
   record", never an older restore as the latest. **The one residual case**
   (verification addendum 2026-10-21, V2): if BOTH writes fail AND the stale
   file cannot even be removed (a folder that refuses every write and every
   delete), then nothing can correct the file and the next start MAY still
   show an older restore as the latest - the audit event
   `backup.restore.persist_fallback {"how": "failed"}` records that this
   happened, and the in-memory record still says the truth for this run.
3. **Exact restored names in the audit and the receipt.** `_apply_restore`
   now returns, beside the counts, the exact filenames it put back, grouped
   as the archive is: `{"databases": ["memory.db", ...], "settings_files":
   ["a.json", ...], "notes_files": [...], "voice_files": [...],
   "source_files": [...], "framework_toml": ["jarvis-framework.toml"],
   "keys": ["chat-history-key", ...]}`. It rides in `last_restore.restored`
   and in the audit event `backup.restored`'s `applied.restored`; the counts
   are still there, so an older reader loses nothing. **A chat-history key is
   listed only when it was PROVED to open the chat history now on this PC**
   (data-integrity audit F1, 2026-10-28): an archive whose key opens nothing
   leaves the live Credential Manager entry exactly as it was, sets
   `applied.chat_history_key_refused`, and the receipt says so in
   `last_restore.warning`/`message`. A chat history in the archive that
   **neither** its own key **nor** this PC's current key opens is **not applied
   at all**: the live `chat-history.db` and the live key stay exactly as they
   were, `applied.chat_history_refused` is set, and `message`/`warning` NAME
   `chat-history.db` and say it was NOT restored. A **partial** failure
   (the restore failed AND putting things back failed too) names what it had
   replaced before it stopped and sets `"partial": true` on the record - the
   list then means "this may now be the backup's", never "everything went in"
   (audit 2026-10-21, LOW-2). `last-restore.json` itself is Jarvis's own
   bookkeeping, never a settings file: it is excluded from every archive and
   refused as a restored entry, so a backup cannot report an old restore as
   the current one (audit 2026-10-21, M1). `backend/test_backup.py` holds
   each part, and the suite fails if any guard is removed (the fail-closed
   check, the persistence, or the names).
4. **The 2026-10-21 audit findings are closed here** (the independent audit
   in `.dsh-scratch/AUDIT-678-BACKUP-FAIL-CLOSED-2026-10-21.md`; each finding
   id is named in the code and tests that fix it):
   - **M1** `last-restore.json` is not swept into later backups, and an
     archive carrying it cannot restore it (point 3).
   - **M2** a paired device cannot dismiss the notice while the PC has not
     shown this restore's one-time recovery code: **409**, plain words, and
     `recovery_code_pending` in `GET /api/backup` says when that is still
     owed. The PC may always clear it, and after the PC's first read any
     device may. This keeps the ONE copy of the code alive until the owner has
     seen it - the alternative (clearing the notice first) would leave the
     safety backup unopenable for ever.
   - **M3** the fallback marker / stale-file removal in point 2, whose one
     residual triple-failure case (writes AND removal all refused) is stated
     there honestly rather than claimed away (V2 of the addendum).
   - **M1 under NTFS's case-insensitivity** (V1 of the verification
     addendum): the bookkeeping comparison is `casefold()`ed on both the
     archive and the restore side, so a crafted `settings/Last-restore.json`
     or `settings/Backup.json` cannot land on the real lower-case files.
   - **LOW-1** the record's disk write happens under the same lock as its
     becoming visible, so a dismiss can never report success and then have the
     record written back.
   - **LOW-2** partial-failure names (point 3).
   - **LOW-3** an exception in the verification is a clean refusal.
   - **LOW-4** a verification-failed safety backup is removed, or named if it
     cannot be.
   - **LOW-5** after a successful apply the safety backup's presence and size
     are checked once more, cheaply; if it has gone, the message and the
     record's `warning` say so plainly instead of promising a step back that
     is not there.
   - **LOW-6** the wording in this section and the desktop panel: the hidden
     Backup page no longer makes the "first read" that consumes the one-time
     code (`backup-settings.js`: the `onQueue` reload is now
     `document.hidden`-guarded, like the visibility handler); "not
     destructive" for dismiss is qualified by M2; the audit's
     "never a file name" rule carries its one exception (`backup.restored`
     names, by the owner's request).
   - **NIT** the record file is size-capped before it is read, and the
     unreachable-only-by-accident `SafetyBackupUnverified` branch is kept
     solely for a caller that supplies its own `safety_fn`, documented as
     such.

### 45.5 Desktop and phone

Desktop: Settings, Backups (`backup.rs`, `backup-settings.js`). Setting the
folder reuses the exact Windows folder picker "Folders Jarvis may look in"
uses (`folders::picker`, made `pub(crate)` for this); "Back up now" and
listing need no card; restoring is held on a stale link, like setting the
folder.

Phone: `net/Backup.kt`, `ui/screens/BackupPlate.kt`, in Settings. It **reads
the folder** (`GET /api/backup/status`): when the last backup was made, the
folder's last segment, how many are kept of how many the PC keeps, and the
PC's own sentence for what its check of the newest file found - plus that
check's limit, said rather than assumed, and the last attempt's failure when
there was one. It **asks for a backup** in two steps: `POST
/api/backup/prepare` puts the run's one-time recovery code on screen, and -
once the owner has ticked "I have written this code down somewhere safe" -
its finish button sends `POST /api/backup/commit`, which **makes the PC write
the file**: one tap, no step on the PC (2026-10-24, the owner's upgraded
decision; the write still happens on the PC's disk, by the PC's backend). The
finish is **bound to that phone**: `prepare` records the asking device's
identity, and only the device that minted the run or this PC may commit it - a
different paired device holding the same code is refused **403** and writes
nothing (§45.3). The screen says "Nothing has
been written yet" while the run is open, and "Your PC wrote the backup" ONLY
after the answer reports a file - a code shown but never committed writes
nothing at all. `GET /api/backup` from this PC also carries `prepared` while a
run waits, so the desktop can offer `finish_phone_backup` as the **fallback**
if the phone is unavailable: the same route, the same code, the same
one-file guarantee. Choosing a folder, restoring, listing files and deleting
older copies are the PC's alone: the folder picker is Windows', and restoring
needs Windows Hello there.
**2026-10-20 (ruling 8.1, §45.4b):** the phone's `GET /api/backup` answer also
carries the persisted `last_restore` summary - outcome, plain message, the
safety backup's name, time and size, and the exact restored filenames - WITHOUT the
recovery code and without the technical `why`; reading it consumes nothing, so
a poll can never swallow it. **No app draws the dismiss button yet:** the
desktop's panel already shows the persisted outcome (its `last_restore.message`)
and the phone's parser ignores the new field until a screen wants it;
`POST /api/backup/restore/dismiss` is the named follow-up for that control.
Until it is wired, the record is replaced when the next restore finishes and
cleared only by that route - the reading itself never clears it. **2026-10-21
(audit fixes):** a dismiss from a paired device is refused (409, §45.4b
point 4 / M2) until the PC has shown that restore's one-time code, and the
`recovery_code_pending` field says when that is still owed - so a phone can
offer the clear button and show the PC-first refusal in the backend's own
words when it is not allowed yet. The desktop's hidden Backup page no longer
makes the "first read" that consumes the code (`backup-settings.js`'s
`onQueue` reload is `document.hidden`-guarded, like the visibility handler), so
the code is shown on the screen the owner is looking at.
`tools/check_parity.py`: `/api/backup` and `/api/backup/commit` are `ported`
(both apps read the first, at different depths, and since 2026-10-24 both apps
call the second - the phone's finish press, the desktop's fallback; the backend
binds the phone's call to the device that minted the run or to the PC, §45.3);
`/api/backup/status` and `/api/backup/prepare` are `phone-only`; every other
backup route is `deliberate` (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8).

**The phone's "Back up now", and why it is two calls (settled 2026-10-14).**
The owner asked for this button on 2026-10-10; the answer then was that the
phone could not have one that works, because `POST /api/backup/now` is refused
for every caller that is not this PC (`jarvis_backup.request_backup_now` ->
`jarvis_owner_check.from_this_pc`, 403 `pc_only`) and a phone reaching the PC
by its Tailscale or NordVPN Meshnet name is not this PC - measured on the
owner's own install that morning, where the phone's saved address
(`shared_prefs/jarvis_client.xml`, `host`) is a `.nord` name. What settled it
was not the refusal but the CODE:

- Each backup file is locked with its OWN one-time recovery code, the code is
  stored nowhere, and making a new backup **deletes the oldest of the 5 kept**.
- So a phone-triggered run whose code never reached the owner would not merely
  add a file nobody can open - it would **push out an older backup whose own
  code still works**, and the owner's only copy of his memories would be one
  step worse at every tap.
- Therefore the phone's run writes **nothing** when it is asked. `prepare`
  mints the code and holds it in memory; the phone draws it full-screen, in
  four groups of five, with a tick that must be set before the run can be
  finished; `commit` carries that same code back and the PC writes the file
  with it.

A run that is abandoned, or whose link drops, or whose owner changes his mind,
writes no file at all: the five backups already in the folder are untouched.
The code itself travels to the phone once, in the reply to `prepare`, and lives
on that screen until the run finishes - the change `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`
section 8 records for this one screen. The cost is the code's own cost, said on
the screen in those words: a code that is not kept is a backup that can never
be opened, and Jarvis cannot recover it.

### 45.5a What a check can and cannot prove

`GET /api/backup/status` checks the newest kept file against its own bytes:
our magic, a header whose Argon2id parameters are the ones `encrypt_blob`
writes, and a length of at least a whole file's shape. That is the difference
between a backup and a copy that was cut short - and it is deliberately NOT the
claim that the file opens. Opening one needs the recovery code, which is on
disk nowhere and by design cannot be (`generate_code`;
`backend/test_backup.py`'s `t_a_lost_code_truly_cannot_be_recovered`). So the
answer carries `verify.proves_open: false` always, and the phone draws the
limit beside the pass. To prove a backup opens, open it on the PC with its code
(Settings, Backups - the preview route, §45.3).

### 45.6 Known gaps, said plainly

- **A paired device can churn the kept backups** (2026-10-14, found in this
  feature's own audit; sharpened 2026-10-24 by the one-tap decision, and NOT
  closed by that day's asker guard).
  `POST /api/backup/prepare` is open to any paired device, which is what lets
  the phone ask at all, and it returns the run's one-time code to the same
  caller; since 2026-10-24 that caller may then `POST /api/backup/commit`
  **as the device that minted the run**, which the guard allows. So a token
  holder can ask, read the code out of the answer, then immediately commit,
  again and again. Each round makes a real
  backup and deletes the oldest of the 5 kept:
  the owner can push his own older backups out by accident, and someone
  holding the token could push them out on purpose. **What it cannot do is
  read anything**: the code goes only to the caller that asked, the file is
  encrypted, and no route returns a code that has already been used. So this
  is a way to lose OLD copies, never a way to open one. No rate limit is built
  - one that bit would be a new way for the owner to be told "no" by his own
  PC - and this is written here rather than left to be discovered.
- **The asker guard has two stated limits** (2026-10-24). It binds a finish to
  the device that minted the run or to this PC, and refuses any other paired
  device (403, nothing written, the run not spent, device checked before the
  code) - but (a) **a run minted with no recorded identity cannot be bound at
  all**: a backend without `jarvis_devices` (so no `_jarvis_device` stamp) or a
  direct in-process call leaves possession of the live code deciding, exactly
  as before, and the same shared token reaches the route from every device in
  that case; and (b) **the legacy shared key has one identity, `shared`, for
  every holder** until the first device is paired, so a run it minted cannot be
  told apart per device - once any device has a key of its own,
  `jarvis_devices` refuses the shared key from another device. Neither limit is
  a surprise hole: both are said in `jarvis_backup.request_commit`'s docstring
  and held by `backend/test_backup.py`.
- **The "I saved it" tick is a phone-side promise** (2026-10-24, accepted by
  the owner with the one-tap decision). The PC cannot check that the owner
  really wrote the code down; it only knows the phone said so and sent the
  code back. A modified or misused paired phone can therefore make the PC
  write a backup whose code was never kept - an unopenable file that pushes
  the oldest of the five kept out. Said plainly in
  `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8 and in `docs/DECISIONS.md`; the owner
  accepted it because the alternative was a run the phone could never finish.
- **Restoring while Jarvis is running can fail** if another part of the
  backend holds the database file open in a way Windows will not let this
  request replace; the restore fails cleanly (the safety backup already
  made is still there) rather than half-apply. On success the answer says
  to restart Jarvis so every part of it uses the restored data.
- **Not run on Windows.** The Windows Hello prompt for this card is the
  same approval-gap machinery §32.5 already says is untested on Windows.
- **A program already on the PC** that holds the token can raise the
  restore card; approving it still needs Windows Hello at the backend
  (`jarvis_owner_check`). Step 1's known limits (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`
  section 3) apply.

### 45.7 One destination, chosen by the owner (added 2026-10-14)

The `folder` key of `~/.openjarvis/backup.json` - written by `POST
/api/backup/folder`, read by `GET /api/backup` - is **the one setting** that
says where backups go, and it now governs both halves of Jarvis's backups:

- this section's `.jbak` feature, as it has since 2026-09-27;
- `tools/jarvis_data_backup.py` (`docs/DATA-BACKUP.md`), run weekly by the
  `Jarvis Personal Data Backup` task. It reads the same key **at run time**,
  every run, rather than writing to a folder compiled into itself: the task's
  command line carries no destination, so changing the folder changes where the
  next snapshot lands. `--dest` overrides it for one hand-run.

Nothing new on the wire: no route, no card and no setting was added. The tool
never writes `backup.json` (it must not change a setting the owner made in the
app) and never writes into `~/.openjarvis`, which its own suite enforces.

**The folder is checked before it is accepted**, in the words the owner reads,
by two halves that apply the same rules:

| rule | desktop (`backup.rs`, before the card) | weekly tool (`jarvis_data_backup.py`, before it writes) |
|---|---|---|
| it must be there | "is not there any more. Choose the folder again." | "is not a folder on this PC any more ... DID NOT run" |
| it must be writable | one empty probe file, removed at once | the same probe |
| never inside `~/.openjarvis` | refused | refused |
| never in a program folder | refused - this app's own, and the backend's when it can be resolved | refused - the folder the tool itself runs from |
| another drive | a question naming the drive, answered by the owner; nothing is sent until he answers | a note on the run's output, recorded as usual |

The desktop's refusal is shown on the Settings, Backups panel and **no approval
card is raised** - nothing was sent to the backend. The tool's is loud in the
three ways an unattended run can be: exit code 2, the reason printed, and a
`FAILED` `last-run.txt` written where it can be seen. A folder that is gone or
unwritable therefore cannot leave the last good run's `OK` line standing as if
nothing had happened.
---

## 46. News headlines in the morning briefing (added 2026-09-27)

The owner's decision (`CLAUDE.md`, feasibility I49; design source
`docs/CUTTING-EDGE-2026-09-26-round3-knowledge.md`, question 2): "News
headlines and 'tell me when this page changes': yes, the safe version - one
card per address the owner adds, read-only, never follows links elsewhere,
never acts on what it reads." §30.3.1 covers the page-change half; this
section is the news feed half.

`backend/jarvis_news.py`, shipped whole, `news.patch` adds three routes at
start-up the same way `documents.patch` (§35) does. Feeds are RSS or Atom
addresses the owner names; only each item's TITLE is ever read - never an
article's own page, and this module has no code that could fetch one.

**Corrected 2026-10-05.** This sentence used to end "which Jarvis has no
code to fetch at all", and that second half was false of the project as a
whole, not just of this module: §30.3.1's page watch, §115's "read this page
out loud" and `jarvis_browser_control.py`'s `read_page` step all fetch a
page. It is true of `jarvis_news.py`, and the claim that mattered - a feed's
headlines can never become an article's text - still holds, because no feed
is reachable from any of those three.

### 46.1 The list - empty by default, no dedicated settings screen

There is **no add/remove settings screen in either app** for this: like
"tell me when" (§30), a feed is added and removed by the owner's own words,
`jarvis_quick.py`'s fast path, so both apps get it for free from the one
shared chat pipeline:

- **"add this feed: `<url>`"**, "follow this feed `<url>`", "add `<url>` as
  a news feed" - raises the one card below.
- **"remove that feed: `<url>`"** - at once, no card.
- **"what news feeds do I have?"** / "list my news feeds" - the addresses,
  without the model.
- **"read me the news"** / "the news" / "what's in the news" - today's
  headlines from every listed feed, without the model (§46.4).

The three routes below exist so a settings screen can be added later
without changing `jarvis_news.py` - `jarvis_quick.py`'s fast path calls the
exact same `request_add`/`request_remove` functions.

| Route | Body | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/news` | - | **200** `{"available": true, "title", "detail", "feeds": [{"id", "url", "title", "added"}], "empty", "why", "can_add": true, "max": 10, "waiting", "waiting_words", "last", "remove_label"}` |
| `POST /api/news/add` | `{"url"}` | **202** `{"ok": true, "waiting": true, "view", "message"}` while ONE approval card waits; **200** `changed: false` if already listed; **400** a bad address, or one that resolves (real DNS, checked again on every later fetch) to this PC or a private network address; **409** the list is full (10) or a card is already waiting |
| `POST /api/news/remove` | `{"url"}` or `{"id"}` | **200** `{"ok": true, "changed", "view", "message"}` - at once, no card, either app; withdraws a waiting card for the same address |

### 46.2 The card

Action `change_own_config` (tier `ask` only - the shape of every setting
that lets Jarvis reach one more thing), the same action folders (§35) uses
for adding a folder:

```
Let Jarvis show headlines from this feed?

Feed: https://example.com/rss.xml

From now on, Jarvis's morning briefing (and "read me the news") can show
this feed's headlines. It reads only the feed itself, on a plain schedule -
never an article's own page, and never any other link on the feed. The
article text is never read, only each item's title.

Refused if that address turns out to lead to this PC or a private network
address, checked again on every read, in case that changes.

Headlines are outside text: a headline can say anything, so it is never
learned as a fact about you, and it marks the conversation as having read
outside text, exactly like a calendar title.

Removing the feed from the list is instant, from either app.

If you did not just do this, say no.

If you say no: nothing changes.
```

### 46.3 Reading a feed - never a link, never the article

One plain GET of the feed address only, through `jarvis_local_http.opener`
(no proxy) with a redirect followed only where
`jarvis_local_http.private_fetch_problem` would allow it. `jarvis_news.parse_headlines`
reads `<item><title>` (RSS) or `<entry><title>` (Atom), at most 5 per feed,
each capped at 200 characters; a document that declares a `DOCTYPE` or an
`ENTITY` is refused outright and parsed no further (a real feed never needs
either - this is how the parser stays out of XML's entity tricks without a
second dependency such as `defusedxml`). Each fetch is gated as `news_read`
(§4's new egress row) and runs only at tier `"auto"` or `"notify"` - the
same two tiers the briefing's weather and calendar reads accept, since this
runs about once a day, not every few minutes like a "tell me when" look.

### 46.4 In the briefing, and "read me the news"

`jarvis_briefing.py`'s `sources()` gains a `"news"` key, the same shape as
`"weather"`: `"on"` only when at least one feed is listed and its tier
allows an unattended read, else `"off"` (none listed) or `"asks"` (said
under `not_included`). A News section (`state`, `summary`, `items` - one
line per headline, `"<feed's own title>: <headline>"`) is added to the
built briefing when `"on"`, and every headline is OUTSIDE TEXT (a feed can
say anything): a briefing that shows one lists `news_read` in the turn's
`read`, exactly as a calendar title does.

The briefing's last line, when weather and/or news are missing, is now one
of four (all still non-blank, so an older app's own hard-coded fallback
text is never wrongly shown when the PC has something to say):

| Weather | News | Last line |
|---|---|---|
| off | off | `OUTSIDE_LINE` (unchanged wording, for an older PC too) |
| on | off | `NEWS_LINE` - "News: not available. No news feeds are listed ..." |
| off | on | `WEATHER_LINE` - "Weather: not available. It can come only from your own Home Assistant ..." |
| on | on | `BOTH_INCLUDED_LINE` - "Weather and news are both included above." |

Both apps' Settings, "What it includes" (`sourceLines`/its Kotlin
equivalent) now read a fourth key, `"news"`, alongside `calendar`, `email`
and `weather` - one line each, unchanged elsewhere.

"Read me the news" (`jarvis_quick.py`, without the model) reads every
listed feed and answers with the same headlines, marking the turn's `read`
with `news_read` only when a headline was really said (nothing listed:
`read` stays empty).

### 46.5 Egress

A new named way out of the PC: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §4 has the row -
`private_fetch_problem`'s real-DNS guard, shared with §30.3.1's page watch.

---

## 47. Music and video control on this PC (added 2026-09-27)

The owner's decision (`CLAUDE.md`, feasibility I91): "Music/video control
on the PC: no card, only from the owner's own words." Read literally, on
purpose: unlike "Lights, plugs and fans without a card" (§33), CLAUDE.md
gives this feature no on/off setting at all, so none is built - it is
always available, from words alone, never from the AI model's own
initiative and never from outside text (there is no model tool for it to
misuse).

`backend/jarvis_media.py`, shipped whole, `media.patch` adds two routes at
start-up the same way `stop-all.patch` and `documents.patch` do. Windows'
own media session (`GlobalSystemMediaTransportControlsSessionManager`,
reached from Python through `winrt-Windows.Media.Control`, PyPI, MIT) is
asked for whatever session Windows itself judges "current" right now - the
same one the hardware media keys on a keyboard would reach.

### 47.1 The fast path - both apps, the same chat pipeline

`jarvis_quick.py`, without the model, from either app (a spoken command is
already transcribed to text on this PC before it reaches here - CLAUDE.md:
"A client must not do speech-to-text" - so the desktop's typed words and a
phone's spoken words arrive the same way): "pause the music", "play the
song", "resume the video", "next song", "skip this track", "skip it",
"previous track", "what's playing", "now playing", "what song is this".
Bare "pause"/"resume" alone are left to the focus session's own words while
one is running (§26); a media command here always names the music, song,
track, video, media or playback, so the two never collide.

| Route | Body | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/media` | - | **200** `{"ok": bool, "said"}` - "what's playing" |
| `POST /api/media/control` | `{"action": "play" \| "pause" \| "next" \| "previous"}` | **200** `{"ok": true, "said"}`; **503** `{"ok": false, "said"}` when Windows' media controls could not be reached, nothing is playing, or Windows refused; **400** an action off the four |

**Never a card, whatever `jarvis-framework.toml` says**: `jarvis_media.py`
does not import `jarvis_gate` at all (`test_media.py` checks the source),
so there is no action name to give a tier to and nothing here can be made
to ask.

### 47.2 What it never does

Seek, change the volume, change shuffle or repeat, open an app, or choose
WHICH app's session to control - always "the current session". Song titles
and artist names are read only for "what's playing", never learned as a
fact, never saved: the answer marks the turn's `read` with `media_now_playing`
only when a real title or artist was said (nothing playing, or the call
failed: `read` stays empty) - the same reasoning a calendar title's outside
text gets.

### 47.3 Windows-only, and graceful without it

`winrt-Windows.Media.Control` is Windows-only and every import of it is
inside a function, never at module load, so the module imports cleanly
without it (Linux, or a Windows PC that has not run `apply-patches.ps1`'s
install step yet); calling `control()`/`now_playing()` then says plainly
why it could not reach Windows' media controls, the same shape every other
optional tool in this backend uses (MarkItDown, Windows' own OCR).

### 47.4 One code path, not two

The design research (`docs/CUTTING-EDGE-2026-09-26-capabilities.md`, idea
7) flagged that the desktop's `windows` crate could reach the same Windows
API directly, in Rust. It is not wired up: every command - typed on the
desktop or spoken on the phone - already reaches the SAME backend route
through the SAME chat pipeline (rule: "A client must not do speech-to-text"
already means neither app can act on words without the backend seeing them
first), so a second, Rust-native implementation would duplicate this
module's logic for no capability either app gains. The `Media_Control`
Cargo feature was checked (`jarvis-desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml`) and is
not enabled, for the same reason: nothing in the Rust side needs it, and
this is not a `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 "one-sided" decision at all - both
apps reach the feature identically, through words, with no Rust or Kotlin
code calling a route directly.

## 48. "Between us": shared jokes and nicknames (added 2026-09-27)

The owner's decision (`CLAUDE.md`, 2026-09-27): "Inside jokes: yes, a
'between us' list in Brain with Forget, from the owner's own words only."
Full design: `docs/CUTTING-EDGE-2026-09-26-round4-growth.md` section 7.

**What it is not**: a new way to save a fact. "Remember: we call the
printer 'the beast'" is saved exactly as any other "Remember: ..." is
(§19, `jarvis_auto_learn.after_remember`) - this feature never touches
saving. **What it is**: a LABEL - `meta.kind = "shared"` - the owner's own
tap adds to or takes off a fact that already exists, the same shape as
Pin/Unpin for "Always keep in mind" (§6), except the label lives IN the
fact's own meta rather than a separate table, so it is a fact property, not
a second list to keep in sync.

### 48.1 Routes

See §6's table: `GET`/`POST /api/memory/shared`. No approval card and no
confirm for tagging or untagging - the owner's own tap on a fact they can
already see, exactly like Pin. Held on a stale link, like every memory
write.

### 48.2 Only ever the owner's own tap

Never set automatically by auto-learning, however the fact itself was
saved, and never by the model - `MemoryStore.shared()` is called from
nowhere but the route above. The usual sensitive-topic checks are
untouched: a shared fact can also be about health, money or another
sensitive topic, and `shared()` never reads or writes `meta.sensitive`.
Never pinned automatically either: `shared()` never touches the `profile`
