## 126. The big coding model: both cards, with Jarvis paused

`qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-ud-q3-k-xl` (UD-Q3_K_XL, 13,806,312,608 B, Apache 2.0) is
the one model on this PC that needs **both** graphics cards. It is the best
coder and the fastest writer ever measured here - **10/10** on the project's
coding test, about **101 / 76.5 / 76.3 tokens a second** on the three bench
prompts, and **no thinking mode** to default on and return an empty answer -
and its cost is the whole reason it is a mode and not a model: its
GPU-resident footprint at the smallest context tested is **14,813 MiB** against
a 12,288 MiB card and an 8,192 MiB card
(`.dsh-scratch/android-verify/BIG-MODELS-2026-10-10.md`, sections 6b, 6c, 12).

So the owner's decision, which `backend/jarvis_big_coder.py` implements and does
not re-litigate: **OFF by default, never resident beside the two live lanes,
the pause announced before it starts, and both lanes put back exactly as they
were - proved from `/api/ps`.**

### 126.1 The two routes

Both routes are the ONE path `/api/big-coder`, told apart by the method: a
`GET`, and a `POST`. That is exactly what `backend/big-coder.patch` installs -
two route blocks, `if path == "/api/big-coder":` in the GET handler and `if
route == "/api/big-coder":` in the POST handler.

| Route | Method | Body | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/api/big-coder` | GET | - | The switch, the model, the context, what is loaded on all three ports right now, and what a start would do. **Read-only**: it loads nothing, unloads nothing and writes nothing |
| `/api/big-coder` | POST | `{"on": true\|false}`, or `{"action": "start"\|"stop"}` | The one write, and the body says which. **`on`** is the opt-in switch: ON is ONE approval card (`change_own_config`, tier `"ask"`), OFF is immediate. **`action`** starts the mode or stops it and restores the lanes, through `power_manage`, the action that already governs what is on the cards |

The POST answers `400` to anything that is neither shape, so a caller with a
bug finds out rather than getting a silent success. Both go through the
server's own origin and token checks, like every other route, and every call
is loopback only. No new gate action is invented: the opt-in reuses
`change_own_config` (the shape `jarvis_backup.py` and `jarvis_big_model.py`
use) and the mode itself reuses `power_manage`.

There is **no desktop Settings row or phone control yet** - the route is the
backend half, and the switch can also be turned on by asking Jarvis ("turn on
the big coding model", a `BoolSetting` in `jarvis_settings_registry.py`). The
page row needs its own Rust command and JavaScript, like every other switch on
that page.

### 126.2 The order, which is the contract

1. The switch must be on, no multi-step task may be running, and the gate must
   allow it. Otherwise **nothing is touched at all**.
2. **The pause is announced first** - the card names both lanes, their models,
   their contexts and their cards - and it goes out on the event bus and the
   audit log **before** the first unload.
3. One `ollama serve` is started for the mode alone, on its own port
   (`jarvis_big_coder.BIG_PORT`, 11450), with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` **removed**
   (that is what lets Ollama see both cards) and `OLLAMA_VULKAN=0` (without
   which the unset variable silently falls back to Vulkan onto one card). The
   two **lane servers are never touched** - different port, different process.
   A server already answering on that port is used as it is and not stopped
   afterwards.
4. **Both lanes are unloaded and proved gone from `/api/ps`.** If a lane will
   not go, the start is refused (409), **nothing is loaded**, whatever was
   unloaded is put back, and the server is stopped. It never runs beside a lane.
5. The model is loaded **naming the context**, `jarvis_big_coder.NUM_CTX` -
   **28,672**, the largest measured to fit both cards with zero spill. A load
   that spills (`size_vram < size`) or comes up at another context is
   **unloaded again**, the lanes are restored, and the answer says why (503).
6. **Stopping** unloads the model, stops the server this mode started, and puts
   both lanes back - `11436 qwen3.5:9b @196608` on the RTX 2060 and
   `11435 qwen3:8b @16384` on the RTX 2080 SUPER - checking model, context and
   zero spill in `/api/ps` for each. A lane that does not come back is a 503
   naming it, never a success.

Nothing here downloads anything, and nothing leaves this PC.

### 126.3 What is not built

- The desktop Settings row and any phone control (section 126.1).
- `tools/check_parity.py` does not yet classify these routes: they are the
  backend half, called by no client, and a follow-up lists them there.
- No real load was run while this was written: the owner's two lanes are live
  and other work was measuring on the same cards. The contract is proved
  against fakes (`backend/test_big_coder.py`), and the live facts it depends on
  were read, not assumed: on 2026-10-11 the two lanes were resident at
  `qwen3:8b ctx=16384` (11435) and `qwen3.5:9b ctx=196608` (11436), both zero
  spill, and the model was present in the Ollama store on `D:` - **but the
  server on port 11434 did not know the model** (`POST /api/show` answered
  404), so the mode's own both-cards server is what will see it.

## 127. Approval cards read short: the summary, "Explain more", and the setting (added 2026-10-10)

The owner, 2026-10-09, in their own words: *"for approval cards, there should be
a more simple summary, with an explain more button that expands the approval
card total word length and explains the details more. and approval card
preferences such as this should be changeable in the settings"*.

Built by `backend/card-prefs.patch` (one route), the shipped
`backend/jarvis_card_summary.py` (the preference and the "what one card shows"
rule), the shipped `backend/jarvis_card_words.py` (`SUMMARY`, the short words -
the same one source the title already comes from), `backend/approval-notice.patch`
(the two new fields on every pending row), `backend/test_card_short_words.py`,
and the phone's `net/CardSummary.kt` + `ui/screens/ApprovalCardsPlate.kt` +
`CardSummaryTest.kt`. **This section exists because the route and the two fields
were not written down anywhere else.**

### 127.1 One line first, the whole card one tap away

Every pending row already carried `notice` (`approval-notice.patch`, §3). It now
carries **two more fields**, and they are the whole feature:

| field | what it is |
|---|---|
| `notice.summary` | the SHORT line a card shows first: "Jarvis wants to send the email shown." |
| `notice.full` | the WHOLE card, word for word as `body` always was - what "Explain more" opens |

`notice.body` is **unchanged and still equals `notice.full`**, so a client that
has never heard of the control draws exactly what it drew before. Neither field
ever carries `detail`, `prompt` or the contents of `raised`: both are built from
the action NAME, `jarvis_card_words.py`'s own tables and the risk table, which is
what keeps a notice safe to put on a lock screen.

**A summary is never blank and never the raw action id.** In order,
`jarvis_card_words.summary_for`: the written short phrase for that action; else
the card's own FIRST WHOLE SENTENCE ("never cut mid-word"); else the readable
title `title_for` already guarantees. `backend/test_card_short_words.py` pins all
three, and fails by name when an action the gate knows has no short row.

### 127.2 The preference, in one file both apps read

    GET  /api/card-prefs     the setting, its two choices and the words to show
    POST /api/card-prefs     {"mode": "start_short" | "always_full"}

Kept in `<config dir>/card-prefs.json`, **beside `appearance.json` and
`animal.json`** - so the phone and the desktop read one value and cannot
disagree. `start_short` is the default, and it is the default for a missing
file, a damaged one, an unknown mode or a value of the wrong type; none of those
is ever read as a choice. `mode` is the field a client draws from:

| `mode` | what a card does |
|---|---|
| `start_short` | the short summary, with an "Explain more" control |
| `always_full` | drawn open, whole text, **no control** - nothing is folded away |

`available` is the read flag (a client checks it before believing `mode`),
`stored` says whether a real choice is saved or the default is merely in force,
`choices` carries both ids with their labels and the default marked, and
`more_label` / `less_label` are the control's own words - the PC's, so the two
apps cannot word the same button differently.

**Both directions are cosmetic and both are immediate: no approval card, either
way, from either app or by asking.** This changes which words a card draws and
nothing else - it approves nothing, starts nothing and reaches nothing - which is
the same rule the animal options and "How Jarvis talks" follow. An unknown mode
is refused with `400` rather than quietly saved as something else.

**By asking:** "always show me the whole approval card", "show me the whole
card", "the short summary", "start short" - `jarvis_card_summary.spoken`'s own
list, read by `jarvis_settings_registry.find_card_mode` and applied through
`set_card_mode`, which calls the one function the route calls. A sentence it does
not recognise is `None` and falls through to the model rather than picking a card
style on the owner's behalf. "Show everything" on its own deliberately stays
`jarvis_menus.ALL_MENUS_PHRASES` (the older "show me every menu"), which
`jarvis_quick.match` checks first.

### 127.3 Where the control is, in each app

- **Phone** (`jarvis-client`): the card's own text (`ApprovalCard.kt`), folded by
  default, with "Explain more" / "Show less" under the summary. The setting is
  Settings → **"Approval cards"**, right under Appearance
  (`ApprovalCardsPlate.kt`, `item(key = "approval-cards")`). Opening one card
  touches no other: the open/closed state is keyed on the card's own id.
- **Desktop** (`jarvis-desktop/` + `src-tauri/`): **not built on this branch** -
  those folders belong to another conversation, and the owner's brief for this
  work says not to edit them. What it needs is written up in
  `docs/DESKTOP-APPROVAL-CARD-PREF.md`: the file (`src/main.js`,
  `refreshApproval`), the control, and the field it reads (`mode`). Until its
  card in `settings.html` lands, the backend's
  `jarvis_settings_registry.SECTIONS` entry for `approval-cards` stays
  `app="phone"`, so "open approval cards" never names a place the desktop does
  not have; the desktop can still change the setting by asking.

## 128. Work setups: five model combinations for a kind of work (added 2026-10-10)

**SUPERSEDED for `GET /api/work` (2026-10-19).** The public read route now serves the ten FOCUS PRESETS in section 145 (`jarvis_presets.py`); the five work setups below remain only inside `jarvis_work.py` for the old `POST /api/work/recommend` and `POST /api/work/choose` compatibility paths, and are no longer what either app reads. The preset UI contract is section 145.

The owner asked (2026-10-10):

> "analyze what different model combinations from the latest and best models
> available for download would be best for different work for jarvis. like if i
> was going to code an android app, or work on admin stuff from my own life.
> and have these as selectable options that explain what they do before i start
> work. and jarvis can also recommend loading up certain combos if i talk about
> work i'd like to do"

`backend/jarvis_work.py` (shipped whole; `backend/work.patch` adds the three
routes to `jarvis_hud.py`) holds **five combinations of local models**, each
chosen for a kind of work, with the measured cost of each on its own label.
The design note and every measurement are
`.dsh-scratch/android-verify/WORK-SETUPS-DESIGN-2026-10-10.md`,
`MODEL-BENCH-2026-10-10.md` and `MODEL-STRATEGY-2026-10-10.md`, on the owner's
PC and not in this repository; `tools/check_work_claims.py` fails if a number or
a quoted phrase in the module cannot be traced back to them.

### 128.1 The three routes

    GET  /api/work                 the five setups for THIS PC's cards: names,
                                   what each is for, which model goes on which
                                   card, its measured speed and context, what it
                                   costs, what it is honestly worse at, which
                                   models are already downloaded, which is
                                   running now, and which one the owner chose

    POST /api/work/choose          {"setup": "everyday"|"coding"|"admin"|
                                    "long"|"specialist"|null}
                                   Remember a setup, or forget it (null)

    POST /api/work/recommend       {"words": "<what the owner said>"}
                                   Which setup to OFFER for those words, and the
                                   sentence to say

`GET /api/work` also answers **`chosen`** (the remembered id, or `null`) and,
per setup, **`ready`** - one of `ready`, `partial`, `missing` or `unknown`,
worked out from Ollama's own `/api/tags` and never guessed, with the PC's own
`ready_words` sentence beside it. A setup whose model is missing says so in
words and points at the ordinary download card; this module never downloads
anything and names **no** install route.

The answer is model names, card names and measured numbers. It never carries a
token, a prompt, an answer or anything the owner said.

### 128.2 Nothing here changes a model

- **`/api/work/choose` only remembers.** It writes one preference
  (`work-setup-choice.json`, beside the other settings files) and returns the
  **one** step that would switch a model. It changes no model and no Ollama
  setting, and it raises no card of its own.
- **`/api/work/recommend` switches nothing.** The answer carries
  `switched: false`, always (`test_work.py` checks every case in the golden
  file). Acting on an offer is the owner's tap, and the switch itself is the
  existing `/api/models/switch` card - tier `ask`, raised by the app that posts
  it and decided as any other model change is (the owner's decisions of
  2026-09-18 and 2026-09-20). There is no new gate action, no new tier and no
  new route for a model change.

A crisis turn offers nothing, a turn where the owner is already talking about
models says nothing, and one loose word is never enough - each of those is a
case in `jarvis-client/app/src/test/resources/contract/work-setups-cases.json`.

### 128.3 What is built, and the one half that is not

**Built and reachable:** `GET /api/work` and `POST /api/work/choose`, and the
phone's **Work setups** section under Brain → Hardware
(`net/WorkSetups.kt`, `ui/screens/HardwarePlate.kt`'s `WorkSetupsSection`,
`JarvisRuntime.refreshWorkSetups` / `chooseWorkSetup` / `workSetupStep`), with
its own contract test (`WorkSetupsContractTest.kt`) reading the golden file the
PC's module generates.

**Built and NOT wired, deliberately:** the recommendation. Nothing in either
app offers a setup inside a chat turn today, and this section says so outright
because an earlier version of `docs/WORK-SETUPS.md` claimed the phone asked for
it:

- `jarvis_hud.py`'s chat route does not call `jarvis_work.match()`. The route
  is ready and safe to call; the seam is the core file, and `work.patch`
  deliberately does not touch it.
- `JarvisRuntime.offerWorkSetup` is the **only** thing in either app that would
  POST `/api/work/recommend`, and **no Kotlin file under
  `jarvis-client/app/src/main` calls it**. So `JarvisRuntime.workOffer` is never
  set, and the offer panel `HardwarePlate.kt` draws ("Jarvis suggests a
  setup") can never be populated.

Two checks now hold that, rather than a sentence in a document:

- `backend/test_work.py` asserts that no Kotlin file under the phone's `main`
  calls `offerWorkSetup`, with a message naming exactly what to correct when one
  does. It is the check that fails the day the offer is wired up.
- `tools/check_parity.py` carries `/api/work/recommend` in its `UNREACHABLE`
  list, which names the file and the function that build it and why nothing
  calls it. That list is checked in both directions: while the function has no
  caller the entry must stay, and **the moment it is called the checker fails**
  and says to delete the entry, reclassify the route, and correct the docs.
  `backend/test_parity_callgraph.py` proves that second direction on a
  throwaway checkout, including the harder case - a call site inside a function
  nothing calls - which is the defect this whole guard exists to catch.

The desktop never builds this section: its work surface is the focus presets
(§145), which apply through `POST /api/work/apply`
(`src-tauri/src/focus_presets.rs`, `focus-presets.js`). `docs/WORK-SETUPS.md`'s
"Still to build" half predates that replacement (2026-10-18) and is kept as the
older design's history, not as work still wanted.

### 128.4 How `tools/check_parity.py` records them now

`/api/work` is `ported`: both apps read the focus-presets contract on it
(§145). `/api/work/choose` is `phone-only` (the 2026-11-05 parity audit's F6):
it is the superseded setups contract's one write; `net/WorkSetups.kt` still
serves it, the phone's old Work setups section is no longer drawn (the Focus
presets plate replaced it, 2026-10-19), and the desktop has no old-setups
surface - its work surface is the presets, which apply through
`/api/work/apply` (ARCHITECTURE §8). `/api/work/recommend` stays `planned` and
RETIRED: F11 took the phone's builder away and the PC route remains with
nobody calling it, which the checker prints as "RETIRED (no app calls it)" with
that reason. The old line, "the phone calls it", came from a string match and
was never true for `recommend`. `backend/test_parity_callgraph.py` still pins
the direction that matters for shipping - one real call site and the checker
fails instead.
---

## 129. Ask for a picture, and keep it (added 2026-10-11)

`backend/jarvis_pictures.py` (shipped whole), `backend/pictures.patch` (one
`install()` call in `jarvis_hud.py`), `backend/test_pictures.py`. The owner's
decision of 2026-09-27: *"12 GB card: longer conversations with picture
understanding first, and **making pictures too (swapped in when asked, since
both cannot sit on the card at once)**"* (CLAUDE.md).

### 129.1 What it is, in plain words

You ask Jarvis for a picture, in your own words. A picture-making program on
this PC draws it, the picture is saved in a folder on this PC, and both apps
show it to you again with the words that made it. **Nothing leaves the PC**
(CLAUDE.md rule 1): the drawing program is a program on this machine, and the
only address this module ever opens a socket to is the one the owner
configured. The sidecar beside each picture holds the prompt, the seed, the
model and the settings, so the owner can read what a picture was and make it
again.

### 129.2 The routes

    GET  /api/pictures           the folder, how many pictures are in it, how
                                 big it is, the switch, the chosen program and
                                 every picture with its own prompt, seed,
                                 model and when it was made. A read.
    GET  /api/pictures/file      ?id=<id> - ONE picture, as base64 in JSON
                                 with the token header, exactly as the captcha
                                 hand-off sends its own frame
                                 (jarvis_handoff.py). This is how the phone
                                 saves one to itself.
    POST /api/pictures           {"prompt": "...", "seed"?: n,
                                  "settings"?: {"steps","width","height",
                                                "model","negative"},
                                  "free_card"?: true}
                                 Draw one and keep it. `free_card` is the
                                 second request that consents to the everyday
                                 chat stepping aside; it is described in 129.4b
                                 and is never needed when the card is free.
                                 EITHER app may send it (owner decision
                                 2026-10-24): the desktop's confirm and a paired
                                 phone's confirm run the same swap.
    POST /api/pictures/settings  ONE named change, and the PC REFUSES all of it
                                 from anywhere but the PC (403 pc_only):

      {"action": "enabled", "on": true}
      {"action": "runtime", "runtime": "comfyui" | "sd_cpp" | null,
       "address"?: "http://127.0.0.1:8188"}
      {"action": "folder", "folder": "D:\\Jarvis pictures"}

The successful `POST` answers with where the picture went and how long it took:

    {"ok": true, "available": true, "name": "2026-10-11-140509-a-red-panda.png",
     "id": "2026-10-11-140509-a-red-panda", "path": "<the folder>\\<the name>",
     "folder": "<the folder>", "prompt": "a red panda", "seed": 1234,
     "model": "sd_xl_base_1.0.safetensors", "runtime": "comfyui",
     "settings": {"steps": 28, "width": 768, "height": 512},
     "seconds": 41.2, "bytes": 812345, "made_at_words": "11 Oct 2026, 14:05",
     "words": "Drawn in 41.2 seconds and saved as 2026-10-11-140509-a-red-panda.png."}

`prompt` is required and is capped at 2000 characters; `settings` are the
**drawing program's own knobs**, not Jarvis settings, and the two names are
kept apart on purpose. Every refusal is `{"ok": false, "error": "<one plain
sentence>"}` - never a traceback, never an empty 200.

### 129.3 Where pictures are kept, and what is beside them

- **The folder** is `folder` in `pictures.json` in the config folder (the same
  place `folders.json` and `asks_first.json` live), defaulting to
  `%USERPROFILE%\Pictures\Jarvis`. It is chosen **on the PC only**, the same
  shape `jarvis_backup.py` uses for its backup folder.
- **The name** is `YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<slug>.png`, where `<slug>` is the first
  six words of the prompt with everything that is not a letter or a digit
  turned into a dash (48 characters at most, `picture` if that leaves
  nothing). **The date AND the time are both in the name**, and a name already
  on disk gets `-2`, `-3` and so on, so two pictures asked for in the same
  second cannot collide and **nothing is ever overwritten**.
- **The sidecar** is `<same name>.json` beside the picture:
  `{"jarvis_pictures": 1, "picture", "prompt", "seed", "runtime", "model",
  "settings", "made_at", "made_at_words", "seconds"}`.
- **Nothing is deleted on a timer.** Unlike `jarvis_backup.py`'s five kept
  files, the owner's own pictures are never tidied away by Jarvis; the list
  route reports the folder and its total size so the owner can see what it
  costs. A picture whose sidecar is lost is **still listed**, with `prompt`
  empty and `record: false`, rather than disappearing.

A sidecar that cannot be written costs the record, never the picture: the PNG
is written first and the JSON second, so a crash between them leaves a picture
that is merely unexplained.

### 129.4 The switch, and the two things the owner has to do

Both cards are Turing and the everyday model already holds the 12 GB one, so
the drawing program has to be swapped in and only one of the two can be on the
card at a time. The owner's standing rule is that a feature using the second
card keeps **its own switch, off until that feature is measured**; the switch
is:

    Settings > Pictures > "Making pictures"     default OFF

`pictures.json` holds four keys, each read with its own fallback so a
hand-edited or half-written file can never crash a route and can never turn
the feature on:

    {"enabled": false, "runtime": null, "address": null, "folder": null}

`runtime` is **a setting with named supported values, never guessed at**,
because two different programs are plausible and the owner may install either:

| `runtime` | the program | its own default address |
|---|---|---|
| `comfyui` | ComfyUI (`/prompt`, `/history`, `/view`) | `http://127.0.0.1:8188` |
| `sd_cpp` | stable-diffusion.cpp's `sd-server` (`/sdapi/v1/txt2img`) | `http://127.0.0.1:1234` |

`address` overrides that runtime's own default for an owner who runs it on
another port. Nothing here installs, starts, stops or reconfigures the drawing
program, and nothing here chooses or downloads a model: whatever the program is
configured with is what draws, and its model name is written into the sidecar.

**What the owner sees when it is not set up is one plain sentence, never an
error and never a silent nothing:**

- with no `runtime` chosen: *"Jarvis has no picture-making program set up yet,
  so it cannot draw one. Install ComfyUI (https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI)
  or stable-diffusion.cpp's server (https://github.com/leejet/stable-diffusion.cpp),
  then choose which one you installed in Settings, under Pictures."* - `503`,
  `available: false`.
- with `runtime` chosen but the program not answering: *"Jarvis is set to use
  ComfyUI, but it is not answering. Start it on this PC, then ask again."* -
  `503`, `available: false`.
- with the switch off: *"Making pictures is switched off. Turn on \"Making
  pictures\" in Settings, under Pictures, when you want Jarvis to use the
  second card for this."* - `503`, `off: true`.

### 129.4b The swap: the everyday chat steps aside (added 2026-10-25)

The owner's 2026-09-27 decision says the picture-maker is *"swapped in when
asked, since both cannot sit on the card at once"*. Until 2026-10-25 the swap
was never done by Jarvis: the route drew if the program answered and the
owner's chat stayed on the card, which on this PC means a real Chroma1-HD draw
(8.57 GiB of weights) cannot fit. It is now two requests, and nothing moves on
the first one:

    POST /api/pictures  {"prompt": "a red panda"}                 -> 409
    POST /api/pictures  {"prompt": "a red panda", "free_card": true} -> 200

The 409 is the price, said before anything is unloaded:

    {"ok": false, "available": true, "needs": "free_card", "option": "A",
     "estimate": {"draw_seconds": 380.0, "chat_away_seconds": 440.0,
                  "minutes": 7},
     "confirm": {"free_card": true},
     "error": "Drawing needs the 12 GB card, and your everyday chat is using
               it. If you agree, Jarvis sets the everyday chat aside for a few
               minutes, draws the picture, then loads the chat back the way it
               was - the conversation and its settings are kept. Nothing else
               changes. This takes about 7 minutes, and the chat comes back on
               its own afterwards."}

The confirmed request does, in this order: the everyday chat lane is unloaded
(`keep_alive: 0` - Ollama's own "unload now"; the lane's settings are not
changed), the picture is drawn, ComfyUI is asked to release its models (its own
`POST /free`) **and is waited for until its own `/system_stats` shows the models
gone**, and the everyday chat is warmed back. The waiting is not politeness:
`POST /free` only *asks* the program to let go - it answers HTTP 200 with a
**body of 0 bytes**, measured on this PC 2026-10-25 - so the release happens
after it returns. The first version read that empty body as JSON, failed in
0.0 s and warmed the chat back while ~10.9 GB was still being released; it came
back 1.36 GB spilled into system RAM. Since 2026-10-25 the empty answer is
expected (`allow_empty=True` on that one call) and the `/system_stats` poll
does the waiting. `FREE_WAIT_S = 180` bounds the wait; a program that never
lets go is one plain sentence (`models_freed: false`) and the chat is still
warmed back. The 200 carries the normal body plus the swap's own record:

    "card": {"option": "A", "did": true, "chat_away_seconds": 2.5,
             "chat_back_seconds": 9.0, "chat_back": true,
             "models_freed": true}

**One sentence, one field (2026-10-25).** The swap's sentence - *"Your
everyday chat stepped aside for 2.5 seconds and is back on the card after
another 9.0 seconds."* - is appended to the answer's own `words` when the
picture was drawn, and to `error` when the draw failed; `card` carries the
numbers only and has **no `words` key**. It used to be in both, so one answer
handed every app two copies of the same words and a client that joined them
printed it twice (the desktop page did before PR #818; the phone's
`Pictures.madeWords` joins both). The backend is now the one owner: an app
reads `words` for a drawing, `error` for a failure, and the card for the times.

Rules that are part of the feature, not implementation detail:

- **Never silent.** The first request tells the owner what will pause and for
  roughly how long; no `free_card: true` request, no swap.
- **Never on an error path.** The warm-back runs in a `finally`: a refused or
  crashed draw still puts the everyday model back and says so in the answer.
  If it cannot come back the answer says that too - and does not claim a
  picture was the only thing that happened.
- **Either app may confirm it (owner decision 2026-10-24).** The owner asked,
  in their own words, to approve it from their phone too. The swap is local and
  reversible - the chat reloads on its own and nothing is deleted - so a paired
  phone's `free_card: true` is the same deliberate request as the desktop's,
  and both run the swap above. The first 409 question is the same for both, and
  nothing moves on it. What stays PC-only is the settings route below (where
  pictures are kept, which program draws them).
- **One picture at a time.** Because the phone may now confirm, a double tap is
  a real second request: a confirm that arrives while a draw is running is
  refused in one plain sentence (`409`, `needs: "drawing"`), starts no second
  draw beside the first, and leaves the running one (and its warm-back) alone.
- **No approval card.** The card belongs to turning image mode ON (the switch
  above, PC-only and off by default), not to an in-and-out swap of the same
  card whose price is reported before and after in plain seconds - and a
  phone's confirm raises no card either: the 409 question IS the price, and the
  confirm is the owner's own deliberate tap.
- **The three ways are the card module's (`/api/picture-card`).** Way A (the
  recommended one) is the swap above; way C asks for no swap because it never
  touches the chat; way B (moving the chat to the 8 GB card) is recorded but
  not wired, and a draw under B answers one plain sentence rather than
  pretending.
- **It still starts nothing.** Starting ComfyUI remains the owner's own
  program, as 129.4 says; this section only unloads and warms the chat.
- **The chat comes back onto a card that is really free.** The `/free` request
  gets `FREE_WAIT_S` (180 s) and is then followed by a `/system_stats` poll until
  ComfyUI holds no more than 1 GiB (`FREE_FLOOR_BYTES`), so the warm-back starts
  from a freed card. The poll has its OWN `FREE_WAIT_S` deadline, set after the
  `/free` call returns (`free_models()`: `timeout=FREE_WAIT_S`, then
  `deadline = time.time() + FREE_WAIT_S`), so the whole let-go step can cost up
  to 360 s. If the program never lets go, the answer says so
  (`models_freed: false`, with the GB still held) and the chat is still brought
  back, possibly partly spilled.
- **The wait is ten minutes, not two.** `DRAW_WAIT_S = 600` in
  `jarvis_pictures.py`: the measured 274.4 s draw plus a cold load, and still
  a finite wait - a wedged job ends in a sentence, never in a hung route.
- **The confirm is ONE long request.** Measured on this PC: **405.8 s** wall
  clock (draw 381.0 s; the rest is the swap and the warm-back). The app's budget
  must cover the PC's WORST CASE, not that measurement: the five ceilings are
  `unload_lane(timeout=120)` 120 + `DRAW_WAIT_S` (600) + the `/free` call's
  `FREE_WAIT_S` (180) + the `/system_stats` poll's second `FREE_WAIT_S` (180) +
  `warm_lane(timeout=600)` 600 = **1,680 s**, about 28 minutes
  (`backend/jarvis_picture_card.py:526` and `:564-565`;
  `backend/jarvis_pictures.py:197` and `:208`). So an app must give this single
  request a read timeout longer than that. Both apps use **1,740 s**, about 29
  minutes - a minute of headroom - and must not re-send it on a timeout: a
  re-send while the draw runs is answered by the one-at-a-time sentence above,
  and the draw keeps going.
  **Correction (2026-10-25):** an earlier version of this paragraph said the
  ceilings added up to 1,500 s over four terms. That was 180 s short - it
  counted the let-go step once, and `free_models()` waits twice, once for
  `/free` and again for its own poll. The five-term sum is 1,680 s and the
  apps' budget is 1,740 s.

### 129.5 No approval card, and why that is not a loophole

**Making a picture needs no approval card.** The gate exists for things that
leave the PC, change the owner's accounts, or cannot be undone
(`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 4). A picture is none of those: it is a new
file in a folder on this PC, drawn by a program on this PC, from words the
owner typed. It is the same shape as a timer or a note, both of which need no
card.

**Sending that picture to anyone else would be a new named way out of the PC,
and this is deliberately not built.** There is no email, no upload, no chat
attachment and no web search here. The phone's own **"Save to my phone"** reads
the picture over Tailscale or NordMesh - a way to the owner's own device, not a
way out of the PC - exactly as the captcha hand-off's one frame does.

**Where the prompt came from still matters, and is not invented here.** The
prompt is whatever the owner typed in the box. `jarvis_pictures.py` is not a
tool in `jarvis_agent.py`, is not imported by it, and is reachable from no
model turn, so a prompt can never be filled in from email, a web page or a
file by the model. `test_pictures.py` fails if any model path starts importing
it.

### 129.6 Hidden with the private things, on both apps

The prompts are the owner's own words, so the gallery and the prompt text
**hide under "Hide memory lists and chat history" like every other private
surface** - added to that rule rather than beside it. On the desktop the answer
is replaced in Rust (the same shape `brain/progress.rs` uses) so a page script
cannot read round it; on the phone the plate fetches nothing at all while the
switch is on, and shows one line saying so
(`WORDS["hidden_short"]` = *"Turn off Hide memory lists to see your pictures."*).

### 129.7 The two surfaces

Both draw the same feature and both are hidden by their own menu entry -
`brain.projects.pictures` for the gallery, `settings.pictures` for the PC's
setup (JARVIS-API section 109).

- **Desktop.** Two places, and each says where the other is. The SETUP is
  Settings -> **Pictures** (`jarvis-desktop/src/pictures-settings.js`):
  "Making pictures", the program that draws (the two supported values, each
  with what to install), and the folder with its size. The GALLERY is Brain ->
  **Projects** -> **Pictures**
  (`jarvis-desktop/src/pictures-panel.js`, its own pane `#pictures-root`,
  beside the Progress pictures): the box to ask for a new one, and every
  picture with its prompt, its seed, its model and when it was made, a **Make
  another** on each. The four commands are in
  `jarvis-desktop/src-tauri/src/brain/pictures.rs`:
  `brain_pictures`, `brain_pictures_file`, `brain_pictures_make`,
  `brain_pictures_settings` and `choose_pictures_folder` (the same Windows
  "Select folder" dialog "Folders Jarvis may look in" uses). A picture's bytes
  are drawn as a `data:` image, which the packaged CSP already allows
  (`img-src data:`), fetched one at a time as each picture scrolls into view.
  There is no "save to my phone" on the PC: the picture is already on it.
- **Phone.** Brain -> **Pictures**, in `ui/screens/PicturesPlate.kt`, reading
  through `net/Pictures.kt`. Each picture shows with its prompt and when it was
  made, a **Make another** button, and **Save to my phone**, which reads
  `/api/pictures/file` and writes the PNG into the phone's own Pictures
  collection through MediaStore. Nothing about a model, a catalogue or a
  drawing program is on the phone: it sends a prompt and reads a picture.
  **The 409 confirm flow is drawn on the phone** (2026-10-25): the backend
  accepts a phone's `free_card: true` (owner decision 2026-10-24, 129.4b), and
  `PicturesPlate.kt` sends it only on the owner's own tap, on the same long
  1,740 s read budget as the desktop (`Pictures.CONFIRM_TIMEOUT_S`).

### 129.8 Tests, and what is honestly not proved

`python3 backend/test_pictures.py` (with `JARVIS_BACKEND` set the way every
suite here is run). **There is no graphics card, no drawing program and no
model anywhere in it, and there must not be.** Every route is exercised with a
**stub runtime** put in the module's own registry (`register_runtime`), so the
suite proves the routes, the storage, the words and the switch - and proves
**nothing** about whether ComfyUI or stable-diffusion.cpp draws a good picture.
That split is written into the suite's own docstring rather than implied.

What it covers: the route with a stub (200, where it went, how long it took);
the storage round-trip (write, read back, the sidecar intact - prompt, seed,
model and settings all survive); the file name and its slug; **a collision** -
the same prompt in the same second makes two files and overwrites neither; the
"runtime not installed" sentence; the "configured but not answering" sentence;
the mode being **off by default** and off being refused in words that name the
switch; the listing route (newest first, the folder and its size, a lost
sidecar handled); the picture itself as bytes and a refusal for anything that
is not one of our ids; `install()` and its origin/token refusals; and that no
other backend module imports this one.

**The swap (2026-10-25) is covered with the card module stood in for:** the
plan finds A/B/C and the price from a real `handshake_plan` call against a
stand-in card module (A with the chat on the card needs the swap, C never
does, B says it is not wired, a card with no chat needs nothing, a backend
without the card module plans nothing); the first request answers 409 with
`needs: "free_card"` and draws nothing; the confirmed request sets the chat
aside **before** the draw, asks ComfyUI to free its models, warms the chat
back and records the measurement **after** it, and reports both seconds; a
refused draw still warms the chat back; a chat that will not step aside stops
the draw with nothing written; **a phone's first request is the same 409 and
moves nothing, and a phone may confirm the swap and gets the normal success
shape** (owner decision 2026-10-24); **a second confirm while a draw is running
is one plain sentence (`needs: "drawing"`), starts no second draw and leaves a
free lock behind**; the settings route still refuses the phone (`403
pc_only`); and source pins hold the ten-minute wait, the `/free` call, the
empty-bodied `/free` answer, the `finally` warm-back, the phone-open make route
and the one-at-a-time guard.

**Measured on this PC's real card (native proof of this very code, four real
Chroma1-HD draws on the RTX 2060 through ComfyUI 0.39.0, 1152x1152 at 26 steps,
guidance 3.8, each with the everyday chat on the card first):**

- **2026-10-24, the first real draw** (V1): the 409 question, the swap, the draw
  and the warm-back all real; wall 420.8 s, draw 383.6 s, PNG 2,008,307 bytes
  with its sidecar; the chat stepped aside in 6.4 s and was back after another
  30.9 s - but **1.36 GB spilled**, because the `/free` step was not waited for.
- **2026-10-25, the empty-answer finding:** a second draw (PNG 1,409,863 bytes,
  draw 379.0 s) proved the spill's cause was not a slow `/free` - it answers
  HTTP 200 with a **0-byte body**, which the old client parsed as JSON and gave
  up on in 0.0 s. The wait now accepts that empty answer and polls
  `/system_stats`.
- **2026-10-25, the released card proven** (run3, desktop confirm): PNG
  2,087,566 bytes, draw 381.0 s, wall 405.8 s; `models_freed: true` (ComfyUI
  held 64 MB when the poll first looked), the chat stepped aside in 0.5 s and
  came back **WHOLE - `size_vram == size`, spill 0** - after another 23.6 s.
- **2026-10-25, the phone's confirm proven** (run4): the same route served over
  a real local HTTP server built with this module's own `install()` wrapper,
  **both requests carrying `X-Jarvis-Client: phone`**; the first answered 409
  and moved nothing; the confirm drew a PNG of **1,721,489 bytes** in **382.0**
  s (wall 500.1 s), `models_freed: true`, and the chat came back whole (spill 0)
  117.1 s after stepping aside. That is the request the Android app will send.

The draw's own peak stayed on the 12 GB card (sampled: `torch_vram_total` up to
11.04 GB, card used up to 10,662 MiB; afterwards the card held the everyday chat
alone again). The warm-back varies - 20 to 117 s across these draws - which is
why the confirm is one long request with a timeout bound, not a quick call.

**What is honestly NOT proved by that suite:** that ComfyUI draws a real
picture here (that needs the real card and program - a stub proves the code
path, never the picture), that the warm-back really reloads the owner's model
in a measured number of seconds, and the desktop panel's confirm flow. The first
two are now measured on this PC (the paragraphs above); the panel's flow is
tested as pure logic (`jarvis-desktop/tests/pictures.mjs`) and its real-window
look is not reviewed. The suite's own docstring says all of this out loud.

Desktop: the Rust reading functions are plain functions of `(status, body)` and
are tested without a Tauri app or a network
(`jarvis-desktop/tests/pictures.mjs`). Phone:
`jarvis-client/app/src/test/java/com/jarvis/client/PicturesTest.kt`.

`tools/check_parity.py` carries all three routes.

## 130. Changing a setting by asking, in any words: the `change_setting` tool (added 2026-10-14)

**The defect this closes.** "Jarvis can change all settings if I ask" was false. A
settings request reached a setting only when the sentence fitted the fixed phrase
grammar in `jarvis_quick.py`, which runs BEFORE the model on every `/api/chat` turn. A
sentence that missed it was answered by the model, and the model had no settings tool at
all and was never told it could not change anything - so the failure did not look like a
refusal, it looked like success (`.dsh-scratch/settings-reachability-audit.md`). #360
made the refusal honest and reached eight more switches; this is the other half.

**What it is.** One tool, `change_setting`, with two arguments: `setting` (the owner's
own words for the setting - any wording; the model does the matching, not a fixed phrase)
and `value`. The value is `"on"` or `"off"` for an on/off switch, and one of the
setting's OWN values for a setting whose value is a name (the voice speed, the
personality, the captcha hand-off and so on). Since 2026-10-26 the value is a free
string rather than the old two-word enum, because the enum made every named-choice
setting impossible for the tool to change while the phrase grammar could change it.

It reaches three kinds of setting, and nothing else:

- every switch in `jarvis_settings_registry.BOOL_SETTINGS` - **31** of them;
- every setting in `jarvis_settings_registry.CHOICE_SETTINGS` - **6** of them, whose
  value is one of that setting's own names;
- the two real routes that are not table rows at all, because the contract pins those
  table keys: the PC's "hey Jarvis" wake word (`jarvis_speech.set_wake_enabled`) and
  which browser Jarvis uses (`jarvis_browser_engine.handle_post`). Neither was
  reachable by the tool before 2026-10-26 even though both are real Settings controls.

**Which tree / which tier.** It is deliberately NOT put to `jarvis_gate.check()` in
`jarvis_agent._one_call`, for the same reason `SCHEDULE_TOOLS` and `web_search` are not:
its gate already exists, and it is better placed. Every setting's rule lives in ONE
function - a switch's `BoolSetting.set`, a named choice's own setter, the wake word's
`set_wake_enabled` or the browser's `handle_post` - and that function is what a spoken
sentence runs. `change_setting` CALLS THAT SAME FUNCTION. So:

| on/off setting | ON | OFF |
|---|---|---|
| background learning, the sensitive-topics switch, lights without asking, web search, the watch switch, the phone-notification switch, picture mode, the headless browser, senders in the briefing, the big coder, the better voice | one card | at once |
| asking before every web search (the REVERSED pair) | at once | one card |
| the prompt coach, making pictures, the six PC-notification switches, humour, voice-follows-the-face | at once | at once |
| the PC's "hey Jarvis" wake word (`jarvis_speech.set_wake_enabled`) | one card | at once |

The six settings whose value is a name go through their own setters, so the card is
their own too - and for two of them only ONE value asks, because that value loosens
something:

| named choice | the value that asks | the value that applies at once |
|---|---|---|
| the captcha hand-off (`jarvis_handoff_mode.request`) | "keep offering it" - one card, and the card is PC-only | "stop early" |
| the captcha window (`jarvis_handoff_front.request`) | "bring it to the front" - one card, PC-only | "leave it where it is" |
| the focus preset (`jarvis_presets.apply_from_body`) | every apply raises its one `switch_model` card | - |
| the voice speed, the built-in voice, the personality | none - there is no card either way | every value |

Which browser Jarvis uses (`auto`, `visible` or `headless`) is applied at once with NO
card either way: it picks the engine that does the work and never widens what Jarvis may
reach (both engines go through the same gate and the same card).

Because the card is the setting's OWN, it carries that setting's own risk text, its own
Windows Hello rule and its own PC rule: no second card is ever raised for one change, and
no generic action name has to stand in for 31 different risk texts. The tool's own name
maps to `change_own_config` in `jarvis_gate._TOOL_ACTIONS` - a row added on 2026-10-14 by
`backend/gate-entries.patch` (with its previous version recorded in
`backend/patch-history/`), because `test_agent.py` requires every tool's lookup name to be
a KEY of that table, and the action name alone is not one. That action already carries the
tier (`[autonomy.tiers]`, `ask`) and the card wording ("change one of its settings") that
the lights, briefing-senders and big-coder switches use, so no new tier and no new card
words are invented. `jarvis_reach`'s own row for the tool says in words that what asks
depends on the setting.

**What it refuses.** A name it cannot resolve against the table is answered in words
(`jarvis_settings_registry.cannot_change_setting_words`), listing what CAN be changed:
nothing is changed and NO card is raised, because a card for something that cannot
happen is a lie in card form. It never guesses - changing a switch the owner did not name
is worse than changing nothing. A switch that is on the Settings page but has no route at
all (`NOT_BY_ASKING`) gets a sentence naming the screen and the row. That page-only
refusal is decided FIRST, and on filler-tolerant words: "turn off the windows hello for
memory lists and chat history setting" names a page-only row, so it gets that sentence -
it is never read as `chat_history`, which those same words contain. The phrase grammar
and the "that setting is not available" correction run the same guard, so all three
entrances agree and none of them changes anything.

**Stricter than the spoken path, in one place.** A turn shaped by outside text - a
reading tool ran in THAT turn, the newest message is not the owner's own words, the app
sent text of its own, or planted instructions were seen - changes nothing at all. The
spoken path has no such check; this does. It is deliberately NOT refused on the
conversation's own `tainted` flag alone: that flag is conversation-wide and sticky, so
refusing on it would mean a setting could not be changed by asking for the rest of any
chat in which Jarvis had once read an email or a page - while the spoken path changes a
setting in exactly that chat with no check at all. Both halves are pinned by
`backend/test_settings_tool.py`.

**Honesty, tied to what already exists.** A change still waiting on its card is recorded
as NOT run, so it cannot back an "I have done it" claim
(`jarvis_claims.action_succeeded`): the answer gets the "Nothing was actually done" line
instead of standing as a claim. The model is handed the setter's own sentence, so it
cannot report "done" while a card is waiting.

**A defect found and fixed in the same pass.** `jarvis_settings_registry.set_humor`
called `jarvis_manner.handle_post(...)`, and `jarvis_manner.py` has only `handle_get` and
`handle_set`. So "turn on humour", added by #360, raised AttributeError and could not
work, while the Settings page's own route (`POST /api/manner`) went through `handle_set`
and did. `backend/test_settings_tool.py` now walks every setter's own imports with `ast`
and fails on any module attribute that does not exist.

**What a second reader changed (2026-10-14).** Two weak spots were found in the first
version of this work, and both are fixed with regression cases:

* The tolerant word matcher accepted a request whose every word fitted INSIDE a longer
  alias name, so bare category nouns resolved to switches that had nothing to do with
  them: "second graphics card" reached `better_voice`, "pc sounds" reached
  `pc_alarm_sounds`, "screen mode" reached `screen_picture`, "the big model" reached
  `big_coder`. Every one of those switches applies with NO card, so the owner's own words
  would have flipped a switch they never named - the one outcome the matcher exists to
  prevent. It now runs in ONE direction only: the request must CONTAIN a whole alias's
  words, so a restatement like "stop showing me notifications on my watch" still reaches
  `watch notifications` while a phrase that names no single setting is refused. Eleven of
  the wrong matches are kept as regression cases in `backend/test_settings_tool.py`.
* A change still waiting on its card emitted a `tool_finished` step event, and BOTH apps
  draw that as "<tool> done" (`jarvis-desktop/src/step-words.js`,
  `jarvis-client/.../net/Steps.kt`). The owner would have read "change_setting done" while
  the card was still up and nothing had changed - the looks-like-success failure this
  feature exists to end. No step event is emitted for a waiting change now; the card and
  the answer carry it, exactly as on the spoken path.

**Where it lives.** `jarvis_agent.py` (`SETTINGS_TOOL`, `_settings_call`, the branch in
`_one_call`, `_PLAN_EXCLUDED_STEPS` so a plan can never name it), `jarvis_settings_registry.py`
(`find_bool_setting_words`, `cannot_change_setting_words`), `jarvis_reach.py` (its plain
name). **It ships ON**, by the owner's decision of 2026-10-14 ("yes turn it on for my
pc. it should also be enabled by default") - the second tool after `web_search` to be
switched on out of the box, and `[tools].enabled` in `jarvis-framework.toml` says so.
(Turning it back off is dropping that one name from that list.) Its description is 295
tokens, so it has its own `more_tools` group rather than a place in the core. **The text
of that description was rewritten on 2026-10-14**, from 285 tokens to 295, after the field
test found the model would not call the tool: the old text read as a note ABOUT the tool
(third person, bare setting names as its examples, and "say so plainly" offering an answer
in words as a fine outcome), and the model answered all four of the owner's own requests
about `humour` in words with no call at all. The measurement, the control that proves the
plumbing was never the problem, and the exact sentences are in
`_settings_tool_text`'s own docstring in `jarvis_agent.py`. **Nothing else about the tool
changed**: no tier, no card, no setter, no route.

Desktop and phone: **both, with nothing app-specific** - the tool is reached through the
same `/api/chat` turn both apps already use, so `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 needs no entry.
`tools/check_parity.py` is clean, and the new tool is carried in `features.json` (all
three copies) as "Change a setting by asking, in any words".

**Tests.** `backend/test_settings_tool.py` is the suite: both entrances share one setter,
a pending change is not a done claim, an unknown name changes nothing and raises no card,
outside text stops it, and the `ast` check that every setter calls a function that
exists. `backend/test_tool_text.py`, `test_short_tool_list.py`,
`test_agent_retirement_wiring.py`, `test_reach.py`, `test_private_aloud.py` and
`test_tool_eval.py` carry the new tool in their own lists and generated fixtures.

### Explaining a feature: the `feature_guide` tool and the fixed phrases (added 2026-10-20)

**Why it exists (the 2026-10-19/20 field test).** Chat could change 52 settings by
fixed phrases, but no chat path could EXPLAIN a feature: "how do I turn on the prompt
coach?" was answered thinly by the model (never saying what the coach does or where it
lives), and "is the prompt coach on right now?" was answered "I don't know its current
state directly". The exact answers were already written down - `features/features.json`,
the 141 rows both apps' Features pages draw - and nothing read them.

**One read-only tool, `feature_guide`** (`jarvis_feature_guide.py`; the tool in
`jarvis_agent.py`). Its one argument is `feature`, in the owner's words (or a group
name, or `""` to list the groups). It returns the row's OWN facts - `what`, `where`
(where to switch it on), `asks` (whether a card is needed), `limit`, `surface` (which
apps have it), `surface_reason` (why the other app has none, for a one-sided row),
`aliases` (the owner's other names for it) and `covers` (the settings places it names) -
plus, for a switchable feature, whether its switch is **on or off right now**, read from
the module that owns that switch through the SAME `jarvis_settings_registry.BoolSetting`
entries `change_setting` writes (`jarvis_feature_guide.STATE_READERS`). Its `words`
sentence now also says how to use or change the feature, from the same five labels and
switch table. It changes nothing, so it is decided under the gate's own read-only
`skill_list` action (tier `auto`, **no card**) - no new gate action, no tier line, no
patch. A switch a module cannot answer is reported as "I could not read it", never as
off. An unknown or ambiguous name is said plainly and the real groups are offered;
nothing is guessed.

**The catalogue is a generated module.** `features/features.json` lives in this
repository and is NOT copied to the PC's backend folder, so the guide ships its rows as
`jarvis_feature_catalogue.py`, written by `tools/gen_feature_guide_catalogue.py` from the
same file. `backend/test_feature_guide.py` runs that tool's `--check`, so a changed list
that was not regenerated fails a suite rather than drifting from what the apps show.

**"Write like me" is a new row here (added 2026-10-20).** The list's 138th row says what
it does, where it lives (Settings, How Jarvis talks), that adding your own writing
samples needs no card and Forget asks "are you sure?" first, and the limit: names, dates,
amounts, links and numbers are stripped to `[name]`, `[date]`, `[amount]` before a sample
is kept, and using the style marks the turn private (`style_exemplars`), so it stays on
this PC's own model and never goes to a cloud service. The fixed-phrase grammar also
learned "how do I train/teach you to <feature>" (2026-10-20), answered with that
feature's own facts; "how do I train my dog to sit" still falls to the model. The desktop
training card (`jarvis-desktop/src/manner.js`, `settings.html`) and the phone's Settings
screen are the **next UI slice**: this change adds the row, the generated catalogue and
the two phrases, and neither app's UI changes in this PR.

**Nine questions now, no model at all** (`jarvis_quick.py`, so they work with any model, a
slow one, or none). Until 2026-10-26 only three were wired; the owner's field test asked
for Jarvis to be able to talk about *any* feature of the project, in detail, so the
grammar learned the rest of the questions a person actually asks:

| the owner's question | intent | what the answer carries |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "what is <feature>" / "what does it do" / "tell me about" / "explain" | `feature_explain` | name, what it does, status, Settings place, where, whether it asks first, the honest limit, which apps have it, its current switch state, and how to use or change it |
| "how do I use <feature>" / "how does it work" | `feature_explain` | the same, because using it is the row's own `where` + its real example sentence |
| "where is <feature>" / "where do I find" / "where do I change" | `feature_explain` | the same `where` line, plus the phone's own copy of the list |
| "how do I turn on/off <feature>" / "enable/disable" / "how to" / "where do I" | `feature_howto` | the row's `where` and `asks`, the exact phrase that would change the ONE switch, and the current state |
| "can I change <feature>" / "how do I change" / "is it adjustable" | `feature_change` (new) | which of the five owner-facing kinds it is, whether it has one switch, several or none, and the exact phrase or Settings place - **changing nothing** |
| "make <switch> off" / "set <switch> to off" / "I want <switch> off" / "<switch> should be off" / "make sure it is off" | `feature_change_apply` (new, 2026-10-27) | ONE setting changed through its OWN setter, for the 27 switches on the allow-list: a card is the setter's own, and the reply names the old and the new value only after a re-read |
| "change <switch>" / "toggle <switch>" (no state said) | `feature_change_ask` (new, 2026-10-27) | ONE question back ("Do you want prompt coach on or off?"), changing nothing and raising no card |
| a password, a key, a token, deep config, or an ask that cannot be undone | `feature_change_refused` (new, 2026-10-27) | one plain sentence and nothing changed |
| "how/where do I change <a setting's own name>" / "tell me about <a setting>" | `setting_explain` (new, 2026-10-26) | when NO feature title or alias matched: the settings registry's own name, its real Settings card and one real example phrase - or the page-only refusal. No model turn, no card, nothing changed |
| "is <feature> on?" / "off" / "enabled" / "right now" / "what is the state of" | `feature_state` | the switch's real value, read from the module that owns it, or "I could not read it" |
| "what features do you have?" / "list the features" | `features_list` | the 9 groups with real counts |
| a group's name | `features_group` | that group's rows |
| "what can you do?" / "what are you capable of?" / "what are you able to do?" | `sayable_help` | unchanged: the fixed list of real sentences (`jarvis_sayable.py`) |

Every explain answer is assembled by one renderer (`jarvis_feature_guide.explain_words`), so a
model turn and a fixed phrase cannot say different things. "Can I change it?" is read-only:
it is in `jarvis_quick.READ_ONLY_INTENTS`, so "cancel that" never takes back something it
did not do, and the test suite proves no `BoolSetting.set` runs for any of the 141 rows.

**And a setting can now be CHANGED by asking, not only explained (2026-10-27).** The
plainest sentences - "make the prompt coach off", "set web search to off", "I want the
prompt coach off", "the prompt coach should be off", "make sure it is off" - matched
nothing and reached the model, which has no settings tool. They now resolve against the
real registry, but only for the switches in `jarvis_quick.CHANGE_BY_ASKING` (27 of the 31
`BoolSetting` rows; the allow-list is derived by three rules stated in its own comment).
The write is the SAME `BoolSetting.set` the Settings switch, the HUD route and "turn
on/off <name>" already call, so the card, the tier, the PC-only refusal and the wording are
the setting's own - this lane decides none of them and contains no gate call. What the
answer claims is bounded by what it read: `feature_change_apply` pre-reads the value (and
refuses to write when it cannot be read), says "already on/off" with zero setter calls when
the value is already right, passes the module's own waiting sentence through when its card
is up, and after an immediate apply RE-READS the value and states the old and the new one -
or says plainly that the value did not move. The three switches whose value cannot be read
today (`second_card_*`) and the one whose card is PC-only (`lights_without_card`) are
deliberately outside the list: they keep `feature_change`'s own explanation, word for word,
and are never written from chat. `backend/test_ask_to_change.py` proves all of it,
including a real end-to-end change in a throwaway config folder.

**A SETTINGS NAME ANSWERS TOO (2026-10-26, ruling Q6 Step A).** Five names the owner uses are
not catalogue titles: `personality`, `voice speed` and `focus preset` are
`jarvis_settings_registry.CHOICE_SETTINGS` rows, and `theme` / `hud layout` are desktop-only
controls inside the Appearance and "The big HUD window" Settings cards. "how do i change the
personality?" therefore missed every fixed phrase and reached the local model (~2 s), which
has no settings tool. When no feature title or alias matches, the same sentence is now tried
against the registry's own names and answered on the same fast path (`setting_explain`): the
`CHOICE_SETTINGS` three name their real card and one real `set ... to ...` phrase; the two
desktop-only areas name their card and the `open ... settings` phrase and say plainly that
they cannot be changed by asking. A page-only row still refuses FIRST, including hyphen,
slash and filler forms and a sentence naming two of them - a page-only name is never a
licence to change a switch whose words the sentence happens to contain. An unknown name
still falls through to the model. `backend/test_setting_alias_phrasing.py` proves each of
these, including that every example phrase the answer offers really routes.

**The list learned two fields (2026-10-26).** `features/features.json` rows may carry
`aliases` - the owner's other names for ONE feature, e.g. "customer support" for the row
titled "Deal with customer support for me" (30 rows carry 55 aliases). They are matched
EXACTLY, like the id and the title, so they widen what a person can say without widening
what counts as a guess. Every one-sided row also carries `surface_reason`: 27 of 27 now do
(the 8 `phone` ones already did; the 19 `desktop` ones were written on 2026-10-26 from the
row's own `limit`/`where` or from `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8), so the answer can say *why*
the phone has none instead of only that it does. `tools/check_feature_list.py`'s rule 5 now
demands the sentence in both directions, and `tools/gen_feature_guide_catalogue.py` carries
both fields into `jarvis_feature_catalogue.py` (an unknown row key is still refused, so a
new field has to be looked at by a person).

**Two names that carry "Jarvis" for real.** `normalise()` strips "jarvis" and "for me" from
the end of a sentence because they are usually the address, and four rows are NAMED with
those words ("Floating Jarvis", "How Jarvis talks", "Starting Jarvis for you", "What Jarvis
can reach") - so each fell to the model. The grammar now tries the tidied sentence and,
only if that finds nothing, the same patterns once more on the message with just a leading
"Jarvis," removed; the same exact-name gate applies, so this adds reach for real names and
no guessing. The same fix stopped `_feature_target` from eating a feature's own trailing
"options" ("Animal options" had become "animal"), and `_feature_switch_intent` now tries the
exact name BEFORE stripping context words, which is what had silently emptied the typed
phrase of those four rows in `control_matrix()` (4 of 140 before, 0 after).

**The gate is exact (hardened 2026-10-20 after Gemini's review, §11.8.3):** without the
words "Jarvis", "here" or "my settings" in the message, the subject after "what is [the]
..." / "is [the] ... on" must be EXACTLY a feature name (its id, title or an alias - case,
punctuation and a leading article ignored) - no loose substring. So "what is a focus
session in psychology?", "how do I turn on dark mode in Chrome?", "where is my file
manager?", "how do I use a chainsaw?" and "is my oven on?" are the model's, while "where is
the prompt coach" answers with the feature; "I do not have that one" needs an explicit
"Jarvis"/"here"/"my settings" AND the word feature/option, so a general question never
gets it. One deliberate exception is named in the tests: "what is the morning briefing?"
and "is the morning briefing on?" are the briefing's own read/setup answers
(`briefing_now`/`briefing_list`), which have owned those two sentences since 2026-09-28;
the feature is explained by the other seven questions. `backend/test_feature_guide.py` pins
the exact matcher (`jarvis_feature_guide.find_exact`), the review questions, the positive
controls and the named exception. **Changing** by these words is the existing path: "turn on
<feature>" resolves a feature to the ONE switch it names and calls that setting's own
`BoolSetting.set`, so the card rules are unchanged; a feature naming several switches
(Custom voices) changes nothing and says which ones; the answer is the setter's own
outcome, never a "Done" when nothing happened.

**Both apps, nothing app-specific:** the fixed phrases and the tool are reached through
the same `/api/chat` turn both apps already use, so `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 needs no
entry and `tools/check_parity.py` is clean. It **ships ON** in `[tools].enabled` (the
owner's decision of 2026-10-19/20); on an existing install the model tool is offered once
`"feature_guide"` is in the `[tools].enabled` list of `jarvis-framework.toml` (or the
inherited `config.toml`, if the settings file names no `[tools]` section) - the fixed
phrases need no config at all.

**Tests.** `backend/test_feature_guide.py` (1707 checks, measured 2026-10-26): all 141 rows
found with facts equal to the JSON; every switch has a state reader and the answers never
claim a state they did not read; unknown/ambiguous honesty; the fixed phrases and their near
misses; switching through the real setter with its real words; the tool's 300-token text,
`auto`-tier no-card turn, and exact facts fed to the model. The 2026-10-26 section asks every
one of the 141 rows all nine questions through its title, id AND aliases, and requires the
answer that question needs (the full facts for explain/use/where, where + card + exact phrase
for how-to, status + how for change, the real state for state); "can I change" is proved to
run no setter for any row; every alias is proved to name only its own row; every one-sided
answer is proved to carry its row's reason; the general questions ("how do I use a chainsaw",
"where is my file manager", "where did I put my passport", "can I change my password in
Chrome") are pinned as NOT feature answers; and the matrix build is proved to keep every
row's three typed phrases. `test_tool_text.py`,
`test_short_tool_list.py`, `test_reach.py` and `tools/tool_eval/jarvis_tools.json` carry
the tool; `test_settings_tool.py`, `test_settings_registry.py`, `test_settings_help.py`
and `test_quick_wins.py` are unchanged and green.
