  `/api/skills/suggestions`, exactly as a routine is offered as a card today.
  **Rule 4 is the reason for the shape**: a skill that scheduled itself would be
  acting unattended. The module imports no scheduler and calls nothing that
  could register a job - `backend/test_skill_hub.py` asserts both against the
  source with `ast`, not against the prose.

### 138.7 The permission model, and what this section does not add

**Nothing here approves anything and nothing here adds a route that decides
anything.** The one new route is a read; it is a `GET`, it raises no card, and
the gate's own table already tiers `skill_list`, `skill_load` and `skill_scan` as
`auto` (`jarvis_gate.py:850`). The only writer of SKILL CONTENT in the whole
module is still `write_skill()`, through `POST /api/skills/learn` (§135.3), one
`modify_own_code` card, before the file is written. The lock file gained two
writers on 2026-11-09 - `write_lock()` from the install path and
`forget_lock()` from `uninstall()` - both called from `jarvis_skills.py`;
neither is a permission, neither writes a skill file, and both are no-ops when
the hub is not beside the base.

`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 carries the row for the app surfaces: the lock, the
conventions and the suggestions are readable by either app and **no app calls
them yet**. `tools/check_parity.py` carries the lock read and the suggestions in
`BACKEND_ONLY` (2026-10-28), with that reason in each entry, so the gap is named.

**Related, and NOT a route:** `backend/jarvis_tool_schema.py` was added in the
same work item and serves no route at all. It decides whether a JSON Schema may
be sent as Ollama's `format`, refuses the keywords the live grammar was measured
not to express, and guards the set of keywords a tool's own schema may use
against the ones `jarvis_agent.check_call()` actually validates. **Since
2026-10-18 it IS called:** `jarvis_agent.py` imports it on both sides of a tool
call - `_schemas_for()` sends a tool's parameters only after
`sanitise_schema()` (default REFUSE) and `guard_tool_schemas()` pass, and
`check_call()` validates the parsed arguments against the SAME returned schema
before `prepare()` or the gate. A tool whose shape cannot pass either check is
left out of the request (never sent weakened) and a call to it gets one plain
refusal that names it and says nothing ran; a backend without the module keeps
today's behaviour. The `format`-on-a-tool-call design its docstring warns about
is unchanged and still not used - what is wired is the schema OF a tool, not a
schema in `format`.

## 139. Self-improvement diagnostics: two read-only GETs, and everything they cannot do (added 2026-10-17)

Two modules this repository already ships - `backend/jarvis_self_improve.py`
(file:line-cited diagnosis of Jarvis's own source) and
`backend/jarvis_ollama_contract.py` (the three-outcome check that Ollama is
telling Jarvis the truth about the local model) - had no caller an owner could
reach. This section is the wiring: a drop-in folder,
`plugins/ready/self-improve/`, whose `plugin.json` names the module and whose
`install()` the loader calls. **No patch is replaced, no `$SHIPPED` entry is
added (both modules were already shipped), and nothing in `jarvis_hud.py`
changes.**

The two routes are answered by `jarvis_self_improve.install()`, behind the
server's own origin and token checks like every other route. **Only `do_GET` is
wrapped.** `do_POST` is never touched, so a read cannot be reached by POST, and
there is no route for `draft()` at all - applying a change is Phase 5 of the
self-improvement design and is not here.

### 139.1 `GET /api/self-improve/diagnose?q=<question>`

Read the program's own text files, ask the LOCAL model which of the matching
lines answers the question, and quote the lines that were cited. A citation is
re-read from the file at the moment it is reported, so the quote beside
`file:line` is the line that is really there.

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "read_only": true,
  "route": "diagnose",
  "question": "where is the taint latch written",
  "found": true,
  "answer": "the explanation, in the model's words, over those lines",
  "citations": [
    {"path": "backend/jarvis_gate.py", "line": 1772,
     "where": "backend/jarvis_gate.py:1772", "quote": "def latch_taint(...)"}
  ],
  "why": "",
  "tainted": false,
  "latched": false,
  "model": "qwen3.5:9b",
  "words": "the same answer and citations as one plain block of text"
}
```

- **`ok` is "the route answered". `found` is "this PC established it".** They
  are different questions and are reported separately. `found: false` comes
  back with `why` saying what happened in plain words (no line mentions the
  question, the scrubber is missing, the local model could not be asked, the
  model named no line). It always carries NO citation - a "could not establish
  it" must never look like an answer with a `file:line` attached.
- **Refusals:**
  - `400` and `{"ok": false, "error": "question is empty", ...}` when `q` is
    missing or only spaces;
  - `400` and `"question is too long"` when it is over **500 characters**.
    Nothing is searched and no model is asked for either refusal.
- **`tainted` / `latched`** are the module's own private-material latch: a
  question that touches it, or a line read from a module that holds it, marks
  this conversation local-only via `jarvis_gate.latch_taint`. No text about
  the private material is added to the answer by this route.
- **What is deliberately NOT returned:** `diagnose()`'s raw `evidence` lines.
  Those lines are never scrubbed, so returning them would be more than the
  module's own display path allows. Citation quotes are scrubbed by the route
  before they are serialised; if the scrubber is missing the quote is withheld
  and says so.
- **It is a synchronous read.** The HTTP request stays open while the local
  model answers. `_run` stops waiting after 120 seconds, and the diagnosis then
  comes back as "could not establish it". It is owner-initiated on the PC - no
  background job, no approval card, no file written.
- An internal exception is `503` with
  `{"ok": false, "error": "<exception type>", "message": "plain words, nothing changed"}` -
  never a traceback.

### 139.2 `GET /api/self-improve/contract?model=<name>`

One READ-ONLY `POST` to the local Ollama's `/api/show`, which reads the model's
own metadata and loads nothing. The verdict is the contract module's three
outcomes; `null` is its honest fourth state and is never a pass.

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "read_only": true,
  "route": "contract",
  "model": "qwen3.5:9b",
  "url": "http://127.0.0.1:11434",
  "verdict": "understood",
  "usable": true,
  "said": ["completion", "tools", "vision", "thinking"],
  "unknown": [],
  "missing": [],
  "note": "Ollama says this model can do: ... Jarvis knows every one of those names.",
  "when": "self-improve route",
  "words": "qwen3.5:9b: <the same sentence>"
}
```

- `verdict` is `"understood"`, `"unknown_capabilities"` (Ollama lists a name
  Jarvis has never heard of - news, not an error), `"missing_expected"` (the
  model plainly has a capability that Ollama's list omits, so Jarvis would
  under-use it), or **`null`** when Ollama sent no usable capability list.
- **`null` is not a pass.** `usable` is then `false` and `note` says "NOT a
  pass" in words. `said` is `null` too, not an empty list.
- A missing `model=` uses the module's own default: `JARVIS_MODEL` if that
  environment variable names one, otherwise `qwen3.5:9b` - the same model a
  diagnosis would ask.
- **It cannot be pointed at another machine.** The route passes the probe the
  `jarvis_self_improve` loopback guard, so an `OLLAMA_HOST` naming a host that
  is not `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `localhost` or `0.0.0.0` is not used; the probe
  falls back to loopback.
- `503` when `jarvis_ollama_contract.py` is not in the backend at all; nothing
  was changed.

### 139.3 App surface: PC-only in this slice, said plainly

**Neither app calls either route, and this slice adds no desktop or Android
face.** That is deliberate: the wiring queue asked for a diagnostic the owner
can query, not a product button - and a button that shows source snippets needs
its own redaction/placement design first. **Both routes are this PC's own**: a request from another device
(a phone on the same private network, say) is refused `403` with one plain
sentence by `jarvis_owner_check.from_this_pc`, BEFORE any file is read - the
same rule the guardian and selection routes use, so a paired phone's token
cannot use them either. `tools/check_parity.py` carries both in `BACKEND_ONLY`
(2026-10-28), with this PC-only decision in each reason, so the gap is named
rather than left to read as a clean pass. No app menu, no Brain read section, and no
`features/features.json` entry are added.

`docs/CLAIMS.tsv` gets no row for this: it is a read-only exposure of two
modules whose own claims are already registered, and adding a row would force
an ABOUT recount against every open PR.

### 139.4 The draft boundary reads a path the way Windows does (added 2026-10-20)

`refusal_reason()` compares a diff target by its last path component,
lower-cased and with `/` and `\` treated the same, so a draft naming
`backend\JARVIS_GATE.py`, `Backend/Jarvis_Gate.py` or
`backend/jarvis-backend\JARVIS_GATE.py` is refused exactly as
`backend/jarvis_gate.py` is (`backend/test_self_improve.py`, "a case or
backslash cannot smuggle a protected file"). The `PROTECTED` and
`TIER_TABLE_NAMES` lists are still the two lists; only the comparison stopped
depending on spelling or platform.

## 140. The file guardian's history: what changed, and what did this file look like before (LM-2A, added 2026-10-18)

Jarvis keeps a copy of the bytes of a file BEFORE it overwrites it (the file guardian, `backend/jarvis_file_guardian.py`, JARVIS-API-adjacent design in its own docstring). Until now that store was write-only from the owner's point of view. Two **read-only** routes put it on screen; the restore route is deliberately NOT part of this slice.

### 140.1 `GET /api/guardian/snapshots?limit=<n>`

The owner's snapshot index, newest first, one bounded page. `limit` is optional: **50 by default, 1 to 200 at most** - a request outside that range is refused (`400`, `why: "bad_limit"`) rather than quietly clamped. The answer:

```
{"ok": true, "refused": false, "why": "", "count": <this page>, "total": <all rows>,
 "limit": <n>, "more": <total > this page>,
 "snapshots": [{"path": "<full path>", "label": "<file name, for the drawer>",
                "before_sha256": "<saved version>", "size": <bytes>,
                "timestamp": <epoch>, "when": "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM",
                "reason": "<why the write happened, bounded>",
                "receipt_id": "<the existing jarvis_receipts row, opaque>"}],
 "usage": {"blob_bytes", "blobs", "quota_bytes", "pinned", "over_quota", "words"},
 "words": "<what this page is>"}
```

It reads the journal only. It never opens a saved copy, never reads a file, and carries no file contents - the fields above are what the module already stores, bounded (path 4,096 chars, reason 200, receipt id 120). A row with no path or no sha256 is skipped rather than guessed at. An empty store answers `count: 0` with a sentence, not an error.

### 140.2 `GET /api/guardian/diff?path=<file>&sha_before=<sha256>`

The bounded unified diff the module already works out: `jarvis_file_guardian.diff_versions(path, sha_before)`'s answer, passed back **unchanged** - `{"ok", "refused", "path", "before_sha256", "after_sha256", "diff", "truncated", "binary", "same", "words"}`. The module is the authority on everything: the path must be inside a folder the owner already allows Jarvis to change, the sha must be a saved version, the diff is cut at `MAX_DIFF_BYTES` (64 KiB) and says so (`truncated`), a binary pair answers `binary: true`, an unchanged file answers `same: true`, and a version no longer in the store is refused in plain words. The route itself only refuses a missing pair (`400`, `why: "bad_request"`) or one longer than a path/sha can be. It never reads a file outside the store's allowed folders.

### 140.3 Who may ask, and the one gap

Both routes are **this PC's own**. A request from another device (a phone on the same private network, say) is refused with `403` and `why: "not_this_pc"` by `jarvis_owner_check.from_this_pc` - BEFORE the guardian module is imported or anything is read. The desktop apps are the intent: the drawer belongs where the files are, and the phone has no PC files to show. A missing or older `jarvis_file_guardian.py` answers `501` in the same refusal shape with the "run apply-patches.ps1" sentence.

**The gap, said plainly rather than papered over:** the backend cannot see App lock or "Hide memory lists and chat history" by itself - both are desktop-side state that never reaches the backend process. Since 2026-10-20 (Q1) both read routes DO accept the desktop's own report, `?app_locked=1` / `?hide_memory_lists=1`, and answer the honest marker with an empty page/diff without reading the journal or working out the difference: `{"ok": false, "withheld": true, "why": "Hidden while App lock is on." (or the hidden-lists sentence), "snapshots": [] (or "path": "", "diff": ""), ...}`. Those flags can only ADD withholding - `app_locked=0`, an unknown spelling and a `force_unlock=1` change nothing, and `jarvis_private_view`'s trusted in-process state cannot be cleared by a request. **The remaining gap: the live HUD does not pass the state yet**, so until it does the desktop drawer that will use these routes **must** still hide while App lock is on or those lists are hidden, exactly as its other private surfaces do. The two routes above never write and raise no card.

### 140.4 `POST /api/guardian/restore` - putting a version back, on a person's yes (LM-2B, 2026-10-18)

The one route in this slice that **writes**, and it cannot be reached without the one permission model. Body: `{"path": "<file>", "sha_before": "<saved version's sha256>"}` (POST only - there is no GET form, and a GET of this path is not answered by the history routes at all).

What happens, in this order, all inside `jarvis_file_guardian.restore_version()`:

1. the module's own path rules run FIRST - a link, a path outside the folders the owner allows Jarvis to change, a bad sha256 or a version no longer in the store is refused in plain words **before any card is raised** and nothing is touched. The saved bytes are re-hashed against their content address here (a blob that was altered or corrupted is refused as `damaged`, and one that unpacks over the one-file limit is refused rather than written), and the version must have been saved **from this same file** - a version another file's history saved is refused (`not_this_files_version`), because a content address does not by itself say which file it came from;
2. the EXISTING `undo_action` card is asked through the real `jarvis_gate.check()` - same tier, same words, no new action and no second permission model. Only an outcome of exactly `"approved"` is a person's yes: a denied, timed-out, unraisable, `auto`/`notify` or outcome-less card writes **nothing**;
3. what is here **now** is read AFTER the card (an edit made while the person was deciding is the version saved and the version Undo brings back), then that version is saved with a NEW receipt and journal row BEFORE the write, so the existing Undo button reverses the restore in one click; if any of the save, the receipt or the journal row cannot happen the restore aborts with the file untouched and any receipt already written is taken back;
4. the path rules run once more (the card can wait minutes), then the bytes are replaced in one atomic rename; a write that fails takes its receipt back, so no receipt claims a restore that did not happen.

Answers: on success the module's own dict unchanged - `{"ok": true, "changed": true, "path", "before_sha256", "after_sha256", "restored_sha256", "receipt_id", "pruned", "prune_words", "words"}` (and `changed: false, same: true` when the file is already that version, with no card and no receipt). A refusal is the module's own dict too - `{"ok": false, "refused": true, "gated": true, "outcome"/"error", "path", "words"}` - or, from the route itself: `400 {ok:false, refused:true, why:"bad_request", path:"", receipt_id:"", words}` for a missing/oversized pair, `403 {why:"not_this_pc"}` for another device (refused before the body is read), and `501 {why:"update"}` with the apply-patches sentence for an older backend. A request body over 16 KiB is `413`; a server with no body reader answers `501` and changes nothing.

**This PC only**, for the same reason the reads are: the versions are files on this PC, `jarvis_owner_check.from_this_pc` refuses another device before the body is read, and no gate can be named over the wire - the route passes none, so the module's real `jarvis_gate.check()` is always the one asked. There is still no chat tool that reaches any of this: no model can restore, or even list, a file's history.

`tools/check_parity.py` decides these routes now: the desktop calls both through `brain/guardian.rs`/`brain_read`, the phone calls neither, and all three guardian routes are classified `deliberate` for the one-sided reason above (ARCHITECTURE.md section 8).

### 140.5 The desktop drawer: Brain -> Projects -> File history (LM-2C, 2026-10-18)

The owner's surface for all of this is a pane in the Brain's **Projects** view (`guardian-panel.js`, words and decisions in `guardian.js`), beside Progress and Pictures - the files it keeps copies of are project files and notes, so it lives where those already are. It shows the page from 139.1 **newest first** with each copy's file name, when, why and size - never a file's words and never more than the contract's fields. "Show the difference" calls `guardian_diff` and draws the module's bounded diff (139.2) in one `<pre>`, saying when it was cut. "Put this version back" asks "are you sure?" on the PC, then calls `guardian_restore` (139.4); the PC raises the EXISTING `undo_action` card in the Jarvis bar, this page approves nothing, and the PC's own sentence is shown whether the restore happened or the card was denied, timed out or unraisable. A refused restore changes nothing, so nothing is re-read and nothing is re-sent.

**Hidden whole, in Rust.** While App lock is locked OR "Hide memory lists and chat history" is on, `brain/guardian.rs` replaces the entire answer (`words_hidden`, both flags) with one sentence that names no file, no count, no folder - and while hidden neither the list section nor the two commands ask the PC for anything, so no file name crosses the loopback wire. A flag change also **clears the drawer's rows at once**, before the next read is asked for, and a restore answer that comes back after a flag changed is re-hidden before the page sees it (the card can wait twenty minutes, so the request may well have started while the drawer was still visible). That is the desktop-side half of the gap in 139.3, now built; the phone still has no page (ARCHITECTURE.md section 8).

**Least privilege:** the list rides on the existing `brain_read` allowlist (`guardian_history`), and the two commands that need arguments live in one `brain-guardian` permission set (`allow-guardian-diff`, `allow-guardian-restore`) held by the Brain window only. `tools/check_command_acl.py` and `tools/check_invoke_grants.py` hold that agreement. The restore's Rust budget is twenty minutes because the card waits for a person (the PC's own gate allows fifteen). The `guardian_restore` command is also **held on a stale link**, the same `require_link_live` rule every other Brain write keeps - the page's disabled button is not the enforcement point (F6, 2026-10-18).

## 141. The selection chip: what the owner highlighted when the bar opened (Pillar 24-B, added 2026-10-18)

The owner's spotlight decision (Spotlight 6, 2026-10-18, on top of the 24-A backend): while reading in another program, he highlights text and presses **`Alt+Space`**. BEFORE the Jarvis bar takes focus, the PC reads that selection, with the screen's own privacy rules; if something non-empty (already scrubbed) comes back, the bar shows ONE chip above the input:

`[📎 Attach selection from <program> — "<first ~40 scrubbed chars>…"]` plus `[Explain]` · `[Summarize]` · `[×]`.

`[Remind me about this]` is **NOT drawn yet**: it is the deferred follow-up that waits for GTD-1's `context_bundle`, so no dead button is shown (Pillar 24-B scope note, 2026-10-18).

**Nothing reaches the model by itself.** The chip only puts words in the box; the owner presses Enter. The attached words are tagged `pasted` - the R3 class the repo already uses for text inserted from outside - never `typed`: they were read out of another program's window, so the PC's `OWN_WORDS` rules, the "was pasted in, not typed" card lines, the no-card lights path, the no-model quick path and automatic learning all treat them correctly (`chat-history.js`, `tests/provenance.mjs`). Attach puts the scrubbed selection in exactly as the PC returned it (a truncated one is not completed), Explain/Summarize put a local `Explain this:` / `Summarize this:` prompt there, and all three are local page work: no backend call from the chip. `×` dismisses it and the SAME selection (same program + same scrubbed words) will not come back by itself; a different selection on a later bar-open does. A refusal, an empty selection, an excluded window or a missing scrubber draws NO chip at all - never a fake empty one, and a chip only exists while the page holds the words (the bar's own dismiss clears it; "Hide memory lists and chat history" hides it with the rest).

### 141.1 The route

`GET /api/selection` (served by `jarvis_brain_reads.py`, answered by `jarvis_ui_control.read_selection()`) returns the 24-A dict **unchanged**:

`{"ok": true, "refused": false, "why": "", "text": <scrubbed text>, "app": <program name>, "chars": int, "truncated": bool, "scrubbed": bool, "words": <plain sentence>}`

and, when it will not read, the same keys with `ok: false`, `refused: true`, `why` one of the 24-A reasons (`no_selection`, `never_look`, `private_window`, `password_box`, `lock_screen`, `admin_prompt`, `jarvis`, `protected`, `cannot_check`, `list_unreadable`, `cannot_read`, `scrubber`, `secret`), `text: ""` and a plain `words` sentence. `app` is the PROGRAM's name - the window title is never in the payload and never drawn.

* **Desktop only, on purpose.** The route is read-only and local. A request from another device is refused (`403`, the same dict with `why: "not_this_pc"`) by `jarvis_owner_check.from_this_pc` BEFORE anything is read: the phone has no way to read the PC's screen selection, and it is not a route a phone screen should ever call. See `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8.
* **Before the bar takes focus.** Windows UI Automation reports the FOCUSED control's selection, so the page cannot ask after the bar is up. `windows::toggle_quickbar` (Rust) reads first, then reveals the bar and hands the answer to the page as the `selection-read` event. The bar-open delay is one loopback GET (a few milliseconds; at most 3 s, and then no chip, if the backend is not answering). This is documented, not measured on the owner's PC - the real UI Automation support per program is a measurement.
* **What it does not do:** no card (a read), nothing written, nothing kept, no model and no tool can reach it, and no other window's words are read. The privacy rules are `jarvis_screen`'s own (the Never look at list, private browser windows, password boxes, lock screen, capture protection) and the scrubber is `jarvis_scrub.scrub_text` - not a second copy.
* **An older backend** (no route) answers 404, and the app says "This PC's Jarvis does not have the selection reader yet. Update the backend by running apply-patches.ps1, then try again."
* `tools/check_parity.py` classifies the route `deliberate` (desktop only), and the desktop's chip is in the Jarvis bar's existing attachment strip - no new window and no HUD change.

## 142. The data and maths sandbox's own switch: GET/POST `/api/sandbox` (added 2026-10-18)

The sandbox tool (`run_data_script`, §"Pillar 15", `jarvis_sandbox_exec.py`)
ships OFF: the AI model is not offered it unless the owner turns its switch on.
This section is that switch's route - and the reason it needs no patch.

### 142.1 The route

| Route | Body | Answers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/sandbox` | - | 200 `{"enabled", "waiting", "line", "status", "why", "last"}`; 503 `{"error"}` if the module itself fails |
| `POST /api/sandbox` | `{"enabled": true\|false}` | ON: **202** `{"ok": true, "enabled": false, "waiting": true, "message"}` while ONE normal approval card waits - nothing is written yet. OFF: 200 `{"ok": true, "enabled": false, "waiting": false, "message"}` **at once**, withdrawing a waiting ON card. 400 for a body that is not `{"enabled": <bool>}`. 503 if `change_own_config` is not tier `ask`, or the card cannot be raised - nothing changes either way. |

The POST handler **never writes the setting itself**: it calls
`jarvis_sandbox_exec.request_enabled()`, the same function the chat/voice
phrase uses (`jarvis_quick` → `jarvis_settings_registry.set_sandbox_exec`), and
that only writes after the gate reports a person's approved card. A direct POST
therefore cannot bypass the approval card.

`line` is the PC's own state sentence: off, on, a card waiting, or what the
last card did (denied / timed out / refused / could not be saved). `status`
carries that last-card sentence on its own when a screen has room for it.
`last` is `{"outcome", "message"}` or null. Both apps print `line` unchanged,
so the two Settings rows say one sentence from one source.

### 142.2 Checks before anything is read

The route is installed by `plugins/ready/sandbox/plugin.json`, whose `install`
is `handler`: the core's own plugin loader calls
`jarvis_sandbox_exec.install(Handler, origin_ok=..., token_ok=..., read_body=...)`
at start-up, exactly as it does for `jarvis_receipts.py`. There is **no patch**
and no edit to `jarvis_hud.py` for this route.

- **origin first**: a cross-origin / another-device request is refused with
  **403** *before its body is read* (the read callback is not called at all);
- then the token: **401** without `X-Jarvis-Token`;
- only then is the body parsed;
- **a read-only file must be the file itself** (added 2026-10-20, Area 8): a
  `read_only_files` entry that is a symlink, or that resolves somewhere other
  than the path given, is refused before the script runs, so a link cannot hand
  a script a file it was not given (`backend/test_sandbox_exec.py`).

An older PC that has the module but not this folder answers **404** on the
route. Both apps treat 404 (and 501) as "not on this PC's Jarvis yet" and draw
the row disabled with one sentence naming the command
`scripts\add-plugin.ps1 -Name sandbox`, rather than a switch that does nothing.

### 142.3 Both apps, one sentence

- **Desktop**: `src-tauri/src/sandbox_exec.rs` (`sandbox_exec`: read / on /
  off; "on" held on a stale link, "off" never), `src/sandbox-settings.js` and
  `src/sandbox-rules.js`, and the `#sandbox` card in `src/settings.html`.
  Settings only; the command carries a switch position and nothing else.
- **Phone**: `net/SandboxExec.kt` (the same words, the same read-through),
  `ui/screens/SandboxPlate.kt`, and Settings → Data and maths sandbox. It only
  asks the PC: the switch is decided there, under `change_own_config`.
- Neither app runs a script or sees a file or a piece of data. Every sandbox
  refusal (the AST allow-list, the wall clock, the output cap, the memory cap,
  "only files the owner listed") is unchanged by the switch.

`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 needs no one-sided row: both apps carry the switch,
and the phone deliberately only asks the PC - the same shape as every other
approval-card setting.

### 142.5 A run that reads a file asks on its own card (added 2026-10-18)

`sandbox_file_run` is a tier line of its own, shipped `"ask"`. A
`run_data_script` call whose `files` list is not empty is decided under it,
AFTER the tool's own `file_read` lookup: the card shows the script, its code
and the resolved file names, and no file is read until the owner answers. A
pure calculation stays under the calculator's auto action. The 2026-10-18 host
audit's M7 is why: the sandbox is a language allow-list, so a file-reading run
gets a person in front of it.

The same audit added the OS boundary Windows does have: the Win32 Job Object
that already caps memory now also sets `JOB_OBJECT_UILIMIT_ALL` (clipboard,
screen, desktops, windows and system parameters are denied to the child), and
the child's environment drops proxy variables (`HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`,
`ALL_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY` and neighbours) even if an allow-list ever let one
through. Said plainly: a Job Object cannot block network access, cannot
restrict which files the process opens at the OS level, and is not a
restricted token or AppContainer. `jarvis_sandbox_exec.OS_BOUNDARY_NOTE` is
that sentence in code, and the suite holds it.

## 143. The person dossier: one click in "People and things", read-only (LM-4, added 2026-10-18)

Pillar 16's dossier builder (`backend/jarvis_people_crm.py`, #540) already put
one person's own records in one dict: saved facts (current and retired), the
last kept chat turns that mention them, the newest mail headers that name them,
the open to-dos that name them, and the next shared calendar event. It had no
door an owner could reach. This is the door, on **both apps**: click (or tap)
a person's name in **People and things** and their dossier opens - a read-only
card on the PC's Brain, and the same words under the name on the phone.

### 143.1 `GET /api/people/dossier?name=<the owner's own word for them>`

Served by the EXISTING `jarvis_brain_reads.py` install (no new module, no new
patch, no `$SHIPPED` or registration change) and answered by
`jarvis_people_crm.build_person_dossier()`. The module's own dict is passed
back **unchanged** - `{ok, withheld, why, name, private, aliases, known,
active_facts, retired_facts, recent_chat, recent_email, commitments,
next_event, states, why, read, counts, text}` - so the apps draw the module's
`text` and never a second rendering. The words are the records' own; the model
never writes any of it and never sees it.

* **This PC only.** A request from another device is refused (`403`, in the
  dossier's own shape with `withheld: false`, `name: ""` and one plain
  sentence) by `jarvis_owner_check.from_this_pc` **BEFORE the name is read and
  before the module is imported** - so a phone or other device learns nothing,
  not even whether a name has a dossier, and a refusal never echoes a name.
* **Hidden whole, in the apps.** The backend cannot see App lock or "Hide
  memory lists and chat history" (both are the apps' state). The desktop's
  `people_dossier` command (Rust `brain/people.rs`, granted to the Brain window
  only) asks the PC for **nothing** while either is on and answers one
  sentence with no name, fact, count or mail; it checks again after the answer
  arrives, because the lock can turn on while the read is out. On the phone the
  whole "People and things" plate is already replaced by its hidden section, so
  a name cannot be tapped then and the dossier lives inside the same section.
  The module itself also withholds the dossier when a caller passes either flag
  (`build_person_dossier(hide_memory_lists=..., app_locked=...)`), which is the
  same rule for any future caller. **Since 2026-10-20 (Q1) the route accepts
  `?app_locked=1` / `?hide_memory_lists=1` too** and merges them through
  `jarvis_private_view`: a flag can only ADD withholding, a `0` cannot unlock
  the trusted state, and a locked answer is the module's own withheld dict
  (`{"ok": false, "withheld": true, "why": "Hidden while App lock is on." ...}`)
  with no facts, chats, mail, to-dos or event in it. **The live HUD must
  eventually pass the state** (ARCHITECTURE.md, App lock section); until it
  does, the apps' own hiding above is what protects the view.
* **A refusal is one plain sentence:** an empty name is `400` (`"Say whose
  dossier to put together - a name."`); a PC whose backend predates the route
  answers `501` with the apply-patches sentence; an unreadable module or store
  answers `500` with one sentence. An unknown but real name is **not** an
  error: the module answers `ok: true` with no facts and the sentence "Jarvis
  has no saved facts about them."
* **What it does not do:** no card, no write, nothing stored, no model call,
  no chat tool and no route a phone can use to read the PC's screen. Mail and
  the calendar are read only in the bounded shape the morning briefing already
  uses, and only when the owner's settings and the gate's tier allow that read
  without a person - a dossier never raises an approval card by itself.
* **Older backend:** `404`/`501`, and both apps say
  "Your PC's Jarvis does not have the person dossier yet. Run
  apply-patches.ps1 on the PC."
* **Both apps, on purpose**, and `tools/check_parity.py` calls the route
  `ported`: the desktop's `people_dossier` command (`brain/people.rs`) and
  `brain.js` card, and the phone's `PeopleDossier` read under
  `EntitiesPlate`. There is no other window and no new screen: the card opens
  in the Brain, where People and things already is, and the phone shows it
  under the name it already lists.

## 144. Reading the words in one audio or video file (F5 S1, added 2026-10-18)

The first Feasibility-5 slice: a read-only read of ONE audio or video file that
is already inside a folder on the owner's "Folders Jarvis may look in" list. It
returns a bounded transcript with timestamps, and for a video the on-screen text
from a few sampled frames. **It stores nothing** - no index, no transcript file,
no memory fact - and it has **no HTTP route of its own and no new tool**: it is
the existing `my_files` tool's action `read_media`, decided under the existing
`read_files_readonly` action like every other read of the owner's own files.
The design and measurements are in `docs/MEDIA-READ-DESIGN.md`.

* **Both apps' chats can ask** (it is a backend read, and the file and all the
  reading are on the PC): "read the words in C:\...\talk.mp4". There is no
  one-sided decision here; no route was added, so `tools/check_parity.py` has
  nothing new to classify.
* **No card of its own.** A read of a file already inside an allowed folder is
  the `read_files_readonly` tier, exactly as `my_files` read is; it is not a new
  permission. The result goes through the EXISTING outside-text path:
  `_TurnWatch.took_in` marks it, it never becomes a learned fact, and
  `jarvis_sources.from_tool_result` shows `{kind: "file", path, seconds}` as its
  source. Nothing is sent anywhere.
* **The limits, in the result's own words:** at most 100 MB and 10 minutes per
  file; at most ~20,000 characters of transcript + on-screen text; speech is the
  existing local Parakeet model, **English only**, with segment-level timestamps
  and no speaker labels; on-screen text is Windows OCR on one frame every 10
  seconds. A WAV needs no decoder; every other format needs the LOCAL `ffmpeg`
  already on the PC, run as a child process with `-protocol_whitelist file,pipe`,
  a scrubbed environment, a wall-clock timeout and a bounded stdout. A missing
  ffmpeg is one plain refusal: "This PC has no ffmpeg, so this file's sound
  cannot be read."
* **It is a transcript, not a summary**, and this read itself never writes a
  file. A later slice, S2, was authorised by the owner on 2026-10-19: the
  searchable recordings index (section 149) keeps readable words on this PC,
  ON by default - it is a separate switch with its own storage, deletion and
  backup rules, and this read is unchanged by it.
* **Pause and one-at-a-time:** a caller may pass a "the owner is talking" check;
  the chat turn itself is already single-flight, and this reader takes a
  non-blocking lock so two media reads never run together. The live-voice flag
  is not a public function in this tree yet; the seam and its test are here, and
  the design note says so honestly.
* **Other people's voices and incidental secrets** are not stored by THIS
  read: the words are returned to the model for this answer, marked outside
  text, and the normal taint/card rules apply. Whether they are KEPT for
  searching is the separate switch in section 149 (on by default, off at
  once, one Delete).


## 145. Focus presets: the one read route both apps render (added 2026-10-19)

Owner decision, 2026-10-18: replace the five work setups with **focus presets -
General, General Uncensored, Coding, Agentic + Vision and Fast** - one
selector in both apps' chat bars and a Settings page. The contract is the file
`backend/fixtures/work_presets.json`, generated by `tools/gen_work_presets.py`
from `backend/jarvis_presets.py` (shipped whole, twin in the base); the app UIs
render it verbatim. No new token and no new gate action.

**Ten local presets since 2026-11-09.** The owner asked for the strong
integrated abilities to be preset choices that load the best local model for
the job, so four capability rows joined the original five: **Reflective Coach**
(talking a difficult thought through), **Pictures & Screens** (a screenshot or
picture), **Documents & Notes** (long reading and study) and **Browser &
Forms** (long pages and multi-step form work). All four run `qwen3.5:9b` on the
RTX 2060 12 GB - Reflective Coach, Documents & Notes and Browser & Forms at
196,608 tokens, the measured General setup (44.9 tokens a second, 9.17 of the
12 GB, no spill), and Pictures & Screens at 32,768 tokens, whose window and
speed are not separately measured (the model's vision capability is
documented). **Fast** now runs `qwen3.5:4b` on the RTX 2080 SUPER (the `coding`
lane) at 16,384 tokens, the window that lane serves; measured 2026-10-10 on the
same card: 77.1 tokens a second and 4.15 GB of video memory at a 65,536-token
window, the file 3.16 GB on disk. **Medical Expert** is the tenth row, appended
last on 2026-11-09: `medgemma:27b` on the same pooled lane Coding uses, at
32,768 tokens - its measured numbers are in §145.1b. The split is deliberate:
only the 12 GB card
holds the 196,608-token window (Qwen3.5's recurrent layers keep no KV cache),
while the 8 GB card is the display card and runs the small model with about
4 GB of video memory, leaving headroom for Windows, DWM and WebView2; Coding's
30B model and Medical's 27B use all three cards only while one is applied.
Nothing switches by itself:
an apply that needs a different model raises the ONE existing `switch_model`
approval card, a model already loaded is simply chosen with nothing to approve,
and no automatic per-feature model switching exists.

**`GET /api/work` (and its alias `GET /api/presets`) - READ ONLY.** The same
origin and token checks as the old route; the answer is:

    {"found", "presets": [ten], "old_ids_replaced": [...],
     "hardware": {"detected": {"count",
                               "cards": [{"index","name","vram_gib","uuid",
                                          "pci_id","monitor"}],
                               "source": "jarvis_hardware.detect()"},
                  "questionnaire": {"focus_choices", "priority_choices", "answers"}},
     "recommendations": {"basis", "by_gpu_count": {"1","2","3": {...}},
                         "three_gpu_plan": {"confirmed", "layout", "cards",
                                            "heavy_pooled", "link_note",
                                            "future_not_a_preset"}},
     "chosen": "<preset id or null>", "chosen_preset", "chosen_model",
     "lane": {"key", "base_url", "card", "words", "label", "ready", "why"},
     "lane_status": <same object>, "active_lane": {"key", "base_url"},
     "apply_path": "/api/work/apply", "switch_path": "/api/models/switch",
     "auto": false, "not_a_catalogue"}

The `hardware` block is the SAME shape as the generated contract fixture
(`detected` + `questionnaire` nested, no second top-level `questionnaire`);
this is what the desktop and Android readers expect. `chosen`, `lane` and
`active_lane` are live PC state and are deliberately not in the fixture.

Each preset carries `id/title/focus/what/cost/worse/model/lane{key,card,port,
words}/context/helper/policy/measured/pending/heavy_mode/heavy_words/apply{action,
switch_route,apply_route,lane_start,auto:false}`. A `pending` preset has no
model tag or figure and says it is waiting. `heavy_mode` (Coding on the 30B
coder, and since 2026-11-09 Medical on `medgemma:27b` at 32,768) means the
preset's model needs ALL THREE cards as ONE pooled lane; since
2026-11-02 that lane exists and the row is applicable like every other one,
with `heavy_words` carrying the PC's own plain-words cost (all three cards, and
the other two models paused while it runs). Both fields are additive: a reader that
ignores them behaves exactly as before. `chosen` is the id last applied;
`active_lane` is the lane chat is pointed at now.

**`POST /api/work/apply` - the ONE asked action.** `{"preset": "<id>"}`: one
`switch_model` approval card (never automatic). The lane is started on demand
BEFORE that card - a lane that is down cannot answer the switch's installed-
model read, so switch-first is not possible. The contract key `"main"` is
translated to the model starter's own `"everyday"` lane (`"coding"` stays
`"coding"`); the apps and fixture keep `"main"`. After approval the model is
switched, chat is pointed at the lane and the chosen id saved; once the model
has switched, any later failure rolls it back with the auto-tier
`jarvis_models.rollback()` as well as restoring the chat lane and chosen
preset. **Every one of those three restores is CHECKED, and only what was seen
is claimed** (silent-failure audit 2026-10-27, row 2): a refused apply answers
`{"ok": false, "changed": false, "error": "...", "restored": [...],
"not_restored": [...]}`, where the two lists name which of `"the pooled lane"`,
`"the model"`, `"the chat lane"` and `"the chosen preset"` were put back and
which could not be, and `error` says the same in words - it contains "were
rolled back" only when every attempted restore succeeded. `changed: false`
means the preset is not the chosen one; it says nothing about the model, the
lane or the choice file, and `not_restored` is the fact about those. Both keys
are additive, so a reader that ignores them behaves exactly as before. **Said
plainly:** a card the owner DENIES leaves the started lane
running - it starts no model and switches nothing. A `pending` preset refuses
before anything happens. Both apps call this route now: the desktop's
focus-presets bridge sends it, and the Android preset screen reads and sends
the same `apply_path` the GET advertises.

**Changed 2026-11-09: a local preset picked in either app raises NO card.**
This is the owner's own reversible click, and this route is the one road it
takes; the model/chat path still raises the `switch_model` card. The apply now
also answers `receipt_id` (the `preset_apply` receipt naming the preset, model
and lane it replaced) and the preset it replaced is one click away in the same
menu. Coding (its pooled lane pauses both other models) and the Cloud row still
raise their card exactly as this section describes. See section 209 for the
preset's own rule, and section 210 for the whole manual-click allow-list it now
belongs to (a model already installed and picked in either app's own model list
switches without a card too).

### 145.1 The Coding preset's pooled both-card lane (2026-11-02, added)

Coding is the ONE preset whose model cannot run on either named lane: 14.8 GB
against a 12 GB card and an 8 GB card. Its `lane` is therefore `pooled` - ONE
Ollama on port 11450, started on demand by this apply with **no card pin**, so
the engine sees both cards (`jarvis_model_lanes.start_pooled_lane`, reusing
`jarvis_big_coder`'s server, pause, load and restore - `jarvis_model_lanes.py`
and `jarvis_big_coder.py` ship whole).

What an apply does, in order, and what it never does:

1. **ONE `switch_model` card first**, raised by the pooled lane's start, with
   the same `from`/`to`/`why` detail `jarvis_models.switch_to` sends and the
   preset's own `heavy_words` as the card's text. It names both cards and the
   two lane models about to be paused. **Nothing is unloaded before it is
   answered**, so a denied card changes NOTHING on this path (that is stricter
   than the named-lane path, where the lane start comes first and a denied card
   leaves it running).
2. The pause is ANNOUNCED (event bus + audit log) before the first unload, both
   lane models are unloaded and proved gone from `/api/ps`, the model is loaded
   **naming 32,768 tokens** (since 2026-11-03; 16,384 before it), and `/api/ps`
   must show it present, at that context and with no spill beyond this one
   window's measured allowance - **352 MiB**
   (`jarvis_model_lanes.POOLED_SPILL_ALLOWANCE`: the 323.5 MiB measured at
   32,768 on 2026-11-03 plus about 9%). A load that comes up elsewhere, spills
   past the allowance, or does not report its spill is unloaded again, both
   lanes are restored and the answer says why (503) - the refusal is the machine's own
   words, never a canned one. **That allowance is the ONE exception:**
   `load_coder` with no allowance still refuses any spill at all, and that is
   every other caller, the big-coder mode's own 28,672-token load included.
3. The model is then recorded as the one chat uses. It is NOT a second card and
   NOT `switch_to`: `jarvis_models.switch_to` runs its tripwire smoke test at
   `jarvis_models.OLLAMA`, which is a single-card lane, so asking it for a
   14 GB model would load it on a 12 GB card (or evict the model the pooled
   lane just loaded). The preset writes the same record `switch_to` writes,
   through that module's own state read/write, only after the card was approved
   and the model really loaded.
4. Chat is pointed at `http://127.0.0.1:11450` and the preset id saved. Any
   later failure stops the pooled lane FIRST (unload, stop the server, restore
   both lane models), then rolls the model back with the auto-tier
   `jarvis_models.rollback()`, then restores the lane pointer and the choice.
5. **Leaving it:** applying any preset that is not heavy stops the pooled lane
   before anything else, in the same apply - it unloads the 30B, restores both
   lane models and proves it from `/api/ps`. If it cannot be stopped, the apply
   refuses in plain words (503) and changes nothing else.

`POST /api/big-coder {"action":"stop"}` stops the same server by the same code
(§126). Both routes are loopback only and behind the server's own origin and
token checks.

**One interaction that is stated rather than hidden.** The background learner
(`jarvis_extract`, which `jarvis_hud.py` feeds the chat's own current model)
talks to the address in `OLLAMA_URL` - the everyday lane - not to the preset's
lane pointer. While the Coding preset is applied, that lane holds no model and
cannot hold the 30B, so a learning pass asks for a model the lane cannot load
and the learner fails in its own words (it will not load 14 GB on a 12 GB
card). Nothing is sent anywhere and nothing is corrupted; learning pauses while
the heavy preset is on and resumes when another preset is applied. It is not
claimed to work, and it was not driven live in this slice. The same is true of
`GET /api/models`' resident list, which reads the everyday lane: while Coding
runs, the Current Models panel does not show the pooled model.

**Measured on this PC, 2026-11-02** (`docs/MEASURED-2026-11-02-POOLED-LANE.md`):
cold load 32.5 s, **77.5 / 85.3 / 85.6 tokens a second** on a fixed
three-prompt coding set (median 85.3), the model 14,886 MiB **entirely in video
memory** (zero spill), 11,899 MiB used on the RTX 2060 and 7,674 MiB on the
RTX 2080 SUPER while it ran, and both lane models proved back afterwards at
`qwen3.5:9b ctx=196608` and `qwen3:8b ctx=16384` with zero spill. The whole
start took 69.9 s and the stop 59.1 s, the pause and the restores included.
**The 28,672-token rung the 2026-10-18 measurement used no longer fits this
PC**: 28,672, 24,576 and 20,480 all spilled 204-212 MiB, and 16,384 was the
largest rung that loaded with none, which is why the preset asked for 16,384
from 2026-11-02 until the amendment below. `jarvis_big_coder.NUM_CTX` (28,672)
is that mode's own measured rung and was not changed.

**2026-11-03 amendment: the preset now asks for 32,768, and the allowance is
still one window's.** The same day's read-only measurement on this PC, through
the same shipped path, put the whole context ladder on one table: 16,384 at
14,886.2 MiB with **no spill** (still the zero-spill ceiling), then 20,480 at
203.5 MiB spilled, 24,576 at 207.5, 28,672 at 211.5 and **32,768 at 323.5 MiB**
(16,513.7 MiB in all, 16,190.1 of it in video memory). Above 16,384 every rung
spills; the 8 GB card is what runs out first (7,591 of 8,192 MiB at 32,768),
which is why the top rung's spill jumps by 112 MiB rather than growing smoothly.
The owner chose 32,768, the largest rung measured to load on this PC: cold load
36.0 s against 37.0 s at 16,384, and a decode median of 80.36 against 79.88
tokens a second on the three prompts, inside the model's own run-to-run noise.
The owner accepted the 323.5 MiB of the model in system RAM, so the preset's
`context` is now **32,768** (`jarvis_model_lanes.POOLED_CTX`, pinned to it by
test; `POOLED_SPILL_MEASURED_MIB` is 323.5, `context_measured` is 32,768, and
`context_zero_spill` stays 16,384 as the historical fact), and the start passes
`load_coder(..., allow_spill=...)` the cap of **352 MiB** - the 323.5 MiB
measurement plus about 9%. **Nothing else relaxes:** no allowance is the default
and still means any spill is refused; `jarvis_big_coder.start()` never passes
one; the big-coder mode's 28,672 rung and its zero-spill check are unchanged;
and a load above the cap, or one that does not report its spill, is still
refused (503) with both the actual spill and the allowance named. The extra
16,384 tokens over the old window were not filled by the measurement (all
prompts were 40-43 tokens), so a genuinely long conversation is still
unmeasured - the decode speed of a nearly-full 32,768-token window was not
measured either; a 15-minute real coding test runs after deployment. Full
numbers: `docs/MEASURED-2026-11-02-POOLED-LANE.md`'s 2026-11-03 amendment; raw
output: `.dsh-scratch/CODING-TAKEOVER-2026-11-03/WINDOW-20480.md` and
`WINDOW-HIGHER-RUNGS.md`.

**The HUD's left rail renders this contract too** (the owner's request of
2026-10-21: "i would like this part of the jarvis HUD to have the presets we
created instead, with one of the buttons being for the cloud"). The HUD window
holds no pairing token, so it reaches both routes the way every other HUD read
does: `GET /api/presets` is on the HUD window's fixed read list
(`jarvis-desktop/src-tauri/src/hud_proxy.rs` `HUD_GET_PATHS`, returned through
`hud_get`),
and a preset click calls the BAR'S own Tauri command `apply_focus_preset`
(`focus_presets.rs`, the same command the bar's "Use this preset" sends), so
the PC raises the same ONE `switch_model` card and the page never posts
`/api/work/apply` itself. The rail marks a preset chosen only when the next
refetch says `chosen_preset`; after a successful apply the page clears its own
lane override so the next chat turn is an ordinary routed turn at the PC's
active lane (what the bar and the phone send). The single **Cloud** button is
NOT this contract: it sets the next message's lane to the general cloud lane
(`jarvis-escalate` when the PC lists it) through the HUD's existing lane
mechanism, raises no card, and when `/api/status` says `proxy: false` it says
plainly that the cloud lane is down and marks nothing. **Since 2026-10-27 the
Studio stage's own words row carries a third door to the same one menu:**
`#stage-presets`, after Telemetry and beside the new "Galaxy options" word,
dispatches the same `jarvis:hud-presets-open` event with itself as the anchor -
so the menu is reachable from the words beside Galaxy, Approvals, Reminders and
the rest, and no second menu or route is added. The same row's **Galaxy
options** word opens the page's own `#galaxy-options` panel, which holds the
lenses, the Look switch, the search box, Reset view, Pause spin and Hide the
galaxy; that panel is the HUD's existing `galaxy` view and its existing
device-local preferences only - it reads `/api/graph` exactly as before and
adds no route, command or permission. Tests:
`jarvis-desktop/tests/hud-presets.mjs`.

**The Studio dock's "Current Models" panel** (2026-10-26) is a second reader of
this contract, plus the PC's model facts: it shows `GET /api/models`'s
`current`, `previous` and `offload.models`, `GET /api/status`'s `default_model`
when it differs, and `chosen_preset`/`chosen_model` from here. Its lane routes
are the same HUD lane mechanism the Cloud button uses (the page's own `#lanes`
buttons), so it starts nothing, applies nothing, resets nothing and raises no
card. `/api/models` is on the same fixed read list (`HUD_GET_PATHS`), read
through `hud_get`; every model write (`/api/models/switch`, `/install`,
`/rollback`) and the `?recommend=1` catalogue query stay off it.

Tests: `backend/test_presets.py`, `test_presets_lanes.py`,
`test_presets_apply.py` (route shape, origin/token, old shape not served,
pending/heavy refusals, rollback), and `tools/gen_work_presets.py --check`.

### 145.1b The Medical preset on the same pooled lane (added 2026-11-09)

**Medical Expert** (`id: "medical"`) is the tenth row, appended after Browser &
Forms so the nine older rows keep their order, ids and `focus_choices` order.
Its model is `medgemma:27b` on the `pooled` lane at **32,768 tokens** - the same
one-Ollama-on-port-11450 shape Coding's row uses, with `heavy_mode: true` and
`mode: "medical"`. Its words are on the row: clinical reading and
patient-advocate questions, **no tool calling** (`ollama show` reports no
`tools` capability, so it cannot use Jarvis's tools, browser or files), vision
reported but not measured here, and plainly that it is not a doctor - no
diagnosis, no prescription, no replacement for the owner's own clinician.

Measured on this PC on 2026-11-09 (`model-bench` run
`run-20261109-105956`, the `medgemma` window row): **17.31 GiB loaded, 100% in
video memory, 0 B spilled**, a **46.8 s** cold load and **9.27 tokens a
second** on the summary/coding prompt, 11.1 on the measured ~150-word
explanation and 7.89 on the four-token answer. That is the honest
**7.9-11.1 tok/s** range, not a single optimistic figure.

The preset changes no wording: choose the **Patient Advocate** personality in
How Jarvis talks if that manner is wanted - a preset is a model, a lane and a
window, never a personality.

Applying it starts that lane **in its own mode**: the row's `mode: "medical"`
reaches the pooled lane's start, so `medgemma:27b` is what loads, and the
window this backend reports for the pooled lane follows the preset that is
applied (`pooled_num_ctx()`), so a Medical turn asks for 32,768 tokens - the
window the lane really loaded - never Coding's 49,152. Stopping the lane and
`GET /api/work`'s lane state recognise `medgemma:27b` the same way, from the
preset layer's own `pooled_modes()` rows.

### 145.1 The Cloud row, the provider list, and the standing escalation switch (added 2026-10-27)

Owner decision, 2026-10-27: the Cloud row belongs in the Presets menu beside
General/Coding/Agentic+Vision/Fast, picking one of the connected API services
is an APPLY, and underneath it there is ONE checkbox - "escalate to the cloud
when the work is too complex". **The answer stays `version` 1 and gains keys
only**: no existing key moved, changed meaning or disappeared, so a reader that
does not know them is unaffected (the phone's `FocusPresets.parse` reads named
keys and ignores the rest, which is why the phone needs no change to keep
working).

Two new top-level keys on `GET /api/work` / `GET /api/presets`:

    "cloud_preset": {"id": "cloud", "title": "Cloud", "focus", "what", "cost",
                     "worse", "model": "", "lane": {"key": "cloud", "card": "",
                     "port": 0, "words": "the cloud"}, "context": 0,
                     "helper": null, "policy": {...}, "measured": null,
                     "pending": false, "heavy_mode": false,
                     "apply": {"action", "switch_route", "apply_route",
                               "lane_start": false, "auto": false,
                               "cloud": true, "needs_provider": true}}

    "cloud": {"provider": "<service id or \\"\\">",
              "providers": [{"id", "short", "name", "company", "host", "model",
                             "key_saved": true|false|null, "ready", "why",
                             "chosen", "money": {...}|null, "key_line",
                             "key_where"}],
              "escalate": {"on": false, "why": "not turned on for this PC"}}

* `cloud_preset` is an ELEVENTH row in the same shape as a preset, and it is
  deliberately **not** in `presets[]` - both apps' ten-row list stays ten
  rows. Its `apply` block says the two things that make it different: it is a
  cloud row (`cloud: true`) and it needs a provider (`needs_provider: true`);
  it starts no lane and switches no model (`lane_start: false`).
* `cloud.providers` has one row per service in `jarvis_chatbot_api.PRESETS`
  (openai, deepseek, mistral, xai, openrouter, groq), in that dict's order.
  `key_saved` is `true`/`false`, or **`null` when Windows Credential Manager
  cannot be asked** - an honest "this PC cannot say", never guessed. `why` is
  the PC's own sentence for why a service cannot be used yet. `key_line` is the
  one honest connect action from an app: the command line to run ON THE PC
  (`py -3 jarvis_chatbot_api.py key <service>`), because keys are added on the
  PC only and **no route accepts one** (rule 3). No key, no fragment of one and
  no message is ever in this answer.
* `cloud.escalate` is the PC's own standing switch. `on` is true only when
  `escalate-cloud.json` says `{"on": true}` literally; absent, unreadable,
  corrupt or any other value reads as OFF. `why` is `""` when it is on, else
  the plain reason it is not.

**`POST /api/work/apply` gains ONE optional field.** `{"preset": "cloud",
"provider": "deepseek_api"}` uses that service. `provider` is read only for the
cloud preset and ignored for the local ten, so **a body with no `provider` is
the same request it always was, byte for byte**. The cloud apply:

1. refuses `400` for no provider or an id this PC does not know, naming the six;
2. refuses `409` with the PC's own sentence, BEFORE any card, when the service
   has no key saved, no price, or no monthly limit (`jarvis_chatbot_api
   .ready_for`) - no approval is asked for something that cannot work;
3. raises exactly ONE `change_own_config` approval card that names the company,
   its host, its model and the money line;
4. **only after that yes** writes `cloud-choice.json` and
   `presets-choice.json {"preset": "cloud"}`;
5. **starts no lane and switches no model.** That is the one apply branch that
   must not run `start_lane`/`switch_model`/`set_active_url`: a cloud preset
   changes nothing local, and starting a GPU lane for it would unload the model
   the owner is using. `backend/test_presets_cloud.py` asserts all three spies
   were never called.

A refused card changes nothing and marks nothing. One provider is in use at a
time; `cloud.provider` is the truth and a click is never what marks a row.

**`POST /api/work/cloud-escalate` - NEW, the standing switch.**

    {"on": true}  -> ONE change_own_config card, then escalate-cloud.json
    {"on": false} -> immediate, no card, nothing asked

ON is a **loosening** - Jarvis may then send a hard question to that service
with no per-question yes - so it follows every loosening in this program: ONE
card, and nothing written before the answer. Its text says what changes in the
owner's words ("Jarvis may send a hard question to <Company> without asking you
first"), and what still does NOT go (anything private, a tainted conversation,
a picture, your screen) and that the monthly money limit still applies. OFF is
a tightening and is instant. ON with no provider chosen refuses `409` **before**
a card, because a standing yes to a service nobody picked cannot do anything.
The body is checked exactly: a missing or non-boolean `on` is a `400` - there
is no truthiness shortcut on a privacy switch. The answer is
`{ok, on, changed, card, escalate{on, why}, message|error}`; `card: true` means
one was raised and the app should say it is waiting.

**Where the standing yes is read, and what cannot forge it.** The switch is a
FILE on the PC, read by `jarvis_router.standing_escalation()` at gate 6 of
`choose()` and from **nowhere else** - no request body, no header and no client
flag is consulted for it, so a stale page or a phone cannot make a standing
decision the PC has not made. The HUD page keeps sending `cloud_yes` while its
box is on, and `cloud-escalate.patch` makes that flag count **only while the
PC's own file still says on**, so turning the box off cannot be defeated by a
page that has not refreshed. Another client's `cloud_yes` - the phone's "Try
the cloud model", the desktop window's strip - is the per-question tap it
always was, and is unchanged.

**Asking in the message.** On the newest message only, a fixed phrase list
(`jarvis_router.ESCALATE_PHRASES`: "escalate this", "escalate it", "use the
cloud", "use the cloud for this", "send this to the cloud", "send it to the
cloud", "ask the cloud", "use the bigger model", "the bigger model for this")
counts as the owner's yes **for that turn only**. Nothing is stored and the
next message has to ask again. It is evaluated at gate 6, after every privacy
gate, so a Lockdown, a tainted conversation, a picture, the words off the
screen, a private question or a pasted secret all still answer local and name
the gate that refused - the phrase can only turn `offer` into `escalate`.

**`X-Jarvis-Route` gains one key: `auto`.** `false` on every local turn and on
a turn the owner clicked for; `true` when the turn was escalated **with no
click** (the standing switch, or the phrase). It is additive and every reader
this project has reads named keys.

**A cloud answer nobody asked for is not dressed up as one.** The measured
failure on exactly the questions that escalate is `finish_reason: "length"`
with empty `content` and the whole cap spent on DeepSeek's hidden reasoning
(four of four, `docs/FIELD-TEST-CLOUD-ESCALATION-2026-10-14.md`; reproduced by
the 2026-11-03 field test at Jarvis's own 2,048-token default - HTTP 200,
`content: ""`, `reasoning_tokens: 2048/2048`). **Changed 2026-11-03 (the
owner's decision after the second field test):** the working-out is never
shown as an answer, on a clicked turn or an automatic one.
`jarvis_chatbot_api.CloudAnswer` withholds the `reasoning_content` events and,
when there is no usable answer, shows ONE honest line followed by the local
model's own answer (`jarvis_agent.answer_here`):

- the reply carried working-out and spent the budget: `CLOUD_USED_BUDGET` -
  "The cloud model used its whole answer budget thinking and sent nothing
  back; here is the local answer:";
- the reply carried neither visible text nor working-out:
  `CLOUD_ANSWERED_HERE` - "The cloud did not answer this one, so this PC
  answered it instead:";
- the local turn produced nothing either: `NO_CLOUD_ANSWER_HERE` says so and
  nothing is invented (`NO_ANSWER_AT_ALL` remains the no-working-out case).

This replaces the 2026-10-14 "a clicked turn still shows the working-out,
marked" rule. `used_reasoning` is kept for callers that read it and is never
set True any more.

**The request cap (2026-11-03).** A service this PC measured to bill hidden
reasoning INSIDE `max_tokens` is marked `Preset.thinking_inside = True`
(DeepSeek today); its relay call is sent
`cloud_request_cap(lane_state, asked)` = the lane's own answer cap PLUS
`REASONING_ROOM` (`jarvis_chatbot_api.py`: `REASONING_ROOM = 8000`) - on this
PC's DeepSeek lane an 8,000-token cap is sent as **16,000**, the same worst
case `reply_cap()` already priced, so it cannot pass the month's limit. Every
other service, or a lane with no cap, gets the caller's `max_tokens` untouched
(the relay's 2,048 default is not changed). The relay applies it once, in
`jarvis_hud.py`'s `_open`, via `ollama-direct.patch`:
`body["max_tokens"] = _api.cloud_request_cap(_state, int(body.get("max_tokens") or 0))`,
inside a `try/except` that changes nothing on a backend without the module.

Tests: `backend/test_reasoning_fallback.py` (the withheld `reasoning_content`
events, both framings, `t_cloud_request_cap` and
`t_the_twins_match`) and `backend/test_cloud_say_yes.py` (the
ordinary-turn lanes and the PC-only gate).

**The one lane.** `jarvis_router.cloud_lanes()` keeps only `jarvis-escalate`
and drops every other name, so an older `litellm-proxy.yaml` listing
`jarvis-critic` and `jarvis-bulk` cannot bring a second lane back; a list with
only dead names is an EMPTY list, which is gate `"unavailable"` - never a
substituted name. `degrade_chain` in `jarvis-framework.toml` is
`["jarvis-escalate"]`. Those two names are gone from `CLOUD_LANES`,
`jarvis_auto_router` and `jarvis_projects`.

**PC-only.** Turning the switch on and choosing a provider are the PC's, by
`tools/check_parity.py`'s `deliberate` row. The phone reads `cloud.escalate`
and `cloud.provider` and never writes either: there is no phone route, and
`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 records why.

Tests: `backend/test_presets_cloud.py`,
`backend/test_cloud_escalate_setting.py` (the switch, the card, the phrase, the
gates, the patch round trip on the published base, and the automatic-turn
fallback).

**The chat now says the real cloud state (2026-10-31, owner-reported).** With
the Cloud preset set to DeepSeek (API) and its key saved, the local model told
the owner "I have no connection to any external API" and "no external
connections or handoff paths". Both were false. Two additions fix it without
moving any state, route, card or gate:

- **The model's prompt.** Every local prompt (only when a Cloud provider is
  chosen) carries ONE redacted system line from
  `jarvis_presets.cloud_state_line()`: the chosen service, host and model;
  whether its key is saved (a bool, never a value or fragment); whether it can
  be used now and why not; and the standing switch. It also says that choosing
  the preset sends nothing and that email, files, credentials, stored memory,
  pictures, the screen and a tainted conversation never go. No key, message or
  private text is in it. A backend with no chosen provider adds no line, so a
  PC with no cloud set up keeps the old prompt byte for byte.
- **The fixed chat answers.** Ten sentence shapes are answered with no model
  from `jarvis_presets.cloud_state()` and `jarvis_chatbot_api`'s presence-only
  key reads: "are you connected to my deepseek api?", "do you have my deepseek
  key?", "are you using the cloud right now?", "is this answer from deepseek or
  the local model?", "how do I escalate something to the cloud?", "what gets
  sent when you use the cloud?", "what never gets sent?", "can you call the
  deepseek api for this?", "is the cloud on/off?" and "which provider is the
  cloud preset using?". They say the real provider/key/readiness/switch state,
  never the key or a fragment, and quote the one privacy rule. A generic "what
  is the cloud?" is not over-captured. The three real doors are named exactly:
  the Try the cloud model button, the standing switch, and "send this to the
  cloud" in the newest message.

Tests: `backend/test_cloud_honesty_state.py` (40 checks: the system line in a
stub prompt, all ten shapes in every state, no key in any answer, no model
call, no over-capture). A chosen provider whose key is not saved, whose monthly
limit is unset, or whose model cannot be used says so rather than pretending.

### 145.1a The provider you choose is the provider that answers (added 2026-11-07)

The owner's Q1/B6 ruling, after the 2026-11-07 options-understanding audit
measured the defect in the live code. `jarvis_chatbot_api.lane_service()` was a
hard-coded `("deepseek_api", "deepseek-flash")`: the Presets Cloud row, the
approval card and `/api/reach` named the chosen service while the request still
went to `api.deepseek.com`. Since this change the ONE lane resolves its service
**at request time** from `cloud-choice.json` (`jarvis_presets.cloud_chosen()`);
`DEFAULT_LANE` (DeepSeek, the owner's 2026-10-06 choice) is only the fallback
when **no** provider is chosen. That single read puts the chosen provider behind
the key lookup (`lane_key`), the host and URL (`cloud_lane`), `/api/reach`'s
cloud row (`lane_status`), the one `change_own_config` card's words
(`_cloud_card_text`, `_escalate_card_text`) and the chat answers
(`cloud_state_line` and the key question, which now names the CHOSEN provider's
company and key state instead of hard-wired DeepSeek). A chosen Mistral, OpenAI,
Groq, xAI or OpenRouter therefore can never send to DeepSeek - and a chosen
provider whose key is not saved keeps the old behaviour: no lane is offered, and
the PC's own sentence says why. A lane name this module does not know resolves
to the chosen service too (one cloud service per PC), and only to
`DEFAULT_LANE` while no choice is recorded. **There is no Anthropic service in
this tree**; the six are openai, deepseek, mistral, xai, openrouter and groq.

**The fixed chat answers: see the six, and change the choice.**
`cloud_provider_list` (READ-ONLY) answers "which cloud providers can I use?",
"what cloud providers are supported", "do you support <service>", "can I use
<service>", "can I use two cloud providers" and "which provider is the cloud
preset using" from `jarvis_presets.cloud_providers()`/`cloud_chosen()`: the six
by their own company and short name, whether each key is saved (presence only -
never a key or a fragment), which one is chosen, and the one-at-a-time rule.
`cloud_provider_ask` (READ-ONLY) answers "change the cloud provider" with no
service named: which six there are, the exact sentence that works, and that ONE
card asks first. `cloud_provider_choose` - "switch my cloud provider to
mistral", "switch to mistral", "use mistral instead of deepseek", "choose
openrouter as my cloud provider" - calls
`jarvis_presets.apply_cloud(provider=...)`, the SAME function the Presets Cloud
row calls: a service this PC cannot use is refused BEFORE any card, ONE
`change_own_config` card is raised, and `cloud-choice.json` is written only
after that yes. It is a PC action like the row itself - the phone still only
reads the cloud state - and the answer never claims a change the route did not
make.

Tests: `backend/test_options_understanding.py` (the chosen-provider proof for
all six patched in memory, the key answer naming the chosen provider, the chat
door's `change_own_config` card and its refusal-before-card, and
reach/card/answer/lane agreement after a chosen Mistral),
`backend/test_chatbot_api.py` (the lane's transport).

**Q7 P0 - the privacy backstop is harder to get past (2026-11-07).**
`jarvis_router._PRIVATE_TERMS` gains home address, street address, mailing
address, postal address, "my/our address" and phone number (it already held
ssn, social security, passport, driver's licence, routing number, credit card,
bank words and "medical"). Its old `\bdiagnos\w*` was too broad and is narrowed
to MEDICAL contexts - `medical diagnosis`, `diagnosed with <condition>`, and the
owner's or a family member's possessive ("my diagnosis", "my son's diagnosis") -
so a technical prompt such as "diagnose this test failure", "the diagnostic
logs" or "root-cause diagnosis of the crash" can escalate normally again. The
health words further down the list still catch a condition named without the
word "diagnosis". A false match only keeps a question local (quality), a miss
sends words to a cloud model (privacy), so the list errs toward local.
Tests: `backend/test_router_private_terms.py`.

**Q7 - auto-escalation semantics (kept, and now pinned).** The default when the
standing cloud-escalation switch is OFF is detect-and-ask: a hard question is
only OFFERED (gate `"offer"`, one card, `auto: false`). When the owner turns the
standing switch ON through its own `change_own_config` card, the complexity
router may auto-escalate (`auto: true`) **only** a prompt that passes every
gate above the yes: Lockdown, a tainted conversation, a picture, the screen's
words, an attached file, a private word, a pasted secret, complexity under the
threshold, a spent budget, and a PC with no lane offered. The switch waives the
per-question yes and nothing else. Tests:
`backend/test_options_understanding.py` (every gate driven with the switch ON
and OFF) and `backend/test_cloud_escalate_setting.py`.

### 145.2 What a cloud answer is corrected with, and `cloud_refused` (added 2026-10-28)

From the 2026-10-27 AI-safety audit (`.dsh-scratch/AUDITS-2026-10-27/partner-ai-safety.md`, H1 and M1). Two things changed about a cloud turn, and **no existing key moved or changed meaning** - the header gains ONE key, and only when it applies.

**The answer carries the honesty lines.** An answer that came back on a cloud lane is now followed, in the same body, by the same plain lines a local answer gets: the "nothing was actually done" line when the answer claims an action nothing ran, and the four newer corrections (a claimed search, the feature guide's contents, a calculation, a setting claimed unavailable). A cloud lane offers no tools at all, so on that lane a claim of action can never be backed - which is exactly why the line matters there. In a streamed answer the lines arrive as one ordinary `delta.content` chunk AFTER the model's words and BEFORE the `finish_reason` / `data: [DONE]` event; in a whole JSON reply they are appended to `choices[0].message.content`. Nothing else about the answer changes, and a spoken turn gets the version with no brackets.

**A crisis turn is answered on this PC, whatever lane was picked.** When the newest message is a distress message (`jarvis_wellbeing.crisis_in_turn` - the last message, when it is the owner's), a cloud lane is refused for that turn: the local model answers it and the fixed 988/911 help text follows the answer. This is not a setting and no client can turn it off. The route header says what happened rather than pretending the pick was honoured:

| key | what it holds |
|---|---|
| `cloud_refused` | **New, 2026-10-28.** `"crisis"` - this turn was picked or routed for a cloud lane and was answered on this PC instead, because the newest message is a distress message. Absent on every other turn. |
| `lane` | the model that REALLY answered - the local one when `cloud_refused` is present |
| `where` | `"local"` when `cloud_refused` is present |
| `reason` | the router's own reason, then `"; answered on this PC: a message like this is never sent to a cloud provider"` |

Both apps already draw the calm panel from `"wellbeing": "crisis"` (§38.1) and never read the answer aloud for such a turn; `cloud_refused` is there so a reader can say WHY the badge says Local after a cloud lane was chosen. A client that does not know the key is unaffected - it sees an ordinary local answer.

Tests: `backend/test_cloud_honesty.py` (the patch round trip on the published base, the cloud lines equal to a local turn's for the same words, the lines landing before the stream ends for a streamed and a whole reply, and the crisis block rebinding the lane), `backend/test_wellbeing.py` (the pasted/share/voice-unverified cases and the fast path's refusal).

## 146. App control on the phone: one allow-list, ONE card, ONE atomic step (backend half, added 2026-10-19)

The owner asked for "fuller automation inside other apps" and then for the
accessibility service to be an **option** in the Android app (2026-10-19). The
architecture that follows this project's rules is: **the PC is the brain and
the gate; the phone is the hands.** The phone may never decide or approve
anything - this PC-side module turns one request into ONE approval card and
then hands back exactly the step that card listed, one at a time, re-checking
the screen the phone shows it.

**The run starts on the phone** (the owner's decision, 2026-10-20): the owner
types what they want in the app on the phone; the phone sends those words and
its masked screen to the PC, and the PC's **local model** proposes exactly ONE
atomic step. That model is picked deliberately, through the project's own lane
table: the **Agentic + Vision preset's model, `qwen3.5:9b` on the main lane**
(the 2060, 196k context), never the fast lane by accident, never a cloud model
and never the heavy Coding 30B - one strict-JSON step does not justify evicting
every other lane. That proposal is not trusted: it goes through this module's
own validation and refusal list before any card, and the card names the app,
the ONE step, that the phone asked, and **which local model planned it**. There
is **no PC-to-phone channel**, no multi-step plan on one card: the next step is
another request and another card.

**The backend half.** The Android `AccessibilityService`, the allow-list
screen, the running banner and the one-tap Stop live in `jarvis-client` (its
own slice), and the feature is **OFF by default**. It is added by
`backend/app-control.patch` (three POST routes in `jarvis_hud.py`) and the
shipped module `backend/jarvis_app_control.py` (twin in `jarvis-backend/`); the
patch sits after `presets.patch` and before `plugin-loader.patch`, which must
stay last.

**The switch.** `[app_control] enabled = false` in the framework template. A
settings file with no `[app_control]` table reads as OFF - a missing section is
never permission - and this slice adds no way to switch it on. While it is
off, all three routes answer `409 {"ok": false, "available": false, "error":
"App control is switched off on this PC. It is off by default, and this build
has no switch yet - nothing was changed."}` - and the planning route calls no
model at all.

### `POST /api/app-control/run` - start ONE carded action

Same origin and token checks as every other write; body is one JSON object:

```
{"allowed": ["com.google.android.deskclock"], the OWNER'S allow-list, from the phone's Settings
 "app": "com.google.android.deskclock",      the app the ONE step is in; must be on the list
 "app_name": "Clock",                        the label the card shows (falls back to the package)
 "step": {"action": "tap",                   tap | swipe | type | back | home
          "target": {"id": "com.google.android.deskclock:id/search", "text": "Search",
                     "class": "android.widget.TextView", "bounds": [0,100,1080,200]},
          "text": "only for type", "why": "open search"},
 "snapshot": {"app": "com.google.android.deskclock", "title": "Clock",
              "controls": [ ...the masked controls read just now... ]}}
```

Answers:

| code | body | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `202` | `{"ok": true, "run": "<id>", "status": "pending", "app": ..., "verb": ..., "message": "Approve the card ... Nothing runs until you do."}` | ONE `change_own_config` card is up. **Nothing has run.** |
| `400` | `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}` | bad JSON/allow-list/step shape, a type step with no text (or over 200 characters) - a sentence, never a traceback |
