| `409` | `{"ok": false, "available": false, "error": ...}` | the feature is off; or an empty allow-list ("No apps are allowed yet..."); or the app is not on the list; or one of the refusals below; or another run is already waiting; or the framework tier is not `ask` |
| `503` | `{"available": false, "error": "ImportError: ..."}` | `jarvis_app_control.py` is not in the backend folder |

**The card** (action `change_own_config`, raised on the card's own thread; its
`detail` carries the same text plus `app`, `app_name`, `verb` and a `what` line
- never a snapshot). Since F17 (2026-10-20) it names the human app, its
package, the exact verb and target label, and **where the permission came
from**:

> Jarvis wants to perform 1 step in Clock (com.google.android.deskclock) on
> your phone (allowed on phone): tap "Search".
>
> Nothing else will be tapped or sent without another card.
>
> You asked: open search.
>
> Nothing is touched until you say yes. The phone checks the screen again just
> before it acts; a screen that changed stops the run. Stop on the phone
> cancels it.
>
> If you say no: nothing is touched, and nothing runs.

`(allowed on phone)` means the phone's list is the only permission;
`(allowed on this PC and your phone)` means the PC keeps its own list and the
app is on both. A `type` step adds `The exact text: "<the text>"` so the owner
approves the exact words; that text is on the local card only, never in the
audit log.

**The allow-list is the owner's, and empty means nothing.** It lives on the
phone (his Settings screen), is carried in every request, and this module only
validates and enforces it: it never adds an app, never has a default, and
refuses shapes that are not Android package names (at most 64 per request).
`allowed: []` or a missing list refuses every request in words and raises no
card.

**The PC's own allow-list (F17, 2026-10-20).** `[app_control]
allowed_packages` in the PC's framework config is a second list, **empty by
default**. Empty keeps the rule above - the phone's list is the permission, and
the card says `(allowed on phone)`. Non-empty means the app must be on **both**
lists: a run request can never widen it, and an app the phone allows but the PC
does not is refused before any card. Every entry is still subject to the hard
denylist below.

**Refused outright, before any card exists - the hard denylist first (F17,
2026-10-20), whatever either allow-list says:** Jarvis's own packages
(`com.jarvis.*`); Android's system settings, permission controller and package
installer (`com.android.settings`, `com.google.android.permissioncontroller`,
`com.android.packageinstaller` and their variants); well-known password
managers (1Password, Bitwarden, KeePass, LastPass, Dashlane and others); and
well-known banking, wallet and payment apps. Each is refused in plain words
naming the human app, so **the enable runbook's measurement app can no longer
be Android Settings** - use a harmless app such as the phone's calculator or
clock.

Then, also before any card: a password/credential field (target flagged
`password`, or the label/target/why names one); a 2FA/one-time code field; an
app or label that looks like a bank, payment or money app; a step that would
send, post, share, message or email; a step that would delete, move, rename or
uninstall; any action other than tap/swipe/type/back/home; a plan that names one
of `jarvis_gate._PROTECTED`'s files; and any run while
`jarvis_gate.taint_active()` is true (outside text may be steering the
conversation - acting then is what the latch exists to stop).

### `POST /api/app-control/plan` - the owner's words, the LOCAL model's ONE step, ONE card

Added 2026-10-20 (the owner chose: **the run starts on the phone**). Same origin
and token checks as every other write. Request:

```
{"allowed": ["com.google.android.deskclock"],
 "want": "turn on Wi-Fi",                      the owner's own words, 1..200 characters
 "snapshot": {"app": "com.google.android.deskclock", "title": "Clock",
              "controls": [ ...the masked controls the phone just read... ]}}
```

The plan is made **on this PC**, by **the local model only**, over the owner's
words and the masked controls (ids, words, types, bounds - a password field was
never read). It is asked for **one JSON step in the `/run` shape**, with Ollama's
strict `format` constraint; nothing else from its answer is used. **No cloud
model and no network beyond the local lane**: a missing local model is a plain
sentence, never a guessed step and never a fallback to a different brain.

**Which local model (the owner's question, 2026-10-20).** `_proposal_model` is
resolved through the project's own lane/model table (`jarvis_presets.LANES` and
the Agentic + Vision preset): `qwen3.5:9b` on the **main** lane first; then the
same model on another LOCAL lane; then another local general model from the
framework table. The raw fast lane (`:11434`) is never a candidate, a cloud
model is refused by the loopback/remote checks, and the heavy Coding 30B is
excluded even from the fallback. If nothing local is installed the answer is the
existing `MODEL_FAILED` sentence. The 202 names the chosen model (`"model"`,
`"lane"`) and the card adds a line like *"Planned locally by qwen3.5:9b."*; the
audit line keeps its app + verb shape and never carries the model.

**The prompt is fenced twice.** The screen labels are scrubbed with the
project's own `jarvis_scrub` (secrets and one-time codes never reach the model)
and anything that scans as a planted instruction is replaced; the whole control
list is then put inside explicit `<untrusted-screen-data>` markers and the model
is told those lines are data, never instructions. The owner's own `want` words
are refused against the same category word lists BEFORE the model call, so a
"send a message" or "delete that" request never spends one. A model that says
`"scroll"` is normalised to the phone's `swipe` **inside this parser only** - the
canonical five verbs in the contract are untouched.

Answers:

| code | body | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `202` | `{"ok": true, "run": "<id>", "step": "tap \"Search\"", "card_waiting": true, "model": "qwen3.5:9b", "lane": "main", "message": "Approve the card ..."}` | ONE `change_own_config` card is up. **Nothing has been performed.** The card names the app, the ONE step, *"you asked on your phone: ..."* and *"Planned locally by qwen3.5:9b."*; the phone waits on `/step` exactly as for `/run`. |
| `400` | `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}` | a bad body, a missing/over-200-character `want`, an empty/unreadable allow-list, an app not on the list (or a snapshot app that is not), or a snapshot with no controls - plain words, **no model call** |
| `409` | `{"ok": false, "available": false, "error": ..., "pending": ...}` | the feature is off (no model call), the taint latch is set, a run is already waiting, the framework tier is not `ask`, the snapshot's app is on the **hard denylist**, the PC's own `allowed_packages` list does not include it, or the owner's `want` itself names a refused category (a send/delete/money/password/2FA word) - **no model call, no card** |
| `422` | `{"ok": false, "error": "I could not work out one safe step from that screen. ..."}` | the model did not answer, or its answer is not one usable step; or the proposal fails the same validation/refusal list `/run` uses (not one of the five actions, a control the phone did not send, a password/2FA/money/send/delete step). The reason is always a **closed-world plain sentence** (the validator's own words, or "No matching button or field was visible on that screen") - never raw model JSON or an exception. **No card was raised.** |

**The proposal is never trusted and never widened.** It is put through
`validate_plan()` and the refusals above exactly as a phone-sent `/run` plan is,
so the model cannot name a control the phone did not send, a refused category,
or an action outside `tap/swipe/type/back/home`; the phone still never chooses
the step and still can only perform the ONE step the `/step` route returns. The
audit line stays app + verb only; the owner's words and any typed text are on
the local card, never in the audit log.

### `POST /api/app-control/step` - the phone asks for the ONE approved step

```
{"run": "<id>", "snapshot": {...}}     -> the ONE approved step, or a state
{"run": "<id>", "stop": true}          -> stops at once (no card: stopping is the safe direction)
{"run": "<id>", "result": "done"|"failed"}   after doing it
```

| answer | body | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `202` | `{"ok": true, "status": "pending", "message": "..."}` | the card is not answered yet; **no step is handed over** |
| `200` | `{"ok": true, "status": "step", "run": ..., "step": {"action", "target"?, "text"?}}` | exactly ONE step, taken from the approved plan - never from this request; it is handed out once |
| `200` | `{"ok": false, "status": "stopped", "error": "The screen changed ..."}` | the fresh snapshot no longer matches: wrong app in front, the control gone, renamed, disabled, or now a password field - the run STOPS rather than guess |
| `200` | `{"ok": false, "status": "denied"}` / `"timed_out"` / `"refused"` | the card was not approved: **nothing ran** |
| `409` | `{"ok": false, "status": "delivered"}` | the step was sent; report `"result": "done"` or `"failed"` after it runs |
| `409` | `{"ok": false, "status": "done"|"stopped"}` | that run is finished |
| `400`/`404` | `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}` | bad body, or an unknown run id |

**The run state machine:** `pending -> approved -> delivered -> done`, with
`stopped` (changed screen, expired after 900 s, stopped by the owner, or taint
latched), `denied`, `timed_out`, `refused` and `failed` as the ways a run ends.
ONE run at a time: a second request while one waits is a `409` and raises no
second card. The approved step is re-verified against the phone's fresh
snapshot, and the sentence says which thing changed in plain words.

**Audit:** `app_control.requested`, `.approved/.denied/.timed_out/.refused`,
`.step`, `.done/.stopped` - each line carries the app package and the verb (and
counts), **never the typed text, never the screen's words, never a snapshot**.
The card (a local approvals row) is the only place the exact step is written
down, so the owner can judge it; the audit trail cannot become the leak the
gate's own `_redact` comment warns about.

**What this does not do:** it never performs a step on the PC (there is no
desktop input here); it never runs anything before the card says yes; it never
lets the phone change the plan; it never switches itself on; and it sends
nothing anywhere - the three routes are the owner's own private link, local
model only, with no cloud service and no public tunnel.

Tests: `backend/test_app_control.py` - off by default, empty allow-list refuses
everything, unlisted app refuses, ONE card and nothing runs before approval,
denied/timed-out/refused/wrong-tier runs nothing, the approved step is the
plan's own, stop-on-change (wrong app / vanished / renamed / disabled / became
a password field), every refused category before any card, Stop is immediate,
one run at a time, the audit line is app+verb only while the card shows the

typed text; the planning round (the local model pinned to the main lane's
`qwen3.5:9b`, only masked and scrubbed labels inside the untrusted-data block,
the owner's refused words and the hard denylist refused BEFORE the model, the
`"scroll" -> "swipe"` normalisation in the parser only, a closed-world 422, the
model named on the 202 and the card but never in the audit); and the patch's
own pins (three routes, harness position, no install-block line, `_stack.py`'s
RATCHET unchanged).

## 147. The setup questionnaire: a guided path through the settings that already exist (backend half, added 2026-10-20)

The owner asked (2026-10-20): *"there should be a setup questionnaire when
someone first starts jarvis (or can be filled out again) if they want jarvis to
act a different way overall ... a series of questions with multiple choices ...
jarvis sets the settings with a summary for the user at the end ... that the
user can choose to accept afterwards".* The design is
`.dsh-scratch/DESIGN-SETUP-QUESTIONNAIRE-2026-10-20.md`. **The backend half and
the app half are both built** (S2, added 2026-10-20, below): the desktop page
and the phone's read-only card call these routes now, and nothing about the
permission model changes.

**It is a GUIDE, not a second settings system.** `backend/jarvis_setup.py`
(shipped whole, twin in `jarvis-backend/`) holds 25 ordered questions in seven
sections, and their options, as pure data. Every option maps to an EXISTING
setter: the `BoolSetting`s and named setters in `jarvis_settings_registry.py`
(which call the exact function the matching Settings control calls, with the
same tier check and the same words), plus `jarvis_asks_first.py` for the "how
careful" bundle and the reading tools. It invents no gate action or tier, adds no latch,
switches no model, and never calls a preset's apply route: the "what will you
mostly use it for" answer is a **recommendation** only (its `id`/`title` come
from `jarvis_presets.PRESETS`; applying one stays the preset selector's own
`POST /api/work/apply` and its ONE `switch_model` card).

**Wave B (2026-11-03) renamed the card "Personalize Jarvis"** and widened the
question set to these 25 in seven sections. The answers already saved still
prefill it, and a partial retake now keeps every earlier answer: the PC merges
what was submitted into what was saved instead of replacing it.

**The switch/flag:** none of its own. The routes are installed by
`backend/setup.patch` (ONE install block, after `presets.patch` and
`app-control.patch`, immediately before `plugin-loader.patch`, whose hunk is
re-anchored onto setup.patch's last two printed lines). When `jarvis_setup.py`
is missing, the four routes are simply absent and the boot banner says so.
Nothing about the questionnaire is on by itself: it is only read when an app
asks, and an app that never calls it changes nothing.

### `GET /api/setup` - the questions, the current values, the last answers

Read-only, behind the same origin and token checks as every route:

    {"available", "version": 2, "completed_version": 1, "runs": 3,
     "dismissed_at": <float or null>, "answered_count": 9,
     "in_progress": {"section", "question", "started_at", "draft_answers"},
     "sections": [{"id", "title"}],
     "questions": [{"id", "title", "help", "section", "version", "multi",
                    "options": [{"id", "label", "detail"}], "all_none"}],
     "current": {"<change key>": <current value>},
     "answers": {<question id>: <option id> | [<option id>...]},
     "completed_at": <float or null>,
     "last_outcomes": [{"setting", "label", "effect", "state", "message"}],
     "storage": "setup.json in the Jarvis settings folder",
     "card_wait_s": <seconds>, "about": "..."}

`current` is the PC's own reading, one entry per change; a value that cannot be
read is LEFT OUT rather than guessed. For the "what asks first" rows it is a
boolean: `true` means that action asks first today (its tier in
`jarvis-framework.toml` is `ask`). `answers` and `completed_at` are the last
accepted run, for a re-run's prefill and for a first-run offer to show once.

`version` is the question-set version (`2` today), and `completed_version` is
the one the owner last finished - every question answered - or explicitly kept
with "Keep current settings" (`0` when never, `1` for a file completed before
the new questions, so the first launch after deploy offers the new ones once
instead of claiming the old file is current). **A partial apply does not move
it** (DEF-043, 2026-11-04): answering one question saves that answer and counts
a run, but the offer, the HUD banner and the chat line stay until all 25 are
answered, so `completed_version` and `answered_count` never disagree about the
same read. `runs` is how
many applies have been accepted. `dismissed_at` is when "Not now" was last
pressed, or `null`. `in_progress` is where the desktop card is
(`{section, question, started_at, draft_answers}`), or `{}` when it has not
said. A file from before versioning reads as `version 1`, with
`completed_version 1` when it has a `completed_at` and `0` when it does not;
reading never writes.

`sections` is the seven `{id, title}` pairs in card order, and every question
carries its own `section` and `version`, so neither app types a section id or a
question count. The PC holds 25 questions in seven sections. `answered_count`
counts the question ids that have an answer in `answers` or in the card's draft
- it is the one number both apps and the HUD say "9 of 25" from, and an id that
is no longer in the quiz does not count.

**GET is metadata only** (audited 2026-10-20, Gemini Area 1B): it returns
question text and setting values, and it reads no folder, no account and no
lock/hide list - so there is none in it to leak while App lock or the hide
lists are on. `storage` names the file, not a path. The suite pins that the
whole GET body holds no drive path, home path, email/account id, token or
secret, and that every `current` value is a plain setting value.

### `POST /api/setup/plan` - a READ-ONLY summary

Body `{"answers": {"<question id>": "<option id>" | ["<option id>", ...]}}`;
the two data-level answers `"all"` and `"none"` are expanded for every
choose-any question. Answers for questions the caller leaves out change
nothing. The answer is:

    {"ok", "changes": [{"setting", "label", "question", "from", "to", "effect",
                        "pc_only", "sentence", "change"}],
     "summary": ["Takes effect immediately: ..." | "Will ask you on a card: ..."],
     "skipped": [{"setting", "reason"}],
     "recommendation": {"id", "title", "why"} | null}

**Nothing is written and no card is raised.** `pc_only` is `true` for the
answers Settings itself only lets the PC change - loosening "what asks first",
offering a reading tool, and the face's sky switch - so a caller can say so
before the owner accepts; it is a label on the EXISTING rule, not a new tier.
`effect` is `"card"` exactly where the existing setter would ask: the change's direction is the one its own module
cards (e.g. web search ON, "ask before every search" OFF, an "asks first"
loosening, offering a reading tool), AND the action's tier is read-only checked
through `jarvis_framework.action_tier` - the same machinery the setter uses. If
that tier is not `"ask"` the setter itself refuses, so the change is reported
in `skipped`, never promised. A value that cannot be read is skipped in words,
and an answer already in force is skipped as "already ...". No transcript,
audio, fact or file is ever in this payload.

### `POST /api/setup/apply` - one change at a time, through the existing setters

Body `{"answers": {...}, "confirm": true}`. **Without `confirm: true` it
refuses with 400 and does nothing at all** - the summary must have been accepted
by a person first. Then it calls the mapped setters in a fixed safest-first
order (tightening and cosmetic changes first, then the carded ONs), and:

* every loosening change still raises **its OWN existing card** - never a
  combined card and never an auto-approval. After a carded change it WAITS for
  that card (up to `card_wait_s`, default 300 s), reading only what the
  module already reports (`view()`/`state()`/`status()` and the setting's own
  new value), before raising the next one, so two cards are never on screen at
  once. A card still unanswered when the wait ends is left waiting and the
  outcome says so; nothing is approved by this module;
* a denied, unavailable or failed setting never aborts the rest; `outcomes`
  carries one row per attempted change with a `state` of `changed`,
  `asked-and-approved`, `asked-and-denied`, `asked-no-answer`, `not-available`,
  `not-changed` or `failed`, and a plain sentence;
* only then are the owner's own answers and `completed_at` saved (atomically)
  in `<CONFIG_DIR>/setup.json`. **No chat, fact, voice, picture or file is
  written** - the file holds choice ids and one timestamp. `completed_version`
  becomes `QUIZ_VERSION` only when every question now has an answer; a partial
  apply saves what it was given, counts the run and leaves completion where it
  was, so the offer/banner/chat line continue (DEF-043, 2026-11-04). A partial
  retake also keeps an older `completed_version` a file already had. A damaged
  file is reported by `GET /api/data-health` like every other settings JSON;
  this module falls back to "no answers" rather than raising.

A body that is not a JSON object, or `answers` that is not an object, is 400 in
plain words. **Two more refusals were added by the 2026-10-20 audit (Gemini
Area 1B), both before any setter runs:**

* **Taint:** if `jarvis_gate.taint_active()` says outside text may be steering
  this turn, apply answers **`409`** with `"tainted": true` and the same plain
  sentence every change uses - nothing is changed, no card is raised. The check
  fails CLOSED: a backend whose gate cannot be asked counts as tainted. This
  module only READS the latch (no `latch_taint`, no `clear_taint`, no card of
  its own).
* **PC-only, from another device:** if any answer maps to a PC-only setting
  (loosening "what asks first", offering a reading tool, the sky switch) and
  the request did not come from this PC, the WHOLE apply is refused **`403`**
  with `"pc_only": true` - nothing runs, not even the cosmetic answers in the
  same batch. A LOCAL apply goes ahead and still goes through the EXISTING
  setter, so that setter's own card and its Windows Hello check are never
  bypassed by this questionnaire; the suite proves the local path waits for
  that card and never reports a change while it waits.

Every route is behind the same origin and token checks as every other write;
the answers are the owner's own choices, never private data.
**The apply route passes the request's own `peer`/`local` down to the existing
setters** (read the same way `owner-check.patch`'s wrappers read them), so a
loosening rule or a reading-tool ON still refuses from the phone - and fails
closed when the PC cannot tell where the request came from. `peer is None` is
only the project's documented in-process convention, never how a routed
request is treated.

### `POST /api/setup/progress` - where the owner is in the card (desktop only)

One of three small bodies:

    {"section": "learning", "question": "reworded_memories",
     "draft_answers": {"reworded_memories": "on"}}
        -> 200 {"ok": true, "in_progress": {...}}
    {"dismiss": true}
        -> 200 {"ok": true, "dismissed_at": 1793...}
    {"keep_current": true}
        -> 200 {"ok": true, "completed_version": 2, "dismissed_at": 1793...}

The first records where the owner is: the section and question the card has
open, and the answers drafted so far. `section` is optional, and a value that
is not one of the seven falls back to the question's own section. Every draft
answer is cleaned to the questionnaire's own question ids, and only a string or
a list of strings/numbers is kept - an unknown id or a value of another shape
is dropped, never stored. An explicit empty `draft_answers` (`{}`) clears the
stored draft; a non-empty one is merged, so a choice staged in chat and the
card's own answer both survive.

`{"dismiss": true}` stores `dismissed_at` - the 24-hour "Not now".
`{"keep_current": true}` stores `completed_version = QUIZ_VERSION` and the same
timestamp without touching one answer or one setting: it is "Keep current
settings", not a quiz answer. Both answer `{"ok": true}` with the fields they
recorded.

**It records the owner's own Option ids; it calls no setter, raises no card and
never applies.** It is cardless and gateless on the PC: no approval card, no
taint check, no gate action and no setter. The only file it writes is
`setup.json`, through the module's one save, and the whole read document is
written back, so `answers`, `completed_at`, `outcomes`, `completed_version`,
`runs` and `dismissed_at` are preserved by construction. The draft is never
applied: applying stays `POST /api/setup/apply`, the card's two-press action.

**It is desktop-only.** A request from another device is **`403`** with
`"pc_only": true` and writes nothing - the same `from_this_pc` rule
`/api/setup/apply` uses for its PC-only answers. The desktop card is the
route's only caller for a place and for the two buttons. The HUD banner's
"Not now" reaches it through the shell's `hud_setup_dismiss` command, because
the HUD holds no token and cannot POST. The phone reads progress from
`GET /api/setup` and never moves it.

A body that is not a JSON object, or one that carries neither a known
`question` nor `dismiss`/`keep_current`, is **`400`** in plain words. A missing
or wrong token is **`401`**, before anything is read. **`503`** means the
progress could not be saved, so nothing was recorded.

### The apps (S2, added 2026-10-20; "Personalize Jarvis" from 2026-11-03)

**Desktop Settings → "Personalize Jarvis".** The same card, upgraded in place:
no new window and no second page. Three files and one Rust command
(`jarvis-desktop/src/setup-questionnaire.js`, `setup-bridge.js`,
`setup-settings.js`, `src-tauri/src/setup_questionnaire.rs`). The card shows
the PC's 25 questions in its own order, split by its seven sections behind a
row of section tabs, with the last accepted answers as the prefill. It opens
stepped one question at a time ("Step through one by one"), with Back, Skip and
Next; "Show all" draws the whole list instead. Skip leaves the question out of
the submitted body, so the earlier answer survives. A "show only new /
unanswered" filter shows a question that has no answer yet, or whose own
`version` is newer than `completed_version`, and the count in its label is
computed from that data, never typed. A "8 of 25 answered" line is counted from
the draft. "Take it again" clears the draft and starts at the first question,
and a partial retake now keeps every earlier answer, because the PC merges the
submitted answers into the saved ones instead of replacing them.

Changing an answer asks `POST /api/setup/plan` and draws every change
in the PC's own sentence with its effect - **Instant**, **Asks you on a card**
or **Blocked** - plus everything the PC says would not change and why, and the
preset answer labelled a recommendation only. **A plan writes nothing and
raises no card**, so it is asked whenever the answers change. The one write to
a setting is a two-press action: "Apply these changes", then "Yes, apply them
now". Only the second press builds and sends `confirm: true`; loading the card,
reconnecting the link and changing an answer never apply anything. Applying is
held while the event stream is stale (rule 4). The card says how long one
approval card may wait, and while it runs it says the PC works through the
changes one at a time. An outcome the PC reports as `asked-no-answer` is drawn
as **still waiting** - never as done, never as failed - and the last run's
outcomes are drawn from `GET /api/setup` exactly as the PC saved them. The Rust
command sends only the four bodies, refuses `apply` unless its `confirm`
argument is exactly `true`, and puts `confirm` in no other body; the page
itself names no route and no gate action, so nothing here invents an action or
a tier. A plan or a progress note can never carry `confirm`.

**Two buttons write progress, not settings.** "Not now" sends
`{"dismiss": true}`, and "Keep current settings" sends `{"keep_current": true}`:
neither carries an answer, calls a setter or raises a card, and the second is
how the owner says they are happy as they are in one press. The stepper's own
position is sent the same way, debounced, so the phone and the HUD can say
where the PC's card is. None of this is held on a stale link: a position or a
dismissal is not a change.

**The rest of the desktop is the offer, never a second control.** While
`completed_version` is behind `version`, the shell raises ONE quiet
notification per launch - after the app has been up for a minute, and only if
the notification store's `Setup` switch says yes (on by default; quiet hours
hold it, because the quiz can wait). Its body is two counts and nothing else
("9 of 25 answered. Finish now from the Settings card, or press Not now.") -
never a question, never an answer. The HUD draws a banner with the same counts
and two buttons: "Finish now" opens Settings at the card through the HUD's
already-granted navigation, and "Not now" hides the banner for this launch and
records the same 24-hour dismissal through the shell's `hud_setup_dismiss`
command. The tray carries a "Setup unfinished — 9 of 25" row that opens the
same card, and the row is absent, not greyed, once the quiz is done. Nothing
steals focus: the Settings window opens only after the first-run walkthrough
and when the owner presses "Finish now".

**The prompt line follows the same switch** (DEF-044, 2026-11-04). On a local
turn, `jarvis_agent.setup_state_note()` adds ONE system line - "Personalize
Jarvis: the setup quiz is unfinished - N of 25 answered ... nothing in chat may
apply them" - just before the newest user message, only while
`completed_version` is behind `version` AND the `[notifications] setup` switch
(`jarvis_notify_prefs.read()["setup"]`, the "Personalize Jarvis" switch on both
apps' Notifications cards, on by default) is on. Turning the reminder off is
the owner saying they do not want to be reminded, and a chat line is a
reminder; turning it back on restores the line. A finished quiz costs no
tokens, and the line is local-model only. It reads `setup.json` and the one
notification value - it never calls `apply()`, never raises a card, and never
touches a setting.

**Phone: the same questions, read-only.** `net/SetupQuestionnaire.kt` and
`ui/screens/SetupQuestionnairePlate.kt`, on Settings. It reads
`GET /api/setup`, prefills the last accepted answers and draws the same 25
questions split by the PC's own seven sections, behind a row of section tabs
("All sections" first, then the PC's order). It may ask the read-only plan on
one button, drawing the same effects and the same "would not change" reasons.
ONE line says where the PC is: "Not finished - 9 of 25 answered. On the PC this
is at question 8 of 25." while the set is unfinished, or "Finished <date>."
once `completed_version` has reached `version`. It reads the answered count and
`in_progress` from GET and never moves them: **it has no apply path and no
progress path at all**, never posts `/api/setup/apply` or
`/api/setup/progress`, and the card says the changes are made on the PC. That
is a decision, not a missing screen: applying calls the existing setters one at
a time and waits on each existing card (a pass can take minutes), and several
of those changes are PC-only by rules that already exist - `jarvis_asks_first`
refuses a loosening request from any device but the PC. A phone button would
either fail halfway or sit behind cards it cannot answer.
`tools/check_parity.py` classifies `/api/setup` and `/api/setup/plan` as
`ported` and `/api/setup/apply` and `/api/setup/progress` as `deliberate` (the
403 from another device is the enforcement, not this sentence);
`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8 records it with the reason.

**The questions are the PC's, in both apps.** Neither app hardcodes a question
id, title, section or option. Both tests read the generated
`backend/fixtures/setup_questions.json` (`tools/gen_setup_questions.py`, written
from `backend/jarvis_setup.py`'s own `QUESTIONS`; the desktop suite runs
`--check` and compares it to the live module), so a reworded question fails a
test until the fixture is regenerated. The desktop suite is
`jarvis-desktop/tests/setup-questionnaire.mjs` (the PC's real 25 questions, the
seven sections, the stepper's next-question rule, the "new / unanswered" filter,
the draft and "All"/"None", the read-only plan body, the one apply body, the
three progress bodies, the stale-link gate, honest outcomes, the bridge's four
calls, and source pins that no route or gate action is in the page, nothing
applies on load, and the HUD's one dismissal command is the only write the
banner needs); the Rust module carries its own body/timeout tests; the phone's
is `SetupQuestionnaireTest.kt` (the same fixture, the prefill, the read-only
plan, the sections and the one progress line, and a pin that no apply or
progress path exists in the two phone files).

`backend/test_setup.py` is the proof, with no network, no model, no
microphone and no owner's PC: every question/option maps to a real setter;
`plan()` writes nothing and marks every direction's card correctly (and marks a
non-`ask` tier as skipped); "All"/"None" expand at the data level; `apply()`
refuses without confirm, calls exactly the mapped setters, waits for each card
before the next (approved and denied), continues past a failed setting, saves
only the answers, and round-trips them for prefill; the module imports no
model lane and no network, reads the gate's taint latch and never sets or
clears it; the taint refusal (409) and the remote PC-only whole-refusal (403)
happen before any setter; `pc_only` marks exactly the three PC-only families;
GET exposes no path or account id; and the four routes keep the origin/token
order.

`backend/test_setup_quiz.py` is the Wave B proof, with the same no-network,
no-PC rule: the question set is 25 in seven sections with the 14 existing ids
unchanged and in their order; every new `choice`/`number` change names a real
Settings row and one of its own Option ids; a partial retake keeps every
earlier answer, and an old three-key file reads as version 1 with
`completed_version` 1; a partial apply saves its answer and counts its run but
does NOT move `completed_version` (the offer, banner and chat line stay), while
an apply with all 25 answered does (DEF-043); `progress()` writes only
`in_progress` and preserves
every other key, refuses a non-object and a body with nothing to record, cleans
a bogus draft answer away, and is refused with 403 from another device; the
progress route keeps the origin/token order and a bad body is 400;
`{"keep_current": true}` sets `completed_version` without touching an answer or
calling `apply()`; `setup_state_note()` adds its one line only while the quiz is
unfinished AND the "Personalize Jarvis" notification switch is on, and with the
switch off the turn gets the plain messages back (DEF-044); and the module still
imports no model lane, switches no model, and `_run_setup_quiz` carries no
`confirm`.

typed text, and the patch's own pins (two routes, harness position, no
install-block line, `_stack.py`'s RATCHET unchanged).

## 148. Reverse engineering with REA: the full toolbox through one tool, one card per action (added 2026-10-20, expanded 2026-11-04)

The owner asked for "reverse engineer anything" integration on 2026-10-20, and on
2026-11-04, asked how far it should go, chose **"Also install the full REA toolbox"**: *"debug
and patch, not just read: attach a debugger, watch a running program, use Frida and patch files -
the real toolkit, all local"*, plus REA's own package installed by Jarvis and all of its actions
exposed through the one tool. The upstream is REA (`morluto/rea`, npm `rea-agents@6.7.0`, MIT) -
a separate local program. It is **not** linked into Jarvis, no code is copied, and it ships
**OFF**.

**Why one tool and not 207.** REA's MCP server really serves **207 tools**. Measured from the
real server on 2026-10-20: 723,936 bytes of input schemas and 92,270 bytes of descriptions -
about **272,000 tokens** by `jarvis_agent.estimate_tokens`'s own rule, many times the 9B model's
whole window. So `backend/jarvis_rea.py` exposes ONE tool, `rea_investigate`, and the model never
sees REA's schemas. The existing MCP bridge (`jarvis_mcp.py`) supplies the transport (a Windows
Job Object, the stdio JSON-RPC reader, the caps) - this module does not write a second MCP
client. The bridge's read-only-first rule would hide every REA tool anyway: only 2 of REA's 71
inspection-family tools claim `readOnlyHint`.

**Two switches, both off by default.** `[rea] enabled = false` in the template, and the tool must
also be named in `[tools].enabled`. With either missing the tool costs no tokens and is not
offered.

**The one tool, and its 200 actions.** Arguments: `action`, `target` (a full path inside "Folders
Jarvis may look in", when the action takes a file or folder), `arguments` (that action's own
settings, by name), and for the two first-slice actions `query`/`what` and `format`. Actions:

| category | what it covers (REA's own tool names, one action each) |
|---|---|
| ready / install | `doctor`, `install` |
| the first slice | `inspect_javascript_app`, `inspect_binary`, `inspect_apk`, `inspect_capture`, `inspect_sqlite`, `open_native_binary`, `query_native_binary` |
| static analysis | one action per REA tool: `inspect_pe_resources`, `analyze_swift_types`, `inspect_managed_artifact`, `inspect_wasm_artifact`, `inspect_go_binary`, `inspect_rust_binary`, `inspect_firmware_regions`, `inspect_packet_capture`, `decode_android_resources`, ... |
| dynamic debugging | `start_gdb_session`, `close_gdb_session`, `gdb_console`, `gdb_session_status`, `start_rizin_debug_session`, `close_rizin_debug_session`, `rizin_debug_command`, `rizin_debug_session_status`, `execute_rizin_command`, `cutter_command`, `list_cutter_sessions` |
| Frida | `start_frida_session`, `close_frida_session`, `load_frida_script`, `unload_frida_script`, `instrument_with_frida`, `resume_frida_session`, `frida_session_status`, `list_frida_devices`, `list_frida_processes` |
| live runtime capture | `capture_process_scenario`, `capture_native_ui_scenario`, `capture_browser_scenario`, `capture_electron_scenario`, `capture_web_screenshot`, `observe_javascript_runtime`, `observe_web_session`, `observe_web_execution`, `observe_native_ui`, `observe_native_calls` |
| process memory | `read_bytes`, `search_bytes`, `read_function_instructions`, `trace_native_values` |
| sessions | `binary_session`, `close_binary`, `list_documents`, `list_segments`, `list_procedures`, `list_strings`, `list_names`, `list_bookmarks`, `gdb_session_status`, ... |
| export (local folder only) | `export_evidence_bundle`, `export_web_scripts`, `pull_adb_file`, `pull_adb_package`, `capture_adb_screen`, `collect_adb_bugreport`, `extract_artifact`, `extract_firmware`, `recover_javascript_sources` |
| the owner's own phone | every ADB READ and CAPTURE: `list_adb_devices`, `list_adb_packages`, `list_adb_processes`, `read_adb_logcat`, `read_adb_setting`, `inspect_adb_*`, `capture_adb_screen`, `collect_adb_bugreport`, `pull_adb_*` |

The full list is `jarvis_rea.ACTION_ORDER` (200 names), and the model's schema enum is read from
that same tuple, so the two cannot drift. Every name there was measured on this PC on 2026-11-04
by starting the pinned package's own server and asking `tools/list`: **207 tools**, catalogue
digest `af39310c...`, which is what this module pins. No name is guessed, and the names the first
slice refused that no REA tool answers to (including `debug_with_gdb`) are gone.

**One gap in the catalogue itself.** REA 6.7.0 has no "apply this patch file" tool. Patching a
local copy is done with a debugger session's own commands (`cutter_command`,
`rizin_debug_command`, `gdb_console`, `instrument_with_frida`), so no action claims to patch a
file when only the session's memory changed. GDB sessions are Linux-only in REA, so on this
Windows PC those four actions refuse before the card and say why.

**The owner's Q1 guardrails, enforced in this module (2026-11-04).** The ruling approved the
full toolbox with five guardrails; two were already code (rule 2's local-only scan of every
setting, rule 5's pinned install). The other three were the recorded residual and are now
enforced in `jarvis_rea.py`, before the card, not trusted to REA:

1. **A credential store is never a target.** `lsass` (by name or `lsass.exe`), `vaultcmd`,
   Windows Credential Manager's own folders (`Microsoft\Credentials`, `Microsoft\Protect`,
   `Windows\NTDS\ntds.dit`), and the browser login stores (`Login Data`, `cookies.sqlite`,
   `logins.json`, `key4.db`) are refused by process name, by file name and by any part of a
   path. A live action (`capture_*`, `observe_*`, `start_*_session`, `instrument_with_frida`,
   `load_frida_script`, `gdb_console`, `rizin_debug_command`, `cutter_command`,
   `execute_rizin_command`, the process-memory reads) is scanned in **every** setting, because a
   command, a script or an `argv` list can name the store instead of a plain path. Every other
   action is scanned where a setting names a file or a program, so a static read of a copied
   `logins.json` is refused the same way - while a search query that merely contains the word is
   not, because a word is not a target. The sentence says which rule it serves and that nothing
   was run: `CREDENTIAL_REFUSED`.
2. **Nothing is written in place.** `cutter_command`, `rizin_debug_command`,
   `execute_rizin_command`, `gdb_console`, `instrument_with_frida` and `load_frida_script` are
   the write-capable surfaces. A command carrying a write form - rizin's `w` family (`w`, `wa`,
   `wb`, `wt`, `wx`, `wo`, `wv`, `wop`, ...) and `oo+`/`ood`, GDB's `set write on`, `restore`,
   `dump binary|ihex|srec|verilog|tekhex` and `set {type}addr`, Frida's `Memory.write*` /
   `writeByteArray` / `writeUtf8String` / `writePointer` / `File.write` / `writeAll` - is refused
   unless it names a NEW `<name>.patched<extension>` output inside a listed folder, or the
   session's own file is already such a copy (remembered from `start_rizin_debug_session`).
   `C:\Windows\`, `C:\Program Files\Windows Defender\`, and `python.exe` (and `pythonw.exe`),
   `jarvis-desktop.exe`, `ollama.exe` are refused as patch targets outright. An allowed write
   records a **before/after SHA-256 receipt** in the module (`write_receipts()`, and in the
   result), so "the original is untouched" is a measurement: the original's hash before and
   after, whether it changed, and the new file's hash.
3. **Every live session has a deadline.** A live action takes `duration_limit_sec` - **60 by
   default, 300 at most** - which is this module's own setting: it is never sent to REA, it is
   named on the one card, and it caps the call's own timeout, so a live call cannot sit there
   longer than the card said. A watch window setting (`duration_ms`, `observation_ms`,
   `timeout_ms`) longer than the approved duration is refused before the card. The module keeps
   a registry of live sessions with their deadlines; a session that outlives its deadline is
   detached with REA's own `close_frida_session` / `close_gdb_session` /
   `close_rizin_debug_session`, and when that cannot be done the REA helper itself is terminated
   (which takes every hook and child with it). This happens in a `finally`, so a failed or
   timed-out call detaches too.

**Still not enforced, said plainly.** (a) Rizin's own `>file` redirection writes a text dump; it
is not on the ruling's list and is not analysed as a write, because it cannot overwrite the file
being analysed. (b) A Frida script given by path is read and scanned up to 200 KB; a longer
script is only partly scanned, and an unreadable one is not scanned at all. (c) The write forms
are the ruling's named list: a write reached through some other primitive (GDB's `call`, for one)
is not detected, and a command that sources ANOTHER script by path (`rizin -i`, GDB's `source`)
is not read - the card still shows the command itself, which is what the owner approves. (d) The
deadline is enforced by the call's own timeout and by the registry sweep at the next live call;
if the whole Jarvis process dies mid-call, the helper dies with it (a Windows Job Object) but no
close tool is called. (e) The receipt proves the original's bytes did not change; it does not say
what the `.patched` copy differs by.

**Every call is ONE approval card.** `rea_investigate` is in `jarvis_agent.NEEDS_A_PERSON`, so a
person's yes is required whatever the tier - including for `doctor` and `install`. `prepare()`
validates the action, its settings, its engine and its target **before** the card, so a bad
request never asks and never starts a program. The target must pass the existing
`jarvis_documents.allowed_path()` folder rule **and** this module's own private-place refusal
(`~/.openjarvis`, browser profiles, credential stores, `.ssh`/`.gnupg`, `Windows\System32\config`);
a listed folder that contains those still cannot be inspected there. An output folder is the one
case where the path need not exist yet.

**Everything stays on this PC (rules 1 and 2).** Every string in `arguments`, and `target`,
is checked: a URL, a `host:port`, a UNC network share or a bare remote address in a setting whose
name says it is an address is refused unless it is loopback (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `::1`).
That is why `capture_browser_scenario` can drive a local page but not a website, and why Frida's
`remote` and CDP's `cdp_endpoint` have to point at this machine.

**Closed-world settings, not a denylist.** The model chooses an action, never a REA tool: an
action not in the table is refused. Inside an action, a setting name that is not one of that
tool's own top-level settings (read from the pinned catalogue) is refused with the list of the
ones it does have, and a required setting that is missing is refused the same way - so nothing
unexpected is ever sent, and no 724 KB of schemas has to be shipped to say so. One setting is
this module's own and is never sent: `duration_limit_sec`, accepted on a live action only, taken
out of the settings before the call and carried on the card instead. The runtime identity check
(`binary_session`) confirms the running program is `rea-agents@6.7.0` with the 207-tool catalog
and digest this build was written against; a mismatch closes the session.

**What is refused, and the rule it serves.** ONE card per call (rule 4). Nothing leaves this PC
(rules 1 and 2). The REA child receives `jarvis_child_env`'s allow-list plus only the provider
paths and switches the owner set - never `HUD_TOKEN`, `JARVIS_TOKEN`, any `*_KEY`, or REA's own
`REA_TOKEN` (rule 3). MIT stays MIT (rule 5). The only by-name refusal left is the six ADB device
**mutators** (`install_adb_package`, `uninstall_adb_package`, `push_adb_file`, `start_adb_app`,
`start_adb_activity`, `stop_adb_app`), and that one is cross-module ownership rather than a core
rule: phone changes already belong to `control_phone` / `[phone_apps]`, with their own card and
allow-list. Debuggers, Frida, live capture, process memory, export and ADB reads are all ordinary
card-gated actions - and every one of them is now under the three Q1 guardrails above: a
credential store is refused as a target, a write is refused unless it lands on a new `.patched`
copy, and a live session carries a duration the owner saw on the card and is detached when it
runs out.

**It installs itself (the owner's decision).** The `install` action runs
`npm install --prefix <config>/tools/rea rea-agents@6.7.0 --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund`
after its own card, then the static egress scan and `doctor`. It installs exactly the pinned
version, writes only inside that folder, and refuses to call the result ready if the package's
`package.json` carries an `install`/`preinstall`/`postinstall` script or if the scan finds a known
analytics or telemetry host in the package's own `dist/`. **The owner's four-point audit's point 3
did not exist in code before this** - the docstring named the scan and nothing performed it - so
it is implemented (`egress_report`) rather than "kept intact". Points 1 and 2 were re-measured on
this PC on 2026-11-04: the npm tarball's sha512 matches `PINNED_INTEGRITY` exactly, and
`package.json` has no lifecycle scripts.

**What comes back.** Chat-template markers are stripped, prompt-injection patterns are flagged,
secrets are scrubbed by `jarvis_scrub`, the text is cut to 6000 characters, and the result is
labelled `untrusted`; the conversation is latched local with
`jarvis_gate.latch_taint(why="rea_analysis")`. The module reports Evidence ids only when REA's own
answer carries them. Since 2026-11-04 the tool is no longer in `jarvis_claims.READ_ONLY_TOOLS`:
it can patch, export and install, so an "I did it" after it is a claim the checker must read.

**Readiness (`doctor`, read-only, no network).** `jarvis_rea.doctor()` answers with
`ready: true|false` and one plain `why` sentence, plus these signals:

| signal | field | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Node | `node.ok`, `node.version` | 22.19+/24.11+/26+; Node 23 and 25 are refused |
| package present | `installed` | a `rea-agents` package exists under `<user>\.openjarvis\tools\rea` |
| pinned version | `version_pinned_ok` | exactly 6.7.0 (and MIT) |
| recorded sha512 | `integrity.ok` | npm's local record compared with the pinned tarball: true, false, or null |
| egress scan | `egress.ok`, `egress.hosts`, `egress.telemetry` | the static scan of the package's own `dist/`: which remote hosts it names, and whether one is a known analytics or telemetry service (false refuses readiness) |
| the audit's four lifecycle names | `egress.lifecycle` | `preinstall`/`install`/`postinstall` found in the package (false refuses readiness) |
| signatures | `signatures.checked` | always false here: npm signatures and SLSA provenance need the network |
| Tier 1 static | `tier1_static_ready` | package + pin + supported Node + clean scans |
| Tier 2 Ghidra | `tier2_ghidra_ready` | `GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR` and `JAVA_HOME` both set |
| Tier 2 JADX | `tier2_jadx_ready` | `REA_JADX_MCP_JAR` or a `jadx` on PATH |
| can it install | `install_ready`, `install_why` | a supported Node and npm on PATH |
| per action | `actions[name].available`, `.why` | whether this PC can do that action right now, and one plain reason when it cannot (JADX, Ghidra, adb, JEB, tshark, or GDB being Linux-only) |

**No route, no patch, no tier change.** There is still no `GET /api/rea/doctor` and no
`jarvis_rea.install()` wiring into the HUD: the actions are reached through the model tool, which
is what the owner asked for. `jarvis_gate`'s mapping is unchanged (`rea_investigate` ->
`run_shell_on_host`, tier `ask`), so this is not a new gate action and no patch is added. Nothing
here becomes a new switch: the two that already existed still decide everything.

Tests: `backend/test_rea.py` - private targets refused before any start, every one of the 200
actions maps to exactly one tool in a fixture of the pinned catalogue's 207 names, every action's
card action is `ask`, the retained refusals are exactly the six ADB mutators, an unknown action
and an unknown setting are refused, a remote endpoint is refused, an output folder may be absent
while a target may not, the install runs the pinned version only and refuses a package with an
install script or a telemetry host, the egress scan reads a fixture package, timeouts per action
class, the child environment carries no Jarvis secret, the taint latch is called, markers
stripped and secrets scrubbed and injections flagged, the bounded output, the Node version range
(22.19+/24.11+/26+, never 23/25), missing-engine refusals before the card, one compact tool in
exactly one group selected by the tool diet, and off-by-default gating on both switches. The
three Q1 guardrails have their own checks: each credential store (LSASS, `vaultcmd`, Credential
Manager's folders, `Login Data`, `cookies.sqlite`, `logins.json`, `key4.db`) denied as a live
target and a static one, an ordinary program and file still allowed, every rizin/GDB/Frida write
form denied, a NEW `.patched` path allowed with its before/after SHA-256 receipt, Windows,
Windows Defender and Jarvis's own programs denied as patch targets, the 60-second default and
the 300-second ceiling on the card, a longer watch window refused, a fake clock proving a
session under its deadline stays and over it is detached with the family's close tool, and the
`finally` path detaching a call that timed out or failed (with the helper terminated when it
cannot be detached by name). A real
REA analysis is NOT-TESTABLE on CI (no engines, no pinned install) and is not claimed as tested;
so is a real Frida attach, a real patch and a real deadline expiry on a live program - those are
covered by fakes and a fake clock, and are not claimed as driven.

## 149. Searchable recordings and videos: readable words and a video's on-screen text kept on the PC, ON by the owner's decision (F5 S2+S3, added 2026-10-19/20)

F5 slice S2, built to the owner's decision of **2026-10-19 14:50 PT**: they
chose **B - keep the transcript text**, over the brief's word-list-only
recommendation, and added **"built in the next slice, on by default."** So this
ships with its switch **ON**: a deliberate owner override, recorded where it
lives (`backend/rebuilt/jarvis-framework.toml`, `[media_index] enabled =
true`, and the same section in the published base's copy).

**S3 (2026-10-20, Gemini post-review item 10) adds the on-screen text of
videos.** S1 already reads a few frames of a video per answer; S3 keeps those
words in the same index, so a slide title, a subtitle or a form on screen is
searchable beside what was said. It is bounded on purpose: at most
`INDEX_OCR_FRAMES` frames per video (spread across the whole file, not just its
opening minutes), at most `INDEX_OCR_CHARS` characters of on-screen text per
video, and the existing per-run cap unchanged. A video with no recognisable
speech is still indexed from its on-screen text. The rows live in the same
table, file, disclosure and Delete as the transcript - no second store.

**What it is.** An index on this PC of the recordings and videos inside the
owner's "Folders Jarvis may look in" list, so "which of my recordings mention
X?" is answered once, from the words themselves. It is ONE SQLite file,
`~/.openjarvis/media-index.db` (`jarvis_framework.CONFIG_DIR`), modelled on
`documents-index.db` but with the difference the owner chose: the **readable
transcript lines are stored**, with their times, because that is what makes a
search show the exact sentence instantly. Since S3 the same file also holds a
video's **readable on-screen text** (from a capped number of frames), one row
per line with its frame time. The module is `backend/jarvis_media_index.py`
and its own docstring is the contract.

**The safeguards (none of them optional in that decision).**

* **Only the listed folders.** Every file goes through the SAME
  `jarvis_documents.allowed_path()` rule S1 uses (hidden folders and protected
  places refused); an index run only walks those folders.
* **Never the audio or video.** The recording is only read, never copied, and
  the original file is untouched. The index stores the words and file details.
* **On-screen text is bounded, and never faked.** For a video only, the PC's
  own text reader reads at most `INDEX_OCR_FRAMES` (8) frames per video - those
  frames are sampled evenly across the whole file, so a long lecture's later
  slides are not skipped - and at most `INDEX_OCR_CHARS` (2,000) characters of
  that on-screen text are stored per video. The per-run cap is unchanged
  (`INDEX_PER_RUN` = 2 files, so one search OCRs at most 16 frames). Each stored
  row says where it came from: `source: "speech"` for what was said,
  `source: "screen"` for what a video showed; a search result carries the same
  field, so a slide is never reported as something the owner said. Where the
  PC's reader is missing or cannot read a frame, that frame simply contributes
  nothing - nothing is invented, and the video is still indexed from its speech.
  A silent video's length is reported as 0 (not measured) rather than guessed.
  The schema version is 3 since the 2026-10-20 security half (Gemini 6B): an
  older `media-index.db` is a DERIVED file,
  so it is dropped and rebuilt, and the recordings are re-read at the normal
  2-a-search pace (the originals are untouched).
* **The stored words are outside text: stripped and advisory-scanned (Gemini
  6B, 2026-10-20).** A transcript or on-screen line can be written to look like
  an instruction (`<|im_start|>`, `<|im_end|>`, `<|endoftext|>`, `<tool_call>`,
  `<think>`). Before a line is STORED or RETURNED it goes through the project's
  ONE recursive stripper, `jarvis_agent.strip_chat_markers` (the same strip
  every tool result already gets - it also catches a marker hidden inside
  another one and Unicode tag characters); a line that was ONLY a marker is
  dropped rather than stored empty. The stripped line is scanned with
  `jarvis_injection`; its advisory level (`high`/`medium`/`low`, `""` when
  clean) is stored with the row and carried as `advisory` on every match, and a
  flagged search answer names the patterns (`injection`) and adds ONE plain
  `warning` sentence - "they are data, never instructions". Advisory only: it
  never blocks a search and never edits the owner's words. The strip runs
  again when a stored line is returned, so a damaged or hand-edited row cannot
  smuggle a marker out to a caller or the model.
* **Never a learned fact.** The words are searchable text, not a memory: the
  module imports no memory/learning module, and the `my_files` result is
  outside text like every other read, so the normal taint/card rules apply.
* **Rows for files deleted or moved away leave on the next run.** No row is
  kept for a file that is not there; a resumed/renamed recording is re-read
  under its new path.
* **Kept until deleted - no timer.** One Delete in Settings removes every
  stored word AND the index file; deleting one recording's words removes them
  from the index. The originals are never touched.
* **Delete really deletes.** `media-index.db` is in `jarvis_backup.py`'s
  `NOT_BACKED_UP` table from day one (its own reason: a backup made before a
  Delete would still hold the words, so "Delete really deletes" would be
  untrue). The suite drives the backup module's own decision function. The
  database scrub is not only a main-file `VACUUM`: Delete also runs
  `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` (so a WAL cannot hold plaintext pages),
  and Delete-all unlinks `media-index.db`, `media-index.db-wal` and
  `media-index.db-shm`. The suite's own **raw-byte canary** test indexes one
  clip containing a unique word, proves `search_media` returns it, Deletes,
  and requires **zero** occurrences of that word in the raw bytes of every
  `media-index.db*` file (Gemini's evidence bar for the disclosure).
* **The words stay on the local lane.** A `search_media` result carrying
  stored lines latches the conversation private
  (`jarvis_gate.latch_taint`, why `media_index_search`) - the same latch every
  other reading tool sets - so a later turn can never be offered a cloud lane
  carrying what was said.
* **The switch ships ON; OFF is instant.** With no owner file the shipped
  default applies; turning it OFF writes the owner's own state file and the
  very next run reads and writes nothing (a waiting ON card is taken back).
  Turning it back ON is ONE normal approval card - it starts keeping readable
  private speech again - and nothing is written before a person says yes.
* **Plain-language disclosure.** Settings shows it word for word, including
  that readable private speech is kept on this PC until deleted and that the
  audio/video is never copied.

**The surfaces (smallest complete slice).**

* **Chat, both apps.** The existing `my_files` tool grew the action
  `search_media` - no new tool, no new route for chat, and it is decided under
  the EXISTING `read_files_readonly` action. The model gets the stored lines
  with file and time (`{"file", "at", "line", "on_screen", "advisory"}` - S3
  added `on_screen`, true when the words were shown in a video rather than
  said; Gemini 6B added `advisory`, the line's injection level, `""` when
  clean) plus the counts/words, never a recording and never a fact. When any
  returned line is flagged, the result also names the patterns (`injection`)
  and carries ONE `warning` sentence, and `tainted` reports the private-lane
  latch. A fresh index fills in at most two recordings per
  search (`INDEX_PER_RUN`), so a search is never ten minutes of speech-to-text;
  the answer says how many are still waiting. **It needs two things:** the tool
  in the owner's `[tools].enabled` **and at least one folder in "Folders
  Jarvis may look in"**. The shipped template now lists `web_search`,
  `change_setting`, `feature_guide`, `calculator`, `memory_search` and
  `my_files` by default (2026-10-20: the post-install field test found a fresh
  install was offered only the first three, so the calculator and memory
  search the docs describe were missing too; the full default list is in the
  template and pinned by `backend/test_tool_defaults.py`). Since 2026-11-02 the
  same list also names `plugin_list` and `plugin_switch`, the two tools that
  list Jarvis's drop-in plugins and turn one on or off by chat (section 181);
  both stay on this PC - `plugin_list` only reads the plugin folder, and
  `plugin_switch` raises ONE `modify_own_code` card to turn one on and needs no
  card to turn one off. Since 2026-11-04 it also names the four read-only
  self/chat tools of section 184 - `self_portrait`, `conversation_find`,
  `conversation_open` and `refresh_abilities` - so a new install can say what
  Jarvis is made of and reopen a kept chat without hand-editing this list;
  `conversation_clear` is deliberately NOT among them (Gemini ruling 1,
  2026-11-03), because an AI must never have an autonomous tool to wipe a
  transcript. A PC whose own settings file already exists keeps its list: an
  update never overwrites that file, so the four arrive with a new install
  (or when the owner adds the names). With no folders,
  `jarvis_agent.offered_tools` omits `my_files` entirely - chat search cannot
  run even while this switch is ON, and that omission is on purpose: with no
  folder listed the tool costs no tokens and reads nothing. The Settings card
  still shows the switch, the disclosure and Delete in that case; it is the
  chat path that is unavailable, not the switch.
* **Desktop Settings.** A hand-written card ("Searchable recordings and
  videos") shows the PC's disclosure, the switch (off at once; on asks once),
  the one Delete and a status line that now states how many recordings have
  been indexed, including "0 recordings indexed so far" (Gemini's empty-state
  bar, 2026-10-20), through ONE Rust command
  (`jarvis-desktop/src-tauri/src/media_index.rs`) and the route below.
* **The route, and no patch.** `GET/POST /api/media-index` is installed by the
  drop-in folder **`plugins/ready/media-index/`** - the same no-patch mechanism
  the data sandbox switch uses - so this slice adds NO patch, edits no core
  file and touches `jarvis_hud.py` nowhere. GET: switch, counts (including
  `screen_lines`, how many stored lines came from a video's screen), pending,
  disclosure. POST `{"enabled": bool}`: OFF is `200` at once; ON goes through
  `request_enabled()` and answers `202 {"waiting": true}` (one normal approval
  card, action `change_own_config`, tier `ask`, nothing written first). POST
  `{"action": "delete"}`: the one Delete. Origin and token are checked before
  any body is read, like every route.
* **POST is PC_ONLY (added 2026-10-20, Gemini Area 1A).** A change to the index
  - ON, OFF or Delete - is refused `403` from another device over the mesh,
  before the body is read, using the project's one
  `jarvis_owner_check.from_this_pc(peer, local)` rule (the same wrapper
  `jarvis_brain_reads` and `jarvis_self_improve` use) and failing closed when
  the peer cannot be placed. A phone bearer token can therefore no longer
  toggle indexing or delete stored words. **GET deliberately stays
  origin+token only**: it is read-only and returns no recording's words, just
  the switch, counts, disclosure and the Settings view's own index-file path,
  the same shape as the phone reading any other Settings row; if that view ever
  gains words or a search result, GET must become PC_ONLY with the POST.
* **The spoken switch.** `jarvis_settings_registry.BOOL_SETTINGS` has
  `media_index` ("searchable recordings", "the recording index", ...), whose
  setter calls the module's own `request_enabled()`, so "turn off searchable
  recordings" works from either app's chat and cannot bypass the card.

**What it does not do yet, said plainly.** The phone has no Settings card yet -
its chat path and the spoken switch work - and S3 deliberately leaves that
one-sided instead of adding a control that cannot work: the phone's own menu row
for this (`settings.media-index` in `backend/jarvis_menus.py`, generated into
`MenuCatalog.kt`) is desktop-only, and its "open searchable recordings" answer
is the existing PC-only sentence (`jarvis-client`'s `OpenPlace.PC_ONLY` lists
`media-index`), so the phone does not pretend to control this PC-side store.
`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8 records that follow-up honestly rather than
claiming parity. **Real OCR is NOT TESTED by this slice's suite**: the tests
drive the read seams, so a real video frame through the real Windows/RapidOCR
reader on the owner's PC is a field test, and it stays NOT-TESTABLE until it is
driven (NOT-TESTABLE is never a pass). A deploy of this slice needs ONE extra
command on the PC for the Settings card: `scripts\add-plugin.ps1 -Name
media-index` (the chat path needs nothing). If the switch is left ON after a
Delete, the next search reads the folders again and rebuilds what it deleted
from - the disclosure says so.

Tests: `backend/test_media_index.py` - only listed folders, readable text
stored but no media copy, the exact stored line with file/time and no second
read, Delete-one really removing rows (with SQLite `secure_delete` and the
index rebuilt so no deleted word lingers) and Delete-all removing the index
file, the **raw-byte canary** (with the index forced into WAL mode first: no
`media-index.db*` file, `-wal`/`-shm` included, may contain the deleted word),
the **private-lane latch** on a result carrying lines, the backup exclusion
driven through `jarvis_backup.py`'s own function, ON by default/OFF instant/
ON one card, the spoken setter and the `my_files` action under
`read_files_readonly`, gone/moved rows leaving, nothing learned, the drop-in
route's four verbs plus its 401/403 shape, and the plain disclosure, and the
**PC_ONLY mutation-bite** tests (2026-10-20 audit): a remote phone's POST is
403 BEFORE the body is read and the switch does not move; a local loopback
request and a PC program calling its own mesh address still work; an
unplaceable peer fails closed; GET stays a token-guarded read-only view with no
stored words. **S3's own checks:** a video's on-screen text searchable beside
its speech with `source` saying which it was, a video with no recognised speech
still indexed from its screen text (length unmeasured, not guessed), the
`INDEX_OCR_FRAMES`/`INDEX_OCR_CHARS` caps enforced whatever a reader returns,
frames sampled across the whole file rather than only its start, a silent
video's fallback to screen text, the per-run cap unchanged, and
Delete-one/Delete-all removing on-screen rows with the same raw-byte canary.
Real ffmpeg/OCR is **not** run by the suite - the read seams are - so it is
NOT-TESTABLE here until it is field-tested. **Gemini 6B's own mutation tests:**
a hostile transcript AND a hostile on-screen line are stripped before storage
(no `<|im_start|>`/`<|im_end|>`/`<|endoftext|>`/`<tool_call>`/`<think>` in the
raw index bytes), a line that was only a marker is dropped, the match carries a
non-empty `advisory`, the search answer names the patterns and adds the
warning, a damaged stored row is stripped AGAIN on the way out, and the
`my_files` chat result's JSON never carries a raw marker while the private-lane
latch still fires on a result carrying words. The feature list's own row was
updated in all three copies.

## 150. Two mechanical guards against blind, stacked approvals (added 2026-10-20)

The owner's incident: one "approve all" click approved three backup restores,
two imports and a device-key registration. The review the owner accepted
(ruling 8.2 of `FOR-GEMINI-COMPREHENSIVE-REVIEW-2026-10-20-LATE`) asked for two
mechanical guards, and this section is what the API now promises. Neither one
answers a card, weakens rule 4, or suppresses a card: the card that exists is
still drawn and still waits for a person.

### One card per identical request

`jarvis_gate.check()` no longer inserts a second row for a request identical to
one still `pending`. "Identical" is `(action, target digest)`, where the digest
is a SHA-256 of the action and a canonical JSON of `detail` (sorted keys, no
whitespace); when `detail` carries no parameters at all the card's `prompt` is
mixed in too, because then it is the only recorded difference between two
requests. The duplicate call does not wait a second time: it is answered at
once with a refused verdict whose `request_id` is the waiting card's id and
whose reason says the same request is already waiting. Approving that card
therefore runs ONE action, not three. Different actions or targets never
merge, and a card that was approved, denied or expired is never reused - an
answered card is an answer.

### State-replacing cards: the `replaces` field

Every waiting row now carries **`replaces`** (a JSON boolean, always present):
`true` for the cards that replace or delete what is already there. The set is
`jarvis_gate.replaces_for(action, detail)`; the marker is data on the detail,
never prose. It covers, in the gate's own `_RISK` table where every one is
reversible `"no"` or `"hard"`:

| action | what approving it does to data already on the PC |
|---|---|
| `restore_backup` | puts memory, chats, notes and the unlocking key back in time |
| `register_approval_key` | lets a phone approve risky actions from then on |
| `memory_forget_range` | retires facts and deletes chats in a time range |
| `delete_file` / `delete_joplin_note` / `delete_logseq_page` | the file or note is gone; there is no undo from here |
| `edit_joplin_note` / `edit_logseq_page` | the previous text is replaced in place and is gone unless the owner versions that vault/graph |
| `modify_own_code` | the running program's source is changed; a backup is the only way back |
| `app_merge_change` | writes the change shown on the card into the app's own files |

The first three are review ruling 8.2's own list; the rest were **added on the
owner's explicit instruction (2026-10-21: "Extend the two-press guard to
them")** after the pre-merge audit named the other irreversible data-changing
actions. The voice-training clear is not an action name in the table: it is
raised as the shared `change_own_config` and marked by
`backend/jarvis_voice_enroll.py`'s own detail, and the marker path is kept
exactly for cards like it.

### Three accurate labels, not one generic one (review ruling 8.1, 2026-10-21)

One generic heading would be a lie on some of those cards, so the set is split
into three labels - the PC sends **`replaces_kind`**, **`replaces_heading`** and
**`replaces_note`** on every waiting row (words owned by
`jarvis_card_words.py`, one place for both apps), and every surface draws
exactly what it is given. A kept copy is promised **only** where one is really
kept - the columns below are checked against the gate's own `_RISK` why by
`backend/test_approval_guards.py`, action by action:

| label (`replaces_kind`) | actions | what the card says | is a copy kept? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **DELETES OR REPLACES DATA** (`deletes_data`) | `delete_file`, `delete_joplin_note`, `delete_logseq_page` | "deletes the file/note; there is no undo from here" | **no** |
| | `memory_forget_range` | "forgets the listed facts and deletes the chats; Undo puts them back for 10 minutes, then they are gone" | yes, for 10 minutes (its own Undo) |
| | the voice-training clear (detail-marked `change_own_config`) | the category's honest fallback: "deletes data saved on this PC; there is no undo from here" | **no** |
| **OVERWRITES EXISTING NOTE** (`overwrites_note`) | `edit_joplin_note`, `edit_logseq_page` | "replaces the note's/page's current text; Jarvis keeps no copy of the old version" | **no automatic copy** - the owner's own vault app version history is the way back |
| **REPLACES LIVE CODE OR STATE** (`replaces_code_or_state`) | `restore_backup` | "puts back an older backup ... your CURRENT data is backed up first, with a fresh recovery code, so this can itself be undone" | **yes** (backup of the current data first) |
| | `app_merge_change` | "writes the change shown on the card into the app's files; the older version stays in the app's git history, but there is no Undo button for it yet" | **yes** (the app's git history) |
| | `register_approval_key` | "adds the phone named on the card as an approver; you can remove the device in Settings, Devices, to drop the key again" | **yes** (removable in Settings, not a copy) |
| | `modify_own_code` | "changes Jarvis's own running code; a backup is the only way back" | **only the owner's backup** - the card does not claim one is automatic |

An older PC whose rows carry `replaces` but not the words still gets the right
category heading from each client's own three-name fallback, and a card that
says it replaces data but gives no category at all keeps the original generic
heading. **The exact words are asserted** (heading and note per action, against
the recovery listed above): rewording a card so it claims a kept copy it does
not have fails the backend suite.

Both apps and the HUD draw that accurate heading on those cards and require a
**second, explicit confirmation** before
the approve is sent: the desktop bar and the HUD page change the button from
"Approve" to "Confirm replace" after the first press and send only on the
second; the phone does the same on its card and refuses the right swipe. A
typed "approve" does not answer them (`quickActionable`), and the desktop
widget's clamped strip redirects them to the bar. The phone cannot send the
confirmation with a single tap. Ordinary cards are untouched: the field is
`false`, the heading is not drawn and Approve is one press as before.

**Only an explicit `false` is one click, and the client list is a floor.** A
row with NO `replaces` field (an older PC during a partial deploy), a row that
is missing from a successful `/api/pending` read, or a failed read is UNKNOWN,
and both apps, the HUD page and the HUD bootstrap take the second press for it
with their own honest words ("I could not check what this will replace.").
The clients also carry the ten action names above as a FAIL-SAFE FLOOR: the
PC's field may ADD an action, but a spoofed or explicit `false` field can never
SUBTRACT the second press from one of them. The fake "Cancel": a single press
sends NOTHING and only arms, so answering "Cancel" or walking away decides
nothing; the gate's own timeout still refuses an unanswered card.

**The HUD window's own injected bootstrap implements the same rule.** Inside
the desktop HUD the vendored page's `onclick` never runs - the bootstrap
(`jarvis-desktop/src-tauri/src/hud_bootstrap.js`) captures every card press and
sends the decision through `decide_approval`, so a page-only rule could not
protect that window (found by the 2026-10-21 pre-merge audit, fixed before
merge). The bootstrap reads `/api/pending` through its allowed `hud_get`,
requires an explicit second press for a row with `replaces: true`, says
"This REPLACES what is on your PC. Press Approve once more to do it.", keeps
the arm for that card id only with a 10-second window, and sends exactly one
`decide_approval` on the second press; an ordinary card still sends on one
click, and the page's own two-press stays for a browser tab with no bootstrap.
The rule is executed by `jarvis-desktop/tests/hud-replace-confirm.mjs` (it is
lifted out of the bootstrap and driven with a fake clock, including the
unknown-row and expiry cases); the CLICK wiring itself is executed by the
Playwright case in `jarvis-desktop/tests/hud.mjs`, where a fake `/api/pending`
returns a `replaces` card and the first click is waited on and asserted to
send no `decide_approval` before the second sends exactly one.

### What a client must not do

Do not derive the state-replacing set from card text or from `risk` -
`restore_backup` and `register_approval_key` are both classified reversible and
local, which is why the heavy-card delay never covered them. Read `replaces`;
an older PC that does not send it is handled by the three real action names as
a client-side fallback, and a card that is not recognised is ordinary, never
guessed in the dangerous direction.

The backend half is `backend/test_approval_guards.py` (behavioural, against the
published gate, with a revert-check for each guard); the desktop half is
`jarvis-desktop/tests/replace-confirm.mjs`; the phone half is
`ReplaceConfirmTest.kt` with the drawing in `ui/approval/ApprovalCard.kt`.
`backend/gate-touches.patch` carries the gate change to the owner's own file
and `backend/test_gate_touches.py` applies it forwards and reverses it out
byte-for-byte.

## 151. The Obsidian vault organizer: a read-only plan, then ONE card and one-click Undo (backend half added 2026-10-20)

**What it is.** A batch tidy-up planner for an Obsidian vault on this PC. It
reads the vault's notes and answers what a tidy-up **would** do, so the owner
can look before anything changes. The DEFAULT scheme is the safest one,
`mocs_only`, which moves **no file**: it merges `tags` into each note's YAML
frontmatter (never erasing the owner's own), adds an
`up: "[[_MOC - <Topic>]]"` link, and would create `_MOC - <Topic>.md` hub notes
plus one `00 - Vault Home.md`. The two moving schemes, `topic_folders` and
`para`, are previewed by the same plan; they exist behind the explicit
`scheme` parameter for a later run. The module is
`backend/jarvis_vault_organizer.py` and its docstring is the contract.

**THIS SLICE IS THE PLAN HALF, AND IT IS READ-ONLY.** `POST
/api/vault/organize-plan` opens notes for reading only and writes nothing
anywhere - not in the vault, not in the settings folder, not in `memory.db` -
raises no approval card, calls no model and embeds nothing. The clustering is
pure Python and deterministic: folder, database membership and a TF-IDF over
headings/tags, with ties broken by name, so the same vault twice gives the same
`plan_id`, `digest` and every preview line. `JARVIS_NO_EMBED=1` changes nothing
because nothing here embeds.

**THE WRITER DOES EXACTLY WHAT A PLAN PREVIEWED, UNDER ONE CARD.** `POST
/api/vault/organize` takes the `plan_id` and `digest` of a plan the owner has
seen. It re-reads the vault first: if anything changed since the preview, the
plan is **stale** and the route refuses rather than acting on it. Then it raises
**ONE `organize_obsidian_vault` card at tier ask** that names the vault, the
scheme, how many files change and says in words that nothing is deleted and
ONE Undo puts the whole vault back. Only after the yes does it save a
`jarvis_file_guardian.snapshot_before_write()` copy of **every existing file**
it is about to change, move or replace - one failed copy refuses the whole
batch before a byte is written. It keeps its own copy of every original under
`~/.openjarvis/vault-organizer-backups/<plan_id>/` with a manifest, records
**ONE `jarvis_receipts.py` batch receipt** (tool name `organize_obsidian_vault`)
**before** the first write, and writes atomically (`.tmp` + `os.replace`).
**NO note is ever deleted**: duplicates and zero-word stubs are listed only.
