ONE Undo - the receipt's own - restores the exact bytes AND paths (moved files
included), removes only the notes the batch created, and takes off only the
folders it made. It works after a backend restart because it reads its own
manifest; the receipt stores no absolute path (the receipt scrubber would
redact it), only the plan id. A write that fails part-way is reported
honestly as **partial**, with the receipt and copy it already saved.

**THE FIRST REAL RUN IS APPLIED TO A COPY, AND THAT IS ENFORCED (R7,
Ruling 14, 2026-10-21).** A vault with no `.jarvis-organizer-verified.json`
marker in it is never written to by `/api/vault/organize`: the writer first
makes a **sibling copy** (`<Vault> - Jarvis Copy (<date>)`, ` (2)`, ` (3)` ...
on a second run the same day), then plans and writes **in that copy only**. The
card says so in its own words and names the copy; the answer carries
`"mode": "copy"`, `"copy": <path>`, `"original_unchanged": true` and
`copy_checks` (files, bytes, space needed, space free). The real vault is left
byte-for-byte untouched - proved by a tree hash before and after. The copy is
refused **before a byte is copied** when the vault holds a symbolic link (a
copy of a link is not a copy of the note, and following it could leave the
vault), when the vault is bigger than the bounded copy size
(`MAX_COPY_BYTES = 2 GiB`, `MAX_COPY_FILES = 20,000`), or when the parent folder
does not have `FREE_SPACE_FACTOR` (1.10) x the vault's size free. A failed copy
is removed, so a refused first run leaves neither a half copy nor a changed
vault.

**Inspect the copy, then mark it verified.** The owner opens the copy in
Obsidian and looks. If it is right, the marker goes into the **real** vault -
`backend/jarvis_vault_organizer.py`'s `mark_verified(vault, copy=...)` writes
`.jarvis-organizer-verified.json` (a tiny JSON file: `verified`, `at`, `copy`).
From the next plan, `/api/vault/organize` writes **in place**, with exactly the
same card, snapshots, receipt and one-click Undo as before. Creating that file
by hand is the same decision; a later screen can call the helper. The marker is
never written by the writer itself, and nothing is marked verified
automatically.


**Database rows stay where they are (Ruling 8.4, accepted 2026-10-21).** Under
the two moving schemes the organizer moves **only standalone pages**. A note
whose frontmatter carries `database:` and the `_Database - <Name>.md` hub it
belongs to are left **exactly where they are**, beside the hub's `.base` -
whose `file.inFolder(...)` filter names that folder - so the database view
keeps resolving instead of silently pointing at an empty folder. Those rows
still get their `tags` and `up:` enrichment in place, exactly as `mocs_only`
does; only the move is skipped. The default scheme is still `mocs_only`, which
moves nothing at all.

**Routes (all PC-only, token-guarded, and OFF by default).**

* `POST /api/vault/organize-plan` - body `{"vault": "<path>", "scheme":
  "mocs_only"|"topic_folders"|"para", "max_clusters": N,
  "archive_empty_stubs": false}`. The vault is optional: it defaults to
  `[notes.obsidian] vault_directory` / `JARVIS_OBSIDIAN_VAULT` through the
  existing `jarvis_notes.obsidian_vault()`, and an unusable vault is refused
  with the notes module's own words. Answers `ok`, `plan_id`, `digest`,
  `scheme`, `summary` (notes_scanned / notes_moved / notes_tagged /
  mocs_to_create / databases_indexed / links_rewritten / duplicates_found /
  empty_stubs_found), `moves_preview`, `mocs_preview`, `home_preview`,
  `tag_plan`, `duplicates_and_stubs`, `partial`, `warnings` and `said`. A plan
  that hits the file/byte/time caps says it is **partial** rather than hanging.
  Duplicates and zero-word stubs are **listed, never deleted**.
* `POST /api/vault/organize` - body `{"plan_id": "...", "digest": "...",
  "apply_on_copy": <bool, optional>}`. The writer above: ONE card, guardian
  snapshots, atomic writes, one batch receipt, one-click Undo. With no verified
  marker the batch runs on a sibling copy (`apply_on_copy` defaults to the
  ruling's `true`; `false` is the explicit in-place choice for a vault the
  owner has already checked), and the answer says `mode`, `copy`,
  `original_unchanged` and `copy_checks`. Refusals: a plan_id that is not in
  memory (a restart forgets plans), a digest that does not match, a vault that
  changed since the preview, a denied/timed-out card, a snapshot that cannot be
  taken, a batch over 2,000 existing files, a second writer already running, and
  (first run only) a symlinked / oversized / no-room-to-copy vault. Each
  refusal changes nothing and says why.
* `GET /api/vault/organizer` - the switch, its action and tier, the default
  scheme, the schemes that exist, and whether the writer can apply
  (`can_apply`, `apply_action`, `apply_tier`).
* `POST /api/vault/organizer/enabled` - body `{"enabled": true|false}`. **OFF
  is immediate** (200, withdraws a waiting card); **ON is ONE
  `change_own_config` card at tier ask** (202 `waiting`), and a denied,
  timed-out, refused or unraisable card changes nothing. Turning it off needs
  no card.

**Ship state, said plainly.** The shipped template has
`[vault_organizer] enabled = false` (`backend/rebuilt/jarvis-framework.toml`):
the feature is OFF until the owner turns it on with the card above. The plan
route answers `{"ok": false, "enabled": false, "why": ...}` while it is off.
Every route is refused for a caller that is not this PC (`403 not_this_pc`):
the plan reads a vault of the owner's own writing, and no phone control for it
exists or is planned.

**Safety limits.** Every note is resolved and must stay inside the vault
(`jarvis_notes._inside`, the notes search's own rule); symlinks and paths that
resolve outside are refused and named in `warnings`. The work is bounded:
`MAX_FILES`, `MAX_FILE_BYTES`, `MAX_SECONDS` and `MAX_CLUSTERS`, with a file
over the byte ceiling skipped (not read) and reported. No note text is stored
anywhere: `jarvis_memory` is not imported by this module, and the only note
wording a plan returns is the one-line preview snippet it renders for a MOC,
passed through the project's own scrubbers (`jarvis_scrub.scrub_text`,
`jarvis_agent.strip_chat_markers`) when they are present.

**The owner's runbook: the FIRST REAL RUN IS ON A COPY OF THE VAULT (now
automatic).**
1. Plan as usual: `POST /api/vault/organize-plan`. Read the answer's `summary`,
   `moves_preview`, `mocs_preview` and `duplicates_and_stubs`. Nothing has
   changed yet.
2. Apply that plan: `POST /api/vault/organize` with its `plan_id` and `digest`,
   and approve the ONE card. With no verified marker, the writer makes the
   sibling copy first and applies to **that**; the real vault is not touched.
   (If the plan is stale, nothing happens: plan again.)
3. Open the copy in Obsidian and look. If it is not wanted, press Undo once on
   the receipt - the copy comes back exactly, and the real vault was never
   touched at all.
4. If the copy looks right, mark it verified: `mark_verified(<real vault>,
   copy=<copy>)`, or create `<real vault>/.jarvis-organizer-verified.json`
   yourself. The next run works on the real vault, with the same one-Undo
   safety.
5. Keeping the copy until the real run has been looked at is still the safe
   habit. (Copying the vault by hand in File Explorer and pointing the plan at
   the copy also still works, but the writer now does the copy and the checks
   for you.)

**The write half's limits, said plainly.** `archive_empty_stubs` is recorded in
the plan but nothing is archived by the writer yet - stubs stay listed. A
wiki-link is rewritten only when a MOVE changes a note's title (a folder move
keeps the name, so Obsidian resolves it untouched); a title two notes share is
ambiguous and is left exactly as written. The moving schemes are previewed and
writable, but the default remains `mocs_only`. The writer needs a vault the
plan scan could read inside its caps, and one batch stops at 2,000 existing
files so one receipt stays readable. None of this has been run against the
owner's real Notion vault yet - that is the runbook above.

**Checked by** `backend/test_vault_organizer.py` (187 checks, runs anywhere):
the plan is byte-for-byte read-only on a real vault, the tag merge never erases
an owner tag, duplicates/stubs are listed not deleted, both moving schemes
preview only inside the vault, an empty vault is a clean no-op, planning writes
nothing to `memory.db`, two plans of one vault are byte-identical, the caps
report `partial`, symlink escape is refused, the switch is off by default and
is ONE card, the plan route is PC-only and flag-gated, and `install()` wraps
the routes. Two revert-checks were measured while building it: one cache write
in the planner made four read-only checks fail; a clock in the digest made the
determinism check fail. The writer half adds: the tree it changes is
exactly the planned set, ONE card with the right words, a denied/low-tier/
unraisable card changes nothing byte-for-byte, a stale or wrong digest and an
unknown plan refuse, a snapshot is taken for every changed file (and a failed
snapshot refuses the whole batch), ONE Undo restores the exact tree including
moves and works after a restart, a second Undo refuses, a second apply writes
nothing, no note is ever deleted, a partial failure is honest and still
undoable, taint is latched by the writer and not the plan, the writer writes no
memory row, the routes are PC-only and flag-gated, and an existing MOC is
snapshotted and put back exactly. Two writer revert-checks were measured too: a
stale-check removed made four checks fail; skipped snapshots made three fail.
Ruling 8.4 adds its own bites: under BOTH moving schemes a database's child and
its hub stay at their original paths (no `Databases/` destination exists), a
standalone page still moves, the `.base` is byte-identical so its filter still
names the rows' folder, the plan count is the standalone moves only, and ONE
Undo restores the exact tree.
## 152. Bringing a Notion export into an Obsidian vault: `/api/notion/preview` and `/api/notion/import` (backend only, added 2026-10-16, audit fixes 2026-10-21)

Notion can export a whole workspace as Markdown & CSV or as HTML, and what it
writes is not an Obsidian vault: ids sit on every file and folder name, page
properties are loose lines under the title, each database is a CSV beside its
pages, links point at names that no longer exist, and pictures and PDFs are
scattered. The plugin folder `plugins/ready/notion-obsidian` calls
`jarvis_notion_obsidian.install()`, which wraps the core handler and answers the
two routes below. There is **no patch**: the module ships as a plugin, the same
way `/api/folders` does, and it imports `jarvis_documents.safe_parts`,
`jarvis_documents.protected` and `jarvis_documents.ImportRefused` rather than
writing a second extractor.

**Both routes are PC only, before the body is read.** After the server's own
origin and token checks, `jarvis_owner_check.from_this_pc(peer, local)` decides:
loopback is this PC, a program on this PC calling its own mesh address is this
PC, and a peer that cannot be placed **fails closed**. A phone (or any other
device) gets:

```
403 {"ok": false, "pc_only": true,
     "reason": "Jarvis brings a Notion export in on the PC only - the export file and the vault are chosen here."}
```

The refusal names no path and no folder. This is the same rule
`/api/folders/import` keeps, for the same reason: the export and the vault are
folders on this PC, and the preview works out what is inside the export.
`GET /api/notion/preview` remains a token+origin read of the route's title and
detail only (no paths, no plan); both POST routes are the PC-only pair.

| route | body | answer |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/notion/preview` | `{"source": "<path to the .zip or the unzipped folder>", "vault": "<path to an Obsidian vault>"}` | `200 {"ok": true\|false, "plan": {...}, "said": "<plain words>"}` |
| `POST /api/notion/import` | the same, plus optional `"digest"` copied from the preview | `200 {"ok": true, "folder", "receipt_id", "notes", "attachments", "databases", "rows", "rows_without_notes", "html_pages", "said"}` or `{"ok": false, "reason"}` |

**A phone door exists beside them, and it takes no path at all (added 2026-11-05).** The two routes above are unchanged and still refuse any other device, because the export file and the vault are folders on this PC and a phone has neither to name. What a phone gets instead is two thin routes that never accept a path: the first offers the vaults this PC already validated, and the second takes the id of an export that `jarvis_upload` is holding, plus the id of one of those vaults.

```
GET  /api/notion/vaults
POST /api/notion/phone-import   {"upload": "<upload id>", "vault": "<vault id>", "digest": "<optional>"}
```

| route | answer |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/notion/vaults` | `200 {"ok": true, "ready": true\|false, "vaults": [{"id": "<opaque, 12 hex>", "name": "My Vault", "path": "C:\\..."}], "said": "<plain sentence>"}`; `ready: false` with *"Choose your Obsidian vault on the PC first - Settings, Notes."* |
| `POST /api/notion/phone-import` | `200 {"ok": true, "plan": {...}, "said": "<the card's words>", "vault": "<name>", "vault_id": "<id>"}` for the dry run, and nothing is written into the vault; `200 {"ok": true, "imported": true, "folder": "<the new folder's NAME>", "receipt_id", "notes", "attachments", "databases", "rows", "rows_without_notes", "html_pages", "vault", "said"}` for the import; `200 {"ok": false, "reason": "<why>"}` for a plan that cannot be made; `400` for a vault Jarvis did not offer; `410` for an upload that is no longer waiting |

**Where the vault list comes from: two sources, in order, and no new settings screen.** `jarvis_notes.obsidian_vault()` - the vault the owner already configured for notes (`JARVIS_OBSIDIAN_VAULT`, else `[notes.obsidian] vault_directory`) - and then the last vault a Notion import used, which this module records in its own `notion-obsidian.json` beside `folders.json`. **Every candidate goes through `_vault_or_refuse` before it is offered**, so the phone can only ever see a folder that really is an Obsidian vault (it has a `.obsidian` folder) and is not a protected place. The phone picks by id from that list; it never types a path, and a value that was not offered is refused whatever it says. Returning a `path` is consistent with `GET /api/folders`, which already gives the phone the folder paths it picked from.

**No `digest` is the dry run, and it is the same dry run `preview` is.** `plan_import` extracts into a throw-away folder, `describe` words the card, and **nothing is written into the vault and no card is raised**. A `digest` calls the EXISTING `request_import`, unchanged: the digest is re-checked, ONE `import_notion_export` card is raised at its own tier, `run_import(approved=True)` lands the whole tree in one atomic move, one reversible `jarvis_receipts` entry is recorded, and Undo takes the folder back off. This door adds **no writer, no permission and no second extractor**. **The answer names the vault and the new folder, never a path** - `folder` is the new folder's NAME - and the plan's own `source` is removed, because that is Jarvis's temporary staging folder and the phone has no business with it. **The staged export is deleted as soon as an import attempt ends** - success, refusal, a denied card or an error - in a `finally`; a dry run keeps it, because the import it is a dry run for comes next, and a phone that dies in between is cleaned up by the 30-minute expiry in section 188.


**`/api/notion/preview` is a dry run.** It plans, extracts into a throw-away
folder under the system temp folder, and writes nothing into the vault, nothing
into the settings folder, and raises **no approval card**. The `plan` object
carries `source`, `vault`, `name`, `notes`, `attachments`, `databases`, `rows`,
`renamed`, `collisions`, `html_pages`, `refused`, `digest`, `said` (the
extraction map is deliberately not exposed). A plan whose target folder already
exists answers `ok: false` with the plain reason.

**`/api/notion/import` writes the vault after ONE person's yes.** It asks the
gate once for `import_notion_export` (tier `ask` in
`backend/rebuilt/jarvis-framework.toml`), and a denied, timed-out or refused
card brings nothing in. When a `digest` is supplied and no longer matches the
plan, it refuses rather than importing a changed export. The whole tree lands
in one atomic move inside a new folder named after the export, and one
reversible entry is recorded in `jarvis_receipts`, so Undo takes the folder
back off.

**What the vault looks like.** Notion's ids come off file and folder names
(collisions decided deterministically: `Meeting Notes.md`, `Meeting Notes 2.md`
in walk order); page properties become YAML frontmatter with `notion_id` kept,
so importing the same export twice is refused rather than doubled; HTML pages
become Markdown (callouts, toggles, checklists, fenced code with its language,
pipe tables); relative links become wikilinks through the cleaned-name map; and
pictures/PDFs/audio/video move into the vault's single `attachments/` folder
and are rewritten to `![[name]]`.

Each exported CSV database gets:

* its row's columns merged into the child note's frontmatter, with a relation
  value that names a page of the export becoming `"[[That Page]]"`. Notion's id
  is taken off **only** when the id-free value names a page of this export;
  every other value is left byte-for-byte (an ordinary `ref <32 hex>` stays
  whole; a number with a thousands separator stays a number);
* a hub note `_Database - <Name>.md`: frontmatter `type: database-index`,
  `title`, `rows`, `columns`, `rows_without_notes`; a rendered Markdown table
  whose title column links every row; a collapsible `<details>` summary of row
  counts by Status/Category/Tags when one is present; and a sentence saying how
  many rows have no page. A row whose page is missing **stays in the table** as
  an unresolved `[[wikilink]]` and is counted, never dropped;
* a `.base` beside it, whose filter is `file.inFolder("<export folder>/<database folder>")`.

**Every frontmatter value parses back as itself (Ruling 8.6, accepted
2026-10-21).** A database cell is a CSV field, and Notion's Shift+Enter puts a
real newline inside one. The converter normalizes line endings (CRLF and CR
become LF, so the same note hashes the same on every OS) and writes any
ambiguous value - one with a newline, a colon, a comment hash, a leading flow
or structure indicator, a tab, or a YAML word such as `yes`/`True`/`~` - as a
single-line JSON double-quoted scalar. The newline is escaped, so Obsidian's
YAML parser (or any YAML 1.2 parser) reads the exact original text; before
this ruling one raw newline made the note's whole frontmatter unreadable and
lost **every** property on that note, not just the multi-line cell. Simple
values are byte-for-byte unchanged (a plain word bare, a number bare, a value
that needed quoting gets the same quotes).

Two CSV exports of one database (`X.csv` and `X_all.csv`) are ONE database:
their rows are merged, `_all`'s non-empty values win, rows only one file holds
are all kept, and two rows with one title in one file stay **two rows** (rows
are matched across the two files by occurrence, never by title alone). A
generated hub note or `.base` goes through the same deterministic collision
rule as a page, so a real page named `_Database - Tasks` is never replaced: the
hub gets a free name instead (`_Database - Tasks 2.md`). The comparison is
case-folded, so two databases called `Alpha` and `alpha` do not write one file
on the owner's NTFS (the two hub files get distinct names).

**The limits, in one place.** The same numbers cap a folder and a zip:

| limit | value | where |
|---|---|---|
| files in the export | 20,000 | counted as files are written, both ingest paths |
| total bytes written | 1 GiB | counted as bytes are written |
| one file | 200 MiB | declared size pre-checked; streamed cap as backstop |
| the `.zip` itself | 2 GiB | refused before it is opened |
| declared unpacked total | 500 MiB | `jarvis_documents.zip_bomb_problem`, before a member is opened |
| compression ratio | 100:1 | the extra zip-bomb rule, before a member is opened |
| members / largest member | `MAX_FILES` / `MAX_ONE` | pre-checked on the zip's own `infolist()` |

The 500 MiB total is deliberately different from
`jarvis_documents.EXPORT_UNCOMPRESSED_MAX` (250 MiB): that import unpacks a
Notion export only to **read** it, while this one **writes** a new vault and
copies its attachments too. Each number is stated here once; the total check
itself is imported from `jarvis_documents`, not copied.

**Known limitations, said plainly.**
* `rows_without_notes` appears in the **import** response and the hub note, not
  in `preview`: it needs the built page map, and the plan is deliberately cheap.
  The card therefore cannot promise the exact count before the owner approves;
  it reports it after the import (and the rows themselves are kept either way).
* Two rows with the same title in one database are kept as separate rows and
  separate child pages, but the hub links both to the **first** page of that
  title: Notion's CSV carries no row-to-page id, and guessing which page is
  which would be worse than an honest duplicate link.
* The hub note and `.base` live in the export's folder beside the child pages.
  **Ruling 8.4 (2026-10-21) settled the organizer's side:** it moves only
  standalone pages, so a database's rows and its hub stay in the folder the
  `.base` filter names, the filter keeps resolving, and the organizer never
  moves or edits the hub or the `.base`. See section 151.
* Neither app is wired yet (see `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8): the desktop file
  picker for this is not built, the phone has no view of the PC's folders, and
  the approval card is raised by the backend route itself.

Tests: `backend/test_notion_obsidian.py` - ids/collisions, zip-slip and the
caps (declared total, ratio, member count and largest member refused from the
zip's own directory before a member is opened, streamed caps as the
lying-header backstop), properties and dates, the hub note's frontmatter/table/
summary/missing-row count, `X.csv`+`X_all.csv` union and precedence, duplicate
row titles inside one file surviving with both values, relation wikilinks and
the byte-for-byte preservation of everything that is not a page, a database
genuinely named `*_all` keeping its name, a page and a hub never replacing each
other (both file orders and the case-only variant), case-only database names
never sharing a file, HTML/Markdown same-title pages both surviving, the
plan/gate/one-card/receipt/undo shape, one card for an import and none for a
preview, the installed handler's PC-only 403 on both routes with no path in the

answer, the run path keeping a refusal's plain sentence, and Ruling 8.6's YAML
safety: a multi-line cell and a CRLF cell round-trip exactly through PyYAML (a
full synthetic export's imported note included), colon/hash/leading-bracket/
leading-dash/quote/tab/boolean-word values read back as the strings they were,
and a simple frontmatter block is byte-for-byte what it was.

## 153. Asking Jarvis Live to read the screen or the highlighted text (backend only, added 2026-10-21)

**What it is.** In **Jarvis Live** (a back-and-forth spoken conversation,
`jarvis_live.py`) a question may now ask Jarvis to **read what is already on
this PC's screen**, or **the text the owner has highlighted**, and answer from
it. It is the READ half of the audit finding **V7** ("voice bridge to the UI
modules") and it is deliberately tiny: the two reads are the **existing**
primitives, called unchanged, and nothing new is granted.

**The two asks, and the exact words that count.**

* *"What's on my screen?"* / *"read my screen"* / *"look at my screen"* /
  *"summarise what's on my screen"* -> ONE look through
  `jarvis_screen.py`'s own **"Look at this"** path (`ENGINE.look_at_this`):
  the same pause rules decide first (a password box, a program on the
  owner's "Never look at" list, a private window, Jarvis's own windows, the
  lock screen or a UAC prompt), the picture is dropped as soon as its words
  are read, nothing is kept, and the words arrive labelled **OUTSIDE TEXT**
  exactly as a "Look at this" turn's do.
* *"Read this selection"* / *"read what I selected"* / *"what did I
  highlight?"* / *"summarise what I selected"* -> the same
  `jarvis_ui_control.read_selection()` that `GET /api/selection` (section 141,
  Pillar 24-B) serves the bar: the same refusals (no selection, an excluded
  program, the window changed while reading, a scrubbed secret), the same
  `MAX_SELECTION_CHARS`, and the words are handed on as OUTSIDE TEXT of their
  own. This bridge adds the label and a second, smaller ceiling
  (`MAX_VOICE_SELECTION_CHARS`).

The matching is **narrow on purpose**: a question must actually ask to read
the screen or the selection. "The cinema screen was huge" and "I selected the
blue paint" are ordinary questions and are answered as before - no look, no
read. The words go into **that one request** and nowhere else.

**What it never does.** It never clicks, types, presses a key, or raises a
card - a read is not an approval, and the bridge does not ask the gate. It adds
**no tool to the model's tool list** (typed chat is untouched and has no
screen-query tool), no route, no `[autonomy.tiers]` line, no switch and no new
capture code. Nothing it reads is written to a file, the audit log,
chat history or memory: the words exist only in the request the model is about
to answer, and the turn is recorded as a read of the existing `read_screen`
(so a note write or a web search afterwards asks first, as after any read).

**Actions that change things are NOT part of this bridge, and keep their one
card.** "Click Export" / "press Search" still goes through the existing
`control_computer` tool (opt-in via `[tools].enabled`, as before): it plans
from the accessibility tree (a read), raises its **ONE existing
`jarvis_ui_control_run` approval card**, and runs only after a **physical
tap/click**. Jarvis Live already **pauses while a card waits**, so a spoken
"yes" is not even heard; a voice command can only RAISE the card, never answer
it. No safe navigation (scroll/back/home) was added: `jarvis_ui_control`
treats those as plan steps under the same card, and there is no card-free
primitive to reuse, so inventing one would have been a new permission.

**One-sided on purpose: the phone.** The reads are for **this PC's** screen.
A Live session started on the **phone** asking either question gets a fixed
line ("Reading this PC's screen or highlighted text is for the PC's own Live
session") and **nothing is read** - `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8 records
why. If the backend cannot tell which device the session is on, it reads
nothing (fail closed).

**Checked by** `backend/test_voice_ui.py` (57 checks, runs anywhere, no
desktop and no screen needed): the intent words are narrow (ordinary
sentences are not hijacked); each read returns the expected shaped answer from
a **stubbed** existing primitive and adds OUTSIDE TEXT as a part of the
owner's own message while their words stay separate; a paused look passes the
screen module's own fixed words; a phone or unknown session reads nothing; a
missing/raising primitive answers plainly; a long selection is cut and says
so; chat-template markers in a selection are stripped; a read never asks the
gate and latches the turn private once with a plain reason; a read writes no
file and leaks no word into any file; typed chat has no screen-query tool; and
the carded path still raises exactly ONE existing card and runs nothing before
a person answers (then runs once). Two revert-checks were measured while
building it: removing the phone guard made 3 checks fail; broadening the
intent match made 2 fail.

**Honest limits.** The real Windows look and the real UIA selection read are
**NOT-TESTABLE here** (no desktop in CI; the seams and the tool contract are
what the suite drives) - a real Live sentence must be owner-tested before this
row can be called a PASS. There is no visual "what is on screen" description
beyond the words the screen reader already returns; the phone keeps no
screen-read parity by decision; and the bridge needs the Live turn's session
to be known (a session whose device cannot be read is refused, never guessed).

to be known (a session whose device cannot be read is refused, never guessed).

## 154. Spoken-command normaliser and the speaking-speed reflex (Voice Slice A, added 2026-10-21)

The owner approved the whole Live & Voice program on 2026-10-21. This is its
**Slice A**, as revised by `.dsh-scratch/FOR-GEMINI-OVERNIGHT-WAVE-2026-10-21.md`
section 10.4 (the audit document that proposed it had a two-day-stale
baseline: three of its headline optimisations had already shipped, and its
verification battery used direct `test_*.py` runs, which are now banned -
section 10.1-10.3 there). Slice A is the part that is pure, dependency-free
and fully testable on text alone: one normaliser in `jarvis_quick.py` plus a
deterministic voice reflex that is **a router into an action that already
existed with its own permission model**. No new subsystem, no new route, no
new approval card, no GPU work, no privacy change.
`backend/test_voice_reflex.py` is the suite.

### 154.1 `normalize_spoken_command` - and what it actually fixed

`jarvis_quick.py` runs it before the grammar (inside `_match`, where
`normalise` used to be called). It does `normalise`'s own tidying, then:

1. **Polite lead-ins `normalise` did not strip.** `normalise` already strips
   "hey jarvis", "jarvis", "please", "can/could/would you". Measured gaps it
   did not: "would you mind ...", "can you kindly ...", "would you be so kind
   as to ...", "i would like you to ...", "i was wondering if you could ...",
   "do you think you could ...", "any chance you could ...", "could you
   possibly ...", "would it be possible to ...", "kindly ...". After a lead is
   stripped, a first-word **gerund** is put back to the verb the grammar uses
   ("would you mind **setting** a timer" -> "**set** a timer"), for a short
   fixed list of verbs the fast path already acts on.
2. **Number words in the three whole-sentence grammars that demanded digits.**
   Everything else the audit proposed rewriting was measured first and found
   to ALREADY work (`parse_duration` reads number words inside a length of
   time), so it is deliberately not rewritten - the audit's own "always hit
   the fast path" premise was stale for those:

   | Spoken form | Before this change | After |
   |---|---|---|
   | "watch **five** more minutes" | model answered | `screen_more`, 5 minutes |
   | "watch for **ten** more minutes" | model answered | `screen_more`, 10 minutes |
   | "speak up **three** times a day" | model answered | `settings_budget`, 3/day |
   | "the brief arrives at **eight**" | model answered | `settings_budget`, hour 8 |
   | "the brief arrives at **eight** in the morning" | model answered | `settings_budget`, hour 8 |
   | "the brief at **eight** pm" | model answered | `settings_budget`, hour 20 |
   | "set a timer for **two** minutes" | already worked | unchanged (no rewrite) |
   | "set a timer for **fifteen** minutes" | already worked | unchanged (no rewrite) |
   | "set a timer for **a couple of** minutes" | already worked | unchanged (no rewrite) |
   | "set a timer for **half an hour**" / "**an hour and a half**" | already worked | unchanged (no rewrite) |

   **The safe number rule, stated once:** a number word (one..ninety nine)
   becomes digits ONLY when it is (a) followed by a length-of-time word,
   directly or after "more"; (b) followed by "time(s) a/per day"; or (c)
   directly after "at" and ending the sentence or followed by am/pm / "in the
   morning|afternoon|evening" / "at night". Everything else is left alone:
   "one of the files", "show me the one with the error", "call me three
   times", "twenty five" on its own and the duration forms in the table's
   bottom rows all come out byte-for-byte unchanged.
   **It only decides a MATCH.** The model is still asked the owner's ORIGINAL
   words whenever nothing matches, so a rewrite can never change the question
   put to the AI. The function is idempotent (the suite runs it twice on every
   sentence it uses).

### 154.2 "Speak faster / slower / normally" (a reflex, not a new action)

"speak faster", "speak slower", "speak more slowly", "speak normally",
"speak at normal speed", "talk faster" and "would you mind speaking slower"
now answer without the model. They call the SAME
`jarvis_voices.set_speed({"speed": ...})` that `POST /api/voice/voices/speed`
calls: the existing speaking-speed setting, **no card either way** (the voices
module's own words: it "trusts nothing more, shows nothing more and sends
nothing anywhere"), saved in `voices/state.json`, audited `voices.speed`. The
answer is the voice module's OWN sentence (`SPEED_SAID`), so both apps show
the same words they already show for that setting - no app work, no new
route. The suite spies the call (exactly one, exactly that body) and proves
the setting really changed.

### 154.3 The selection and screen reads are #691's - and this fast path leaves them alone

The revised slice also named "read this selection" / "what's on my screen" /
"summarise what I selected". They are NOT in this file, and that is
deliberate: **PR #691** (merged 2026-10-21, the audit's V7 read half) shipped
them for a Live turn through the SAME primitives - `jarvis_screen.py`'s own
"Look at this" for the screen and `jarvis_ui_control.read_selection()` for the
selection - as OUTSIDE TEXT the model answers from (`jarvis_voice_ui.py`).
`/api/chat` runs this fast path BEFORE the Live turn, so a 0-ms matcher here
would intercept those phrases even inside Live, answer with raw text, and the
#691 path would never run. So the slice **dropped its own read reflex when
#691 merged**, and `backend/test_voice_reflex.py` holds this file to NOT
matching all sixteen phrases #691 claims, and holds #691's own matchers to
still claiming them. No capability is lost: in Live, #691 answers them (with
the model); elsewhere the model answers them, and the no-model read the bar
already has is `GET /api/selection` (section 141).

### 154.4 What was NOT built, and why (said plainly)

Each command below would need a NEW subsystem or a new app-side channel, so
none was added - a handler that cannot do the thing would be a lie in code
form. `backend/test_voice_reflex.py` holds every one of them to still being
chat (except where noted, where the pre-existing generic path already
answers):

| Command | Why it is not built | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| "switch to cockpit/studio/ambient [mode/layout]" | The HUD layout is a DESKTOP LOCAL STORAGE setting; the backend cannot write a webview's storage, and no settings-write or route-field for it exists | `jarvis-desktop/src/hud-window.js:120` (`HUD_LAYOUT_KEY = "jarvis.hud.layout"`), `:179` (`storage.setItem`); `git grep hud_layout -- '*.py'` finds nothing; the `X-Jarvis-Route` whitelist in `jarvis-desktop/src-tauri/src/commands.rs` has no such key |
| "pin/unpin the bar" | Pinning is a Tauri window command, not a backend setting | `jarvis-desktop/src/main.js:5437` (`invoke("set_quickbar_pinned")`); the bar's open state is `jarvis.hud.openBar` in local storage (`jarvis-desktop/src/hud-window.js:41`, `:74`); no Python route or setting for it |
| "open galaxy" / "open today" | No honest navigation channel: `open_place` is a Jarvis Settings SECTION id, and `open_brain` is handled by the apps for `history`, `topics`, `forget-range`, `brain` and `tutorials` (the last two since 2026-10-31); there is no `galaxy`/`today` place to name, and adding one needs BOTH apps | `jarvis-desktop/src/main.js` `openBrainFromRoute`; `jarvis-desktop/src/main.js:1755` (`open_place`); `jarvis-client` `ui/OpenPlace.kt` maps menu ids, not route places. These two phrases keep whatever the PRE-EXISTING "open a program" path does - unchanged - which does not open the HUD |
| "mute / unmute / mute for N minutes" | Live's mute is the app's microphone control; there is no timed mute and no TTS-output mute. A muted microphone cannot HEAR "unmute", so a voice unmute is impossible by construction | `jarvis_live.py:1053` (`LiveSession.mute`, driven by the app's Mute button/`/api/voice/live` body); no timer for it anywhere |
| "repeat that" | Nothing stores the last spoken reply for replay, and no route field asks a client to say it again | no `last_reply`/replay path in `backend/*.py`; the route whitelist has no key for it |
| "scroll down/up", "go back", "go home" | `jarvis_ui_control` acts only through an APPROVED carded plan (`plan`/`run`); there is no standalone non-carded navigation primitive, and adding one would be a new screen action without a card - forbidden | `jarvis_ui_control.py` "ONE WINDOW AT A TIME, AND PROOF THAT AN ACTION LANDED"; the phone's `scroll` is `jarvis_app_control`'s swipe on the PHONE's screen, a different device |

### 154.5 Tests, cards, and both apps

`backend/test_voice_reflex.py` (108 checks in a tree with #691; the three
#691-matcher checks SKIP - never pass - when that module is absent, and the
suite counts its skips on their own line): the measured number gaps above; the
polite lead-ins and their gerund forms; the duration forms that already
worked, held unchanged; the safe number rule and its "stays chat" cases ("one
of the files", "call me three times", "twenty five"); idempotence on every
sentence; a measured **< 5 ms in the test** bound for every new form (the only
speed claim made here - the turn's end-to-end speed is owner-only to measure
and is not claimed); the speed reflex's real state change and the voices
module's own words; the sixteen #691 read phrases NOT matching this fast path
(and #691's matchers still claiming them); every command in 154.4 NOT being a
new intent; and the plain missing-module sentence. Against the pre-fix module
the same suite is **50 passed, 31 failed**, so every claim above bites.

**Approval cards are unchanged: they are decided by a physical tap, never by
voice.** The reflex never consults `jarvis_gate` (the suite spies it and
proves it is never called): there is nothing to approve in a cosmetic speed
change. Both apps get all of this through the SAME chat pipeline with **no app
change** (a quick answer is already rendered by both), so
`tools/check_parity.py` is unaffected and there is no
`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8 one-sidedness to record from this slice.


## 155. Duet Wave D-2: read-only work that does not wait, two outbound tiers, source provenance, and the walk brain-dump (backend only, added 2026-10-22)

**What it is.** Four pieces of the DeepSeek Duet wave, all additive: a plan of
background steps whose read-only parts keep working while an approval card
waits; a two-tier classifier for anything about to be staged outbound, plus
three categories the browser tool refuses outright; a `source_provenance` tag
on spending and document summaries; and the walk brain-dump that becomes an
evening report. No new route, no new dependency, no deploy: the backend files
are the whole change and the twins in `jarvis-backend/` are byte-identical.

**D-2.1 - a plan's read-only steps do not wait for a card.** `jarvis_jobs.py`
gains `create_plan(steps, *, label, caps, when, tainted)`. Each step is
`{"handler": <registered name>, "params": {}, "readonly": bool,
"depends_on": [earlier step indexes]}` (at most 24 steps; a dependency must
name an EARLIER step, so a plan is acyclic by construction). It is the same
job row, capability set and taint as `create()`; the difference is what
happens when a step asks for a capability outside the frozen set:

* that step is marked `waiting_approval` with `pending_action` and
  `card_id` (the job's one-shot grant request is the card channel - jobs never
  call `jarvis_gate.check`, and this module has no approval API at all);
* every remaining step that is `readonly: true` and does not transitively
  depend on the waiting step **keeps running in the same tick**;
* every remaining step that depends on it, or that changes something and is
  ordered after it without being read-only, is marked
  `queued_behind_approval` and runs on a later tick - after the owner's yes
  is spent by `ctx.require`;
* Stop/Cancel halts at the next step boundary (`ctx.checkpoint()`), and the
  statuses already reached are saved first. There is no Pause state in this
  module (a job is one row in `queued|running|waiting_approval|done|failed|
  cancelled`); the HUD's Stop is `cancel()`.
* When every step is done, the result carries piece D-1.4's exact vocabulary:
  `"review_status": "ready_for_review"`. Nothing in the runner marks the job
  reviewed, collected or delivered - only the owner's action does.

Continuing steps can never approve, deny or mutate the waiting card: the
runner does not touch the grants table, and a step only ever gets the same
`JobContext` a single-handler job gets.

**D-2.2 - two tiers outbound, and three outright refusals.**
`jarvis_scrub.classify_outbound_sensitivity(outbound_text, *, user_prompt="",
tainted=False)` is a pure function (no clock, no network, no model) answering
`{allowed, tier, reasons, categories, redacted_text, tainted}`:

* **Tier 1 - never out, even when asked.** Luhn-valid 13-19 digit card
  numbers (the shape alone is not enough; the checksum decides), US
  SSNs/government ids, `vault://` handles, API-key shapes (`sk-`, `sk_live_`,
  `ghp_`, `github_pat_`, `AKIA`, `AIza`, `xox*`, PEM private keys), and
  pairing tokens (`jdk1.d<8 hex>.<43>`, exactly `jarvis_devices.KEY_PATTERN`).
  `redacted_text` masks the shapes with the module's own `[redacted ...]`
  marker, so a refusal can show a scrubbed draft and never the value.
* **Tier 2 - health and personal-finance figures.** Allowed ONLY when
  `tainted is False` AND the owner's own `user_prompt` explicitly authorises
  sharing that category (a documented regex: "send/email/share/forward/...
  <category> words"). Otherwise refused with a reason. A bare "send it" is
  not an authorisation; a tainted turn (it read outside text) is refused even
  when asked. **The owner's own records are not outside text** (RA-6,
  2026-10-23): reading the spending table (`my_spending`) or a saved memory
  (`memory_search`) in the turn does not taint it for this gate, so "read my
  Q3 tax total from my spending CSV and email it to my accountant" stages the
  draft card as usual; every other reading tool (email, web pages, files,
  notes read back, the screen, the phone) still does. Only the tool path can
  tell those apart - the classifier itself stays the pure function above -
  and a later turn of the same conversation is still treated as tainted
  (the chat log records only that a tool ran).

`jarvis_email_draft.plan()` runs the classifier on the subject+body BEFORE the
card is built: a refused draft is a `Plan` with a `problem` and no card, and
the words say which tier and why. Ordinary drafts are unchanged.

`jarvis_browser_control.check_outright_refusal(url="", action_text="")` answers
`None` or `{ok: False, code: "outright_refused_category", category, why,
allowed_with_approval: False}` for **securities trading**, **inter-account
money transfer / wire / ACH / crypto**, and **third-party account access**.
`plan()`, `run()` and `run_steps()` call it at the top, so those requests are
refused before a card is ever raised: a card would offer a yes this tool will
never act on.

**D-2.3 - source provenance on summaries and hits.**
`jarvis_spending`: `result_for_model`/`subscriptions_for_model` (the summaries
the model reads) carry `"source_provenance": {"kind": "spreadsheet", "files":
[...], "label": "From: <file>"}` in `_run_tool`. `jarvis_documents`: every
`search()` hit and every `read()` answer carries the same shape with
`kind: "file"` and the exact filename. It is **additive** - every existing key
and sentence is unchanged - and it is **withheld** (`None` / absent) when the
trusted private-view state says `app_locked` or `hide_memory_lists`, because
the file names are the owner's own material. The drawn spending TABLE keeps
exactly its old keys, because it is the two-apps contract fixture
(`tools/gen_spending_cases.py` serialises it) and adding a key there would
change both apps' snapshots for no user-visible gain.

**D-2.4 - the walk brain-dump and the evening report.**
`jarvis_live.stage_walk_brain_dump(text_or_utterances, *, session_id="default",
now_ts=None)` splits the owner's spoken paragraph on ordinal markers ("first",
"second", "also", "and another thing", "next", "finally") and sentence
boundaries, classifies each item `read_only_prep` (research/read/check/prepare/
draft/note/review/find) or `needs_approval_card` (email/send/buy/book/pay/call/
remind/schedule/publish...), stores them per session (bounded at 60) and
answers counts + words. `build_evening_report(session_id="default", *,
hide_memory_lists=False, app_locked=False, now_ts=None)` bundles the prepared
items (each with `source_provenance.kind = "walk_note"`) and the items still
waiting for a card; under the hidden/locked state the item text and provenance
are withheld while the counts stay. **Nothing is sent and nothing is approved**
- there is no outbound path in this section.

**Tests.** `backend/test_duet_d2.py` (45 checks): the four-step continuation
(step 3's read-only step runs while step 2 waits, step 4 queues; the bite is
the recorded order, so removing the continuation fails it), the owner's yes
completes the plan and the result says `ready_for_review`, cancellation runs
no handler; Tier 1 refused with an explicit prompt (card, SSN, vault handle,
API key, pairing token) and redacted; Tier 2 refused unrequested and tainted,
allowed explicitly requested and untainted; an email draft with a card number
gets a `problem` instead of a card; brokerage/wire/third-party refusals from
`check_outright_refusal`, `run_steps` and `plan()`; spending and document
provenance present and withheld; the three-item walk splits 1 prep + 2 cards
and the report withholds under lock.

## 156. A private chat: reads-only, and nothing reaches the disk (backend Slice 1, added 2026-10-25)

The architect's H10 ruling (2026-10-25, design A): a **private chat** is a
temporary chat plus a strict zero-write promise. A request to `POST /api/chat`
carrying `"private": true` (JSON `true` and nothing else - the same strict
reading `temporary` gets in §18.1) implies `temporary: true` for memory and
history, and additionally:

- **writes nothing to disk.** Every writer a chat turn can reach is refused:
  `chat-history.db` (the row AND `jarvis_chat_log`'s own housekeeping - the
  module is not called at all), `memory.db` and the background learner,
  `feedback.db`'s turn row, `speed.jsonl`, the route-audit line
  (`~/.openjarvis/logs/jarvis-<date>.jsonl`), `hud-budget.json`,
  `approvals.db`, `receipts.db`, the answer-sources row and the device's
  `last_seen`. The gate is **fail-closed**: if the shipped
  `jarvis_private_chat.py` is missing or broken, the strict one-line flag
  reading still applies and every private write is still refused - a missing
  file can never turn a private turn into an ordinary one. The device sighting
  is written by the token check before the body is read, so it is held for the
  length of the request and dropped as soon as the body says private; if the
  request fails before that drop, the wrapper drops it too, so a failed private
  request writes no sighting either. In the agent turn, `private` also switches
  off the end-of-turn tool-chain audit line (`jarvis_skill_discovery`) and the
  `jarvis_next_time` brought-up mark and `jarvis_energy` row, and it skips the
  **Write Like Me drafting block entirely**: no `voiceprint.db` read, no
  embedding-model download, no latch and no stored writing samples in the
  prompt.
- **runs no tool.** The hud tells the agent the turn is private (the
  `private: true` handed in beside the deny-all gate), and the agent enforces
  it where every local turn passes: it empties the tool list ITSELF - the
  owner's own `jarvis-framework.toml` cannot re-enable one, which is why the
  flag is not merely a config the agent might ignore - offers no tool to the
  model, and answers any tool call that still arrives with a refusal instead
  of dispatching it. That last point matters because the settings and schedule
  shortcuts deliberately bypass the approval gate: in a private chat they are
  never reached, so `change_setting` cannot run and no setting can change; no
  tool runs, no `approvals.db` row is written and no undo receipt from a
  tool-based action can be produced. `jarvis_quick.answer()` refuses a
  state-changing fast-path command BEFORE running it, so no reminder, timer,
  setting, personality, goal or note is touched and no cardless receipt is
  written either. A private chat reads, searches and answers from the model
  alone: no stored memory, no stored writing samples and no tools; it does not
  act.
- **answers a mutating FAST-PATH command with one sentence**: "A private chat
  can read, search, and answer, but it doesn't change settings, save items, or
  run actions — switch back to a normal chat to do that." (the sentence has one
  copy, in the shipped `jarvis_private_chat.py`; a backend without the module
  still refuses with a byte-identical fallback). A request that would need a
  card-gated tool never gets as far as a card: the tool list is empty and the
  AGENT answers any remaining tool call with a short refusal instead of
  dispatching it - the approval gate is never even reached. The sentence is
  not a promise that every private request receives it.
- **the RAM-only parts stay RAM-only**: the live-turn registry is not called
  either, so a private turn leaves no hash and no marker - there is nothing
  on disk to correlate.

`X-Jarvis-Route` carries **`"private": true`** on every answer the turn
actually produces after the body was read (with the temporary keys when memory
is not Jarvis's own upstream's), so an app can prove the PC treated the turn as
private; a request rejected earlier as malformed never reaches the header.
`GET /api/version`'s `capabilities.private_chat` is true only when the running
server has BOTH `private-chat.patch`'s `_private_chat` and the shipped
`jarvis_private_chat.py` - asked of the server by name, exactly like
`capabilities.temporary_chat`. A server with the patch and no module reports
false, so an app sends nothing rather than believing a half-gate.

**Desktop Slice 2 (2026-10-26):** the desktop chat window now has a Private chip
beside Incognito. It sends ONLY `"private": true` (never `temporary` too - the
server implies that half), starts a new conversation when it is turned on or
off, and refuses to offer the mode when `/api/version` does not advertise
`capabilities.private_chat`; the Rust command fails closed with an honest
sentence and sends nothing. The private turn answers with the model alone (no
stored memory, no writing samples, no tools). The phone deliberately sends no
flag: its private mode is Incognito, and this half is desktop-only.

**Tests.** `backend/test_private_chat.py`: the gate module's strict reading and
fail-closed `persist()`; the fast path refusing every mutating sentence before
the scheduler is asked anything, and a read-only one going to the model; the
real hud guard blocks lifted from the installed file and run against writing
stubs, plus an **eight-store table** naming each store above and the evidence
for it; a private read turn and two private action turns (a cardless fast-path
command and a carded tool request) write nothing, the positive control writes
with `private: false`, and a writer that would raise is never called
(fail-closed); a **driven agent turn with the owner's framework file naming
tools**, whose scripted model asks for `change_setting` - the settings
shortcut that bypasses the gate - proving the offer is empty, nothing is
dispatched, no card is asked, no chain line and no energy row is written, and
the same turn without the flag does each of those; a drafted request in a
private turn never reaches the Write Like Me block (no `voiceprint.db`, no
stored sample in the prompt) while the same turn without the flag does; the
device `last_seen`
hold / commit / drop-on-failure driven through the real devices wrapper; the
missing/broken-gate case (private stays refused and the capability reports
false); the patch applying to the published base AND to the owner's live
`jarvis_hud.py`, and reversing out of it; and the module's SHIPPED and twin
delivery. A dated entry in `docs/DECISIONS.md` records the ruling.

## 157. The owner-secret hand-off: a card the host draws, and the 15-minute read taint (wired 2026-10-26)

The rule engine is `jarvis_secret_handoff.py` and the host half is
`jarvis_secret_handoff_wiring.py`. Together they let the owner type a password
into ONE card the host draws and have the host type it into the control the
owner approved, without the value ever entering the model's context, a tool
result, a log line, the clipboard, a database or a file.

**How a card is raised.** When an agent's UI-control plan
(`jarvis_ui_control.plan()`) carries a `type` request aimed at a
password-masked control, the plan does not bind a step and does not run the
request. The host measures that control with Windows UI Automation (pid, hwnd,
window class, control identity, `IsPassword=True`), raises one card through the
engine, and the plan reports the unmatched request as
`code: "secret_handoff_raised"`. The agent's own `why` is the card's second box
and is always labelled unverified. The model never supplies a target field.

**Routes (host-only: pairing token AND a loopback caller; the body is never
logged or echoed).**

| route | what it does |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/secret-handoff/pending` | the cards waiting for the owner: `handoff_id`, `verified_target` (host-measured), `target_kind`, `is_https`, `agent_claimed_purpose`, `agent_purpose_is_untrusted`, `expires_in_seconds`. Never a secret. |
| `POST /api/secret-handoff/create` | raises a card from the password-masked control that has focus **right now** (the honest fallback for a host caller; the HUD does not use it - its own click moves focus). Body: `{"purpose": "..."}` optionally. Refuses 409 when the focused control is not password-masked. |
| `POST /api/secret-handoff/fill` | body `{"handoff_id": "...", "secret": "..."}`. Re-measures the stored window/control, builds a live `VerifiedTargetSnapshot`, and calls the engine's `execute_owner_fill(..., from_this_pc=True)`. The ENGINE decides every void (changed target, changed control, no longer password-masked, expired, empty/oversized, used card); this route does not repeat those checks. A changed target therefore types zero characters and answers 409 with the engine's own sentence. |
| `POST /api/secret-handoff/cancel` | body `{"handoff_id": "..."}`. The owner pressed Cancel; drops the card. |

Both POST routes refuse a non-loopback caller **before the body is read** (403
with a plain sentence), and origin/token are checked before that. The body
reader is the server's own; no route logs, stores or returns the request body.

A refused `create` (409) carries a safe `reason_code` - one of `E_UIA_IMPORT`,
`E_NO_FOCUSED_CONTROL`, `E_NOT_PASSWORD`, `E_NO_TOP_WINDOW`,
`E_NOT_IN_WINDOW_TREE`, `E_UIA_READ_FAIL`, or the exception's type name - and
never a secret or any part of the request body. Windows UI Automation is a COM
API and every thread that calls it must initialise COM itself, so the host does
that once per thread (`jarvis_ui_control.ensure_uia_com_on_this_thread`) before
every UIA call; without it the live backend's HTTP request threads refused every
card with `CoInitialize has not been called` (measured 2026-10-26).

**The HUD card holds no token, and its writes go through the shell.** The page
never receives the pairing token (apps security audit M2): the pending read is
one more entry on hud_proxy.rs's fixed GET list (GET /api/secret-handoff/pending),
and Fill and Cancel are two Rust commands - hud_secret_handoff_fill and
hud_secret_handoff_cancel - granted to the HUD window through the hud-link
permission set and registered in uild.rs's command list. They add the token
in Rust, validate the card id shape before sending, never log or include the
secret in an error, and POST the two host-only routes above; the bootstrap
fetch shim still refuses the page's own POSTs, exactly like every other HUD
write. Nothing about this weakens the rule: the page gets no token.

**What the fill does, in order.** The taint is marked by the engine BEFORE the
first character is typed (so a typing failure still leaves the target
read-locked); typing goes through `jarvis_ui_control.secret_handoff_type`,
which refuses a control that is no longer password-masked, focuses it and sends
the keys through the same SendKeys path every other UI-control type step uses.
The receipt names the verified target and the taint duration - never the value.

**The read side.** While a target key is tainted (15 minutes, in memory only),
`jarvis_ui_control.get_window_state()` answers
`{"ok": false, "code": "secret_read_restricted"}` before it reads the tree or
pixels, and `read_selection()` returns the same refusal before it reads a
character. The keys are page addresses or `pid:hwnd:window class`, never a
secret.

**What is deliberately NOT wired.** The browser path: `jarvis_browser_control`
sessions are tool-scoped, so the HUD has no session handle to name and this
slice does not invent one (see `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8). The phone: the card
is PC-only. No approval card is raised by this feature itself: the owner's
typing is the approval, and the existing gate still governs the plan that
asked.

## 158. Updates in chat: "is there an update?", "what changed?", "update Jarvis" (added 2026-10-26)

The owner's request, in their own words: *"can jarvis talk about an update if
theres one availabale and the changes? and start the update process for me?"* -
*"if i ask in chat"*. **No new route.** The two questions are answers from the
`/api/chat` fast path (`backend/jarvis_quick.py`, no model), and starting the
update is ONE approval card on the gate every other change already uses.

### 158.1 What the desktop shell tells its backend: the `desktop` body field

The only party that knows which version is running, and whether this build can
verify a download, is the Tauri shell (`jarvis-desktop/src-tauri/src/update.rs`
`desktop_chat_facts`). Both chat paths this app owns add a top-level field to
the `POST /api/chat` body, **after** the field whitelist, so a page cannot set
it:

```json
{ "messages": [...], "desktop": { "version": "0.2.320", "can_update": true } }
```

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | string, `\d+\.\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?` | the build actually running. Anything else is treated as absent |
| `can_update` | boolean | `true` only when `tauri.conf.json` has a real `plugins.updater.pubkey`. A missing key, or a truthy non-boolean, is **not** a yes |

It is additive and optional: a client that does not send it (the phone, a
browser, an older desktop) gets honest words instead of a guess. The HUD page
cannot supply it - `hud_proxy.rs`'s `chat_payload` keeps only the page's own
fields and `hud_chat` inserts the shell's facts afterwards - and the quickbar's
`stream_chat` adds the same value. It goes to the owner's own backend only,
carries no identifier, and is not read by any other route.

### 158.2 The answers, and what each state says

Matched as whole sentences, like every other fast path: `update_ask` ("is
there an update?", "any updates?", "is Jarvis up to date", "what version am I
on", "check for updates"), `update_notes` ("what changed in the update?",
"what's new in the update", "what does the update change", "the update notes")
and `update_start` ("update Jarvis", "update", "start/do/install the update",
"update to the latest version"). Bare "what's new", "how do I update Jarvis",
"when is the next update", "did the update break anything" and "update my
settings" are **not** ours and go to the model as before.

| state | the answer says |
|---|---|
| no `desktop` field | it cannot tell which build is asking; points at Settings -> Updates on the PC and Platform checks on the phone |
| `can_update: false` | this build has no update key, so it cannot check or install a download |
| the manifest could not be read | **the check failed**, so it cannot say whether there is an update; nothing was changed |
| same version | this is the newest published version |
| this build newer | a development build, newer than the published release; nothing to install |
| a newer version | the version, the running one, and how to hear what changed or start it |

`update_notes` quotes the release's own `notes` from
`desktop-latest/latest.json` (the same string Settings -> Updates shows), never
a list of its own. An empty field says the release does not say. A gap of more
than one version adds one sentence: the notes are for that release only and do
not cover the releases in between. The notes are written by
`jarvis-desktop/scripts/release-notes.mjs` from `changelog.d/` (and the rolled
`CHANGELOG.md` bullets only when a roll has emptied the folder), one summary
sentence per change, capped at 20 entries.

### 158.3 Starting it: ONE card, and nothing before the yes

`update_start` raises **one** approval card through `jarvis_gate.check`, action
**`desktop_update`**:

* tier `ask` in `jarvis-framework.toml` (an unlisted action would be `ask` too,
  but the row is written down so a later edit to `unknown_action_tier` cannot
  move it silently);
* in `jarvis_owner_check.PC_ONLY_ACTIONS` - **only this PC can approve it**, and
  Windows Hello comes first, whatever the tier table says. The phone shows the
  card and its Approve is refused with the standard `pc_only` 403; the card's
  own words say "only on this PC";
* on the **What asks first** page (`jarvis_asks_first.py`, in "Jarvis's own
  settings, memory and voice", and in its `HARD_LIMITS`/`MUST_ASK` sets), so the
  owner can find it beside the other cards over Jarvis's own code, with no
  switch: like everything there whose module refuses a looser tier, it can
  never be changed to run without asking;
* the card names both halves, the version, the restart, the pace (Balanced),
  the signature check, and that nothing is downloaded, installed or changed
  before the yes.

**What the approval runs.** The owner's Approve goes through
`decide_approval` (`POST /api/approve` with the token, the stale-link refusal
and Windows Hello just as for any card). `commands.rs` `answer_approval` reads
the card's own `action` from the pending queue it already holds **before** the
decision is sent, and only when it is `desktop_update` does it call
`update.rs` `run_approved_update`: a fresh check, then the SAME `update_both`
the Settings button runs - backend first, then the signed desktop release,
then a restart. A denial, a timeout, a stale link, a locked PC or a card that
cannot be read starts nothing.

**What deliberately does not exist.** No route downloads an installer, no page
may start one (the HUD window still holds no update command in
`capabilities/hud.json`), no timer or startup path reaches it, and the chat's
"do it now" is still only the card.

**What this does and does not close (S3).** The self-improvement audit's
finding S3 named the desktop updater as the one self-modification path outside
the gate. The CHAT-STARTED path now has the gate card, Windows Hello and the
approvals row as its audit line. The Settings window's own Install and
"update both halves" buttons are unchanged and are still direct `update_both`
calls with only their own in-window question - S3 is improved for the new
path, not closed for the old one, and closing it there is a separate decision.

### 158.4 The two apps

The desktop answers both questions and starts the update. The phone is
**one-sided on purpose** (recorded in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8): a message from
the phone carries no `desktop` field, so the reply says it can only check the
PC's build from the PC's app and points at **Platform checks**, the phone's own
update card, where the owner downloads its APK and Android's installer asks for
the tap. Nothing installs itself on either device.

## 159. The Anti-Slop filter: three routes, a card on the desktop and three controls on the phone (added 2026-10-28)

`GET` and `POST /api/antislop`, plus the read-only `POST /api/antislop/audit`,
are the whole contract. They carry the state of the **Anti-Slop filter** - a
wording and output-quality filter over what Jarvis writes - whose rules are the
MIT-licensed [`miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop`](https://github.com/miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop)
ruleset (`v3.2.23`), distilled on the PC into `backend/jarvis_antislop.py` (and
its byte-identical `jarvis-backend/` twin) to the few rules that fit a local
model's prompt budget. Nothing is fetched at run time: no `npx`, no network, no
folder beyond the PC's own config file, and none of the source rulebook's
installer or Markdown skills is downloaded, run or shipped. The credit line is
in `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt`.

The three routes come from the module's own
`install(handler_cls, *, origin_ok, token_ok, read_body)` - the shape every
drop-in module uses - which `plugins/ready/antislop/plugin.json` asks
`jarvis_plugins.py` to call. **No patch of its own.** All three sit behind the
server's usual origin and token checks, before anything is read.

It filters the **words** Jarvis writes and audits a page or a file. It opens no
network door, reads no folder, takes no action and loosens no gate, so
**turning it on or off raises no approval card** - the same class as the prompt
coach (`docs/DECISIONS.md`, 2026-10-28). Every change still leaves ONE action
receipt with a one-click Undo through `jarvis_receipts.py`, action name
`antislop`.

**OFF is inert, and that is a promise the card repeats in one line:** the
prompt block is the empty string, `post_process_reply()` returns its input
unchanged and `reply_filter()` returns `None`, so nothing is added to a prompt
(**0 prompt tokens**) and no reply is rewritten. ON adds a short rules block
matched to the parts the owner ticked.

### 159.1 What it does, and what it costs

* **On, `during`** (the default when switched ON): a
  `<antislop_filter mode="during">` system message of at most 1,050 characters
  (about 240 tokens), placed just before the newest user message exactly like
  the manner and focus notes (never first, so the rules block stays first),
  plus a deterministic scrub of the words as they stream: em dashes out of
  prose (R-02), and decorative banners and emoji comments out of fenced code
  (`antislop-code`). The scrub holds back only a trailing space, a trailing em
  dash or a line inside a code block, so the answer still streams.
* **On, `after`**: the note asks for a numbered findings list and no edits, and
  the scrub is bypassed - an audit may quote the very em dash it reports.
* **`R-37` wins over `R-02`, always.** When "Write Like Me" is on and the
  owner's own writing samples use em dashes, the ban yields in both the note
  and the scrub, because the owner's own prose is direction rather than slop.
  `jarvis_antislop.voiceprint_uses_em_dash()` is the single place that decides,
  and it answers False whenever it cannot read the samples - no exemption is
  ever invented.
* **The owner can allow em dashes outright**: `allow_em_dashes` (default
  `false`) drops the R-02 line from the note and leaves prose dashes alone
  while the REST of the copy scope keeps working - generic CTAs (R-15) and AI
  buzzwords (R-16) are still flagged in the audit and still named in the note.
  It is a stored flag rather than a second voiceprint reading, so a preference
  the owner set cannot move when their samples change. It is the blanket "keep
  them everywhere" on top of `R-37`, deliberately not the voiceprint rule.
* **The scrub only ever sees the model's own chat words**: its prose and the
  fenced code blocks inside that answer. Never a tool's input or output, a file
  Jarvis writes, a diff or a patch, or a file already in a repository - and
  `audit_text_or_ui` is read-only, so a file handed to it is reported on and
  left exactly as it was. Inside fenced code it removes **only** a wordless
  separator line (`# ============`) or a comment led by one of the ten
  decorative emoji; a shebang, a coding/`type`/`noqa`/`pragma` line, a Rust doc
  comment, a diff header and any comment carrying real words are never touched.
  A headed banner (`# --- Phase 2: Database Migration ---`) is left to the
  prompt rule and the `after` audit.

### 159.2 What is enforced, and what is only guided

The audit report says which is which, on every run, in its own `words` header
and in the `enforcement` object, before any finding is read. The split is data
(`ENFORCEMENT_CLASS_A` / `ENFORCEMENT_CLASS_B` in `jarvis_antislop.py`), so the
header cannot drift from what the code really does.

| Class | Rules | How it is described |
|---|---|---|
| **A - deterministic, checked here** | `R-02` (with the `R-37` voiceprint exemption and the `allow_em_dashes` override), `R-10` / `R-13` dose caps, `R-15`, `R-16`, `R-17`/`R-36`/`R-38` (through `jarvis_claims.py`), `R-24`/`R-26` **static** dead links and unwired buttons, `R-25` **unrounded** WCAG 2.1 contrast on a static hex pair, `R-32` **static** `outline: none` with no ring put back, `antislop-code` banners | may be claimed as checked by `jarvis_antislop.py` |
| **B - prompt-guided only** | `R-03` dynamic overflow and rendered 44x44 tap targets, `R-18` a fabricated testimonial, `R-20` the identity test, `R-23` asset confirmation, `R-27` semantic state completeness, `R-28` a generic FAQ, `R-30` clone detection, `R-34`/`R-35` live theme switching and click-through | **PROMPT-GUIDED ONLY, never mechanically enforced** - they need a live browser, a person's judgement or the data source. The project's Playwright suites (`themecheck.mjs`, `hud.mjs`) are what prove R-34/R-35, not this module |

The card carries that split as ONE sentence (the `REALITY` line in
`src/antislop.js`, the same words in `net/Antislop.kt`), and
`jarvis-desktop/tests/antislop.mjs` fails if the line stops saying "guidance
only", or starts naming a browser-only rule as checked. No screen and no record
may claim that every anti-slop rule is mechanically enforced.

### 159.3 The routes

Three routes, written method-first on their own lines - the shape
`tools/check_parity.py` reads a documented route from, so none of them can go
missing from its parity check:

    GET  /api/antislop          the whole state, in the PC's own shape
    POST /api/antislop          one control sends ONE change, through its own setter
    POST /api/antislop/audit    read-only: the rule findings for text the caller already has

**`GET /api/antislop`** - the whole state, in the PC's own shape:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "enabled": false,
  "mode": "during",
  "scopes": {"copy": true, "code": true, "ui": true},
  "dials": {"energy": 1, "rhythm": 2, "motion": 1},
  "allow_em_dashes": false,
  "show_delivery_gate_on_ui_tasks": true,
  "updated_at": 1793164200.0,
  "words": "The Anti-Slop filter is off, so it adds nothing to the prompt and changes nothing in an answer.",
  "source": "miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop v3.2.23 (MIT), rules distilled and vendored",
  "max_prompt_chars": 1050
}
```

`mode` is `during` (filter while writing - the default when switched ON) or
`after` (change nothing; list numbered findings by `R-01..R-38` and let the
owner pick). `scopes` is what is filtered; `dials` are the Liveliness Toolkit's
three 1-3 dials (ENERGY, RHYTHM, MOTION). `allow_em_dashes` is the em-dash
exemption and is **OFF unless it is a real `true`** - a backend that predates
the field simply has no key, and both apps paint the box unticked, which is the
state that PC really holds. `words` is the same state as one plain sentence,
and `max_prompt_chars` is the hard ceiling the prompt block can never pass. A
read is never held.

A PC whose backend predates this section answers `404`, or `503` with
`{"available": false, "why": "..."}`. **A body with no `enabled` yes-or-no is
never read as "off":** both apps say the route is missing, because a state
nobody could read is not a filter that is switched off.

**`POST /api/antislop`** - one control sends ONE change; the route accepts
several parts at once and applies each through its own setter:

| Body | What it changes |
| --- | --- |
| `{"enabled": true \| false}` | the master switch |
| `{"mode": "during" \| "after"}` | the mode |
| `{"scopes": {"copy" \| "code" \| "ui": true \| false}}` | one scope |
| `{"dials": {"energy" \| "rhythm" \| "motion": 1..3}}` | one or more dials |
| `{"show_delivery_gate_on_ui_tasks": true \| false}` | the Delivery Gate on a finished screen |
| `{"allow_em_dashes": true \| false}` | keep em-dashes everywhere (the blanket exemption) |

The PC merges the named field(s) into its stored state and answers with the
whole state back (`ok`, the fields above and `words`), so a client paints the
PC's answer rather than its own optimism. Errors are named rather than generic:
`unknown_setting` for a key the PC does not have (a typo must never read back
as "saved"), `bad_mode` for a mode that is neither, `bad_value` for a dial
outside 1..3 or a value a setter refuses, `nothing_to_change` for an empty
body, and `bad_body` when the body is not a JSON object; a write that throws is
`503` with the error named. There is no `tier`, no card and no Windows Hello in
either direction.

**Takes effect on the very next turn** (the state is read per turn, never
cached at start-up), and is announced on the event stream as kind
**`antislop`** carrying the whole state - one kind per feature, the shape
`appearance`, `devices` and `big-coder` already use. The blueprint called it a
"settings" event; no such kind exists in this backend and none was invented.
The desktop Settings card re-reads on that frame, and so does the phone's
plate (`JarvisRuntime.antislopTick`) - a change made by chat, by the desktop
card or by another phone reaches an OPEN plate without reopening Settings. The
phone's plate also re-reads after every write of its own, and while it is not
open nothing is fetched for it.

**`POST /api/antislop/audit`** - read-only; it changes no setting:

| Body | Answer |
|---|---|
| `{"content": "...", "kind": "auto"\|"text"\|"markdown"\|"md"\|"html"\|"css"\|"js"\|"code"\|"ui"}` | **200** `{ok, kind, findings[{rule, tier, line, detail}], counts{HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW}, total, gate{blocks[4], passes, words}, checked, state, source, enforcement{class_a, class_b, class_b_enforced, header}, words}` and, for a UI kind in `during` mode, `delivery_gate`. **400** `"no_content"` / `"too_long"` (over 400,000 characters). An unknown `kind` falls back to `auto`, which reads the content's own shape. |

Each finding names the rule it comes from and the line it is on, sorted by line
and then rule so two runs are byte-identical:

| Rule | Tier | What it reports |
|---|---|---|
| `R-02` | HIGH | an em dash in agent-written prose |
| `R-25` | HIGH | WCAG AA contrast below 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text), compared **unrounded** - `#777777` on white is 4.4781:1 and fails even though it rounds to 4.5; `#757575` is 4.6075:1 and passes |
| `R-26` | HIGH | an `<a href="#">` / `javascript:void` link, or a `<button>` with no id, handler, form or data attribute |
| `R-32` | HIGH | `outline: none` (or `0`) with no `:focus`/`:focus-visible` ring put back |
| `R-10` | MEDIUM | more than 2 glassmorphism declarations (`backdrop-filter`) |
| `R-13` | MEDIUM | more than 2 glow shadows (a `box-shadow` with no offset) |
| `R-15` | LOW | a generic call to action ("Get Started", "Learn More", ...) |
| `R-16` | LOW | an AI buzzword ("seamless", "revolutionary", ...) |
| `antislop-code` | LOW | a decorative comment banner or an emoji comment |

The answer also carries the rulebook's **4-block Delivery Gate** (Hard Gate,
Purpose-Gate, Liveliness, Craftsmanship). Liveliness is reported as `NOT
CHECKED`, never as a pass: a focal point, one accent and real whitespace are a
judgement, and no regex may certify them. The Class B rules above are not
reported as passes either - they are named in the header as prompt-guided, and
no finding is ever attributed to one of them. What the auditor cannot see at
all - a rendered page, a real keyboard focus ring, the empty/loading/error
states of a data source - is named here rather than silently passed.

### 159.4 The two apps

**Desktop - Settings, How Jarvis talks, Anti-Slop filter**
(`src/antislop-settings.js`, drawn from `src/antislop.js`; two Rust commands in
`src-tauri/src/antislop.rs`, granted to the Settings window alone by
`permissions/surfaces.toml`). The card has the master switch, the three scope
pills, the "Allow em-dashes (—)" box inside "What it filters", the During/After
radio, the Delivery Gate switch and the three dials, and the ON-only halves are
hidden while it is off. Each control sends one change and re-reads afterwards;
a refusal shows the PC's own sentence and springs the control back. **None of
it is held on a stale link, on purpose:** the filter opens no way out of the PC
and takes no action, so a link that is catching up says nothing about whether
an answer should be de-slopped. That is a decision, not an omission - it is
said in the module, in `surfaces.toml` and in `src-tauri/src/antislop.rs`.

**Phone - Settings, How Jarvis talks** (`net/Antislop.kt`,
`ui/screens/AntislopPlate.kt`), bound to the same route: the master switch, the
"Allow em-dashes (—)" box and the During/After mode, in the same words. The
scopes, the gate switch and the dials are the desktop card's on purpose - the
phone is a settings mirror, not a second editor (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8).
Its writes ARE held on a stale link (`JarvisRuntime.setAntislop`,
`setAntislopMode`, `setAntislopEmDashes`), the same reading every other phone
setting takes: "at once" means no approval card, not "works while the link is
down".

**By asking, on either app** (`backend/jarvis_settings_registry.py`,
`backend/jarvis_quick.py`): "turn on anti-slop", "turn off anti-slop", "enable
anti-slop", "disable anti-slop", "is anti-slop on?", "set anti-slop mode to
during/after", "turn on/off anti-slop for copy/code/ui", and the generic "set
`<name>` to `<value>`". Typed on the PC's fast path, so no client change is
needed for them and no model is called. `antislop` is a `BOOL_SETTINGS` row and
`antislop_mode` a `CHOICE_SETTINGS` row, so a spoken change reaches the same
setters this route does, and `jarvis_feature_guide.read_state("antislop")`
reads the switch itself, so "is it on?" can never be a guess. The `antislop`
row's `section` is `None` on purpose: its desktop control is a bespoke card,
not one of the generated `<label class="toggle">` rows, and pointing the guide
at `manner` made the manner feature carry two switches - which
`backend/test_feature_guide.py`'s single-switch count caught. `antislop_mode`
names `manner` because the mode does live on that card. The em-dash exemption
has **no** typed phrase of its own: it is a checkbox in Settings, and inventing
a spoken name for it would be a second control surface the PC's grammar does
not have.

**What deliberately does not exist.** No model tool, no card, no background
run, and no second rulebook: nothing of `anti-slop`'s own installer, Markdown
