chat and is why nothing special was added for it.

| device | what it gets |
|---|---|
| the PC (`client_surface="hud"`) | the full breakdown: up to three legal options, each with its minute-by-minute maths and its walk time, then what it cannot know |
| a phone (`client_surface="phone"`) | two thumb-sized options, a `geo:` link each (`geo:47.60940,-122.34250?q=...`), and **not one desktop-only phrase** - `backend/test_parking.py` checks the short answer against `DESKTOP_ONLY` |

**How the device is known, said plainly.** `/api/chat`'s body carries no client
kind, and `jarvis_quick.answer_turn` never sees the `X-Jarvis-Client` header, so
this path does **not** read it. `answer_turn(client_surface=...)` takes an
explicit answer when a caller really knows; otherwise the reply is inferred with
`jarvis_owner_check.from_this_pc(peer, local)` - the project's own "is this the
PC" test, with its documented "cannot be placed counts as this PC" rule. A
request that plainly did **not** come from this PC therefore gets the phone's
short form; everything else gets the PC's full one. That is the honest shape of
what is available today, and a header-reading caller can change it without
touching this module.

### 165.6 The calendar bridge, and the one thing it will not do

"parking for my next meeting" reads the next upcoming event that has a
**location**, through `jarvis_google_calendar.list_events` (§161) when that
module and a way in are available, and degrades to one plain sentence when they
are not. The parking window is the event's own, **15 minutes either side**.

It reads the event's **times and its location line**. It never reads, returns
or sends the event's **title**.

**It deliberately does not send the location line to a public map service.** A
calendar entry is private even when the venue in it is public, and the rule this
module is built on is that only a place name the owner said out loud, or a
latitude and longitude, ever leaves the PC. So the answer quotes the venue back
locally and offers the **exact sentence to say, with the times already filled
in**:

```
Your next event with a place is at Pike Place Market, and parking for it would
run 2:45 PM to 4:15 PM (15 minutes either side). I have not sent the event's
own words to a map service, on purpose: say "parking near Pike Place Market"
and I will look it up from your own words.
```

Saying it makes it the owner's own words and the lookup runs normally. When the
event's location **already is** a coordinate pair there is nothing to send, and
the lookup runs in one step. And when the owner says a place in the SAME
sentence - "find cheap parking for my next meeting at the space needle" - that
place is his own words too, so it is looked up at once with the event's padded
window, and the calendar's location line is still not sent anywhere.

The reply quotes the calendar's own location line, so the turn counts as having
read outside text (`read=["calendar_read"]`) - the same conservative rule a
briefing that quotes event titles follows.

### 165.7 Tests

`backend/test_parking.py` - **140 checks, no network** (every socket and every
`urlopen` is made to fail for the whole run, and every provider call is handed a
recording fixture). It proves, among the rest:

* the six mandatory mutation-killing checks: the tail-end overlap is legal
  ($3.50, 105 paid + 180 free), an exceeded limit is refused with the **real**
  150-minute overlap, three rate tiers total **$30.50**, a Sunday and an
  after-hours window are **FREE ($0.00)**, a private lot and a "No Parking
  Allowed" blockface appear nowhere, and the phone's answer has a `geo:` link
  and zero desktop-only strings;
* both adapters from fixtures shaped like the real answers, the tag readers,
  the local cache (a second lookup asks nothing, a stale entry is asked again,
  a broken cache is a miss), a permit zone, a flat day price, an unpublished
  price never quoted at zero, and every failure degrading to a plain sentence;
* the privacy rule: the area services receive coordinates and a radius, the
  geocoder receives only the owner's own words, a coordinate pair makes no
  request at all, and no request ever carries an event title;
* the calendar bridge with an injected reader, its 15-minute padding, and that
  it does not put the calendar on the wire;
* the quick path end to end with `find_parking` recorded, so the wiring is
  proven with no socket, and `backend/test_quick_wins.py` holds the same path
  to answering without the model and without opening a socket.

The three base checks apply as for any shipped module: the byte-identical twin
`jarvis-backend/jarvis_parking.py`, its entry in both `SHIPPED` lists
(`backend/_where.py` and `scripts/apply-patches.ps1`), and the re-taken
`jarvis-backend/_where.py`.

**One manual check the owner may run on his own PC**, with no personal data in
it, is a single live call to each public service for a well-known public place:

```
py -3 -c "import jarvis_parking as P; print(P.find_parking('Pike Place Market', __import__('datetime').datetime(2026,11,2,10,0), __import__('datetime').datetime(2026,11,2,13,0)))"
```

That was **not** run in this checkout (no live call is made by any test or by
CI), so "the real services answer" is NOT-TESTABLE here and is the owner's
field check.

## 166. Building an Android app and putting it on your phone: four routes, no entry point yet (added 2026-10-30)

**Why this section number.** The last section on `main` when this was written
was 162, and four in-flight branches had already claimed 163-167 (the numbers
are named in this branch's brief as off-limits). **166 is the next free
number**, and this section is appended at the very END of the file so a
conflict here is two appends and both sides are kept (`CLAUDE.md`, "Appending
to a shared file").

**The owner's question (2026-10-30):** *"can jarvis build android apps? that
i can sideload into my phone? if not add them"*. The answer before this
section was **no**: milestones C (run a command), F (native Android projects)
and G (install the debug APK) of `docs/APP-BUILDER-DESIGN.md` were unbuilt,
and nothing in the backend had ever started a program that was not git.

**What is built.** The four routes below are the narrowest full path from an
app description to an app on the phone, in three steps, of which TWO COST A
CARD. **What is not built is the way in.** No chat sentence, no model tool and
no button in either app calls these routes yet; only this module's own tests
call them, and the tests drive the module's handlers directly. So the path is
complete for a caller and there is no caller: an entry point still has to be
written, and these contracts are what it would be built against.

The four routes, exactly as they are answered:

``text
GET  /api/projects/<id>/app/tasks/<task>/android
POST /api/projects/<id>/app/tasks/<task>/android/template
POST /api/projects/<id>/app/tasks/<task>/android/build
POST /api/projects/<id>/app/tasks/<task>/android/install
``

| Step | Route | Card | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Write the fixed project | `POST /api/projects/<id>/app/tasks/<task>/android/template` | **none** | - |
| Build it | `POST …/android/build` | **one** (`app_build_android`) | `ask` |
| Put it on the phone | `POST …/android/install` | **one** (`app_install_android`) | `ask` |
| See where it stands | `GET …/android` | none | - |

All three POSTs are **PC only** (`403 pc_only`, `pc_only: true`): the Android
SDK and the phone's cable are on this machine. The CARDS are not PC-only -
either device may approve one, so the owner can say yes from the sofa while
the PC does the work - and both are **risky** (`jarvis_gate._RISK`: reversible
"no"), so they ask for Windows Hello on the PC and the screen lock on the
phone, and a denial never becomes a standing rule
(`jarvis_gate._NO_RULE_FROM_DENIAL`).

### 166.1 The template: what Jarvis writes, and what it will not take from a model

The project is FIXED. It is strings inside `backend/jarvis_android_builder.py`,
and the only pieces that vary are **validated values**:

| Varies | Validation |
|---|---|
| The app's package | derived from the app folder's name, `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,39}$`, always under `com.jarvis.made.` |
| The app's name (the label on the phone) | `^[A-Za-z0-9 .,!?():+-]{1,40}$` - no quotes, because an Android string resource treats `'` as a delimiter and a stray one is a BUILD error |
| Two colours | `#rrggbb` |
| `assets/index.html`, `assets/app.js`, `assets/app.css` | a CLOSED list of three names; text; at most 96 KB each |

Everything else is written by Jarvis: `settings.gradle.kts`,
`build.gradle.kts`, `gradle.properties`,
`gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties`, `app/build.gradle.kts`,
`AndroidManifest.xml`, `MainActivity.kt`, `strings.xml`, `colors.xml`,
`themes.xml`, and the two Gradle wrapper files (Gradle's own: the jar is byte for byte `jarvis-client`'s, and the batch file is the same file with the CRLF endings cmd.exe needs put back on the way, because this repository stores text as LF). A request
that names any other file - or hides a path in an asset's name - is refused
with a sentence, never resolved.

**The template's properties, all measured on 2026-10-30** (a real build of
exactly this project; `docs/APP-BUILDER-DESIGN.md` and the scratch note
`.dsh-scratch/ANDROID-APP-BUILDER-2026-10-30.md` carry the numbers):

* Gradle **9.6.0**, with `distributionSha256Sum` set, so a tampered download
  is refused rather than run; Android Gradle plugin **9.4.0**; `compileSdk`
  36, `minSdk` 33, `targetSdk` 36 - the same toolchain `jarvis-client` builds
  with, so the PC has ONE set of numbers to trust.
* **No dependencies at all** - no AndroidX, no Compose - so a first build
  fetches a toolchain and not a dependency graph.
* **No permissions at all.** The manifest declares no `<uses-permission>`, not
  even `INTERNET`, and `MainActivity` sets `allowFileAccess = false`,
  `allowContentAccess = false` and refuses EVERY navigation. The app cannot
  reach the internet, cannot read the phone's files and cannot call Jarvis's
  own routes - proved from the built APK with `aapt2 dump badging`, which
  shows no permission line.
* Debug only. No release signing, no shrinking, never the Play Store (rule 5).

### 166.2 `POST /api/projects/<id>/app/tasks/<task>/android/template`

Body: `{"title"?: str, "background"?: "#rrggbb", "accent"?: "#rrggbb",
"assets"?: {"index.html"?: str, "app.js"?: str, "app.css"?: str}}`. Every
field is optional: with none, the app is called its own project title, uses
two defaults, and gets a **working** page, which is what makes a first build
possible without a single model call.

* **200** `{"ok": true, "template": {"ok", "files", "package", "title"},
  "status": {…166.5…}}`
* **400** a plain sentence: not an Android project, a title with a quote in
  it, a colour that is not `#rrggbb`, a fourth web file, one larger than
  96 KB, one that is not text, or a task that already has a project (a second
  write is refused, never a silent overwrite).
* **403** `pc_only` from the phone.
* **404** no such project, not an app project, no such task.

No card: the files land only in that task's own copy, and nothing runs them
(`docs/APP-BUILDER-DESIGN.md`, "Write files in a task's copy: no card").

### 166.3 `POST /api/projects/<id>/app/tasks/<task>/android/build`

Raises **ONE** card, `app_build_android`, and answers `202`:
`{"ok": true, "waiting": true, "card": "app_build_android", "command":
"<task copy>\gradlew.bat assembleDebug", "message": …}`.

The card's own words carry: the exact command, the exact folder, the SDK and
JDK paths it found, that **the FIRST build downloads the Gradle distribution
(~130 MB) and the Android Gradle plugin** from `services.gradle.org`,
`dl.google.com` and `repo.maven.apache.org` with **nothing of the owner's
sent**, and the APK path it will produce.

A yes runs **exactly** `[<task copy>\gradlew.bat, "assembleDebug"]` with
`cwd` = the task's copy:

* the environment is `jarvis_child_env.inherited()` - the same allowlist every
  child program gets, never a token, key or password - plus `ANDROID_HOME`,
  `ANDROID_SDK_ROOT`, `JAVA_HOME`, and `GRADLE_OPTS=-Dorg.gradle.daemon=false`
  so no Gradle process outlives the card;
* the time limit is 25 minutes, and the output goes to a FILE
  (`build/jarvis-build.log`, gitignored) with only its END kept, because a cap
  applied after reading megabytes into memory is not a cap;
* success requires `exit 0` **and** that the APK exists. Exit 0 without an
  APK is a failure.

Refusals: **400** (no project yet, no Android project), **409** a card for
this task is already waiting, **503** the settings file has the action at a
tier other than `ask` (naming the line), or the PC is missing the SDK, the
JDK or the wrapper files (the sentence names what to install).

### 166.4 `POST /api/projects/<id>/app/tasks/<task>/android/install`

Raises **ONE** card, `app_install_android`, answering `202` with the command
in the body. The card names the exact `adb install -r <apk>`, the file, its
size, that it is a **SIDELOAD** and never the Play Store, and that Jarvis has
no uninstall - so what it installs stays until the owner removes it.

A yes runs **exactly** `[<sdk>\platform-tools\adb.exe, "install", "-r",
<the apk>]`:

* adb is called by **full path** (it is not on PATH on this PC, measured);
* the APK must be a real file **inside the task's own copy**, at the one path
  the build writes, ending `.apk`, and not empty - anything else is refused;
* there is **no** `shell`, `uninstall`, `push`, `pull`, `exec-out` or `-s
  <serial>` anywhere in the module: a source scan in
  `backend/test_android_builder.py` fails the suite if one is added;
* the time limit is 3 minutes.

### 166.5 `GET /api/projects/<id>/app/tasks/<task>/android`

`{"ok", "app", "task", "template": bool, "toolchain": {"sdk", "java", "adb",
"missing"}, "build": {"ready", "refused", "command"}, "install": {"ready",
"refused", "command"}, "apk": {"path", "bytes"}, "waiting": "build"|"install"|
null, "last": {"kind", "outcome", "message", "at"}}`. No secrets and no file
contents; the two `command` strings are what a card WOULD run, so the owner
can see the plan before any card exists.

### 166.6 What this deliberately does not do

No `npm`, no Capacitor, no release signing, no keystore of the owner's, no
Play Store, no `adb shell`, no device management, no arbitrary command - the
Gradle task name and both commands are module constants - and no model call.
Nothing is installed before a build has made the file. The card state is in
memory: a backend restart drops a waiting card and the task simply stays, so
it can be built again.

**The two apps.** Neither has a screen for this: the routes are PC only, the
cards arrive in the card list BOTH apps already draw, and `ARCHITECTURE.md`
section 8 says why the phone has no build button (the SDK and the cable are
not on it).

**Wiring.** No patch: the routes come from `jarvis_android_builder.install()`,
called by the drop-in folder `plugins/ready/android-builder`. The gate rows
are in `jarvis-backend/jarvis_gate.py`, the tier lines in
`backend/rebuilt/jarvis-framework.toml`, and the two Gradle wrapper files are
carried as beside-files (`backend/jarvis-android-gradlew.bat`,
`backend/jarvis-android-wrapper.jar`, Apache-2.0, credited in
`THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt`).

**Tests.** `backend/test_android_builder.py`: the template writes every file
with no placeholder left, the wrapper files are jarvis-client's own (the jar byte for byte, the batch file line endings aside, and the GENERATED batch file CRLF); the manifest declares no permission; every bad name,
colour, title, asset and path is refused; the build command is exactly
`<task copy>/gradlew.bat assembleDebug` in exactly the task copy and a
tampered argv runs nothing; no yes means no run, and a stale-stream gate
answer runs nothing; the environment holds no token, key or password; the
install accepts only the APK inside the copy and no other adb form exists; the
gate rows, tier lines and drop-in folder are all in place, and that the module's own install() wraps a Handler, answers its own routes and lets every other request through untouched. **No test runs a
real Gradle build or a real adb install** - a CI runner has no Android SDK and
no phone. The build in section 166.1 was a manual measurement on the owner's
PC, reported as such.
## 167. Notification styles: a closed look for the phone's notifications, described by talking (phone and backend, added 2026-10-30)

The owner asked, 2026-10-30: *"does jarvis android have custom animated notifications? if not can you
build this feature into it? i want them customizable and buildable by just chatting to jarvis"*.

**The answer Android allows, and the only one this adds.** A notification's own layout may contain
only the View classes `RemoteViews` lists, and the system inflates it in its own process - a class it
does not know is refused outright. Two of those classes animate themselves: `ViewFlipper` (frames, an
`autoStart` layout attribute, a remote flip interval) and an indeterminate `ProgressBar`. So a "custom
animated notification" here means **a closed look that the system animates**, chosen from a menu, and
never a layout, a colour value or code sent from the PC. The full evidence, with links, is
`.dsh-scratch/NOTIFICATION-STYLES-2026-10-30-RESEARCH.md`; the shape is "Widgets you describe"
(§86) applied to the look of a notification instead of the contents of a widget.

### What a style is

A style is one checked JSON object. Every key is required and no other key is allowed:

| Key | Values | Who decides what it draws |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | plain words, 1-40 characters, no web address | the model (a label only) |
| `theme` | `ice`, `azure`, `indigo`, `ember`, `rose`, `mono` | the PHONE maps the name to two of the app's own palette colours |
| `figure` | `spark`, `ring`, `dot`, `star`, `arrow`, `none` | the phone (one character, coloured by the theme) |
| `motion` | `none`, `pulse`, `flip`, `spinner` | the phone (stock SystemUI animations only) |
| `speed` | `slow`, `normal`, `fast` (1800 / 900 / 450 ms) | the phone |
| `kinds` | one or two of `approval`, `reminder` | the phone decides which notifier asks |

`pulse` is a ViewFlipper over two frames of the figure (bright, then dim); `flip` is the figure then a
dot; `spinner` is an indeterminate ProgressBar beside a still figure; `none` is a still figure. **No
frame is posted by the app**, so a style keeps animating when Jarvis' process has been killed and
costs no wakeups.

The model's answer is checked by `backend/jarvis_notification_styles.py`'s `validate()`, which refuses
an unknown key (a colour, a font, a layout, an image, a URL, an `onclick`, code), an unknown value, a
missing key, a web address in the name, a repeated key, `NaN`, prose around the JSON and a far too
long answer. The stored file is checked again on every read, so a hand edit smuggles nothing in. The
**phone** checks the answer a second time (`net/NotificationStyle.kt`) and fails closed: an unknown
name means the plain notification, never a guess.

### Routes

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/notification-styles` | the saved styles, the previews, the menu's words, and `active` - the style live for each kind (the newest one that claims it) |
| POST | `/api/notification-styles/draft` | `{"words": "...", "provenance": "typed"\|"voice"}` -> a preview; nothing is applied |
| POST | `/api/notification-styles/add` | `{"draft": "d0123456789"}` -> keep ONE preview exactly as shown |
| POST | `/api/notification-styles/discard` | `{"draft": "..."}` -> drop ONE preview |
| POST | `/api/notification-styles/delete` | `{"id": "s0123456789"}` -> delete ONE saved style, at once |

The routes are installed by `jarvis_brain_reads.install()` beside the widget routes (no patch of its
own), behind the server's own origin and token checks, with an 8 KB body cap on the POSTs. Caps: 8
saved styles, 5 live previews, 300 characters of the owner's words. Preview ids are "d" plus ten hex
digits; saved ids are "s" plus ten hex digits.

### Asking for it in chat

"make my Jarvis notifications look like a warm orange pulse", "change how notifications look to ...",
"style my notifications like ...". `jarvis_quick.py`'s `_STYLE` rule fires only on words about how
they LOOK - it deliberately does not catch "make my notifications quieter" or "turn my notifications
off", which are the settings grammar's. The reply is a **preview** and a pointer to the phone's Settings -> Notifications, where Add applies it. Refused in a conversation that has read outside text, and
refused for pasted or shared words: the same taint rule as §86, reused rather than re-invented.

### Why there is no approval card

A style shows nothing new, adds no button, grants no capability and changes nothing about what Jarvis
may do; nothing is applied until the owner taps Add. The PC's own sentence says so
(`NO_CARD`). Adding a card would be ceremony without a decision.

### The privacy floor

- The spec has nowhere to put an email, a saved fact, a file, a person or a token.
- The custom layout receives the SAME title and body the notifier already had, already redacted by
  that notifier's own rule. It adds no text of its own.
- While App lock, "Hide memory lists and chat history" or a phone with no secure lock screen is in
  force, the phone does not use the custom layout at all: `NotificationStyle.plan(...)` returns null
  and the notification is built exactly as it was before this feature existed.
- A style changes how the words are drawn and nothing else. On 2026-11-02 the owner asked for an
  Approve button on the approval notification itself; that button (and its five-point security
  envelope) is §177's, and a style may not alter it. Deny and the tap-through are unchanged.

### What it does not style

The alarm that keeps ringing, Live, the chatbot line, the hand-off, the watch line, the wake word and
the link's own ongoing notification keep the plain layout - an animation there is noise. The quiet
"you missed it" notice is never styled (the owner's 2026-09-26 decision). A sound setting is
deliberately absent: sound belongs to the notification channel, and the approval routing already
chooses the channel.

### Tests

`backend/test_notification_styles.py` (160 checks: the menu kept and everything off it refused, no
room in the spec for private data, drafts only from the owner's own words, a tainted chat refused, the
store's caps and expiry and re-check on read, which style is live being the newest that claims a kind,
the routes behind token/origin with the body cap, and the typed grammar) and
`jarvis-client/app/src/test/java/com/jarvis/client/NotificationStyleTest.kt` (the decision layer:
locked means no custom layout, a kind not claimed means none, each motion's frames and interval, the
strict second check, and source pins that the layout files use only RemoteViews-allowed classes and
that the flipper's `autoStart` stays a layout attribute because `setAutoStart` is not remote-callable).

**Not proven here:** the animation on a screen. There is no emulator and no phone at this desk; what is
proven is that every View used is on the allow-list, that the animation is one SystemUI performs, that
the app compiles and the JVM tests pass.


## 168. Calendar in the HUD: the card, three views, one form, its place in Edit HUD and its Settings switch (desktop, added 2026-10-30)

**What this is, in the owner's words.** "a full fledged easy to use calendar
built into Jarvis", local only, drawn in the HUD, **disableable in Settings**,
and - the standing rule of 2026-10-22 - *addable to the main screen from Edit
HUD*. §164 is the store and the four routes; §164's own phone half draws the
phone's plate and widget. **This section is the DESKTOP half**: the HUD's
Calendar card, its month/week/day sheet, its one Add/Edit form, its row in the
Edit HUD editor, and the Settings switch that turns the whole thing off. No
route is added by any of it - every read and write here is one of §164.3's
five.

**This section number.** §164 is the backend slice's contract and §165 the
parking answer; the calendar's own desktop slice was written while 166 was
free, and it sits here in numeric order rather than at the end of the file.
Nothing else was renumbered.

### 168.1 What the owner sees

One **rail card** (`#rail-calendar`, directly above the Reminders card) and one
**full sheet** (`#calendar-panel`, over the stage, dismissed by Escape, its
Close button, or a click outside - the same shape as `#galaxy-options`). Both
draw from the SAME `GET /api/calendar?days=90` read, so the card and the sheet
can never disagree about the owner's day.

- The card says what is next: today's clock and zone, then up to four events
  that have not already ended, each with its time (or "All day"), its title, a
  "Now" marker for the one happening, and a "+N more in the next 7 days" line.
  Its window is seven days **on purpose** - the sentence it shows is "in the
  next 7 days", so the count is of that same window, never of everything.
- The sheet has three views, switched by a `role="tab"` strip and stored in
  `html[data-cal-view]`: **Month** (always six full weeks, Sunday first, so the
  height never jumps; a multi-day event is ONE bar clipped to the week, with
  lanes so two never overlap), **Week** (the seven columns around the chosen
  day, the same bars), and **Day** (an hour-free list in time order - no hour
  grid is faked). Arrow keys move the chosen day; every view names an empty day
  in words rather than showing a blank.
- **One form**, used for both Add and Edit: title, date, all-day, start and end
  time, last day, place, notes, reminder minutes and the repeat choice. Delete
  is in the same form, asks "press again to delete" first because a delete
  cannot be undone, and is hidden until an event is being edited.
- **Every state is a sentence**, never a blank: OFF, an empty window, a day
  with nothing on it, a read that failed (with the PC's own reason where it
  gave one), and the App-lock read ("titles, places and notes are hidden; the
  dates, times and counts are still right"). A card that vanishes reads as a
  fault, so the OFF card keeps its place and says so.

### 168.2 The page itself, and what the twins are

The calendar's script is one block INSIDE `jarvis-desktop/src/jarvis_hud.html`
(the heading `/* ── the calendar (2026-10-29) ──`), not a module: the page is
vendored to the backend and must stay byte-identical in its three copies
(`backend/jarvis_hud.html` and `jarvis-backend/jarvis_hud.html`), which
`tests/hud-calendar.mjs` proves. Its test hook is `window.__hudCalendar`, and
`tests/hud-calendar.mjs` takes that block out of the real page and runs it
against a tiny fake document - the real logic, with no browser.

### 168.3 The read, and the lock

`GET /api/calendar?days=N` is the ONE read, on `hud_proxy.rs`'s fixed
`HUD_GET_PATHS` list. It is also the only path on that list that carries a
query, so `allowed_get` accepts exactly `days=` 1-90 with no sign, no padding
zero, no second parameter, and rebuilds the path from the number it checked -
what reaches the PC is never the page's own string. `/api/calendar/add`,
`/api/calendar/act` and `/api/calendar/settings` are **refused** here: the
writes are the two commands below.

While App lock or "Hide memory lists" is on, `lock/rules.rs` runs the answer
through `brain::calendar::redact_read`: every event keeps its id, date, times,
all-day flag, reminder minutes, recurrence, zone and source, while the title,
place and notes become `""`, and `hidden`/`hidden_count` say how many titles
were blanked - so the card can still say "3 events - hidden" and the sheet can
still draw the shape of the week. A body that is not JSON becomes
`{available:false, hidden:true}` rather than the unreadable original.

### 168.4 The two writes

`hud_calendar_add` and `hud_calendar_act` (`src-tauri/src/hud_calendar.rs`) are
the page's only way to write: the HUD holds no token, so the page cannot POST.
Both are **held on a stale link** (`brain::require_link_live`), and both build
their body in `brain/calendar.rs`, which is the one place the shape is decided:

- `add_body`: one event, title required and capped at 300 characters, a real
  `YYYY-MM-DD` day, `HH:MM` times, an end that cannot be before the start, an
  all-day tick that drops the times, place ≤300, notes ≤2,000, a reminder
  0-10,080 minutes, and a repeat word from the store's own three plus "none".
  An empty optional box is simply not sent.
- `act_body`: exactly two verbs, `delete` or `update` (with the same fields),
  one id of the store's own shape (`c` + 10 lowercase hex). There is no list
  form, no delete-all and no clear-range - the same narrowness
  `/api/schedule/act` has - and a delete that carries fields is refused.

**No approval card, for either** - the owner's 2026-10-29 ruling (decision D1 of
the design brief): one row on this PC, no bulk form, ids-only in the audit line.
The other direction of the same ruling: **the switch is not a HUD write**. The
page only READS the PC's `on` flag and says the feature is off in words;
`capabilities/hud.json` records why the switch is not that window's.

### 168.5 Its place in Edit HUD, and the Settings row

- **Edit HUD.** The calendar is a real registry card: `CARD_REGISTRY`'s
  `"calendar"` row (label "Calendar", `right_rail`, `col_span` 12, ordered above
  the waiting cards, not protected), `MOVABLE_IDS`, and `CARD_DOM.calendar ->
  ["#rail-calendar"]`. Every built-in preset in `src/hud-layout.js` carries it,
  and `contract/hud-presets.json` mirrors them. The half that makes it true for
  the OWNER rather than only for a fresh install is `withRegistryCards` in
  `src/hud-edit.js`: a saved layout is a CLOSED list, so a card a later release
  adds is both invisible and unaddable unless it is put back - that function
  re-adds any movable card the document does not name, at its registry
  defaults, **in memory** (opening the HUD is not an edit; the first real change
  saves the document that by then carries it), and it never un-hides a card the
  owner hid himself.
- **Settings.** `settings.html`'s "Jarvis Calendar" card
  (`src/calendar-settings.js`) draws the ONE switch: `{"on": true|false}` on
  `POST /api/calendar/settings`, the same route and the same value the phone's
  `CalendarSettingsPlate.kt` row and the typed sentence "turn off the Jarvis
  calendar" reach. On the desktop it goes through the `calendar_settings`
  command (`src-tauri/src/calendar_settings.rs`), which reads the switch from
  `GET /api/calendar?days=1`'s `on` (there is no GET settings route) and
  **drops every event, title, place and count in Rust** - the Settings window
  draws one row and cannot read the owner's day. No card either way, immediate,
  never held on a stale link (the same class as the Anti-Slop filter), and
  **OFF never deletes an event**.
- The row it used to have in `jarvis_feature_guide.SETTINGS_GAPS` (a typed
  switch with no page to draw it) is **closed and removed**: both Settings
  halves exist now, and `contract/feature-controls.json`'s `jarvis-calendar` row
  moved from `planned` to `enforced` with a real desktop and phone location.

Both apps have every one of these surfaces, so `tools/check_parity.py`
classifies the four calendar routes `ported` and there is **nothing one-sided
to record in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8** for this feature. The one difference
that stays is a shape, not a missing half: the desktop draws a month/week/day
sheet in its own window and the phone draws its own plate and home-screen
widget, from the same read.

### 168.6 Failing closed

A shape neither app understands must never be drawn as a real calendar, and
this bit was wrong before it shipped (2026-10-30):

- The page's `readCalendar` used to treat every object as a calendar unless it
  said `available: false`. So `?id=`'s answer `{"ok":true,"event":{...}}`, a
  bare event, and an empty body all became **"an available calendar with no
  events"** - drawn as *"Nothing in the next 7 days"*, the most reassuring
  possible lie about the owner's own day. It now requires a real boolean
  `available` AND, when true, an `events` array; anything else is refused in
  words ("answered in a shape this window does not understand ... your events
  are kept on the PC") and draws nothing.
- The two write handlers used to test `reply.ok === false`, so an answer with no
  `ok` at all - an empty body, an older backend - was reported as **"Event
  added."** over a write that may never have happened. They now require
  `ok: true` positively.
- The Settings command applies the same rule in Rust: an answer that does not
  carry `on` as a real boolean is an error, never "off" and never "on".

### 168.7 What is proven, and what is not

- `jarvis-desktop/tests/hud-calendar.mjs`: **33 checks, browser-free** (it runs
  the page's own block against a fake document). Every state in words; the
  three views; the bars and their lanes; the form's exact argument objects for
  both commands; the one allowed read and its bounded query; the redaction arm;
  the registry card, `MOVABLE_IDS`, `CARD_DOM`, every preset and the contract;
  a saved layout getting the card back; the three copies byte-identical; and
  the two fail-closed checks above.
- Rust, beside the code: `brain/calendar.rs` (10 tests - the exact bodies, the
  caps, the refusals, the redaction, and no network of its own),
  `hud_calendar.rs` (2 - the form is the contract, one change is one event and
  two verbs) and `calendar_settings.rs` (5 - one field per request, the read is
  the switch and never an event, an answer without `on` is an error).
  `lock/rules.rs`'s own test names `/api/calendar` in the redaction arm.
- `backend/test_local_calendar.py` is §164's 88 checks; `tools/check_parity.py`
  must print "No undecided drift." with the four rows `ported`.
- **NOT proven here:** the real WebView2 window. This desk has no Playwright
  (the page-level `tests/hud.mjs` and `tests/shots.mjs` cannot run), so a
  rebuilt and installed desktop is the field check, and the geometry of the
  sheet in the real window is the owner's eye rather than a test.


## 169. Long Fuse: starting a job and answering a parked grant (added 2026-10-30)

**What this section is for.** Until 2026-10-30 the background job queue
(`jarvis_jobs.py`, "Long Fuse"; ARCHITECTURE.md section 10) had a read and a
cancel and nothing else: `POST /api/jobs/cancel` existed, `GET /api/jobs`
existed, and **no route created a job and no route answered a parked one**. A
job could only be created by code calling `create()`, and a grant request sat
`pending` for ever. This section is the two missing routes. `backend/jobs-routes.patch`
delivers them; the logic is in `jarvis_jobs.py` (`handle_create` and
`handle_answer`), which this repository ships whole.

### 169.1 `POST /api/jobs`: start ONE job

Request:

    {"kind": "<a registered job body>",   required
     "text": "<the owner's own words>",   optional; becomes the label
     "when": <seconds | epoch | ISO-8601>, optional; default "now"
     "needs": ["<action>", ...]}          optional; the frozen capability set

Answers:

| Status | Body | When |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | `{"ok": true, "id", "job": <row>}` | the job is queued |
| 400 | `{"ok": false, "error": "<a sentence>"}` | no `kind`; a `kind` this PC has not registered; a `kind` that is a plan (`duet_plan_steps`, which needs steps this route does not take); `when` that cannot be read; `needs` that is not a list of names; an action the policy sets to `never` |
| 401 / 403 | the usual words | missing token / cross-origin |
| 503 | `{"ok": false, "available": false, "error": "<a sentence>"}` | `jarvis_jobs.py` is not installed, the jobs database cannot be opened, the tier table cannot be read, **or the background heartbeat is off** - a job created then would never run, so nothing is created |

**What it does NOT do.** It approves nothing. It does not consult the tier table
for a pass (only for `never`, to refuse it), it does not widen a capability set,
and it never creates a second job. The capabilities in `needs` are written onto
the row and frozen there for the job's life - that is the owner-present yes
`create()` has always required. **An empty or missing `needs` is the safe
default**: the job runs with no capabilities and parks the moment it needs one.
The desktop's Work pane sends `[]`, so every job it starts parks on its first
need and asks there.

**`kind` is a name, not code.** It must be one of `GET /api/jobs`'s
`status.handlers`, which is `jarvis_jobs.handlers()` - the bodies this process
registered at start-up. There is no path, module, pickle or eval anywhere in a
job row (jarvis_jobs.py's own "HANDLERS" note says why). At the time of writing
there is **one production body**: `watch_github`, registered by the start-up call
this patch adds to `jarvis_watch.register_job()` - that function existed with no
caller, which is why the queue had nothing useful to run. The suite's own test
handlers are the only others.

### 169.2 `POST /api/jobs/answer`: answer the ONE grant

Request: `{"id": "<job id>", "approved": true | false}`. `by` is an optional
audit label only (the `/api/jobs/cancel` convention), never a permission.

Answers:

| Status | Body | When |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | `{"ok": true, "grant": {"id", "action", "state": "granted"\|"denied", "decided_by"}, "waiting": [...], "stopped": bool, "job": <row>}` | one grant was decided. `stopped` is true when a No ended that job at once. |
| 400 | `{"ok": false, "error": "<a sentence>"}` | no `id`; **`approved` is missing or is not a real boolean** (a string `"false"` is refused rather than read as a yes) |
| 404 | `{"ok": false, "reason": "no_such_job", "error": "<a sentence>"}` | no job with that id |
| 409 | `{"ok": false, "reason": "nothing_waiting"\|"more_than_one"\|"already_answered", "error"}` | the job is not parked; or it is somehow waiting on more than one grant (refused, never guessed); or another tap got there first |
| 503 | as above | the queue cannot be reached |

**One job, one use, no rule.** The grant is flipped `granted`/`denied` and
spent by `_grant_step` the next time the handler asks, so a yes authorises that
one use and the next time it needs the action it asks again. A **No** fails that
job (`_stop_denied`) and writes nothing else - no capability on any row, no entry
in `jarvis-framework.toml`, no memory of the refusal. The next job needing the
same action parks and asks again. There is deliberately no list form, no
"allow all" and no "always allow": that would be a standing rule, and the whole
permission model is one card per action.

**A Yes does not run the job inside the request.** It marks the grant and
returns; the one heartbeat picks the job up (`[jobs] approval_retry_seconds`
after it parked). Both apps say so in the line under the buttons rather than
pretending the work already happened. **A No does stop it immediately**, because
leaving a row saying "waiting for you" about a question already answered, for up
to a heartbeat (thirty minutes as shipped), would make No look like it did
nothing.

### 169.3 The read the Work pane already makes

`GET /api/jobs` gains two keys and changes nothing else:

- **`grants`**: `jarvis_jobs.pending_grants()` - every unspent `pending` grant,
  each with `id`, `job_id`, `action`, `state`, `created` and the job's own
  `label` and `handler`. It is what the pane needs to draw "wants: Send an
  email" under the right job. An action name and a job id - the same class of
  fact the job list already carries, never a param or a result.
- **`ticking`**: a boolean, whether the one background heartbeat is running. It
  is read from the HUD's own engine (`_ENGINE.running`), and `false` is what
  makes the pane say a job started now would never run - and what makes the
  create route answer 503.

**The attention fields are optional, and absence is normal (2026-11-04).**
Each job row MAY carry:

- **`waits_for_person`**: a real boolean, the PC's own answer to "does this job
  wait for a person?". When a row carries it, both apps BELIEVE IT over
  anything they could derive - the server can see a card that a client cannot.
  `null`/absent is not `false`: it means "the PC did not decide", and both apps
  then derive the answer from `state` as below.
- **`dismissed_by_owner`**: a real boolean, meaningful on a `failed` row. A
  failure the owner has already put aside is not still asking for him.

**No backend in this repository sends either field yet.** That is why the
derivation is part of the contract, not a temporary stub: both apps compute

    state in ("waiting_approval", "blocked", "needs_input")
    or (state == "failed" and not dismissed_by_owner)

from the row the read already carries, so a payload without the two fields is
the ordinary case and must keep working. A client must keep that fallback when
a later backend starts sending `waits_for_person`.

**Both keys are also how a client tells an older PC from a busy one.** A body
with no `ticking` at all is a backend that predates this section, so neither
POST exists on it: both apps keep the read-only list they always had and say
which patch the PC needs, rather than offering a form that would 404. The
absence is load-bearing and is not the same fact as an empty list.

### 169.4 In the apps

- **Desktop (built).** The Brain's Work tab → "Start a background job": a select
  of `status.handlers` (nothing else can be chosen) and a text box for the
  owner's words. Under a parked job it draws `wants: <action>` and exactly two
  buttons, "Allow once: <action>" and "No". `brain.rs`'s `brain_create_job` and
  `brain_answer_job` are the only way the page can reach either route; both are
  held on a stale event stream (`require_link_live`, the rule-4 gate), both sit
  in the `brain-act` permission set beside `brain_cancel_job`, and neither is in
  the Brain's read allow-list. `jarvis-desktop/tests/job-list.mjs` holds the
  contracts.
- **Phone (built 2026-10-30, the same slice).** The Brain screen's Work pane,
  "Background jobs" (`ui/screens/JobsPlate.kt`): a "Start a background job" form
  whose only choices are the bodies the PC registered (`status.handlers`), a
  text box for the owner's words, and Start - and under a parked job the
  sentence it is asking about plus exactly two answers, "No" and "Allow once".
  It posts through `JarvisRuntime.startJob` / `JarvisRuntime.answerJob`
  (`net/Jobs.kt` carries the bodies and every sentence), both held on a live
  link (`actionBlocker`, the same rule-4 gate as the desktop's), and the request
  freezes NO capability (`"needs": []`) exactly as the desktop sends - so a job
  started from the phone begins with nothing and parks at its first need. The
  phone's `JobRecord` needed no new row fields: the grants arrive in the same
  GET body, by job id, and `net/Jobs.kt`'s `Feed` reads the whole body.
  `tools/check_parity.py` classifies `/api/jobs/answer` as **`ported`**.
  `BackgroundJobsTest.kt` holds the parse, the two bodies, both answers' words
  and the wiring.
- **Attention first, BOTH apps (2026-11-04, pattern 4).** The job list under the
  form is two sections, decided by ONE predicate per platform (desktop
  `src/attention.js`; phone `net/JobAttention.kt`) and readable from either
  app's `state` field:
  - **"Needs you"** holds every job whose approval, answer, retry or failure a
    person has to look at, drawn expanded with the job's own action. An EMPTY
    "Needs you" is not created at all - no heading, no empty box, no reserved
    gap - so it costs **zero pixels**.
  - **"Quiet / healthy"** is ONE collapsed line, e.g. `Quiet / healthy · 3
    background jobs — 1 still running, 2 finished · last finished 5m ago`, that
    opens on a click (desktop) or tap (phone) to the same rows. Counts and the
    finish time are printed only when the payload supports them.

  The split is STABLE (the read's own order on both sides), so a row never
  jumps between two reads of the same answer. It adds no polling (the existing
  refresh path redraws it), no new action and no approval: the only controls in
  the sections are the ones each row already had (a one-shot grant answer,
  Cancel). Tests: `jarvis-desktop/tests/attention-first.mjs` (truth table and
  the one-line summary, plus Playwright DOM checks for the zero-pixel empty
  state and the folded bar) and `AttentionFirstTest.kt`.

### 169.5 What is proven, and what is not

- `backend/test_jobs.py` (95 checks, 12 test functions): creating validates
  every field and refuses a `never` action, an unknown kind, a plan, a bad time,
  a bad `needs` and a stopped heartbeat; the created row carries the owner's
  words and an empty frozen set; a parked job is exactly what `jobs()` and
  `pending_grants()` say it is; an answer decides ONE job's ONE grant and leaves
  a second job's untouched; the grant is spent by its one use; a second tap is
  409; a denial stops that job at once, leaves the policy file byte-identical,
  and a new job needing the same risky action (`send_email`, tier `ask`) parks
  and asks again; and `backend/jobs-routes.patch` applies to the published
  `jarvis-backend/jarvis_hud.py`, reverses byte for byte, and carries the two
  POST routes, the two GET keys and the start-up registration.
- `jarvis-desktop/tests/job-list.mjs` (25 checks browser-free): the read
  allow-list cannot reach either write, the two commands are registered in
  `lib.rs` and `build.rs`, each has its own generated permission and its place
  in `brain-act`, the create command sends the owner's words and no
  capabilities, the form offers only the server's handlers and says what
  starting with no permissions means, the two answer buttons are matched to
  their own job, and the backend patch sends the keys the pane reads. The DOM
  half (a parked job's two buttons, and the exact `{approved, id}` the click
  sends) needs Playwright and runs in CI.
- `jarvis-client`'s `BackgroundJobsTest.kt` (JVM unit tests, no emulator): the
  whole GET body reads, grants are joined to their OWN job, an answered job is
  not offered its buttons twice, an older PC keeps its read-only list and names
  the patch, `available: false` is never an empty list, both request bodies are
  the contract's letter for letter (the owner's words escaped, `approved` a real
  boolean, `"needs": []` and nothing that could freeze a capability), the form
  is replaced by the server's own reason when it could not work, every start and
  answer sentence including the PC's refusals and a missing route, and the
  wiring that makes it reachable (the same jobs plate on Brain, both writes held
  on a stale link, both using the transport that keeps the PC's own sentence).
- **NOT proven here:** the real WebView2 window on the owner's PC, and
  `watch_github` against GitHub from a job. This desk has no Playwright, and the
  queue has never been ticked on the owner's machine by a route-created job.
  The phone half is compiled and unit-tested here but has NOT been driven on the
  owner's phone against the live backend: that is the field check, and it is
  his - start one job, watch it park, answer it, on either app.

## 170. The Obsidian notes editor: browse, open and save any note in the vault (added 2026-10-31)

**What this section is for.** The owner's decision of 2026-10-31, in his own
words: **"The whole vault, both apps."** Every note in the Obsidian vault can
be listed, searched, opened and edited — from the desktop program and from the
phone. Until this landed the backend could SEARCH the vault (read-only,
`jarvis_notes.py`) and APPEND to today's daily note (`jarvis_note_capture.py`);
it could not browse the vault and it could not change an existing note.

The logic lives in the drop-in module `jarvis_notes_edit.py` (a shipped
module; `plugins/ready/notes-edit/plugin.json` names it and the plugin loader
calls its `install()`, so there is **no patch and no edit to
`jarvis_hud.py`**). The four routes are served after the core's own origin and
token checks, like every other route, and every request sends
`X-Jarvis-Client: hud` from either app. The routes are local only: no model,
no network, no token in a log, and no byte of a note's text in a card, an
audit line or a log.

### 170.1 `GET /api/notes/list`

Request: `?q=<text>` optional. `q` is case-insensitive, matched against the
note's title and its vault-relative path, and bounded at 200 characters.

    GET  /api/notes/list?q=<text>

Answer 200:

    {"ok": true, "root": "<absolute vault path, for display only>",
     "count": 123,
     "notes": [{"path": "Inbox/idea.md", "title": "idea", "size": 812,
                "mtime": 1761900000.0}],
     "truncated": false}

Only `.md` and `.txt` files inside the vault are listed. Hidden folders —
`.obsidian`, `.trash`, anything whose name starts with a dot — are skipped,
and so is any file or folder that is a symlink or a junction. Sorted newest
first by `mtime`. At most **2,000** notes are returned and `truncated: true`
says more exist. **`count` is the number of rows in THIS answer, not the
vault's total** — `truncated` is what says the vault holds more. **It never
returns note text.**

### 170.2 `GET /api/notes/read?path=<vault-relative path>`

    GET  /api/notes/read?path=<vault-relative path>

Answer 200:

    {"ok": true, "path": "Inbox/idea.md", "text": "...",
     "sha256": "<hex of the BYTES on disk>", "size": 812,
     "mtime": 1761900000.0}

`text` is decoded as UTF-8; invalid bytes become replacement characters (a
note written by another editor in another encoding is still readable, and
saving it writes valid UTF-8). The sha256 is always of the bytes.

Errors, each in a plain sentence in `error`:

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| 400 | the path is empty, absolute (drive letter, leading `/`, UNC), climbs out with `..`, names a hidden component, contains a character a filename cannot hold, or is not a `.md`/`.txt` file; a path through a symlink or junction |
| 404 | there is no note at that path in the vault |
| 413 | the note is over **2 MiB** |
| 503 | no Obsidian vault is configured, or the vault cannot be read — the sentence names `[notes.obsidian] vault_directory` and `JARVIS_OBSIDIAN_VAULT` |

### 170.3 `POST /api/notes/save`

    POST /api/notes/save

Request body: `{"path": "...", "text": "...", "expected_sha256": "<hex>"}`,
all three required. `expected_sha256` is the `sha256` from a
`GET /api/notes/read` of the version the edit started from.

Answers:

| Status | Body | When |
|---|---|---|
| 202 | `{"ok": true, "state": "waiting", "id": "<job id>", "path": "..."}` | the approval card is up; the write happens only after Approve |
| 200 | `{"ok": true, "state": "saved", "path": "...", "sha256": "<new hex>"}` | a save that needed no card (a future config with the action at tier `auto`; not the shipped default) |
| 409 | `{"ok": false, "state": "conflict", "path": "...", "current_sha256": "<hex>"}` | `expected_sha256` no longer matches; **nothing written, no card raised** |
| 400 | `{"ok": false, "state": "refused", "error": "<a sentence>"}` | bad/absolute/outside/link path, non-text path, missing `expected_sha256`, missing text, or body not an object |
| 413 | same shape | the new text is over 2 MiB |
| 429 | same shape | `4` saves are already waiting for their cards — the sentence names the limit |
| 503 | same shape | no Obsidian vault is configured; the sentence names the setting |

The POST waits a short moment (1.5 s) for a fast answer; a save that is still
waiting answers `202` with its id, and `GET /api/notes/save?id=` reports how
it ended. A Deny, an expired card or a refused card **leaves the file byte
for byte as it was**.

### 170.4 `GET /api/notes/save?id=<job id>`

    GET  /api/notes/save?id=<job id>

Answer 200:

    {"ok": true, "state": "waiting"|"saved"|"denied"|"failed",
     "path": "...", "sha256": "<hex or null>",
     "message": "<plain sentence>"}

`ok` is true only while waiting or after a save. `sha256` is the NEW hash
after a save and `null` otherwise. `message` is the PC's own sentence ("You
said no, so the note was not changed.", "Saved Inbox/idea.md into your
Obsidian vault.", and so on). A note that changed while the card was up ends
as `failed` with `current_sha256` set and nothing written. An unknown id is
**404** with `{"ok": false, "error": "<plain sentence>"}` — the PC's own words,
so a client shows that instead of inventing its own.

### 170.5 The card, the File Guardian and the limits

- **Every save is ONE approval card.** The gate action is
  **`edit_vault_note`** and its tier is **`"ask"`** in the shipped
  `jarvis-framework.toml` (`[autonomy.tiers]`, in both copies the repository
  ships). The app never approves anything; the owner does, on the existing
  Approve / Deny card.
- **It is unclassified until a patch says otherwise.** Drop-in modules add no
  patch and no gate-table row, and a `_RISK` row is written by patches, so the
  gate has no risk line for `edit_vault_note` yet: it therefore **forces the
  action to ask** whatever the settings file says, and the card carries the
  gate's generic worst-case warning line. That is the safe side — the save can
  never run unattended. A small follow-up patch can classify it properly.
- **The File Guardian copies the note first.** Immediately after the owner's
  yes, and BEFORE the write, the module calls the existing
  `jarvis_notes.snapshot_vault_before_write()` — which is
  `jarvis_file_guardian.snapshot_before_write()` with the configured vault as
  the allowed root. If that copy cannot be made, **nothing is written** and the
  save ends as `failed` with the reason.
- **No clobbering.** The edit carries the sha256 it started from; a mismatch
  is `409 conflict` with the current hash before any card, and the same check
  runs again after the card, in case another editor wrote while it waited.
- **The vault is the world.** A path is vault-relative and normalised; it is
  refused if it is absolute, climbs out with `..`, goes through a symlink or
  junction, is hidden, or is not a `.md`/`.txt` file — all **before any card**.
- **Bounds.** 2 MiB per note; 2,000 notes per list; at most 4 saves waiting at
  once. No create, delete or rename in this slice.
- **The hidden/locked state is unchanged.** This module serves the note text;
  both apps keep their existing Show gate and hidden-list guard in front of it,
  and this module adds no bypass.

### 170.6 What is proven, and what is not

- `backend/test_notes_edit.py` proves: the four route answers above (status
  codes and bodies) against a temporary Obsidian vault; the path sandbox
  (absolute, `..`, hidden, non-text, symlink); the sha256 conflict (no card, no
  write); a Deny writes nothing and takes no snapshot; an approved save takes
  the File Guardian copy, writes the new bytes and reports the new hash; the
  TOCTOU case (the note changed while the card waited) writes nothing; the
  2 MiB bound, the 429 waiting limit, the no-vault 503, the unknown-id 404; the
  `install()` wrapping (origin and token refused, other paths reach the core,
  a second install does not double-wrap); and that `edit_vault_note` resolves
  to tier `"ask"` through the published gate's own tier reader for BOTH shipped
  copies of the settings file.
- **NOT proven here:** the live PC. These routes are built and proved in this
  repository; they are **not deployed by this change** (the live backend
  deploy is its own pass), so the owner's live apps do not show the editor
  until that deploy. The desktop and phone surfaces are the other two lanes of
  the same feature; this section documents the contract they build against.

### 170.7 The wave-1 writes: create ONE note, append to ONE note, tag ONE note (added 2026-10-31)

The owner's flexibility decision, wave 1: three single-file writes on top of the
editor, each with ONE approval card, a File Guardian copy first where there are
old bytes, and an answer that says "You can undo it." Rename, move, delete and
several notes in one request are NOT here (wave 2) and are refused in plain
words.

| route | body | answer |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/notes/create` | `{"path": "...", "text": "..."}` - `text` may be empty | **CARD-FREE only for a DIRECT owner write (owner's decision 2026-10-31; Gemini round-3 ruling 2): creating a brand-new note is additive and can never destroy content. The scope is strict - provenance `typed` or `voice` AND `X-Jarvis-Client: hud`; after outside text, a background job, or any other client the create keeps its ONE approval card (202 `waiting`).** The card-free payload is capped at **64 KB** (413 above it, no card), a same-name collision is a 409 case-insensitively on Windows, and the vault/protected/hidden/reserved/symlink/`..` refusals are unchanged. Synchronous `200` `created` with `sha256`, `receipt` and the module's own `message` ("Created ... You can undo it."); the undo receipt is recorded BEFORE the file exists so one Undo removes exactly the new file. `409` the path already exists (nothing overwritten, and the write itself is `O_EXCL`); `400` bad/absolute/outside/hidden/non-text path or a list body; `413` over **2 MiB**; `403` a protected path; `503` no vault configured or the receipt/write failed (nothing created) |
| `POST /api/notes/append` | `{"path": "...", "text": "...", "expected_sha256": "<hex>"}` | `202`/`200` saved with the new `sha256` and `snapshot` (the File Guardian copy id); `409` the note changed since the request (no card, `current_sha256` named); `404` no note there (create it first); `413` the note or the addition would pass 2 MiB; the same `400`/`429`/`503` shapes |
| `POST /api/notes/tag` | `{"path": "...", "tag": "recipes", "action": "add"\|"remove", "expected_sha256": "<hex>", "where": "auto"\|"frontmatter"\|"line"}` | `200` `saved` with the new `sha256` and `snapshot`, or `200` `unchanged` when the tag was already there / already absent (no card); `409` stale sha; `400` a tag with a space or no letter/`_`/`-`, a `tags:` value that is not a list, two `tags:` lines, unclosed front matter, or a note that is not valid UTF-8 (all BEFORE any card) |
| `GET /api/notes/change?id=<job id>` | - | the same waiting/saved/denied/failed shape as the save, plus `kind` (`create`/`append`/`tag`), `path`, `sha256`, `message`, and `receipt` for a create or `snapshot` for the two changes |

- **One card, under the existing action.** All three ask `edit_vault_note` (tier
  `"ask"` in both shipped `jarvis-framework.toml` files; unclassified, so the
  gate forces ask and uses its generic warning line - the safe side). The card
  names the file, says what changes, and the finished answer says "You can undo
  it." A Deny, an expiry or a refused gate writes nothing.
- **Undo.** Append and tag take `jarvis_notes.snapshot_vault_before_write()` (the
  File Guardian) AFTER the card and BEFORE the write; a copy that cannot be made
  refuses the change in words. Create records one `notes_create` receipt BEFORE
  the file exists; its Undo removes exactly that file, and refuses if the note
  changed since (the created sha256 is in the receipt). A failed create discards
  its receipt.
- **Append is append-only.** The owner's words are added at the end with the
  same paragraph rule the daily-note capture uses; the old bytes are never
  rewritten, and the written block is read back before "Added" is said.
- **Tags are surgical.** Only the frontmatter `tags:` block (list form), or in
  `line` mode a visible `#tag` line, is changed; every other byte - other
  properties, line endings, the body - is kept. `auto` uses the front matter
  when the note has it and the visible line when it does not. Malformed front
  matter is refused rather than rewritten.
- **Hidden lists / App lock unchanged.** The chat fast path refuses to start any
  of these while the lists are hidden (a fixed sentence, no title, NO card); the
  apps keep their existing Show gate in front of the editor. The routes serve
  one file each and no note text goes to a model, a log or a card.
- **Several notes are refused.** Every route takes ONE path; a body that sends a
  list is a 400 with "One note at a time, please", and the chat refuses "all my
  notes"/"every note" in words before any card.

### 170.8 Surgical edits, wave 2: under a heading, at an anchor, formatting, replace (added 2026-10-31)

The owner's follow-up to wave 1: *"add something to a part of the note ... very
specific (add something before this part, or in bold)"*. Three routes, ONE
action each, the same single-file shape as the save:

| route | body | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/notes/insert` | `{"path", "text", "mode": "under_heading"\|"before"\|"after", "target", "expected_sha256"}` | adds ONE line under the ONE heading whose title matches exactly (case-insensitive), at the END of that section (after its last non-empty line, before the next heading of the same or a higher level); or before/after the ONE line whose text contains the literal anchor exactly once |
| `POST /api/notes/format` | `{"path", "target", "style": "bold"\|"italic", "action": "add"\|"remove", "expected_sha256"}` | wraps ONE exact occurrence in `**`/`*`, or unwraps one matching pair; refuses a match inside a fenced code block and a span already wrapped (that is a no-op with no card) |
| `POST /api/notes/replace` | `{"path", "old", "new", "expected_sha256"}` | replaces ONE literal occurrence whose word edges are whole words (a match inside a longer word refuses and says so); never a regex |

- **One exact match or refuse.** Zero or several matching headings/anchors/spans
  get a plain sentence NAMING the count, before any card; nothing is guessed.
- **The card shows the exact change.** The gate's detail carries a bounded
  `preview` (`before`/`after`, plus where it lands). While the hidden lists hide
  the words the preview is `{"counts_only": true, "changes": 1}` and the chat
  refuses the request before a card is raised at all.
- **Undo and safety.** The File Guardian copy is taken AFTER the card and BEFORE
  the write; the sha256 the request started from is checked at the request and
  again after the card (TOCTOU); a Deny/expiry/refused gate writes nothing; one
  Undo restores the exact bytes. Line endings (LF/CRLF), blank lines and the
  anchor's own bytes are preserved. No deletion exists in these routes.
- **Chat sentences, no model:** `add <text> under the <Heading> heading in my
  <note>`, `add <text> before/after <anchor> in my <note>`, `make <text> bold`
  / `put <text> in italic` / `unbold <text> in my <note>`, `replace <old> with
  <new> in my <note>`. A plain `add milk to my <note>` still appends at the end
  (wave 1); an ordinary "make it bold" with no note is still the model's.

### 170.9 Customization, wave 3: one route for the exact edits (added 2026-10-31)

Beyond wave 2's insert/format/replace, ONE action route carries the owner's
"really enhance customizability" edits. Every action keeps the wave-2 shape:
one exact match or a plain refusal, ONE `edit_vault_note` card showing the exact
before/after (or counts only while the hidden lists hide the words), the File
Guardian copy first, an atomic write, one Undo, no deletions.

| route | body | action values |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/notes/customize` | `{"path", "action", "expected_sha256", ...}` | `format` (`style`: bold/italic/strike/code, `format_action`: add/remove, `target`); `line` (`line_action`: bullet/number/checklist/quote/heading/plain/untick, `target` = the whole line, `level` for a heading); `rename_heading` (`old`, `new`); `new_section` (`heading`, optional `text`, `level`); `set_property`/`remove_property` (`key`, `value`); `link` (`note`, optional `heading`); `save_template` (`name` optional) |
| `GET /api/notes/templates` | - | `{"ok", "count", "templates": [names only], "why"}` - never any template text |

- **Exactness.** A line shape needs ONE line equal to `target` after stripping
  its ends; a heading rename needs ONE heading with that title; a property needs
  at most one `key:` line; a link refuses a second identical link. Zero or
  several matches refuse in plain words with the count, before any card.
- **Properties** are written as YAML: `true`/`false` and numbers stay bare,
  anything else is a quoted string. Only that one line changes; every other byte
  (other properties, order, line endings, body) is kept. Malformed front matter
  is refused, never repaired.
- **Line shapes** keep the line's indentation, blank lines and line endings:
  bullet `- `, numbered `1. `, checklist `- [ ] `, quote `> `, heading `#`..`######`;
  `plain` removes one leading shape; `untick` only changes `- [x]` to `- [ ]`.
  "these lines"/batch and "move under a heading" are NOT built: the answer says
  so plainly instead of pretending.
- **Templates.** Built-ins: workout log (`Warm-up`/`Session`/`Cool-down`/`Notes`,
  checkboxes), meeting notes for a topic, daily journal, project note. They are
  created through the existing create route (ONE card, collision refused,
  receipt Undo). "Save my <note> as a template" writes ONE new `.md` in the
  Templates plugin's folder from `.obsidian/templates.json`, else
  `<vault>/Templates/`; an existing template is a 409, never overwritten.
  "List my templates" reads names only; while the hidden lists hide words the
  chat refuses with no names and no card.
- **Not built, said plainly:** deleting a line/note, moving a line under
  another heading, bulk/`these lines` edits (the exact-match rule cannot be
  kept), reciprocal links (one link per request), highlighting (non-standard).

### 170.10 Rename and move ONE note, keeping its links working (wave 4, added 2026-10-31)

The owner's next flexibility item: *"rename and move notes with link
preservation"*. A rename or move is one note's PATH change plus only the link
text that named it, so the plan is read-only, the card names the file and the
counts, and ONE approval writes the move and those link bytes. The module is
still `jarvis_notes_edit.py`; the existing `edit_vault_note` action, one
ordinary card, the File Guardian copy and one Undo are used. No route deletes a
note or changes any byte outside the link target.

| route | body | answer |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/notes/rename` | `{"path": "<rel>", "title": "<new name>"}` | 202 `{"ok": true, "state": "waiting", "id": "<job>", "target": "<new rel>"}`; `GET /api/notes/change?id=` says `saved` / `denied` / `failed` |
| `POST /api/notes/move` | `{"path": "<rel>", "folder": "<rel folder>", "create_folder": false}` | the same shape; `create_folder` must be exactly true to make a missing folder |
| both | `new_title` / `new_name` and `target_folder` accepted as aliases | the same |

- **Validation before any card.** The source must be a real `.md` note, a
  regular file, not a link/junction, not hidden and not protected; the new name
  must be one filename (no `/`, `\`, `..`, `:` or other path character), at most
  120 characters, not dot-leading, and the target folder must be inside the
  vault, real, not hidden and not protected. Rename refuses a name already used
  by another note; move refuses a file already at the destination. Moving to a
  missing folder is refused with the words "say create the folder" unless
  `create_folder` is explicitly true; a folder is never created as a side
  effect.
- **Link preservation, exactly.** Before the card the module scans every
  readable `.md` note in the vault (never protected/hidden text) and builds the
  changes it would make:
  - wikilinks `[[old]]`, `[[old|alias]]`, `[[old#section]]` and embeds
    `![[old]]` are rewritten to the new title on rename; a path-style wikilink
    `[[folder/old]]` is rewritten on either rename or move;
  - relative Markdown links such as `[x](old.md)` or `[x](folder/old.md#part)`
    are resolved from the linking note's folder and rewritten only when they
    really point at the old note; titles, anchors and angle brackets are kept;
  - a move keeps a bare `[[old]]` alone because the title did not change
    (Obsidian resolves it by title), and rewrites only links that named the old
    path;
  - **fenced code blocks and inline code are never touched** (the rule is
    stated in this section and pinned by a test). Links inside them stay
    byte-identical.
  Only the matched link text changes; every other byte of every note is kept.
  The card says the old path -> new path and "updates N link(s) in M note(s)";
  when lists are visible it also names up to the first three affected note
  filenames (`Index.md, Projects.md (+2 more)`), and when there are no links it
  says so and the action is just the file rename/move. While the hidden lists
  hide private words the card carries counts only and names no file at all.
- **The write is one batch.** After approval the worker re-checks the source and
  every link-note hash (a note that changed while the card waited refuses, with
  no write), asks the File Guardian for a copy of the source and of every note
  it will change, records ONE undo receipt, writes the link notes, and then
  atomically moves the source note. A failure puts every copy back; the answer
  says "You can undo it." ONE Undo restores every original byte and path, and
  removes a folder the batch created if it is empty.
- **Chat.** `"rename my Welcome note to Home"`, `"move my Welcome note to
  Archive"`, `"move Welcome into Projects and fix the links"` and
  `"move my Welcome note into Archive and create the folder"` are deterministic
  (no model). The reply gives the same preview counts as the card and the ONE
  card follows; a denied/expired card writes nothing. A name matching more than
  one note is refused with the count and no card. A hidden-lists state refuses
  with no title and no card.
- **Not built, said plainly:** deleting a note, moving outside the vault,
  renaming or moving folders, renaming a note onto an existing name, cloud sync,
  moving several notes at once, updating links inside protected or hidden notes,
  and following links to remote URLs. The chat says these are not built instead
  of pretending.

- **The desktop plate's two controls (2026-10-31).** The Brain -> Notes editor's
  chrome has **Rename…** and **Move…** beside Save, calling these same two
  routes with exactly the bodies above (`{path, title}` and
  `{path, folder, create_folder}`) and following the card with
  `GET /api/notes/change?id=`. Rename is pre-filled with the current title and
  is disabled when the note has no path. Move offers every folder the editor's
  own note list proves exists (plus the vault's top level) and a new-folder
  field whose **"Create it if it does not exist"** checkbox is the only way
  `create_folder` can become true. The plate only asks and follows: it never
  approves the card, never saves, shows the module's own waiting / denied /
  failed / saved words (including "You can undo it."), and after a `saved`
  change opens the note at its new path. The phone has no rename/move control
  by this slice; its chat grammar calls the same routes.

The module's twin `jarvis-backend/jarvis_notes_edit.py` is byte-identical, and
`backend/test_notes_rename_move.py` proves the temp-vault matrix: rename/move
success and exact bytes, collision, no links, alias/section/embed/Markdown links,
fenced and inline-code skips, one batch Undo byte-equality, deny/expiry/guardian
failure/TOCTOU writing nothing, protected/hidden/symlink/`..` refusals, hidden
cards, preview sentences and over-capture. It uses a fake gate and a temporary
vault; the real desktop/phone cards are covered by the field check.

### 170.11 Smart note creation: title, body, pin and date from ONE sentence (added 2026-11-09)

The owner reported, 2026-11-09, having said:

    create a new note called Workout Log, pin it, and add using todays date
    that i used the punching bag

and having got a note whose **title was the whole sentence** and whose body was
empty. Measured on the tree before this change: the file was named
`Workout Log, pin it, and add using todays date that i used the punching
bag.md` and held nothing. The chat grammar in `jarvis_quick.py` took every word
after "called" as the name.

This section is that sentence read as the **four facts** it actually holds. It
is local, deterministic code in `jarvis_quick.py` (no model, no network, no new
route, no new tool). Both apps reach it through the one they already use:
`POST /api/chat` -> `jarvis_quick.answer_turn()` -> `answer()` -> `match()`.

**The four facts, and the words that carry them**

| fact | read from |
|---|---|
| **title** | the words after `called`/`titled`/`named`, up to the first clause boundary: a comma, `with`/`saying`/`containing`, `and add`/`put`/`write`/`say`/`use`/`set`, a pin clause, or a date clause. A title's own `and` ("Salt and Pepper") and `on` ("Notes on Physics") are kept. |
| **body** | after the title: `with X` / `containing X` / `saying X`, `add X` / `put X` / `write X` / `say X`, `that X`, or the words after the title's comma. A trailing `and pin it` or `using <date>` is taken back out, and `and put X in it` leaves X. |
| **pin** | `pin it`, `pin this note`, `and pin it` anywhere in the sentence, before or after the body. `unpin it` in a CREATE writes nothing: a brand-new note is not pinned, so there is no pin to remove and none is pretended. |
| **date** | `today`, `todays date`, `today's date`, `yesterday`, `tomorrow`, or an explicit date (`2026-11-03`, `3 November`, `November 3rd`, `12/11/2026`), normally after `using` / `dated` / `on` / `for`. Normalised to `YYYY-MM-DD`. An explicit date with **no year is THIS year** - a note records what a date was, unlike a reminder, which looks forward to the next time that day comes. |

The parsing runs on the sentence the chat already normalises (lower case,
spoken punctuation folded), and the owner's capital letters are restored for
the title and body exactly as every other chat name is.

**What is written.** A pin and/or a date become the new note's own front
matter, in the same YAML shape `jarvis_notes_edit.py`'s `set_property` already
writes (and Obsidian shows in the note's Properties panel). The owner's
sentence above now writes `Workout Log.md` with exactly:

```markdown
---
pinned: true
date: 2026-11-09
---
i used the punching bag
```

With neither a pin nor a date, the request writes exactly the bytes it wrote
before this change - no front matter - so every older shape keeps its answer.
A body-only sentence ("write a note for me about the gym trip") is still a
body-only note with its title drawn from the words, and `... called Shopping
with milk and eggs` still has exactly `milk and eggs` as its body.

**The permission model is UNCHANGED, on purpose.**

- **A NEW note from chat is card-free**, the owner's decision of 2026-10-31
  (Gemini round-3 ruling 2): additive, it cannot destroy content, it is
  collision-refused (`409` before any card, and the write itself is `O_EXCL`),
  and its undo receipt is recorded **before** the file exists. This change only
  changes WHICH words become the title, the body and the two properties.
- **Pinning or unpinning an EXISTING note is an EDIT**, so it keeps its ONE
  `edit_vault_note` card, the File Guardian copy first and one Undo. It rides
  the customize route's own `set_property` / `remove_property` action - no new
  route, no new card, no second card. Pinning a note that is already pinned is
  a `200 unchanged` with **no card**; unpinning a note that is not pinned says
  so with no card. When the removed property was the note's ONLY property, the
  empty `---`/`---` block is taken away too, so the note is byte-for-byte what
  it was before it was pinned.
- **The hidden lists / App lock rule is unchanged.** A new note is still
  created card-free and its reply names no title and no date; pin/unpin is
  refused with no card and no title.
- **No bulk, no delete, no second note.** One sentence is one note. Several
  notes in one request are still refused in words.

**Both apps, backend-side.** Nothing about this reading is in either client:
the phone's chat (`JarvisApi.chatCall`, `ChatHistory.requestBody`) and the
desktop's both POST `/api/chat`, so both get the same note, the same pin, the
same date and the same reply sentence. The desk's chat and the phone's chat
were both driven through `answer_turn()` with their own body shapes in
`backend/test_notes_smart_create.py`; the phone needs no rebuild for this.

**What this does NOT do (said plainly).**

- **The pin is a note property, not a screen.** Neither app has a "Pinned"
  group, a pin button or pinned-first sorting yet; the property is visible and
  searchable in Obsidian itself. A UI for it would be a separate feature on
  BOTH apps (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8).
- A **standalone `pin it`** with no note named, after some earlier action, is
  not matched: nothing here remembers which note that was. Name it ("pin my
  Workout Log note").
- A note's `date` property is not a calendar entry, a reminder or a daily note;
  it records the day the note is about.
- A "title" longer than 120 characters is not treated as a name: the older
  grammar keeps that request.
- The date is not put into the body as text; it is the note's own property.

**Proven.** `backend/test_notes_smart_create.py` (83 checks) pins all of it on
a temporary vault with a fake gate: the owner's exact sentence and its exact
bytes, the card-free create and its undo receipt, a body-only control, an
existing title's `and`/`on`, a trailing `yesterday` staying in the body, pin +
add in one sentence, every date word above, pin/unpin of an existing note as
exactly ONE `edit_vault_note` card (and no second card when nothing would
change), the hidden-lists refusals, the collision, one note per request, both
apps' chat bodies through `answer_turn()` (and the two `/api/notes` reads their
Notes plate makes), the byte-identical twin and this section. Not tested here:
the live PC (this is a repository change; the deploy is its own pass).

The module's twin `jarvis-backend/jarvis_quick.py` is byte-identical.

## 171. "Protected from Jarvis": a list of folders, files and programs Jarvis may not touch (added 2026-10-31)

The owner's request, in their own words: *"add a list of file folders, and
programs that i can manually add to (or ask jarvis to exclude in chat and get a
card) that blocks jarvis from having any access (read or write) or the ability
to make certain files or folders or programs read only"*. Two answers came with
it: **build it now**, in parallel lanes; and for a protected **program**,
"read only" means **"see it, never act"** - its window title or a screenshot
may be read; clicking, typing, opening, closing or controlling it is refused.
Backend lane: `jarvis_protection.py` (shipped; base twin byte-identical), its
drop-in folder `plugins/ready/protected-items/` (install(); no patch), suite
`backend/test_protection.py`, and this section.

### 171.1 The store

`protected-items.json` in the PC's Jarvis settings folder
(`%USERPROFILE%\.openjarvis`, `jarvis_framework.CONFIG_DIR`), human-readable and
versioned:

```json
{"version": 1,
 "items": [
   {"id": "prot_ab12cd34", "kind": "folder", "target": "C:\\...\\Taxes",
    "mode": "blocked", "added": "2026-10-31T08:00:00Z", "added_by": "owner"}
 ]}
```

`kind` is `folder` | `file` | `program`. A folder target protects its WHOLE
subtree after links and junctions are resolved; a file target covers that file.
Program targets are lowercase executable names (`notepad.exe`) - the name the
desktop's own open/app-control code already resolves. Matching is
case-insensitive, normalises `..` and separators, and resolves the candidate
