before comparing, so a symlink that leads into a protected folder is protected
too. A damaged or missing store is **empty and safe**: no crash, no accidental
protection, never "protect everything".

### 171.2 The routes

| route | who | card |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/protection` | both apps | none - the list, in the PC's own words (`count`, `items`, `modes`, `change_card`) |
| `POST /api/protection/add` | desktop Settings only | none - the owner's own direct act; audit line. 403 from any other device (`from_this_pc`), 400 for a bad kind/mode/target/path, 409 when already protected |
| `POST /api/protection/remove` | either app | **ONE** card, action `unprotect_item`; 202 `waiting`, 404 unknown id |
| `POST /api/protection/propose` | the chat path | **ONE** card, action `protect_item`; 202 `waiting` and a job id; 400/409 before any card |
| `GET /api/protection/propose?id=` | either app | the proposal's end: `waiting` / `added` / `denied` / `failed` |

The chat ability is the model tool **`protect_from_jarvis`** (`{action, kind,
target, mode}`, `action` = `add` | `remove` | `list`, default `add`). It has
three actions since 2026-11-04, because the owner asked to set folder-level
restrictions by plain chat: `add` and `remove` each raise ONE ordinary approval
card - `protect_item` and `unprotect_item` respectively - and the store is
written only after that verdict, with `added_by: "chat"`; `list` changes
nothing, so it answers with **no card** (the whole list, or ONE named target
checked in it: `check: true/false` plus the entry). The model never writes the
list itself and never claims it happened until the PC says so. Removal is
loosening and always raises one card, whichever app or chat asks. The card
words and the tier are the list's own; a `list` answer can never write.

**The same door without the model (2026-11-04).** `jarvis_quick.py`'s fixed
phrasings reach `jarvis_protection`'s own functions directly - `handle_propose`
(one `protect_item` card), `handle_remove` (one `unprotect_item` card), and
`handle_get` / `status_for` for the read. They are the SAME functions the tool
and the apps' routes use, not a second mechanism:

| said in chat | what happens |
|---|---|
| "restrict the folder D:\\Photos from Jarvis", "restrict D:\\Photos", "stop Jarvis reading C:\\X", "don't let Jarvis touch C:\\X" | ONE `protect_item` card; the folder becomes **blocked** once it is approved |
| "unrestrict D:\\Photos", "let Jarvis read D:\\Photos again", "stop protecting D:\\Photos" | ONE `unprotect_item` card; the entry leaves only on the card's yes |
| "what folders are restricted?", "which files are blocked?" | the real list, no card |
| "is Jarvis blocked from C:\\X?" | `Yes` / `No` about THAT path, read from the store, no card |

A sentence that names a path acts on that path; one that only DESCRIBES a
folder ("the folder with my medical scans") names no path, so the answer ASKS
for the whole path and quotes the sentence to repeat ("restrict the folder
D:\\Medical scans from Jarvis"). No target is ever guessed - protecting the
wrong folder is itself a failure - and the answer never falls back to a generic
"I cannot", which is the failure the owner reported. A private chat refuses the
change like every mutation. Both apps chat through the same `/api/chat`, so
this works from the PC and the phone alike with no client change.
Both actions ship as `"ask"` in both copies of `jarvis-framework.toml`; the gate
has no `_RISK` row for them yet (a drop-in module adds no patch, and risk rows
are written by patches), so they are unclassified: the gate forces them to
"ask" whatever the setting says and shows its generic worst-case warning. A
follow-up patch can classify them.

### 171.3 The two modes, exactly

- **`blocked` - no access at all.** Folder/file: no read, no search hit, no
  snippet, no document read, no write, no delete, no rename, no File-Guardian
  restore into it, no note-capture write into it, no generated picture written
  into it. Program: no opening, closing or controlling it, and no screen
  reading of its windows (its window is masked out of a capture; a front-window
  look is paused).
- **`readonly` - reading allowed, changing refused.** Folder/file: reading and
  search results allowed; every write, delete, rename and restore refused.
  Program: **see it, never act** - window title/screenshot allowed; opening,
  clicking, typing, closing or controlling refused.

Protection **wins** over every allow-list ("Folders Jarvis may look in",
app-control's list), over a chat request, and over any default tier (an
`auto`-tier read is still refused). A refusal is a plain sentence and raises no
card.

### 171.4 Where the check is enforced (v1)

One central pair of functions, `jarvis_protection.path_refusal(path, write=)`
and `program_refusal(name, act=)`, is called BEFORE the action by the points
below. Every path is compared in BOTH its lexical form
(`normcase(abspath(p))`) and its resolved form (`normcase(realpath(p))`), so a
link that lives inside a protected folder AND a link elsewhere that resolves
into it are both caught; the list's own store file (and its `.bak`/`.tmp`
siblings) is refused unconditionally and does not need an entry. A `program`
entry matches by bare executable name, with or without `.exe` (`notepad` and
`notepad.exe` are one key).

| point | module | what it covers |
|---|---|---|
| folders allow-list door | `jarvis_documents.allowed_path` (+ `find`, `search`, `read` via it) | blocked paths never read, listed or indexed; read-only files still readable; `read` returns the plain sentence |
| Notion import | `jarvis_documents.import_notion` | a write into a blocked/read-only folder is refused before unzipping |
| file tools | `jarvis_agent` `file_read`, `my_files` read preflight, note-tool prepare | blocked path refused before any card; read-only files still read |
| daily notes | `jarvis_note_capture.plan` (+ `run` belt) | a write into a protected note/file is refused before the card |
| notes vault | `jarvis_notes.snapshot_vault_before_write` | the vault's guarded write door refuses a blocked/read-only file |
| Obsidian notes editor | `jarvis_notes_edit._protection` (`handle_list`, `handle_read`, `handle_save`) | a blocked vault folder refuses the whole list; blocked notes/folders are hidden and the walk never descends into them; a blocked read is refused before any bytes; a save asks the WRITE question before the current bytes are read, so blocked AND read-only refuse with no card; a read-only note still lists and reads; the File Guardian snapshot still runs after the card |
| chat attachments | `jarvis_attached_file.read` | an attachment is bytes; if a client ever sends a PC path by reference it is checked (named limitation below) |
| File Guardian restore | `jarvis_file_guardian._restore_path` | a restore into a protected path is a write and is refused |
| opening a program | `jarvis_open.resolve` | blocked and read-only programs are both refused ("opening" is an act) |
| looking at / acting in a program's window | `jarvis_ui_control.jarvis_target_refusal` (+ `deliver`) | blocked: never looked at; read-only: looked at, never acted in |
| screen capture / OCR | `jarvis_screen.pause_reason`, `jarvis_screen_win.protected_capture_problem` / `whole_screen_protection_problem` / `must_hide` | a blocked program that OWNS the target window refuses the look before the picture; a blocked program VISIBLE on a monitor being captured refuses the whole-screen capture before a pixel is read; identified windows are also masked, and the capture fails closed |
| reminder "open a file" | `jarvis_schedule._path_problem` (+ `_path_problem` is the reminder module's door; there is no `jarvis_reminders.py` on the base) | opening a blocked file is refused; read-only may be opened (a read) |
| launcher / chat tool arguments | `jarvis_open.resolve`, `jarvis_agent._protection_path_args` (before the gate) | a protected program is never started; every absolute PC path in a tool's arguments is checked before any card |
| notes list / read / search | `jarvis_notes._search_vault`, `jarvis_note_capture.plan`/`capture` | a blocked note is not read, searched or listed, and `#obs` capture into a protected place refuses before its card |
| Obsidian wiki | `jarvis_wiki.read_source`, `_shown_pages`, `_existing_pages`, `check_pages`, `_checked`, `ingest` | a blocked source is never read; a blocked page is not shown or listed; ingest refuses blocked and read-only sources before a job/card; every planned/actual page/index/log/cache write asks the WRITE question in `plan()` and again in `run()` |
| background jobs / plans | `jarvis_jobs.create`, `_plan_step`, `_plan_handler` | every PC path anywhere in a job's params is checked when the job is created (fails before it exists) and again per step at the tick: a read-only step asks the read question, a mutating one the write question |
| the list's own store | `jarvis_protection._is_self_path` (inside `path_refusal`/`blocked_path`) | `protected-items.json`, its `.bak`/`.tmp`/atomic siblings are refused to every caller, listed or not; only the module's own `save()` writes it |
| generated pictures | `jarvis_pictures.save_picture` / `file_answer` | no picture written into, or read from, a protected folder |

Each point has its own test in `backend/test_protection.py`, including the
no-card proof (the refusal happens with a stub gate whose `check()` is never
called).

#### The seven mandatory bypass paths (Gemini Q2, 2026-10-31)

The ruling named seven ways a "block access" feature can be bypassed. Each one
is now COVERED, FIXED, or named as a v1 deferral - never silent:

| # | bypass path | verdict | what is in the tree |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Windows Path Canonicalization: both `normcase(abspath(p))` (lexical) and `normcase(realpath(p))` (resolved) | **FIXED** (was realpath-only; the lexical half was missing) | `jarvis_protection._path_forms`; both halves compared for folder subtrees and file equality; test `t_p1_canonicalisation_checks_both_forms` proves each half separately (and a real symlink where the OS allows one) |
| 2 | Self-protection of `protected-items.json` and its `.bak`/temp siblings | **FIXED** (was not hard-coded; the store could be read through a model/file tool) | `jarvis_protection._is_self_path`/`SELF_SENTENCE`; unconditionally refused to every caller (read AND write), only `save()` writes it; tests point a file tool, a document read and an attachment path at it, and prove a same-named file elsewhere is NOT blocked |
| 3 | Obsidian notes editor and wiki: list omits blocked; read refuses blocked; save/`#obs`/wiki ingest refuse blocked AND read-only BEFORE the card | **FIXED** for `jarvis_notes` / `jarvis_note_capture` / `jarvis_wiki` AND for the notes EDITOR (`jarvis_notes_edit`, via its own hook commit `8de06098f0` cherry-picked on top of PR #1017: list hides blocked entries, read refuses blocked, save asks the WRITE question before the job or card) | `jarvis_notes._search_vault` skips blocked folders/notes; `jarvis_wiki.read_source`/`_shown_pages`/`_existing_pages` omit & refuse; `check_pages` asks the write question before a wiki card; `_checked` asks again in `run()`; `ingest` refuses a read-only source before a job exists; `#obs` `capture()` already refused before its card via `plan()`; tests drive each with a fake gate whose `calls` must stay empty |
| 4 | Screen capture/OCR: a blocked program owning the target window, or visible on the captured monitor, refuses before pixels/titles | **FIXED** (the earlier hooks only paused a foreground look and masked identified windows; a whole-monitor capture still read pixels) | `jarvis_screen_win.protected_capture_problem` (target window) and `whole_screen_protection_problem` (window list ∩ monitor rect, blocked only), `jarvis_screen._grab` refuses `protection_visible` before the grab, `take_picture` is a second fail-closed belt; tests prove the grabbing call is never made |
| 5 | Subprocess / launcher / reminders: normalise the executable name and check all path arguments | **FIXED** for the launcher and the chat tools' path arguments; reminders use `jarvis_schedule._path_problem` (there is no `jarvis_reminders.py`) | `jarvis_protection.program_keys` (bare name, with/without `.exe`); `jarvis_open.resolve` refused both spellings; `jarvis_agent._protection_path_args` checks every absolute PC path in every tool's arguments before the gate; tests cover `notepad`/`Notepad.EXE`/full-path spellings and read-vs-write questions |
| 6 | Background jobs and file watchers: ticks must not read blocked or write read-only paths | **FIXED for `jarvis_jobs`; `jarvis_watch` NAMED (no owner-file door)** | `jarvis_jobs._protection_params_refusal` at `create()`, at `_plan_step()` and again per step in `_plan_handler()` (read-only step = read question, mutating = write question); a fake job naming a blocked/read-only path is refused before it exists. `jarvis_watch` only reads GitHub over the network and its own SQLite DB - it never opens an owner path, so there is nothing to check there (named, not silently skipped) |
| 7 | Phone scope: `program` entries govern PC programs (`*.exe`); phone apps stay governed by `AppControlPlate` (deny-by-default) | **FIXED in the docs** (the phone plate's own wording is the phone lane's) | §171.6 states it in plain words; the phone AppControlPlate remains deny-by-default for Android package names |

### 171.5 Named gaps (v1), said plainly rather than left silent

- `shell_exec`, `run_data_script` (the data sandbox) and `rea_investigate` run
  a program or a script that can read any file by itself; there is no path to
  check before the run. They are not blocked by this list in v1 (their own
  cards say what they will run).
- `jarvis_app_control` acts in the PHONE's Android apps (package names), not in
  PC programs, so a protected PC executable has no name to match there.
- `jarvis_browser_control` drives its own bundled Playwright Chromium, not the
  owner's installed browser; there is no link between a protected executable
  and that bundled one.
- `jarvis_media` uses Windows' GLOBAL media session: whatever program is
  playing, including a protected one.
- A full-screen capture is now refused outright when the window list names a
  BLOCKED program visible on that monitor (Q2 #4). What remains: a window whose
  process cannot be identified at all is painted black (fail closed), and a
  window list that cannot be read makes the capture fail closed with no picture
  - a blocked program is then never shown, but the capture is refused rather
  than tailored.
- `jarvis_watch` has no owner-file door in v1 (network + its own SQLite only),
  so Q2 #6's watcher half is named here rather than hooked; `jarvis_jobs`
  handlers are checked centrally (see the table).
- Backup/model installs write inside Jarvis's own folders, not the owner's
  listed folders; the File Guardian restore point above still covers a restore
  path.
- The Obsidian notes editor (`jarvis_notes_edit.py`) is covered by its own
  small hook commit (`8de06098f0`, cherry-picked on top of PR #1017 before this
  list merges): a blocked vault folder refuses the whole list, blocked notes and
  folders are hidden and the walk never descends into them, a blocked read is
  refused before any bytes are read, and a save asks the WRITE question before
  the old bytes are read - so blocked AND read-only refuse with no card, while a
  read-only note still lists and reads and an unprotected note still saves after
  its own one card. Nothing in that lane is left uncovered.

### 171.6 The apps and honest limits

Desktop Settings has the full surface (list, the three native pickers, mode
choice, Remove, and plain sentences for refusals); the phone shows the list, the
mode, Remove (which asks the PC for one card) and one line saying the pickers
are on the PC. Both apps list it either way; there is no phone file browser.

**What a `program` entry governs.** A `program` entry is a PC executable
(`*.exe`) - it governs opening, closing, controlling and screen-reading THAT
program on this PC. It does not govern phone apps: those stay governed by the
phone's own `AppControlPlate` allow-list, which is deny-by-default, and a phone
package name is never matched against this list. Likewise a `folder`/`file`
entry is a PC path.
`POST /api/protection/add` is PC-only and raises no card; the chat add and every
removal are one card each. Adding from the phone is not missing, only one step
slower: the owner asks in chat and the same `protect_item` card waits. Removing
and asking what is on the list are one chat sentence from either app too (§171.2
has the owner's phrasings), and nothing about that is one-sided: the phone chats
through the same `/api/chat`, so it gets the same cards and the same real-state
answers with no client change.

**Implemented and proved in this repository, NOT deployed to the owner's live
PC by this change** - the live deploy is its own pass, so the owner's apps do
not show it until then. Both lanes are in: the desktop Settings surface, the
phone's list, and `tools/check_parity.py` classifies `/api/protection` and
`/api/protection/remove` as ported, `/api/protection/add` as the desktop's alone
on purpose (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8), and the chat door
`/api/protection/propose` as backend-only. The card words, the "What asks first"
rows and the six app-side contract fixtures (`card-words-cases.json`,
`asks-first-cases.json`, `screen-cases.json`, each app's copy) are in this
change. One follow-up is written down rather than hidden: a patch can give the
two actions `_RISK` rows so their cards show classified words instead of the
gate's generic unclassified warning; the gate already forces `ask` on both, so
nothing is loosened in the meantime.

## 172. Send one file from the PC to the phone (added 2026-10-31)

The owner's own words: *"am i able to ask jarvis to search for a file for me and
send it to the jarvis android app to view and or download directly? this would
be a file on the desktop"*. Gemini ruled on it the same day (Q7): build the
bounded slice, NOT a text-only halfway step and NOT a "share folder" the owner
must fill by hand at the PC. This is the backend half; the phone's View / Save
to Downloads screens are the follow-up phone lane, and the desktop needs
nothing. Section number: main ends at 169, the notes-editor PR (#1017) takes
170 and the protection PR (#1019) takes 171, so 172 was chosen to sit after
both (the next REAL free number once their two sections land).

### 172.1 The two phone-facing routes (no path is ever a parameter)

    GET /api/files/send                approved files waiting for the phone
    GET /api/files/download?id=<id>    the bytes of ONE approved file

Both are behind the core's own origin + token checks (`X-Jarvis-Client` and the
pairing token, mesh only in practice), exactly like `/api/protection` and
`/api/pictures/file`; this feature adds no new auth scheme. `send` answers
`{ok, count, files:[{id, name, folder, size_bytes, mime, expires_in}],
cap_bytes, ttl_seconds, single_use, said}`. `download` answers
`{ok, name, size_bytes, mime, sha256, data}` where `data` is base64 (the same
shape `/api/pictures/file` uses), and its ONLY parameter is `id`: a raw path is
never accepted, and the answer never carries one. Unknown, expired, already
downloaded or not-yet-approved ids are `404` with one plain sentence.

### 172.2 The one card, and what happens around it

The chat tool `send_file_to_phone` (schema: `query` or `path`) searches the
existing **"Folders Jarvis may look in"** allow-list through
`jarvis_documents.allowed_path()` - the same door `my_files` uses, so hidden
folders, private places and links out are never candidates. When the
"Protected from Jarvis" module (PR #1019) is importable, its ONE keep-out check
(`path_refusal`) is asked as a soft hook; this section does not duplicate it,
and on a tree without that module the allow-list is the whole story.

With exactly ONE match it raises ONE card under the shipped action
`send_file_to_phone` (tier **"ask"**, in both copies of
`jarvis-framework.toml`). The card's words are built by `prepare()` and name
the EXACT file:

    Send "invoice.pdf" from C:\Users\you\Documents to your phone? It is
    1,482,331 bytes (1.4 MB large). This slice sends ONE file at a time and
    refuses anything over 10 MiB (10,485,760 bytes); the link lasts 10 minutes
    and works once.

`prepare()` refuses, BEFORE any card, with a plain sentence: no match, more
than one match (it lists up to 8 names and asks to narrow), a path outside the
allow-list, or a file over the cap. Nothing becomes fetchable until the gate's
approved verdict runs `execute()`; a Deny leaves nothing behind. A file that
vanished between the card and the fetch answers in plain words; a file that
changed is answered as changed, never silently sent.

The action is not classified in `jarvis_gate._RISK` (a shipped/drop-in tool
cannot add that row; a follow-up patch can), so the gate treats it as an
unclassified action: **forced to "ask"**, carrying its own **outbound**
worst-case line - the bytes leave the PC for the phone and the phone can keep a
copy after downloading it. Nothing about that is looser than the tier row; it
is the same safe side the protection cards use.

The same sentence works **in chat without the model tool being enabled**: a
deterministic fast-path shape ("send me the file invoice.pdf", "send
invoice.pdf to my phone", "send the file invoice.pdf to my phone", "find the
file invoice.pdf and send it to my phone", "send me invoice.pdf from my
Downloads") calls this section's own `prepare()` and raises this same card
under the same action. No new route, no new tool, no new permission: the module
still searches, refuses and words everything, the fast path never approves
anything, and its answer is the card's own sentence plus "Nothing is sent until
you approve the card."

### 172.3 Named limits (all of them)

- **one file per card**, one card at a time;
- **cap 10 MiB** (`10,485,760` bytes; Gemini's ruling allows 10-25 MB). Over
  the cap is a refusal in words - never a silent truncation;
- **TTL 10 minutes** from the card's yes, after which the id is gone;
- **single use**: one successful fetch consumes the id, a second fetch is a
  plain `404` ("already downloaded or the ten-minute window passed"). This is
  the deliberate choice: a bounded slice with a one-shot id is safer than a
  re-downloadable link, and the owner can simply ask again;
- at most **8 ids alive** in memory (oldest dropped first), and a restart
  clears every id - the phone then says "ask Jarvis again";
- only inside the **"Folders Jarvis may look in"** allow-list, minus anything
  the optional protection check refuses;
- the desktop needs nothing, and the desktop app is not part of this slice.

### 172.4 What the phone lane owns now

The phone half is built in the same pull request: `net/SendFile.kt` (the pure
contract and the two route shapes), `ui/screens/SendFilePlate.kt` (the list of
approved files, View via `FileProvider` + `ACTION_VIEW`, and Save to Downloads
via `MediaStore.Downloads`), the Settings row "File from your PC"
(`SettingsScreen.kt`, jump and search entries, `OpenPlace` key `files`), the
manifest `FileProvider` and `res/xml/send_file_paths.xml`, and
`SendFileTest.kt` on the JVM. `tools/check_parity.py` now classifies both
routes as `ported`; `backend/test_file_to_phone.py` proves the backend half and
the phone cannot fetch a file the owner did not approve. The action still
raises its ONE card and the id still lasts ten minutes and works once.


## 173. Which app is asking: the phone or the desktop program (added 2026-10-31)

**It is always on. There is no setting, no opt-in and no first-run step.**

Jarvis can now tell whether the owner is talking to it from the **Android app**
or from the **desktop program**, and it uses that fact in the answers below. A
request that says neither is `unknown` and behaves exactly as it did before this
section existed - so an older client, a script or a test changes nothing.

### 173.1 The header

Both clients add one plain header on **every** request:

    X-Jarvis-Surface: phone        -- the Android app (jarvis-client)
    X-Jarvis-Surface: desktop      -- the desktop program (Rust + the HUD page)

- It is **additive**. The existing `X-Jarvis-Client: hud` header is unchanged,
  byte for byte, because the origin check and the cloud-escalation rules read
  it; nothing here replaces it.
- It is **not authentication and not a secret**. Access is still decided by the
  origin check and the token, exactly as before. This header only chooses words,
  it is never logged, and a request cannot gain anything by sending it.
- Case does not matter (`Phone` is the phone), and anything that is not exactly
  `phone` or `desktop` reads as `unknown` - over-capture is refused on purpose.
- One place per client sends it: the phone's `JarvisApi.Request.Builder.authed()`
  (and the two pairing posts, which are phone requests too), and the desktop's
  Rust `jarvis_headers` (every Tauri command) plus the HUD page's one
  `JARVIS.headers()` builder (every page fetch).

### 173.2 Where the PC reads it

The shipped origin gate - `jarvis_owner_check.origin_ok`, which every chat
request already passes before anything answers - reads the header **once** for
that request into `jarvis_surface` (a new shipped module). It is kept on the
request's own thread, so two requests cannot mix surfaces. A missing module or
odd headers are `unknown`, never a refusal.

It is used by:

- `jarvis_quick.py` - the deterministic quick answers;
- `jarvis_feature_guide.py` - the feature/limits answers, through each row's
  own `surface` and `where` fields;
- `jarvis_agent.py` - one system sentence for the model:
  "The owner is talking to you from the Android app." /
  "... from the desktop program." (nothing when unknown).

### 173.3 What changes in the answers

- **Feature answers use the row's own fields with the app that is asking.** A
  PC-only feature asked from the phone says it is on the PC only and where the
  PC door is; a phone-only feature asked from the desktop says it is on the
  phone only and where the phone door is; a both-apps feature keeps its facts
  and adds only which app is asking. Nothing is reworded: `surface`, `where` and
  `surface_reason` stay the feature list's own words.
- **Room-specific quick asks name that app's doors.** "Open the second brain"
  from the phone says the Brain is in the phone app (tap Brain on Home) and
  where the PC's window opens; "open Jarvis settings" from the phone says the
  phone's own Settings are in the app and the PC's settings window opens on the
  PC. From the desktop the old sentences are unchanged ("Opening the Brain on
  this PC."), and with no header the old words are returned.
- **General conversation** gets the one system sentence above, so the model can
  say "on your phone you can ..." without inventing a route.

No route, no card, no tool and no setting is added or changed by any of this.
The phone still cannot open a window on the PC, and a phone answer carries no
route field that would pretend otherwise.

- **The question "where am I talking from?" is answered from this fact, never by
  the model** (added 2026-11-01; the field test found the desktop HUD answering
  it as a physical-location question - "I don't have access to your location
  data or GPS" - and the phone right only by luck of its model). A deterministic
  lane in `jarvis_quick.py` matches only whole-sentence surface questions
  ("where am I talking from", "where am I talking to you from", "which app am I
  using", "what device am I on", "am I on my phone or pc" and the close shapes)
  and answers with one of three sentences: the desktop sentence ("You are
  talking to me from the desktop program on your PC."), the phone sentence
  ("You are talking to me from the Jarvis app on your Android phone."), or -
  when the request carried no header at all - the honest unknown sentence
  ("This request did not say which app it came from, so I cannot tell whether
  you are talking to me from the phone or the desktop program."). Near misses
  ("where am I", "where am I located", "where is my phone", "which app can use
  the second card") keep their old path on purpose: a miss costs a model answer,
  a hijack would break a real question. It is read-only: no card, no route, no
  write; `backend/test_surface_origin.py` proves the three sentences, the
  deterministic repeat and every near miss.

### 173.4 One-sided? No.

Both clients send the header and both apps' routes are named in the answers, so
there is nothing to record in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 as deliberately
one-sided. `tools/check_parity.py` is unchanged (no route was added).

### 173.5 What proves it

- `backend/test_surface.py` - the header parses to exactly phone/desktop/unknown
  (including over-capture traps), the origin gate still allows and refuses as
  before, "open the second brain"/"open Jarvis settings" flip by surface, a
  phone-only row asked from the desktop and a desktop-only row asked from the
  phone flip wording using the rows' own `where`, the model's rules-first
  system turn carries the sentence for a stub model, and with no header every
  answer is exactly the old one.
- `jarvis-client`'s `SurfaceHeaderTest` - the one authed builder and the pairing
  posts send `X-Jarvis-Surface: phone` and still send `X-Jarvis-Client: hud`.
- the Rust `commands::surface_header_tests` - the one `jarvis_headers` adds
  `X-Jarvis-Surface: desktop` beside the unchanged client header.
- `jarvis-backend/jarvis_surface.py` is the byte-identical published base of
  `backend/jarvis_surface.py`; both `SHIPPED` lists name it.

### 173.6 The HUD question on the phone

The owner's screenshot also showed the phone answering "can I edit the HUD in the
jarvis app?" with *"Jarvis does not currently offer a built-in method…"*, which is
false about the product: the HUD's layout is edited on the PC. With the surface
header, that question from the **phone** is now answered deterministically and
truthfully - the HUD's layout is edited on the PC (Settings' "Edit HUD in the
window", or the "Edit HUD" button in the HUD's own header), while this app's own
look is in Appearance (theme, the face, face size, text size and spacing). No
phone-side HUD editor is claimed, because there is none. With no header, or from
the desktop, the old path is untouched; `backend/test_surface.py` pins both.

## 174. Opening an app on your phone, and starting a media search (backend only, added 2026-11-01)

The owner asked, in these words:

> "id like jarvis live to be able to open certain apps on my android phone if i
> ask it (during a live session on my android phone) and to be able to perform
> certain actions like if i aaid 'hey jarvis open yourube music and play the
> weekend'"

So: from a Live conversation on the phone, "open YouTube Music" and "open
YouTube Music and play The Weeknd" work. The PC is the brain and the gate; the
phone is the hands, over `adb`, exactly as `control_phone` already did. There is
**no new route**: this is the existing `control_phone` tool
(`backend/jarvis_agent.py`) and the existing `jarvis_android_control.py` module,
both shipped whole.

### 174.1 The three actions the model can now ask for

| Action | What it sends (one literal adb command, printed on the card) |
|---|---|
| `list_apps` | **Nothing.** Answered from the settings file; see 174.3. |
| `open_app` | `adb -s <serial> shell monkey -p <package> -c android.intent.category.LAUNCHER 1` |
| `play` | `adb -s <serial> shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d <the app's own search address> -p <package>` |

`play` with YouTube Music, for "play The Weeknd", is exactly:

```
adb -s <serial> shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d 'https://music.youtube.com/search?q=The%20Weeknd' -p com.google.android.apps.youtube.music
```

`open_app` carries no activity name to guess: `monkey` is Android's own "launch
this package's launcher activity". `play` uses `-p`, so only that one package
can receive the intent - no browser and no other app can answer it instead.

The rest of the tool is unchanged: `tap`, `swipe`, `key`, `text`, `screenshot`,
`long_press`, `ui_dump`, all still literal argv lists, all still checked against
the same plan/describe/run model.

`device` is **no longer required** on the tool. "open YouTube Music" said out
loud carries no serial, and a model was never told one; leaving it out now means
the ONE phone connected over adb (`jarvis_android_control.resolve_device`), and
zero or several connected devices is a plain refusal ("no phone is connected over
adb right now…" / "more than one device is connected over adb (A, B), so Jarvis
did not guess which one"), never a guess.

### 174.2 The allow-list IS the permission

`[phone_apps]` in `jarvis-framework.toml` is one line per app - the name you
would say out loud, and the package behind it:

```toml
[phone_apps]
"YouTube Music" = "com.google.android.apps.youtube.music"
```

It ships **EMPTY**, and empty (or no table at all) refuses everything. The rules,
all enforced in `jarvis_android_control.py` before any card exists:

- an app that is not on the list is refused, and the refusal **names the apps
  that are**;
- an empty list is refused with one sentence saying how to add one;
- a package that is not a plain dotted name is refused (`_safe_package`);
- anything under `com.jarvis.` is refused - Jarvis never starts its own app, so
  no tap can reach an Approve button;
- a name and a package that disagree are refused rather than picked between;
- the words of a search are percent-encoded with `urllib.parse.quote(...,
  safe="")`, so `;`, `&`, `"`, backticks and `$(...)` arrive as `%3B`, `%26`,
  `%22`, `%60` and `%24%28…` and mean nothing to the phone's own shell. The
  finished address is then checked against `_SAFE_URL`, which does not admit
  `&` at all: `adb shell` hands the line to `/system/bin/sh`, where an unquoted
  `&` starts a background job;
- a settings line that is not a plain string, and any package `_safe_package`
  refuses, is **left out** of the list rather than trusted, and `list_apps` says
  how many lines were ignored.

Only apps whose search address is documented are in `SEARCH_LINKS`: today that
is YouTube Music alone. Any other app on the list can be **opened**, and `play`
refuses it in plain words ("Jarvis can open 'Maps' on your phone, but it does not
know how to ask it to search… Ask it to open the app instead") rather than
pretending.

### 174.3 `list_apps`: read-only, and never a card

`list_apps` is answered from the settings file with the friendly names only -
never the phone's installed apps, never a package the owner did not write down:

```json
{"ok": true, "count": 1,
 "apps": [{"name": "YouTube Music", "can_play": true}], "note": ""}
```

It sends nothing to the phone and starts nothing, so it raises **no approval
card**: `plan()` refuses it outright (`list_apps` is never a command), and
`_prepare_control_phone` answers a list-only call before the gate. The same is
true of a call where nothing could become a command - an app not on the list, an
empty list, no phone connected - so the owner is never asked to approve an empty
plan, and the model gets the reason to repeat in the owner's own words.

`can_play` is how the model tells "open it" from "open it and search" without
guessing.

### 174.4 What has NOT changed, on purpose

- **The same gate action and the same tier.** Every plan still resolves to
  `jarvis_android_control_run` → `control_phone`, and `[autonomy.tiers]` still
  says `control_phone = "ask"`. One card per plan, printing every literal
  command; nothing is auto-approved; the tool stays in the agent's
  `NEEDS_A_PERSON` set.
- **Still opt-in.** `control_phone` is NOT in the shipped `[tools].enabled`, so
  a fresh install offers no tool that can touch a phone. To turn it on, add
  `"control_phone"` to `[tools].enabled` in `jarvis-framework.toml`, and add the
  apps to `[phone_apps]`. Both files are re-read while Jarvis runs, so an edit
  takes effect on the next message; a change to the CODE needs the reconciled
  backend and a restart.
- **A step that pins its own package is not blocked by the Jarvis-in-front
  guard.** `open_app` and `play` are `PACKAGE_PINNED_ACTIONS`: both commands
  name the package themselves (`monkey -p`, `am start -p`), and a `com.jarvis.`
  package is refused before a command exists, so neither can land a tap inside
  Jarvis's own app - which is the only thing that guard protects. Without this
  the feature would be refused every time it was asked FROM the phone, because
  that is where the Jarvis app is in front. A `tap` is still refused there.
- **`play` is honest about what it does.** It opens the app on that app's own
  search address for the words the owner said. On the phone that is a search
  shown in the app; whether music starts without one tap depends on the app.
  The tool description and the card both say "one tap may still be needed".
- **`am start` and `monkey` exit 0 when they fail.** Both print the failure on
  stdout ("Error: Activity not started, unable to resolve Intent", "No
  activities found, monkey aborted"). `run()` now reads that, so a launch that
  did not happen is reported as a failure instead of `done`.

### 174.5 What this repository cannot prove

The exact intent behaviour on the owner's own phone - whether YouTube Music's
own App Link accepts `https://music.youtube.com/search?q=…` and lands on the
search, and whether the app then starts playing - is verified by the Lead on the
real device. Everything above is proved against injected fakes: no test here
starts `adb` or touches a phone (`backend/test_android_control.py`,
`backend/test_phone_app_launch.py`).

Also unchanged and worth saying: opening a media app takes it to the front, so a
Live session on the phone is backgrounded by it (see `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8,
"One-sided on purpose").

## 175. "You have full approval to search the web for this conversation": ONE card, and search only (added 2026-11-01)

The owner's own words, two messages the same day:

> "also if I ask jarvis and say you have full approval to search the web for
> anything during this conversation. give jarvis the approval to search the web
> for the entire conversation until I say it doesn't have authorization to do
> that. make sure a card comes up that I have to approve before this happens"

> "and if I ask anything further like book a flight for me online then it will
> have to have another card to approve further action beyond just searching the
> web."

Section number: main ended at 173 when this was written, and #1067 (the phone app launch, merged first) took 174, so this one is 175.

### 175.1 What it is, and what it is not

ONE approval card, once, that stands in for the ordinary `search_the_web` card
for the rest of ONE conversation. It is a **standing permission for exactly one
action**, not a general "trust me" switch:

- it covers `search_the_web` and nothing else. The ONLY code that reads a grant
  is `_web_search_call` (the one place whose gate action is
  `jarvis_search.ACTION_SEARCH`), and the only things that write or clear one
  are the two tools below. "Book a flight for me" is `browser_control` (or
  `read_web_page` for one page) and still raises its own card with a grant live;
  so do `send_email`, `control_computer`, `control_phone`, `spend_money`,
  `delete_file`, `run_shell_on_host`, `change_own_config` and everything else.
  `backend/test_web_search_grant.py` names six of them and proves each still
  asks;
- it cannot be made by the words alone. The model asks for the card; a person
  answers it. The store is written only on the generic
  prepare()/gate/execute() path after a verdict that came from a card, so a
  denied, timed-out or unanswered card writes nothing, and a verdict with
  nobody asked (`outcome` `auto`) is refused by `NEEDS_A_PERSON` even if someone
  loosens its tier in their own settings;
- it dies with the conversation, and on its own. The key is the request's own
  `conversation_id`, so conversation A's grant cannot cover conversation B, and
  a request with no conversation id can neither give nor use one (it is refused
  with no card at all). It is capped at 8 hours, and it is **in memory only** -
  no file, no database, no setting - so a restart ends it;
- Lockdown wins. `jarvis_asks_first.lockdown_on()` stops a grant being used for
  as long as it is on, and the card says so.

### 175.2 The two tools and the two gate actions

| model tool | gate action | tier | card? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `approve_web_search_for_conversation` | `grant_web_search_conversation` | `ask` | ONE card, once |
| `stop_web_search_approval` | `revoke_web_search_grant` | `auto` | none - instant |

Both tier lines are in **both** shipped settings copies
(`backend/rebuilt/jarvis-framework.toml` and
`jarvis-backend/jarvis-framework.toml`); `backend/_apply_toml_tiers.py` adds
them to an existing PC's file at the next update, the same way every other new
action reaches it. Both actions have their own `_RISK` row in
`jarvis_gate.py` (the grant is `reversible: yes` / `reach: outbound`, so a
risky approval that a lock screen may not swipe through; the stop is
`yes` / `local`), so neither is an unclassified action - which matters: without
its row the stop would be forced to tier "ask" and the owner would be sent a
card to STOP something they had just asked to stop. The rows are added by one
`_RISK.update({...})` at the END of `jarvis_gate.py`, not inside the table's own
literal: every line in there is some earlier patch's hunk context, and both
placements that were tried inside it broke a real suite (the numbers and the
two failures are in `backend/_stack.py`'s RATCHET note). `_RISK.update` runs at
import, before any `check()` call.

`more_tools` group `web_search_grant`. **Both tools are offered on an ordinary
turn whenever `web_search` itself is offered** (2026-11-02, after the live field
test): they are not rows in Settings -> Tools and `[tools].enabled` does not name
them, so the offered set is `jarvis_agent.GRANT_ASK_TOOLS` riding along with the
web-search tool, and switching web search off in Settings takes both with it.
Offering the ASK grants nothing - the store is written only after a person
answers the card, and the tool refuses with no card when the request carries no
conversation id - and the stop only takes permission away. The earlier design
made them a "Safety and sharing" switch instead, and on the owner's own PC that
switch was never on: the model was offered no tool, no card could be raised, and
a natural request answered "Search is approved for this conversation" with
nothing behind it. `test_tool_defaults.py` and `test_tool_contract.py` pin the
new offered list; `jarvis_asks_first.TOOLS_SWITCHABLE` is 21 rows again.

**An approval cannot be claimed from words.** Two more things were added for the
same field test, so the model never has to guess whether a grant is in force:

- the rules block (`jarvis_agent.LANE_SYSTEM`, and the Modelfile's SYSTEM block)
  says plainly that an approval is not the model's to give or assume, and that a
  web-search approval is real only after a person answers its card - it must not
  say one is in place unless a tool result in that conversation told it so;
- while a grant IS in force, the prompt carries one line read from the store
  itself (`jarvis_agent._grant_prompt_line`, `WEB_SEARCH_GRANT_IN_FORCE`), so
  the "it is on" signal comes from the same function the search consults; with
  no grant the line is absent and costs no tokens. As a backstop, an answer that
  claims a web-search approval the store does not hold gets the same plain
  `(Correction - ...)` postscript as a claimed-but-unrun search
  (`_grant_claim_line`, through `postscript_lines`); an honest "no approval is
  in force" or a conditional is never corrected.

### 175.3 What the card says

The four things the owner asked to see, and nothing else:

    Allow web searches in this chat to run without a card each time?

    While this is on, a web search in THIS conversation runs without asking you
    again - including one whose words repeat something Jarvis has saved about
    you, which would otherwise get its own card.

    Nothing else is covered. Sending an email or a file, booking or buying
    anything, spending money, deleting a file, running a command, changing a
    setting, using a browser, your accounts and your phone each still raise
    their own card and still need your yes. This can never widen to them,
    however open-ended the words that asked for it were.

    It ends when you say stop ("stop searching without asking", "you don't have
    approval", "revoke that"), when this chat ends, after 8 hours, or when
    Jarvis restarts. Every search it covers is written in the approval log with
    this grant's id. Lockdown still asks: while it is on, no search runs without
    its card.

    If you say no, every search keeps asking, exactly as it does now.

The `jarvis_card_words` rows are `grant_web_search_conversation` -> "let web
searches in this chat stop asking" (short summary: "search this chat without
asking each time") and `revoke_web_search_grant` -> "ask before every web search
in this chat again". The words the owner actually says are matched by the model,
not by a phrase list: "you have full approval to search the web for anything
during this conversation", "don't ask me about searches for this chat"; and, to
stop, "stop searching without asking", "you don't have approval", "revoke
that", "ask me before searching again".

### 175.4 What is written down

Three events in the gate's own audit log, written through `jarvis_gate`'s three
new functions (`grant_made`, `granted`, `grant_ended`) rather than by the agent
calling `audit_log` itself - the event names and the redaction rules are the
gate's:

    gate.grant_made   {grant, seconds}          the card was approved
    gate.granted      {action, grant}           ONE search ran with no card
    gate.grant_ended  {grant, state}            state: revoked | expired

`grant` is this process's own random 12 hex characters. The CONVERSATION ID IS
NEVER WRITTEN DOWN - not in the log, not on disk anywhere - so the log says a
search ran unasked and under which grant, and cannot be joined back to a chat.
`gate.granted` is written before the search, because a search that starts is a
search that happened. If the backend's `jarvis_gate.py` is older than its
`jarvis_agent.py` (a half-applied update), the grant is REFUSED rather than
allowed unlogged: "every search under a grant is logged" is part of what the
owner approved.

### 175.5 One-sided? No.

Both apps get this with no new UI: the owner says the sentence in a chat and the
model calls the tools, exactly as with any other tool. Nothing is desktop-only
or phone-only, no route was added, and `tools/check_parity.py` is unchanged. A
"web searches approved for this chat" indicator is deliberately NOT built - the
approval log and the card are the record, and a second on-screen state would be
a thing to keep in sync for no gain.

### 175.6 What proves it

- `backend/test_web_search_grant.py` - 95 checks, all nine cases the brief
  names, driven through the REAL turn loop, the real `jarvis_search` planning
  and the real `jarvis_gate` audit writers, against a throwaway config and log
  folder: no card means no grant; one card and a denial grants nothing; an
  approved grant runs the search with no second card and the log carries
  `gate.granted` with the grant id; six other actions still ask (two of them
  driven on the real path); conversation A does not cover B; revocation is
  instant, logged and idempotent; the 8-hour cap and a restart end it; "book a
  flight" still raises its own card; open-ended words grant search only. It also
  applies `backend/web-search-grant.patch` to `jarvis-backend/jarvis_gate.py`
  and reverses it byte for byte.
- `tools/check_patch_original_text.py` - the patch's four hunks and 21 lines of
  the owner's original text are pinned, with the reason written beside the pin.
- the existing suites: `test_web_search.py` (the search path it sits in),
  `test_card_words.py` and `test_card_short_words.py` (both actions have plain
  words), `test_tool_contract.py`, `test_tool_text.py`, `test_short_tool_list.py`,
  `test_tool_defaults.py` (the offered list now includes the ask and its stop,
  riding with web search; `[tools].enabled` is unchanged),
  `test_reach.py`, `test_smarter_answers.py`, `test_asks_first.py` (21 rows;
  the two tools are no longer "Safety and sharing" switches),
  `test_warm_prefix.py` (the warm-up sends the same ride-alongs a real turn
  does), `test_character.py` and `test_agent.py` (the rules paragraph),
  `test_gate_risk_words.py`,
  `test_gate_names.py`, `test_gate_unknown_risk.py`.

## 176. The phone's app list, managed: add or remove one app, card first (added 2026-11-02)

The owner asked for this in their own words: *"any apps that i ask if to open or
do something with. i would need to approve a card with the apps i would like it
to manipulate first and i can remove or add any android app to that list any
time with an approval card... or by going to the settings and changing it there
too."* Section 174's `[phone_apps]` table is the whole permission, and it ships
empty - so before this the only way to use the feature was to hand-edit
`jarvis-framework.toml`. Now the table is managed, by chat and by the settings
routes below, and every change is ONE approval card that names the app.

### 176.1 The model's tool: `phone_apps`

One tool, three actions, in chat and in Live on both apps (it is in the shipped
`[tools].enabled` - see 175.5):

| action | what it does | a card? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list` | the allowed apps, by the owner's own names, from the settings file | **no** - nothing to approve, nothing is written |
| `add` | one app: `name` (the words the owner says) and `package` (the Android package) | **yes**, ONE `change_own_config` card |
| `remove` | one app, by `name` | **yes**, ONE `change_own_config` card |

The card is built by `jarvis_phone_apps.card_text`, never by the model, and it
names **both** the friendly name and the exact package id - for a removal
exactly as for an add:

```
Let Jarvis open "YouTube Music" (com.google.android.apps.youtube.music) on your phone?

This adds ONE line to the [phone_apps] list in your settings file on this PC:
"YouTube Music" = "com.google.android.apps.youtube.music". Nothing else changes,
and nothing is written until you approve.
```

Nothing is written until that card is approved. A denied card, a timed-out card
and a call refused before a card exists (a bad name, a package that is not a
package, `com.jarvis.`, an app already listed, an app not listed) all leave the
settings file byte-for-byte unchanged - `backend/test_phone_app_allowlist.py`
proves each one, including that no audit line is written.

**No bulk.** One call carries one app. The schema has no array for apps, the
route takes one name and one package, and a list where a string belongs is
refused in the owner's words ("One app at a time, please") before any card - so
there is no "add all of these" path to get wrong.

**The gate mapping.** The tool is put to the gate under the existing
`change_setting` key, which the published gate base already maps to
`change_own_config` - the same action the other settings changes use, with the
`ask` tier it already has. No new gate action, tier, risk row or card wording is
invented, and no `backend/*.patch` hunk in `jarvis_gate.py` is needed. The
mapping is load-bearing: `phone_apps` itself is not a `_TOOL_ACTIONS` key, so
without it `action_for_tool()` would answer `unclassified_tool`.

**Audit.** Every applied add and remove writes one local audit line -
`phone_apps.added` / `phone_apps.removed` - naming the app and the package,
after the write succeeded. A refused or failed write leaves no line claiming it
happened.

### 176.2 `GET /api/phone/apps` - the list (read-only)

Behind `X-Jarvis-Token` like every settings route, from either app. It reads
`[phone_apps]` and nothing else; it never lists the phone's installed apps and
never runs an adb command.

```json
{"ok": true, "available": true, "count": 1, "empty": false, "note": "",
 "apps": [{"name": "YouTube Music",
           "package": "com.google.android.apps.youtube.music",
           "can_play": true}]}
```

`can_play` says whether Jarvis also knows that app's own search address
(`SEARCH_LINKS` in `jarvis_android_control.py`), so a screen can say "open" from
"open and search" without guessing. A line that is not a plain name and a plain
package is left out of `apps` (the reader's rule, the same one the phone tool
uses) and counted in `note` - it is not silently hidden.

**By chat (2026-11-03).** The sentences `which apps on my phone may you open`
and `what can you open on my phone` (and their close phrasings) list this same
allow-list, read-only, through `jarvis_phone_apps.view()` - no card, no write,
and no package id printed.

### 176.3 `POST /api/phone/apps` - ONE change, and its card

`{"action": "add", "name": "YouTube Music", "package": "com.google.android.apps.youtube.music"}`
or `{"action": "remove", "name": "YouTube Music"}`. The module
(`jarvis_phone_apps.change`) validates, raises **ONE** `change_own_config` card
through `jarvis_gate.check` and writes the one line only after a person's yes.
The answers:

| status | when |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | approved and written (`changed` says whether the file moved; `apps` is the new list) |
| `400` | refused before a card: a bad name, a package that is not a package, `com.jarvis.`, an app already listed (or the package already under another name), an app not listed, a list where a string belongs |
| `409` | a card was answered "no", timed out, or the write itself failed - `error` is the owner's sentence |
| `503` | this PC cannot ask (-`jarvis_gate` not there, or the tier is not `ask`), or the settings file cannot be found; nothing changed |

A lower-level `409` is possible in one honest case: the list changed while the
card waited (the app was added or removed meanwhile), so the write re-validates
against the list as it is NOW and says so rather than writing twice or removing
something the card did not show.

### 176.4 The file: one line, the same way the other settings are written

`jarvis_phone_apps.write` follows `jarvis_limits.py` and `jarvis_notify_prefs.py`
exactly: read the owner's bytes, change ONE line of their own text (comments,
ordering and line endings untouched), re-parse the whole file and prove the ONLY
difference is the line it meant to change, then write through a temporary file
and `os.replace` with the file's own permissions, and
`jarvis_framework.reload_framework()` so the next message sees it. There is no
`open(path, "w")` anywhere in this feature. A line the owner wrote by hand, in
either TOML quoting style, can be found and removed.

### 176.5 The surfaces, and the phone decision

- **Chat and Live, both apps**: the `phone_apps` tool (175.1). It ships ON in
  `[tools].enabled`, because a tool that is itself the only way to fill a list
  that ships empty cannot be gated behind a hand edit of the same file. What it
  can reach is that ONE table; the phone tool that OPENS apps (`control_phone`)
  is still opt-in.
- **Desktop Settings**: the apps, with an honest empty state, an add (typed
  package id) and a remove - each through `POST /api/phone/apps`, so each raises
  the normal card. *(This surface is the remaining half of this slice - see the
  PR body; the routes it needs are above.)*
- **Phone Settings**: a READ-ONLY list and "Ask Jarvis to add an app", not an
  editor. This is the standing "no deep config editing on the phone" rule: an
  add needs a friendly name AND a package id, and the phone is the one device
  that cannot look a package up. The owner's own sentence - *"or by going to the
  settings and changing it there too"* - is answered by the PC's Settings and by
  the same card from the phone's chat; the record is in `docs/DECISIONS.md`
  (2026-11-02) and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8. *(This screen is the remaining
  half of this slice too - the route it reads is `GET /api/phone/apps`.)*

### 176.6 What has NOT changed

`control_phone` and its own one-card plan (§174) are untouched: opening an app
still goes to `jarvis_android_control_run` → `control_phone`, still one card
printing every literal command, still opt-in. This section adds the management
of the list; it does not add a way to open an app without a card, a second
permission model, or a bulk approval.

## 177. Approving a card from an Android notification, with Deny, Approve and Review (phone, added 2026-11-02)

The owner asked, 2026-11-02: *"make sure i can approve jarvis cards through an android
notification with a deny or approve button or tap too see more button if the summary that's short
enough to fit into an android notification isn't long enough."*

**What already existed, checked before building anything.** Approval notifications were not
missing: `service/ApprovalNotifier.kt` has posted one per pending card since the foreground service
was built, with the card's safe `notice` words, a group summary, Deny, a tap that opens the card,
`VISIBILITY_PRIVATE` plus a redacted `publicVersion`, restart-safe id bookkeeping, and a `sync()`
that cancels a notification when `/api/pending` stops carrying its id. What was missing was
**Approve**: that file said, in code and in a source-pin test, "Deny only, never Approve", every
approve action on that surface was refused, and the lock screen's public words were a generic
sentence rather than the one the owner asked for.

### 177.1 The five-point envelope (Gemini's ruling, binding)

1. **Deny may run from the lock screen.** Refusing without reading is the safe direction, and it
   was already allowed there.
2. **Approve requires the device unlocked.** Every approve action is built with
   `setAuthenticationRequired(true)`, so Android itself withholds the `PendingIntent` until the
   phone is unlocked. No Kotlin check is the lock-screen wall.
3. **Tier-aware biometric.** Only a card that `SecurityRules.isSmall` exempts (the owner's
   2026-11-01 request, the same small read-only actions) and that the owner's setting does not
   ask about may submit its decision from the notification. Every write, config, send-file,
   phone-app or otherwise non-small card's Approve opens Jarvis on that card and runs the same
   `BiometricPrompt` the card's own Approve runs - forced even where the card alone would not have
   asked (`ApprovalNotificationPolicy.notificationApproveNeedsCheck`). The mapping to this app's
   UI: Jarvis has no separate approval sheet, so "the approval sheet" is Home focused on that
   card, with the system prompt over it.
4. **No blind approval of a clipped card.** When the text the notification shows (title and body
   together) is longer than **240 characters**, Approve is replaced by **Review in Jarvis** and
   Deny stays. The same replacement applies to a PC-only card and to a proposal that needs one of
   several plans chosen, neither of which the phone can approve.
5. **Privacy and lifecycle.** The notification is `VISIBILITY_PRIVATE`; the lock screen's
   `publicVersion` says exactly **"Jarvis: 1 approval waiting"** and carries no title, summary or
   action name; a card that leaves `/api/pending` - answered here, on the PC, or expired - has its
   notification cancelled in the same `sync()` pass. Nothing secret (token, card detail, a
   stranger's words) is added; the text is still the desktop's `notice` and nothing composed on
   the phone.

**One consequence, said plainly.** A redacted notification - App lock on, "Hide memory lists and
chat history" on, or a phone whose own screen lock is not secure - offers **Review in Jarvis and
Deny, and no Approve**. Approving words the notification did not show is the blind approval rule 4
forbids, and the redaction itself is the owner's existing privacy rule (`SecurityRules
.notificationsLocked`, 2026-09-30), not something this feature weakens. **App lock defaults ON at
setup**, so the owner will see Review rather than Approve until he turns App lock off; the app's
Settings, Security row is where that choice lives.

### 177.2 The two Approve routes

- **Direct (`ACTION_APPROVE`, small read-only cards).** The action targets the app's own
  non-exported `EventService`. It waits briefly for a live link, re-reads the card from the live
  queue (with one direct `refreshPending()` if missing), re-checks `isSmall`, the owner's setting
  and the phone's current privacy state, and only then calls the existing
  `JarvisRuntime.decide(item, approve = true)` - the same POST the app makes, with the same stale
  and expiry rules. If any re-check fails it refuses and says "open Jarvis"; the notification is
  never the authority.
- **In-app (`InternalLaunch.APPROVE_ACTION`, everything else).** It opens `MainActivity` on the
  card and calls the same `approveItem` the card's Approve calls, with
  `fromNotification = true`, which forces `confirmed(force = true)` for non-small cards. The
  signed-approval path is unchanged, so a risky card with signed approvals on still signs with the
  key, and one with them off still shows the offer notice instead of approving.

Both routes carry `InternalLaunch`'s secret in the `PendingIntent`, and the in-app one is honoured
only on a fresh launch (not a rotation or a Recents replay). `notice.approve_ok` is still ignored:
the phone's own envelope decides, not the desktop's hint. **No backend change and no new route** -
both routes end at the existing `/api/approve`.

### 177.3 Where it lives

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `jarvis-client/app/src/main/java/com/jarvis/client/service/ApprovalNotificationPolicy.kt` | the pure policy: which buttons, the 240-character line, the unlock flags, the public words, the clear rule |
| `.../service/ApprovalNotifier.kt` | turns the policy into two actions, the redacted public version, and the cancel pass |
| `.../service/EventService.kt` | the direct small-card approve, re-checked against the live queue |
| `.../MainActivity.kt` | the proof-gated in-app approve: opens the card, forces the check, then the existing `decide` |
| `.../InternalLaunch.kt` | `APPROVE_ACTION` and the proof/freshness decision (`approvesApproval`) |

### 177.4 Tests, and what is not proved here

`ApprovalNotificationPolicyTest` (19 checks) holds the envelope on the JVM: Deny unlocked, every
Approve unlock-gated, small direct vs non-small in-app, the forced check for a write card that the
setting alone would skip, 240 vs 241 characters, locked means no Approve, PC-only and
plan-choice cards are Review, the exact public words, the cancel-on-clear rule, the proof rule, and
source pins that the notifier is private/redacted and the two approve routes re-check before
sending. `AppProjectsTest`, `NotificationStyleTest`, `MainActivityLaunchTest` and
`ApprovalDecisionTest` were updated to the new envelope; the other existing suites still pass. The
whole command is **3,223 tests, 0 failed, `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`**; the one pre-existing `main` failure
this branch inherited (`SettingsSearchTest`, after #1079 added the `edit-hud` row) was fixed by
#1089 and merged in, and is nothing this feature changed.

**NOT-TESTABLE without the owner's phone:** that Android really draws two actions in the collapsed
shade, that the lock screen shows the redacted sentence and refuses Approve until unlock, that the
system prompt appears after the in-app Approve on a real device, and that a tap on a direct Approve
reaches the PC over Tailscale after the process was killed. The desk check proves the compile and
the JVM rules only.

## 178. The skills menu: install, import, turn off, edit (added 2026-11-02)

The owner asked, in these words:

> "is jarvis fully compatible with hermes skills? if so, can we make a plug in
> menu where i can add or remove or change plug ins for hermes? only do research
> right now, no actual work"

The research was `.dsh-scratch/OWNER-QUEUE-2026-11-02/HERMES-SKILLS-RESEARCH.md`,
and the owner then chose its **scope B**: the PC's skills menu that installs
from a folder or a `.zip`, enables and disables a skill, edits one behind the
same card, and imports the skills already in `%USERPROFILE%\.hermes\skills` -
with **no marketplace** and nothing downloaded.

A "skill" was already a thing in Jarvis: a folder with a `SKILL.md` in it, whose
frontmatter and body say when the agent should read it (`backend/jarvis_skills.py`,
sections 135 and 138). What did not exist was any way to add one from an app.
`jarvis-skills`' own docstring said so: *"there is deliberately no route that
installs a skill, because installing runs the scanner and the approval gate on
the PC"* (the phone's `Skills.kt`). This section is that route - on the PC,
where the scanner and the card already live.

### 178.1 The module, and the folder that installs it

`backend/jarvis_skill_menu.py`, shipped whole by
`scripts/apply-patches.ps1`, and its five routes come from
`plugins/ready/skill-menu/` (`jarvis_skill_menu.install()`) - **no patch and no
edit to `jarvis_hud.py`**, the same shape `jarvis_skill_hub.py` uses.

It calls `jarvis_skills.py` for everything that matters and re-implements none
of it: `parse_skill`, `scan_text`, `vet`, `install`, `_quarantine`, the index,
and the `modify_own_code` card. One additive change was needed for the card's
words and is a patch of its own - `backend/skill-install-note.patch`:

- `install(..., note="")` puts ONE caller-written line on the same single card
  (the sentence in 178.4). With no `note` the card is byte-identical to before.
- `install()` now re-checks the card's **tier**, the way
  `jarvis_skills.refine()` already did. `jarvis_gate.check` returns
  `allowed=True` on `notify` ("you were told after") and `auto` (nobody in the
  loop), so before this a config that listed `modify_own_code` as `notify`
  would have installed a skill with no person asked. A skill IS instructions
  the agent will follow, so the card has to be a real card.

### 178.2 The five routes

| Route | What it does | Card |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/skills/menu` | every installed skill (verdict, trust, uses, `scripts/` count), every turned-off one, and whether `%USERPROFILE%\.hermes\skills` exists | none |
| `GET /api/skills/menu?name=<skill>` | ONE skill, plus its own `SKILL.md` text so the owner can read and edit it | none |
| `POST /api/skills/install` | `{"path"}` a folder or `.zip` on this PC, or `{"hermes"}` a folder the scan named; `"dry_run": true` stops after the scanner; `"accept_warnings"` for a warning-level skill | **ONE** `modify_own_code` card |
| `POST /api/skills/import/scan` | a READ-ONLY scan of `%USERPROFILE%\.hermes\skills`: every `SKILL.md`, its verdict, its `scripts/` count. Copies, moves and installs nothing | none |
| `POST /api/skills/state` | `{"name", "on"}`: off moves the folder to `skills-off\` and drops its index row; on runs the scanner and the card again. `{"name", "remove": true}` deletes ONE skill that is ALREADY turned off - the parked copy `uninstall` cannot see - and refuses an installed name | on: **ONE**; off and remove: none |
| `POST /api/skills/edit` | `{"name", "text"}`: the new `SKILL.md`, scanned and installed through the same path | **ONE** |

`GET /api/skills` (the list) and `POST /api/skills/decide` (removal, with its
"are you sure?") are unchanged and still the only routes both apps call: the
Settings menu's **Remove** calls the same `brain_remove_skill` command the
Brain already had, so there is one removal path, not two.

**Two objects, two doors, and never two doors to one folder** (2026-11-05).
`POST /api/skills/decide` remains the one removal for an INSTALLED skill.
What it could never reach is the copy this menu itself parked in `skills-off\`:
`jarvis_skills.uninstall` resolves a name only under the skills folder, so a
skill the owner switched off could be switched back on (one card) and never got
rid of - in either app, because the phone's Remove goes through the same route.
`{"name": "…", "remove": true}` on the state route deletes that one parked
folder and its row in `skills-off\.off.json`, with **no card**: it is already
out of the load path, so it only takes a capability away, the same rule that
makes turning one off immediate. It refuses an installed name outright (with the
sentence saying to use Remove), refuses `remove` and `on` in the same request,
and takes ONE name - there is no list form anywhere.

### 178.3 The safety model, in the order it happens

1. **The scanner runs first, on every source.** `parse_skill` + `vet` -
   the same regex-over-raw-bytes scanner, the same limits - run before any card
   exists. A `.zip` is unpacked into a throwaway folder first (below) and its
   contents are scanned exactly as a folder's would be.

   **The four shapes the base scanner does not cover run inside that same
   `vet()` scan (wired 2026-11-09).** `jarvis_skill_hub`'s four checks - the
   Hermes inline host-execution form `` !`command` ``, exfiltration said in
   words, "the approval is already approved" claims, and the bare-URL warning -
   are CALLED by `jarvis_skills.vet()` through `jarvis_skill_hub.extra_findings()`,
   so the install card, the menu's preview, the pack door and a project skill all
   judge the same shapes from the same regexes. Before this fix the four checks
   existed and were tested but were called by NOTHING in production, so a Hermes
   skill using the inline form installed as "clean". The report says
   `extra_checks: 1`, or `0` when an older base has no hub beside it - the layer
   did not run, said out loud rather than silently passed.
2. **A refusal never becomes a card.** A `refuse` verdict is copied into
   `skills-quarantine\` with its report and returns `{"asked": false}`. This is
   the point of the whole module: the attack these rules exist for works by
   producing a dialog that looks routine, so "may I install this?" for a
   curl-pipe-bash skill is the last step of the exploit, not a safeguard.
3. **A warning waits for a person.** A `review` verdict returns
   `{"needs": "accept_warnings"}` and raises no card; the same request again
   with `"accept_warnings": true` raises the ONE card. The page shows the
   warnings first, and asks "Install anyway?".
4. **ONE card, and one only.** `install()` is reached exactly once per request
   (`backend/test_skill_menu.py` counts the calls). Three skills are three
   cards: there is no "install all", no "import all" and no yes-to-all, because
   this project does not build bulk approval.
5. **The person must really answer.** The tier check in 178.1.
6. **The trust is not the client's to set.** A request that sent
   `{"trust": "local"}` is ignored: anything arriving through this route is
   `third_party`, the strictest level, because `local` scans less strictly
   (bundled scripts become a note, and a missing licence is not flagged).
7. **The `.zip` bounds are refusals, never truncations.** A member that is
   absolute, carries a drive letter, climbs with `..`, or is a symlink refuses
   the whole archive before it is written; the file count and total size are
   the skill's own (`MAX_FILES` 64, `MAX_SKILL_DIR` 5 MB). An archive with no
   `SKILL.md`, or with more than one, is refused with the count - guessing at
   which one the owner meant is not this route's business.
8. **A GitHub `.zip` works.** `my-skill-main/SKILL.md` whose frontmatter says
   `name: my-skill` is renamed in the throwaway copy to the name the frontmatter
   declares, and the same `parse_skill` checks the result. The spec's rule (the
   folder IS the name) is what makes a skill addressable, and it is not relaxed
   - only the archive's own folder name is.
9. **Nothing is downloaded, and nothing in a skill is run.** There is no
   marketplace, no catalogue to browse, no URL, and no socket: the module
   imports no network library and starts no process. A skill's `scripts/` is
   copied and never executed - by this route or by anything else in Jarvis.

### 178.4 The sentence on the card and on the row (Gemini's ruling 6)

Skills stay instructions-only, and Hermes skills that ship a `scripts/` folder
say so in the owner's words, on the install card and on the skill's row:

```
Imported SKILL.md instructions (N file(s) in scripts/ are kept inert and never
run automatically).
```

It is built in one place (`jarvis_skill_menu.INERT_SENTENCE`) and reaches the
card through `install(..., note=...)`, so the card and the row cannot drift -
`backend/test_skill_menu.py` and `jarvis-desktop/tests/skills-menu.mjs` both pin
the exact characters. A skill with no `scripts/` folder says nothing about one,
on purpose: a sentence that is always there stops being read.

What a Hermes skill does and does not get here: the format is the same
(agentskills.io - `name`, `description` and a Markdown body), so a Hermes folder
usually installs as it is. Hermes-only metadata (`platforms`,
`metadata.hermes.*` conditional activation, `required_environment_variables`) is
kept in the parsed skill's `extra_fields` and **does nothing** in Jarvis, which
has no OS gating and no toolset-conditional activation for skills. A skill that
relied on a bundled script for its behaviour loses that behaviour entirely -
which is the point of the sentence above, not a bug to work around.

### 178.5 What is NOT built

- **No marketplace and no remote install.** No ClawHub, no skills.sh, no
  GitHub fetch, no auto-install, no "browse skills". The three sources are: a
  folder on this PC, a `.zip` on this PC, and `%USERPROFILE%\.hermes\skills` if
  it is already there. Nothing opens a socket.
- **No phone install, turn-on or edit screen.** The phone keeps exactly what it
  had (`GET /api/skills` and Remove with its "are you sure?"). The five routes
  are classified `deliberate` in `tools/check_parity.py` and the reason is in
  `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8.
- **No phone delete of a TURNED-OFF skill.** That copy is a folder the PC's
  menu parked in `skills-off\`; the phone's list never shows it, and it gains
  no control for it - the same one-sidedness, recorded in
  `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8. The phone therefore removes an installed skill
  and nothing else.
- **No renaming.** An edit cannot change a skill's name: the frontmatter
  `name:` must still match the folder, which is what stops a skill from being
  addressed by a name it does not own. Renaming is a new install plus a
  removal.
- **No Hermes-metadata behaviour.** See 178.4.

### 178.6 What this slice cannot prove at the desk

The Settings card's two Windows dialogs (`src-tauri/src/folders.rs`'s
`What::SkillFolder` and `What::SkillZip`) are compiled and unit-tested but are
not driven here: no test opens a dialog. The owner's own click is the proof.
Everything else - the scanner, the refusal, the ONE card, the `.zip` bounds, the
Hermes scan against a fake folder, the off/on round trip, the edit, the routes'
origin and token checks - is driven against temp folders and a stub gate by
`backend/test_skill_menu.py`, and the page and the Rust are read for their
wiring by `jarvis-desktop/tests/skills-menu.mjs`.

## 179. The to-do list's own day: full daily rollover by default, and day by day as the other way (backend §21, both apps, added 2026-11-02)

The owner's question of 2026-11-02 ~00:20 PT, and his answer the same night
(`.dsh-scratch/OWNER-QUEUE-2026-11-02/OWNER-QUEUE.md` item 4): *is Jarvis smart
enough that, next day, "what's on my to-do list today" brings up yesterday's
unfinished items **while saying they are from yesterday**?* Measured against
`origin/main` before any change: the items DID carry over (they stay until done
or removed), but nothing said they were yesterday's - and the Today board's
`rollover_cards` had never been built. Asked which way he wanted it, he chose
**both**: *"To-do carry-over: build BOTH, with full daily rollover (option B) as
the DEFAULT, changeable by asking Jarvis or in Settings."* This is the todo
half of that; the decision is
`decisions.d/2026-11-02-todo-day-carryover.md`.

**THE ONE NEW FACT: `created_date`, and it never changes.** Every job row gains
`created_date` - the day it was written, `YYYY-MM-DD` in THIS PC's local time
(`jarvis_schedule._day_of`). A to-do item's whole age is measured from it, so
it is written ONCE, inside `Scheduler._insert`, and no later path writes it
again: not midnight, not an `edit`, not `done`, not the mode switch. That is
Gemini's ruling 8 (2026-11-02) and the reason it is a column rather than
arithmetic at read time: a rollover that stamped everything with "today" would
erase the very thing it is meant to show.

**MIGRATION, once, on the open that first finds the column missing.** Every row
with no `created_date` is backfilled from its own `created` stamp, in local
time; a legacy row whose stamp is missing or `0` is stamped **today** - the one
answer that never claims an age the data cannot support. It is idempotent (it
reads only `created_date IS NULL` rows and writes only those), it runs inside
the same `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` as the Phase 2 `ALTER TABLE`s, and after the first
open there is nothing NULL left to stamp.

**THE TWO WAYS OF SHOWING THE SAME LIST.** `todo_mode` is ONE value on the PC
(`meta['todo_mode']`, `Scheduler.todo_mode()`/`set_todo_mode()`), never a copy
per device, and the switch moves no item, copies nothing and re-stamps no day -
so toggling is lossless by construction and `created_date` is identical in both
modes.

- `"rollover"` - **the default**. Today's list is every open item written today
  or earlier, and each older one carries a tag built on the PC
  (`jarvis_schedule.carry_words`), handed out as the item's `carry` field:
  - 1 day old -> `from yesterday`
  - 2 to 6 days old -> `from <Weekday> (<N>d ago)`, e.g. `from Friday (3d ago)`
  - 7 or more days old -> `from <MMM D>`, e.g. `from Oct 26`

  A 3-day-old item therefore never says `from yesterday`: the wording is
  measured from `created_date`, never from "is it still on the list". An item
  written today grows **no** `carry` key at all.
- `"day"` - each item stays on the day it was written, grouped under that
  day's own heading (`Today`, `Yesterday`, `Friday (3d ago)`, `Oct 26`). The
  heading already names the day, so the rows do not repeat the tag.

**WHAT `GET /api/schedule` ADDS (all additive; an older app ignores them).**
`todo` is unchanged in both modes - the same flat list, in the PC's order - and
each to-do item gains `created_date` and, when it is older than today, `carry`.
The answer also carries `todo_mode` (`"rollover"`/`"day"`, read as rollover for
an older PC that sends nothing), `todo_modes` (the two modes in the PC's own
words, for both Settings controls: `{value, label, detail}`) and `todo_days`
(the same open items grouped by day: `{date, label, count, items}` with `items`
the ids of rows in `todo`, so no item is sent twice, today first).

**THE CHANGE: `POST /api/schedule/act` with `{"do": "todo_mode", "mode": ...}`.**
It rides the scheduler's ONE existing write route rather than opening a second
door - the same choice `clear_list` made, and the second form on that route
that is not one job (`Scheduler.handle_act` says so). No approval card either
way: it changes only how the owner's own list is drawn, and it touches no row.
400 in words for anything that is not one of the two modes; 200 carries
`{ok, mode, said, todo_modes}`, `said` being the PC's own sentence.

**THE SAME CHANGE BY ASKING.** `jarvis_settings_registry.py` gains the choice
