**The dry run names every path.** `GET /api/storage/cleanup/plan?categories=`
builds the exact list of absolute paths, bytes and per-category totals, one
single-use token good for 15 minutes, the quarantine folder a move would use,
and every candidate it refused with the reason. It writes nothing at all
(`plan_cleanup()`'s docstring and the tests). A plan of more than 60 items is
refused rather than summarised - "clear one category at a time" - because a card
that cannot list what it authorises is not a card. Only Python cache is planned
when no category is named: the other three are offered, never assumed.

**Nothing happens without ONE card.** `POST /api/storage/cleanup` builds a fresh
plan and raises ONE approval card under the action `storage_cleanup`, which is
tier `ask` in both shipped `jarvis-framework.toml` copies; any other tier is
refused with a `503` rather than obeyed. The card says, in full: every category
with its item count and bytes and a plain-words line about what it is; then
**"Exactly this, nothing else"** followed by one line per path - `delete <path>
(<size>)` or `move <path> -> <quarantine folder>` - and what saying no means
(*"A deleted file cannot be undone. Moved files are kept in the quarantine
folder above so you can put them back."*, *"Nothing of yours - no memory, chat
history, approvals, receipts or notes - is touched. If you say no, nothing
changes at all."*). One plan is in flight at a time (`409` while one waits). A
plan with nothing to clear raises no card and answers `200 nothing_to_clear` with
the refusals that stopped it.

**On a yes, the plan is carried out exactly as shown** (`apply_cleanup`). The
token must be the one the plan minted, single-use, and the categories must still
match; an expired plan is refused. Before touching each item it re-checks the
path (absolute, no `..`, inside the category's allowlisted roots, not a link,
the right shape for its category) and, for a deletion, that its file count, size
and newest time are exactly what was planned. **The first discrepancy stops the
whole run** and the result says where and what was already done. Python cache and
`%TEMP%` scratch files are DELETED; logs and old deploy snapshots are MOVED into
`_jarvis-quarantine-<yyyy-mm-dd>` beside the live program, never deleted. The
receipt is exact: `freed_bytes` counts only what was really deleted, `moved_bytes`
is reported separately because it is still on disk, `deleted` and `quarantined`
name every path (`quarantined[].moved_to` says where it went), `stopped_at` is
null on a clean run, and `message` is one plain sentence - "Done: 3 items
deleted, freeing 12.4 MB; 2 items moved into ... (still on disk)."

**What it refuses, before anything else.** `~/.openjarvis` (memory, chat history,
approvals, receipts, the voiceprint and projects), the Downloads folder, a
relative path, a path with a `..` step, a link or junction anywhere between the
root and the file, anything outside the allowlisted roots for its category, and
**any file the repository tracks in git** (read with `git ls-files`; when that
cannot be known it refuses with "Jarvis cannot prove this repository does not
track this file"). The live program's own files are on the same list. There is
no network, no socket, no elevation and no subprocess except that read-only
`git ls-files`, and `backend/test_storage_health.py` proves the user-data folder
is byte-identical before and after a cleanup.

**No app screen, said plainly.** Neither app draws a storage page and the HUD's
fixed read allowlist does not carry the storage routes; the model's tools are the
owner's door once they are wired (§184.10 says exactly what is and is not built
on the tree this was written from).

### 184.9 Refreshing its own abilities awareness

The owner's ask *"refresh its function and capabilities awareness"* is two small
pieces, and neither restarts anything.

**`POST /api/self/refresh`** (GET answers `405` with a sentence saying to use
POST) re-reads the inventory NOW: it clears the 20-second portrait cache and the
60-second installer-identity cache, rebuilds the portrait, compares the counts
before and after, and answers one small document
(`refresh()`):

```json
{"ok": true, "schema": "jarvis-self-portrait/1", "client": "hud",
 "counts": {"places": 190, "settings": 48,
            "tools": 13, "tools_enabled": 13, "tools_registered": 51,
            "asks_first_rows": 136,
            "abilities": 175, "plugins": 0, "settings_places": 59,
            "menu_places": 131,
            "stored_memory": 42, "stored_conversations": 31,
            "app_version": "...", "started_at": 1790000000.0},
 "changed": {"<key>": {"before": ..., "after": ...}},
 "said": "I re-read what I can do and have now: ... Everything matches what I
          had. Nothing was restarted."}
```

**`counts["tools"]` is the tool count, and it used to be a lie.** On the tree the
2026-11-04 self-awareness audit measured, `tools` held **136** - the number of
asks-first permission rows - and the model's own `self_portrait` tool handed that
dict straight back, so "how many tools do you have" could be answered "136" while
the backend had **51** tools and **13** switched on. Since 2026-11-04 the key holds
`tools_enabled` (the owner's `[tools].enabled`, read through
`jarvis_asks_first.tools_enabled_set()` - the same read the What-asks-first page
makes), with **`tools_registered`** beside it, and the old number kept under its
true name, **`asks_first_rows`**. The old key name still exists, so a caller that
only knows `tools` keeps working - it now gets the true number. An unreadable
settings file is `null` in both tool keys, never 0.

The sentence names every number it read, says "Nothing was restarted" in both
cases, and when something moved names each key that changed - a setting count, a
plugin, the version, a store's count. `started_at` is carried straight through,
so a reader can see it is the same process. **No card**, because it writes
nothing, changes no setting, reads nothing outside this PC and restarts nothing.
A refresh never touches a pending card or a store.

**The `refresh_abilities` chat tool** (`backend/jarvis_agent.py`'s `REFRESH_ABILITIES_TOOL` block,
its `_run_refresh_abilities`, and its `Tool(...)` definition) is the same thing by asking: no arguments, a
read-only tool that calls the refresh and hands its `said` sentence and counts
back. It is decided under the gate's existing `skill_list` action ("listing what
Jarvis can do", tier `auto`) exactly like `feature_guide`, so no new action, tier
or card wording is invented; it is in the `settings` tool group beside
`feature_guide` and `change_setting`, and it is NOT recorded as reading outside
text (nothing outside is read). Its own description says what it is not: not the
feature explainer, nothing restarted, nothing changed, no approval needed.
Whether it is OFFERED on a given PC is `[tools].enabled`'s business like every
other tool, and §184.10 says what the shipped list names on this tree.

### 184.10 What is not built, and what is not proved

- **The conversation tools: `conversation_find` and `conversation_open` ARE
  built** (read-only, under the gate's own `skill_list`, no card).
  `conversation_clear` is DELIBERATELY NOT a model tool (Gemini ruling 1,
  2026-11-03): an LLM must never have an autonomous tool to wipe the
  transcript, because an injected or hallucinated "clear that up for me" would
  delete chat history. Clearing stays the REST route (`POST
  /api/conversations/clear`), an app UI action, or the fast path - always
  behind its ONE `conversation_clear` card. The explainer and `open_area` from
  the first sketch are still NOT built; the portrait's routes and the existing
  `feature_guide` answer that side.
- **The storage routes have no chat tools and no app screen yet**, on the tree
  this was written from: `/api/storage/scan`, `/api/storage/cleanup/plan` and
  `/api/storage/cleanup` answer and are fully tested, but no `storage_scan`/
  `storage_cleanup` model tool is registered and neither app draws a storage
  page. The storage module itself carries the exact tool names its wiring
  worker is to add (`TOOL_ROWS`), and its card wording is already built; this
  section says what is real, not what is next.
- **`refresh_abilities` now ships ON in the shipped `[tools].enabled` list**
  (2026-11-04, Gemini's ruling Q2), beside `self_portrait`,
  `conversation_find`, `conversation_open`, `feature_guide`, `change_setting`,
  `plugin_list` and the rest. Before that date it was defined and grouped but
  left out of the list, so a PC with the shipped settings file had the POST
  route but not the tool by asking. An existing PC keeps its own list either
  way: an update never overwrites the owner's settings file, so the four reach
  a new install (or the owner's own file when they add the names).
- **The backend does not yet emit `open_area`.** Both apps accept it and the
  desktop's table can act on it; `resolve_place` is the hook with no caller yet
  (184.3).
- **No new event kind is added, and there is deliberately no stream listener
  for a navigation frame.** The contract is the per-answer route field; the
  desktop's `hud_nav.rs` header says plainly that a `ui.navigate` listener with
  no publisher would be "a doorbell into an empty room", so none is wired.
  If a navigation frame is ever added it must be label-filtered and ship with
  a real publisher and a client handler together (the F6 research's F5).
- **Not driven on hardware.** No real phone, no installed desktop app and no
  live backend were run for this section; the routes, the portrait, the card,
  the conversation adapters and the clear are proved by their suites, the
  desktop's navigation and window code by its own tests, and the phone's tables
  by JVM tests. What is proved is code and tests, not a field test.

### 184.11 Both apps, the one-sided parts, and the tests

| Piece | Desktop | Phone | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/api/self`, `/api/self/version`, `/api/conversations` | **reachable from the page on this tree** - `hud_proxy.rs` carries all three (`HUD_GET_PATHS` has 14 paths, `/api/self` among them, landed by the desktop's own PR #1115). The version STRING is also read by the shell's version handshake, not only the page | can read them like any route; the phone has no self screen | it is a read; both apps' chats already reach the PC |
| "Open a place" | `hud_nav.rs` table + `open_jarvis_area` | `OpenPlace` table + the one-time settings request | same field, each app's own surfaces |
| More than one conversation window | **desktop only** - the extra `chat-*` windows | one screen at a time | recorded in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8 |
| Clearing one conversation | the card is answered in any window (Windows Hello where the gate asks) | the card is answered on Home like any card; its History delete keeps its own confirm | one action, one decision, everywhere |
| The version handshake / Update | **desktop only** | none | a phone cannot patch this PC's backend (the existing one-sided decision, ARCHITECTURE section 8) |
| Storage scan and cleanup (184.8) | **no screen, no tool on this tree** | **no screen, no tool on this tree** | the routes and the ONE card are built and tested; the door is the model tool the wiring worker adds, never a client-side clear |
| Refreshing the abilities (184.9) | the `refresh_abilities` tool in either app's chat - it is in the shipped `[tools].enabled` since 2026-11-04, and an existing settings file keeps whatever it had; `POST /api/self/refresh` is a route both apps may call | same | one read of this PC's own modules; no card and nothing restarted |

**Tests.** `backend/test_self_portrait.py` (added with the module; it is what
holds the portrait to the two registries, the settings' live values, the refresh
endpoint and its sentence, the clear card's four phases, the adapters'
one-truth rule, the fail-closed tier, the "a cleared chat does not forget a
fact" proof, and the never-in-it list), `backend/test_storage_health.py` (the
bounded scan, every refusal, the plan's token and expiry, the ONE card, the
re-check that stops a changed item, the delete-vs-quarantine split, the freed
bytes, and the user-data folder byte-identical before and after),
`backend/test_asks_first.py` and the shipped-whole twin checks
(`backend/test_base_matches_repo.py`, `backend/test_base_regeneration.py`,
`tools/check_stale_twins.py`) for the new modules and their `jarvis-backend/`
copies; the desktop's `cargo test` unit tests in `hud_nav.rs`, `chat_windows.rs`
and `backend_self.rs`; the phone's `OpenPlaceTest`, `OpenPlaceAreasTest` and
`ConversationClearTest`. The two
checkers named by the parity rule do NOT classify nothing: `tools/check_parity.py`
classifies the three read routes in `CLASSIFICATION` - `/api/self` as `todo`, and
`/api/self/version` and `/api/conversations` as `deliberate`, because the
desktop calls all three - and adds **six `BACKEND_ONLY` entries** for the rest of
this feature: `/api/self/refresh`, `/api/conversations/{id}`,
`/api/conversations/clear`, and the storage self-scan's `/api/storage/scan`,
`/api/storage/cleanup/plan`, `/api/storage/cleanup` - each carrying its
follow-up lane in the reason, because neither app calls any of them on this
tree. `tools/check_event_names.py`
classifies nothing new because no event kind is added (navigation stays on the
existing per-answer `X-Jarvis-Route` field). **No `features/features.json` entry
is added by this work** - that row is still waiting on the app lanes; the PR
says exactly what each checker reported.

## 185. Jarvis measures its own token speed: one run, two rates, and its own history (backend phase 1, added 2026-11-04)

The owner's ask of 2026-11-04: measure Jarvis's own token speed across the
local models, the RAM/GPU layer placement and the context sizes, keep a
**separate** history of those runs, and explain the results in plain words.
This section is phase 1 of the design in
`.dsh-scratch/BENCHMARK-2026-11-04/DESIGN.md` - the measurement engine and its
store, with **no screens yet**. `backend/jarvis_bench.py` (shipped whole, and
its `jarvis-backend/` twin) does the work; `backend/bench.patch` is the five
route branches in `jarvis_hud.py` that reach it, and it holds no logic of its
own.

**ONE RUN = one model + one setup + N repeats + one target lane.** A repeat
asks Ollama one question, reads Ollama's own counters out of the reply, samples
both graphics cards, and writes ONE row; the run then writes a second row with
the setup and the median/min/max over its repeats. Every row goes to
`~/.openjarvis/bench.jsonl` - a NEW file with its own allowlist, its own 500-run
cap and a 2 MB ceiling. **`speed.jsonl` is never opened**: that file's promise
is that rows are never deleted or rewritten, and this feature has a DELETE in a
later phase, so mixing them would widen the allowlist that currently guarantees
no conversation text can be written and would overload `speed.jsonl`'s
`view()`.

| Route | What it is |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/bench` | the controls screen's whole data: the defaults, the ladders the snapping controls snap to, each lane with the card it really is and what that lane has installed, the two cards and the driver from `nvidia-smi`, whether Jarvis is on standby, whether a run is in flight, and the last run. **Read-only: it starts and loads nothing.** `?model=` adds that model's `block_count` and trained `context_length`, which is one `/api/show` round trip and is paid only when a model is picked |
| `POST /api/bench/run` | start ONE run. Body `{model, lane, num_ctx, num_gpu, num_predict, prefill_tokens, repeats, warmup, unload, confirm: {model, lane, may_evict: true}}`. **No approval card, and `confirm` is mandatory** (below). Asynchronous: it spawns and returns 200 `{ok, run_id, notes}`, so a two-minute run cannot hang a request thread |
| `GET /api/bench/run/<id>` | how the run is going, and its numbers when it is done: `200 {state: running\|done\|failed, step, of, partial, result?}`; `404` when no run has that id |
| `POST /api/bench/cancel` | `{run_id}` - stop after the repeat in flight. The repeat already running is **not** killed: a request cut off mid-answer leaves Ollama's counters unusable, and half a measured repeat is not a number. `409` when that run has already finished |
| `GET /api/bench/history` | the run rows, newest first. `?limit=&model=&lane=&preset=`; a filter is an **exact** match on the stored name, because a fuzzy one would let a screen say `qwen3.5:9b` and mean `qwen3.5:4b`. `{runs, total, note}`, and `note` is always a sentence - "No benchmark runs on file yet." and "No benchmark runs match that filter." are different facts |

Status codes follow the house style `hardware.patch` already uses: `200` ok,
`400` bad body or missing `confirm`, `401` bad token, `403` cross-origin, `409`
refused with a sentence, `503` could not start.

**WHAT A RUN REFUSES, and why each one is a sentence rather than a silent no.**
A benchmark started while something else is using the model measures the
QUEUE, not the model. In this order:

```
409  a benchmark is already running; it takes a minute or two
409  Jarvis is answering. Measuring now would time the queue, not the model.
409  Jarvis is on standby, which keeps the graphics card free; measuring would
     load a model onto it. Wake Jarvis first
409  a task is running; it uses the model, so the benchmark would time the
     queue instead of the model
409  the <lane> lane is not running; start it first
409  <model> is not installed on the <lane> lane. It has: <what is>
400  Nothing was measured: Ollama's address (<base>) is not this PC, and a
     benchmark only talks to this PC.
400  nothing was measured: the run was not confirmed
```

**The lane is never started as a side effect.** If the chosen lane's Ollama is
not running the run is refused; the only thing in Jarvis that starts a lane
stays a preset apply (`jarvis_presets.APPLY_ACTION`). **"Jarvis is answering"
is already wired to the real chat path without a patch hunk inside the chat
handler**: the check asks `jarvis_power_switch._busy_reason()`, which reads the
HUD's own activity state - `_activity("speaking")` when the first chunk goes
out, `_activity("working")` during a tool call, `_activity("idle")` at the end -
the same signal both apps already show the owner. A module flag
(`jarvis_bench.note_answer_start()`) makes the same refusal reachable exactly
from a caller that knows it is about to stream.

**NO APPROVAL CARD, AND THAT IS THE RECORDED DECISION** (DESIGN section 7):
`POST /api/hardware/measure` already runs with no card, for the stated reason
that it "runs one short prompt per model on this PC and changes no setting", and
here the owner pressing Measure is the actor - a card would ask him to approve
his own button press. What a card would have bought is bought explicitly
instead: the POST must carry `confirm: {model, lane, may_evict: true}`, and the
UI fills it only after naming exactly what will happen. A `confirm` that names a
different model or lane than the body is **not** a confirmation of this run and
is refused too, so a stale screen cannot start a run nobody agreed to. Nothing
is auto-approved and rule 4 is untouched.

**THE PREFILL TRAP, WHICH IS THE REASON THIS FEATURE NEEDS ITS OWN FORMULA.**
`prompt_eval_duration` times only the prompt tokens Ollama actually COMPUTED,
while `prompt_eval_count` counts the WHOLE prompt including the part it read
from its cache. So prompt speed is **always**

```
(prompt_eval_count - prompt_eval_cached_count) / (prompt_eval_duration / 1e9)
```

and never `prompt_eval_count / prompt_eval_duration`. The measured example
(Ollama 0.34.0, `qwen2.5:7b`, RESEARCH section 3.1): 318 prompt tokens, **317 of
them cached**, 23.00 ms of evaluation. The naive division reports **13,826
tokens a second**; the model really read one token in 23 ms, which is **43** - a
318x lie built from two numbers that are each individually correct. Two more
rules follow and both are stored: when `cached == count` there is nothing left
to time, so the row says **"cached - prefill not measured"** and never `0` and
never infinity; and when `prompt_eval_cached_count` is absent (Ollama before
0.33.3) the answer is **unknown, never 0**, because defaulting it to zero turns
"I do not know" into a confident, too-high number. `jarvis_speed.timing_from_reply()`
is deliberately **not** reused for this: its `first_word_ms` is
`load_duration + prompt_eval_duration`, i.e. the UNCACHED prefill time, which
under-reports time-to-first-token whenever part of the prompt was cached.

**THE REST OF WHAT IS REPORTED**, all on the row and all from something that
measured it: generation as `eval_count / eval_duration`; **two**
time-to-first-token numbers - the harness's own wall clock from POST to the
first streamed chunk (the one the owner waited), and Ollama's
`load_duration + prompt_eval_duration` - with the row saying so when they
disagree by more than 15%; `total_ms` and Ollama's `total_duration`; VRAM peak
and base **per card** from `nvidia-smi` (`memory.used` sampled before, after
every repeat and at the end) and `utilization.gpu`; the context really in use
from `/api/ps` `context_length`, recorded **beside** the one that was asked for
because they are not always the same; the model's `block_count` read from
`/api/show`; and the offload from **two independent sources** - `/api/ps`
`size` vs `size_vram` (`on_card_percent`) and `offloaded N/M layers to GPU`
through `jarvis_hardware.parse_ollama_log`, which already had that parser and is
not re-implemented here. When the two disagree **both are kept**. Per-process
VRAM is not claimed at all: `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps used_memory`
answers `[N/A]` for every process on driver 617.42, so the row says "card 0 rose
by X MB while this ran" and never "this model used X MB".

**A SPILLED RUN IS LABELLED AND IS NEVER PRESENTED AS FAST.** When any of the
model was off the card the run's one sentence opens with `PARTIAL:` and says the
numbers are not comparable with a fully-on-card run, and the setup is described
as what was **asked for** rather than as what happened - "32 of 32 layers on the
card" beside "only 93% of it was in video memory" would be a sentence that
contradicts itself, with no way for a reader to tell which half is the
measurement. **A run that could not measure writes `ok: false` with a `why`
sentence and never a zero**: there is no silent gap, because the next reader
cannot tell a gap from a run that was never started. `ollama_version` and
`driver_version` go on every row - this PC's driver has already moved once
(616.56 to 617.42) and a tok/s number without them is not comparable to
anything.

**THE ROWS ARE TWO FLAT KINDS, with the same allowlist discipline as
`jarvis_speed._clean()`**: `kind: "bench"` is one repeat and `kind:
"bench-run"` is one run with its setup, its medians, `spilled`,
`worst_repeat_ok`, and `words` - the one sentence both apps display, built in
the engine so the desktop and the phone cannot word the same result two
different ways. **No prompt text is ever stored**: the prefill prompt is
generated from a fixed, counted word list with a per-repeat tag **at the front**
- Ollama serves the LONGEST COMMON PREFIX from its cache, so a tag at the tail
would leave the whole word body cacheable and every repeat after the first
would measure the tail instead of the depth - and it is thrown away; what is
stored is how many tokens Ollama said it really counted. The
allowlist is why `{"prompt": ...}` handed in by a caller that made a mistake is
dropped rather than written.

**THE ADVICE SENTENCE IS BUILT AND TESTED, AND IT IS NOT REACHABLE YET.**
`jarvis_bench.advice()` returns `{note, numbers, enough}` from `bench.jsonl` and
nothing else - it cannot run a benchmark, delete a row, or reach the network.
**There is no route for it on this tree**: `/api/bench/advice` does not exist in
`backend/bench.patch`, there is no `benchmark_results` chat tool and no app
draws an "Explain this result" button; the only caller in this repository is
`backend/test_bench.py`, and `tools/check_parity.py`'s bench block says so
beside the five routes that DO exist. **Under three usable runs of a model it
refuses to compare**, with "Only 2
runs of that model are on file; three are needed before I compare them" - the
same floor `jarvis_speed.compare_latency()` refuses under, because two lists of
two can differ by 40% from noise alone. At three it names the fastest and the
fastest that did not spill, and a comparison that spans a driver or Ollama
version change says so rather than quietly mixing two machines into one
verdict.

**WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED YET, and this is not an accident.** The routes
of DESIGN section 6 that phase 1 does **not** wire are `/api/bench/history/{id}`
and its DELETE (the separate History window, phase 3), `/api/bench/presets`
(two routes - benchmark presets are phase 4), `/api/bench/advice` (phase 4) and
the read-only `benchmark_results` chat tool (phase 4). The desktop Benchmark
panel is phase 2 and the phone's `BenchScreen`/`BenchHistoryScreen` are phase 5.
**The five routes that DO exist are the ones `tools/check_parity.py` carries in
`BACKEND_ONLY`**, with the lane named in each reason, because neither app calls
any of them on this tree - a state that check FAILS the day an app starts
calling one, which is the point of putting it there. **The routes above do not
exist yet, so the checker classifies none of them**: an entry there would name a
route the backend does not serve. **Nothing here has been measured on real
hardware**: `backend/test_bench.py` drives every formula and every refusal from
a fake Ollama reply and fake `nvidia-smi` text, and one real run is a field
test, not a test (DESIGN section 12) - a CI runner has no cards and no models,
so those rows are BLOCKED, never PASS.

**PROVED BY** `backend/test_bench.py`: 253 checks, 0 failed - every refusal row
of DESIGN section 2 with its exact sentence, the 318x trap (a reply of 318/317/
23 ms must yield 43.48 and must NOT yield 13,826), the fully-cached case, absent
is not zero, generation rate against a literal, both time-to-first-token
numbers, the median/spread/warmup-drop pure functions, a run that is not fully
on the card (its sentence leads with `PARTIAL:`), a failed run that writes
`ok: false` + `why` and no zero, the store's append/tail/filters/get/delete, the
500-run cap keeping whole runs, the byte ceiling, the allowlist, the
three-run comparison floor, and that no run can start without `confirm`.

**Two guards were added on 2026-11-04, and each failed before its fix:** the
prefill prompt's per-repeat tag now leads, so two repeats at one depth share no
word of prefix and 25 characters out of 3,690 (before: 512 of 518 words,
3,653 characters - a tail measurement), and `lane` is dropped when it is not one
of the three, because it used to sit in both the text-field and the enum table
and the text-field branch won ("everyday lane" was stored as "everyday lan").


**ALL LAYERS MEANS EVERY LAYER, AND THE REFUSAL NAMES WHAT HELD IT (2026-11-06).**
Two measured corrections from the same morning. (1) `num_gpu` counts the layers
kept on the graphics card and the OUTPUT layer is offloadable too, so "all of
them" is `block_count + 1`, not `block_count`: measured on the live 11436 lane
with qwen3.5:9b (block_count 32), `num_gpu: 32` loaded 5.12 GB of 6.13 GB
(83.6% on card) while 33, 34, 40 and 99 all loaded 5.49 GB of 5.49 GB (100%).
A `null`/omitted `num_gpu` now resolves to `block_count + 1`, and an explicit
larger value is clamped to the same number with a note saying every layer is
requested - so a 100% on-card baseline is reachable at all. The control the
screen draws keeps its range, and the stored rows are unchanged. (2) A finished
chat turn could leave the event bus saying "thinking" (a `jarvis_quick`
fast-path answer returned before `/api/chat`'s own idle write), and
`POST /api/bench/run` then refused with "Jarvis is answering" for over four
hours - the only cure was a restart. The activity mark now has a five-minute
lease: a busy state with no progress (no streamed chunk, no tool step) for
`jarvis_events.ACTIVITY_STALE_SECONDS` is auto-cleared with ONE structured
warning, every `/api/chat` exit resets it in a `finally`, and the boot sequence
resets it explicitly. The 409 body gains `busy_reason` and `activity_age_s`, and
`GET /api/status` gains `activity`, `activity_age_s` and `busy_reason` - all
additive, so a client that ignores them behaves exactly as before, and a stuck
turn is visible from the API instead of from the source.


## 186. Watchers that earn the right to interrupt: `observe` mode, one batch per pull request, and the durable outbox (added 2026-11-04)

A watcher that speaks about everything gets muted. That is the whole of this
section. Three patterns from `deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype` (MIT) were
adopted on the owner's decision of 2026-11-04 - *"implement Part II patterns 1,
2, 3 and 5B ... natively in Python"* - because they are the mechanisms that stop
a GitHub watcher becoming noise, and because the same slice can close a defect
this project already had: **a backend restart lost a pending approval card**
(the job row survived; the event that told the apps about it did not).

Three modules and one drop-in folder carry it:

| Piece | File | What it is |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| stage one, pure | `backend/jarvis_watch_policy.py` | `gate()`: which checks are required, one batch per (pr, head_sha), the settle rules. Imports nothing from Jarvis - no disk, no network, no model. |
| the watcher | `backend/jarvis_watch_ci.py` | poll `gh`, fold the seven checks into one thread, log a decision row (`observe`) or notify (`active`), the decisions ring buffer, `watch-receipts.json`, the job body `watch_pr_checks`. |
| the record | `backend/jarvis_outbox.py` | what is still owed to the owner, written to `outbox.json` BEFORE it is said, re-announced on startup. |
| the route | `plugins/ready/watch-decisions/` | calls `jarvis_watch_ci.install()` for the one GET below. No patch: `jarvis_hud.py` is not shipped, and a route there would need a hunk in its dispatch tuple. |

### 186.1 The three modes, and why the middle one is the default

`WATCH_MODES = ("off", "observe", "active")` (`backend/jarvis_watch.py`).

- **`off`** - nothing is polled, nothing is recorded. This is what "no watcher"
  means, and it is the state of a machine that has never created a
  `watch_pr_checks` job.
- **`observe`** - the WHOLE pipeline runs: poll, batch, gate, and (only for a
  failed required check) the second stage. Nothing interrupts. One decision row
  is written instead, saying exactly what would have been said.
- **`active`** - the same pipeline, and a terminal verdict is delivered.

**A new proactive rule defaults to `observe`.** The setting is
`[watch] pr_checks_mode` in the owner's settings file, and an absent,
unreadable or misspelt value reads as `observe` - never as `active`, because a
typo in a settings file must not turn a shadow watcher into one that speaks.
Promotion is the owner's own edit once the log below has no noise in it; there
is no route that promotes it, and nothing here auto-promotes.

**Nothing becomes always-on.** `jarvis_watch_ci.py` registers a job body and
answers a route; it starts no thread, no timer and no polling of its own. The
watcher looks at a pull request only when a `watch_pr_checks` job names one,
created through the existing `POST /api/jobs`.

### 186.2 `GET /api/watch/decisions?limit=50`

The read that makes `observe` worth having: *"what would your GitHub watcher
have told me today?"* Newest first, `limit` clamped to 1..200 (default 50,
anything that is not a whole number is treated as 50 rather than refused - this
is a read). Origin and token checked exactly like every other route.

```json
{"available": true, "mode": "observe",
 "modes": ["off", "observe", "active"],
 "required_jobs": ["rust", "frontend", "backend", "backend-windows",
                   "credential-manager", "powershell-5", "phone-unit-tests"],
 "informational_jobs": ["audit", "python-advisories"],
 "count": 2,
 "decisions": [
   {"id": 2, "at": 1762300000.0, "source": "github_pr_ci",
    "thread_key": "pr:1135:a1b2c3d4e", "outcome": "would_notify",
    "reason_code": "ci_all_required_green", "verdict": "all_green",
    "mode": "observe", "shadow_reason_code": "observe_shadow_logged",
    "delivery": "shadow", "receipt_key": "1135:a1b2c3d4e...:all_green",
    "preview_text": "PR #1135 is green: all 7 required checks passed and GitHub says it is mergeable (a1b2c3d4e)."},
   {"id": 1, "at": 1762299000.0, "source": "github_pr_ci",
    "thread_key": "pr:1135:a1b2c3d4e", "outcome": "ignored",
    "reason_code": "ci_still_running_debounced", "verdict": "running",
    "mode": "observe", "shadow_reason_code": "", "delivery": "shadow",
    "preview_text": "PR #1135: 3 of 7 required checks finished, none failed - staying quiet until it settles (a1b2c3d4e)."}],
 "reasons": {"ci_all_required_green": "All 7 required checks passed and the PR is mergeable", "...": "..."}}
```

Every row carries `at`, `source`, `thread_key`, `outcome`, `reason_code` and
`preview_text`; the rest is for reading the log later.

- `source` is one of `github_pr_ci`, `github_notifications`, `repo_check`, `github-watch-repos` (the per-repository watcher, 2026-11-07).
- A **per-repository watch** (2026-11-07) writes the same row shape with
  `source` = `github-watch-repos` and `thread_key` `repo:<owner/name>` (or
  `follow:<topic>` for a followed topic). Its `reason_code` is one of
  `repo_new_release`, `repo_new_commit`, `repo_new_issue`, `repo_new_pr`,
  `repo_ci_changed`, `repo_new_repo`, `repo_observe_shadow`,
  `repo_frequency_off`, `repo_digest_due`, `repo_instant_due`,
  `repo_baseline`, `repo_poll_skipped` or `repo_unauthenticated_public` - every
  one of them a key of the same closed `WATCH_REASONS` set. `mode` is the
  watch's cadence (`instant`, `daily`, `weekly`, `off`) or `observe`; the extra
  `repo`, `freq` and `url` fields are for reading the log later. These rows are
  written by the same store this route already serves, so no new route was
  added: `GET /api/watch/repos` does not exist, and the watch itself is
  controlled from chat or Live (`backend/test_watch_repos.py`). The repeating half is the SCHEDULER's, not a new route either: starting a watch calls `Scheduler.add_repeat` for the scheduler kind `repo_watch`, so the row appears in the existing schedule list (`GET /api/schedule`), its ONE `schedule_repeat` card is the approval, and `DELETE`-equivalent scheduler act removes it with the watch.
- `thread_key` is the batch: `pr:<number>:<head sha[:9]>` for a pull request,
  `notification:<id>`, `repo:<name>`.
- `outcome` is `would_notify` (worth telling him), `ignored` (the batch rule
  dropped it) or `notified` (active mode, and it was delivered).
- `reason_code` is a CLOSED set, `WATCH_REASONS` in `backend/jarvis_watch.py`:
  `ci_all_required_green`, `ci_required_failed`, `ci_still_running_debounced`,
  `ci_green_not_mergeable`, `ci_no_required_checks`, `duplicate_sha_state`,
  `observe_shadow_logged`, `filtered_bot_actor`, `notification_for_you`,
  `attention_budget_dropped`, `repo_check_clean`, `repo_check_failed`,
  `watch_off`, `source_not_allowed`, `unreadable_trigger`. A client that does not
  know a new code must fall back to showing `preview_text`, which is always a
  whole sentence in the owner's words.
- `preview_text` is the EXACT one-line message that was, or would have been,
  shown. Never more than one line: a `\n` in it is a bug, and the suite says so.
- In `observe` mode a `would_notify` row also carries
  `shadow_reason_code: "observe_shadow_logged"` - the reason code that says
  "written down instead of delivered". `reason_code` still names the verdict, so
  the log answers both questions at once.
- `delivery` is `shadow` (observe), `sent`, `dropped` (the interruption budget
  said no - the arbiter's own decision, `§123.4`), `failed` (the notifier raised;
  the outbox is still holding it) or `already`.

The buffer holds the newest 500 rows in `watch-decisions.json`, written
temp-file-then-rename, so a crash leaves the previous whole file.

### 186.3 One batch per pull request, and the seven that matter

A pull request runs **seven** checks that gate a merge - `rust`, `frontend`,
`backend`, `backend-windows`, `credential-manager`, `powershell-5`,
`phone-unit-tests` - plus `audit` and `python-advisories`, which are
**informational**. The seven were read from the repository ruleset itself; the
two informational ones are red on `main` regularly and merges still land, which
is what "informational" means. They finish minutes apart (`rust` in about three,
`frontend` in five, `backend` in fifty-five to sixty), so:

- `thread_key = f"pr:{number}:{head_sha[:9]}"` - ONE thread per commit. A new
  push is a new thread, a new batch and a new receipt.
- **fail fast**: any required check whose conclusion is `FAILURE`,
  `TIMED_OUT` or `ACTION_REQUIRED` speaks ONCE, immediately. So does any other
  terminal non-`SUCCESS` (`CANCELLED`, `STALE`, `NEUTRAL`, `SKIPPED`) - a
  required check that ended without passing would otherwise hold the batch open
  for ever, and on a protected branch it blocks the merge.
- **settle green**: all seven `SUCCESS` *and* `mergeable == "MERGEABLE"` speaks
  ONCE. All seven green with `CONFLICTING`/`UNKNOWN` is its own sentence
  (`ci_green_not_mergeable`), because green is not mergeable.
- **quiet while it works**: any required check still running, none failed ->
  `ci_still_running_debounced`, and NOTHING is delivered however many times it
  is polled.
- **`audit` and `python-advisories` never trigger a notification.** They are
  dropped by name before any count is taken, so a red `audit` on a green pull
  request produces `ci_all_required_green` and one quiet line.

**Idempotent receipts** (`watch-receipts.json`, newest 2000) are keyed
`(pr_number, head_sha, terminal_verdict)`. A terminal verdict is recorded once -
in `observe` mode too, so promoting a watcher later cannot re-report a commit
that is already finished - and every later poll of that commit answers
`duplicate_sha_state` and delivers nothing. The verdict is part of the key on
purpose: a commit that fails `rust`, is re-run and settles green owes the owner
two different sentences.

### 186.4 The two-stage gate, and what may never reach stage two

1. **`gate(trigger, thread)`** - pure. Allowlists, required-vs-informational
   names, receipts, settle rules, bot filtering. No disk, no network, no model,
   no clock: `now` is an argument. `backend/test_watch_ci.py` parses its imports
   and fails if one of them could reach anything.
2. **`assess()`** - reached ONLY when the gate admits a terminal failure of a
   REQUIRED check. It reads the failing run's own log through the same
   deterministic `gh` path the poll uses (the run id is taken from the check's
   own details URL, never guessed) and formats the one line. A filtered event, a
   duplicate, an informational check, a bot notification and a quiet batch never
   reach it, and the suite proves that with a counter that must stay at zero.

**No model is called on this PC by this slice, said plainly.**
`assess_failure()` has a `summarizer` seam and nothing passes one: the line is
built by plain string work over the log. So this is 0 GPU today, and the seam is
where a local-model summary would go if that is ever wanted.

### 186.5 The durable outbox, and what a restart owes (pattern 5B)

`backend/jarvis_outbox.py` holds what Jarvis still owes the owner, in
`outbox.json` beside `jobs.db` (`JARVIS_OUTBOX_PATH` overrides it; the path is
resolved on each call so a moved queue moves it). Three kinds, and the kind is
part of the dedupe key:

| kind | key | settled by |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `job_card` | `job:<id>:grant:<action>` | being ANSWERED: `answer()`, `_stop_denied()`, `cancel()` |
| `job_done` | `job:<id>:<state>` | being delivered |
| `pr_ci_notice` | `<thread_key>:<verdict>` | being delivered (or dropped by the arbiter) |

The order is the guarantee, and it is the same everywhere: **write it down, then
record the receipt, then deliver, then settle.** A crash after the write leaves a
pending entry that the next start re-announces; a crash after the receipt cannot
cause a second report. The file is written to a temp name, flushed and renamed,
so a reader never sees half of one.

On startup `jarvis_jobs._init()` re-hydrates, once per process:
parked jobs with a pending grant get their `job_card` entry back (the ROW is the
authority, so this also covers a card from a build with no outbox), then every
pending entry is announced once. That is what closes the restart card loss: the
card is re-announced, and it is still the owner's to answer - rehydration
APPROVES NOTHING, and `decide_grant()` remains the only thing that decides a
grant. A cancelled job's card is settled by the cancel (the owner already
answered), and a cancelled job gets no completion notice, because telling
somebody about the interruption they asked to stop is the interruption.

**The honest limit: this is at-least-once, not exactly-once.** A process that
dies between the send and the settle repeats ONE notice on the next start. It
cannot do the opposite - an entry that exists is an entry somebody will be told
about - because the write comes first. Given one repeated notice or one lost
approval card, this takes the repeat.

Settled entries are pruned back to 500; a pending one is never dropped, however
old, because dropping it is the defect this module exists to prevent.

### 186.6 Tests

`backend/test_watch_ci.py` (139 checks) and `backend/test_outbox.py` (63), both
plain Python with a fake clock, a fake `gh` runner and temp files - no network,
no `gh`, no model. Between them: observe-vs-active (including that observe calls
the notifier ZERO times), the quiet period, fail fast, the all-green settle,
informational checks ignored, duplicate-receipt silence, a new push being a new
thread, a fixed failure then green owing two sentences, `gate` never calling
`assess` for a filtered event, a crash between the write and the send being
delivered exactly once afterwards, a restart re-announcing an unanswered card
once and not repeating a delivered notice, and the route's own wrapper.

### 186.7 What is NOT built, and said plainly

- **No app screen for this route yet.** It is read on the PC while the mode is
  being decided; `tools/check_parity.py` classifies it `BACKEND_ONLY` with that
  reason, and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 carries the one-sided row. When a screen
  is built it goes on BOTH apps.
- **No promotion route and no auto-promotion.** The mode is the owner's settings
  file.
- **No push, merge, label or comment.** This watcher reads; the only writes it
  can make are its own three files and the notification it hands to the arbiter.
- **The second stage never calls a model today** (§186.4).
- **Not measured on the owner's PC**: the route and the job body are tested
  against the real modules and a fake `gh`, not against a live pull request.---

## 187. Talking to Jarvis about any of its own tools, in depth: a dossier answer and a bounded prompt block (added 2026-11-04)

The owner's ask of 2026-11-04, in his own words: Jarvis should be able to hold
*"FULL DETAILED discussions about any of its tools/plug-ins and how they change
its real-world capabilities"*. Before this, "tell me about the github tool" fell
through to the model, which invented an answer, and "what does browser_control
do" was answered by `jarvis_feature_guide`'s prose for a *different* thing - the
catalogue does not use the tool names.

What was built is ONE hand-written, code-checked page per tool and per
capability family (`backend/jarvis_tool_profiles.py`), plus a deterministic
answer and a bounded system note that put it in front of the model. **No new
route and no new model tool** - both are explained in 186.3.

**Where the dossiers live.** `backend/jarvis_tool_profiles.py`, shipped whole
(in `backend/` and `jarvis-backend/`, listed in `_where.py`'s `SHIPPED`):
`PROFILES` (`jarvis_tool_profiles.py:82`, one entry per name in the REAL
`jarvis_agent.TOOLS` dict - 51 on this tree) and `FAMILIES`
(`jarvis_tool_profiles.py:1820`, 11 capability families). Its own suite,
`backend/test_tool_profiles.py`, re-checks the load-bearing claims against the
modules that would have to implement them, so a sentence that cannot be backed
is written as a limit rather than as a promise. The wiring is
`backend/test_tool_profiles_chat.py`.

### 187.1 What it answers, and what it still leaves to the model

The fast path answers a sentence that names a tool **as a tool** - the word
"tool", or the tool's own code name typed with its underscore:

| The owner says | Intent | The fact comes from |
|---|---|---|
| "what does `browser_control` do" | `tool_profile` | `PROFILES["browser_control"]` |
| "tell me about the github tool" | `tool_profile` | `PROFILES["github_search"]` |
| "what does the web search tool do" | `tool_profile` | `PROFILES["web_search"]` |
| "tell me about the memory tool" | `tool_profile` | `FAMILIES` / `PROFILES` |

The answer is `answer_about`'s own words (`jarvis_tool_profiles.py:2257`): what
the thing is in beginner words, what it lets the owner do, what it refuses,
what it pairs with, and how to switch it on. It is `quick: tool_profile`,
`where: local`, `lane: "no AI model"` in `X-Jarvis-Route`, so **both apps show
it with no client change** and it costs no model turn.

Everything else naming a tool - an opinion, a comparison, "would it help me
with X" - is the **model's**, now with the dossier block in 186.3. A question
that names no tool returns `None` from the fast path, which is exactly the old
behaviour.

**Why the "as a tool" gate is not optional.** 42 of the catalogue's 175 feature
titles open with words that also name a tool ("Web search", "Goals", "Read your
own calendar", "Spending summaries", "Jarvis reads your email"), and one feature
row's alias is the exact phrase "plugin list", which is also the tool id
`plugin_list`. `backend/test_feature_answers.py` and
`backend/test_feature_guide.py` require every one of those to keep the feature
guide's answer, so the marker is `_TOOL_SAID`
(`jarvis_quick.py:6538`) and NOT a bare shape match. The feature layer keeps its
answers; the tool layer is addressed by its own vocabulary.

**Why it sits where it sits.** In `_match`, the call is
`jarvis_quick.py:1272`: after the plug-in block (`_plugins_question`,
`jarvis_quick.py:6391`, called at `:1262`) so a plug-in question keeps its own
answer, and before the Android block and every capability family
(`:1273` onward) and well before `_feature_guide` (`jarvis_quick.py:1762`),
because a tool's own dossier is deeper than a feature row's prose. The runner is
`_run_tool_profile` (`jarvis_quick.py:6602`), dispatched at
`jarvis_quick.py:19097`, and the intent is in `READ_ONLY_INTENTS`
(`jarvis_quick.py:19977`): it reads a fixed module, calls nothing, raises no
card - so a **private chat hands it to the model** like every other read-only
intent, and it cannot take away what "cancel that" would undo.

### 187.2 What the model is given, and what it costs

`jarvis_agent.tool_profile_note` (`jarvis_agent.py:12614`) builds ONE bounded
block from `context_for` (`jarvis_tool_profiles.py:2311`), which never returns
more than `CONTEXT_LIMIT = 1200` characters
(`jarvis_tool_profiles.py:77`). `TOOL_PROFILE_CHARS` (`jarvis_agent.py:12517`)
re-states that cap on this side, so a changed module cannot silently spend more
of the window, and the note is the block plus ONE fixed 142-character line
(`TOOL_NOTE_PREFIX`, `jarvis_agent.py:12524`) saying where the facts came from
and to answer only from them.

- **The budget, in this repository's own arithmetic.** `estimate_tokens`
  (`jarvis_agent.py:6793`) counts 3 characters a token plus 6 of framing, so the
  worst case is `6 + (1200 + 142) // 3` = **453 tokens**, and the ordinary
  `browser_control` turn is 1,285 characters = **434 tokens**. Both `context_for`
  and the cap it is given are checked in `test_tool_profiles_chat.py`.
- **No tool named -> no note -> the same bytes.** That is the rule that keeps
  every ordinary prompt exactly as it was, and it is why the note is keyed on a
  tool's own name and never on a nickname: "what is on my calendar tomorrow" is
  a turn to READ the calendar, and `backend/test_warm_prefix.py` pins the warm-up
  and a real first question to the same bytes before the question.
- **A follow-up keeps it.** If the newest message carries on from the last one
  ("would that let you fill in a form?"), the note looks back at most two earlier
  user messages. That is what makes a *discussion* possible rather than one
  answer - and it is still nothing when no earlier message named a tool.
- **It is held out of the room** like every other note:
  `room -= estimate_tokens({"role": "system", "content": tool_note})`
  (`jarvis_agent.py:13769`), before `clear_old_tool_results` and
  `compact_messages`, so a block can never push the window over.
- **Placement** is `with_tool_profile_note` (`jarvis_agent.py:12652`), copied
  from `with_pc_facts_note`: inserted just before the newest user message, after
  the PC-facts line and before the grant note (`jarvis_agent.py:12874`), with the
  `at == 0` case prepending `LANE_SYSTEM` so the rules stay first. It is fixed
  dossier data - no path, no count, no chat word, nothing read live - so it is
  safe in a private chat.

### 187.3 No route and no new tool, deliberately

- **No route.** A route adds a consumer that does not exist: `/api/reach`
  (`backend/jarvis_reach.py`) already lists every tool in one sentence for both
  apps, and `/api/self` already carries abilities and plug-ins. A third copy
  would need a `tools/check_parity.py` classification, a phone decision and a
  `HUD_GET_PATHS` entry in `hud_proxy.rs` for a screen that does not exist. The
  one worth adding later, **named and not built**: `GET /api/self/tools` (the
  list plus one profile each), the day a Tools page exists, served from
  `jarvis_self_portrait` the way `/api/self/version` is and classified in
  `check_parity.py` in the same PR.
- **No new model tool.** A tool costs five mandatory registrations, each with
  its own test: `TOOLS` plus offer/gate wiring; a description under 300 tokens
  (`test_tool_text.py`); a `jarvis_claims` classification (`test_smarter_answers.py`
  fails a tool in neither set); a `jarvis_reach.TOOL_NAMES` row (`test_reach.py`
  demands one); and the tool contract/schema suites. It also ships **off**: it
  would need its own switch row on Settings, What asks first ("Let the AI use
  this") - one of the lists `jarvis_asks_first.TOOLS_SWITCHABLE` is built from -
  and that switch's PC-only card before the owner could turn it on. And it buys
  nothing: these are facts that fit in 400 prompt tokens, and every tool call
  is a round trip on an 8B.

### 187.4 What it does not cover

- **Features** stay `feature_guide`'s, by chat and as a model tool. A feature is
  a row with a title, a where, an asks-first and a limit; a tool's dossier is
  deeper and answers different questions. The two vocabularies are kept apart by
  `_TOOL_SAID` (186.1).
- **Drop-in plug-ins** (`plugins/ready/`, 49 folders) stay
  `plugin_list`/`plugin_about`'s, which already answers them; the plug-in block
  runs first, so it is never hijacked.
- **Development "plug-ins"** - the patch stack in `plugins/registry.json` - are
  developer vocabulary and not a chat topic.
- **Listing questions** ("which tools ask first") already have their own
  answers (`tools_asking`); `answer_about` returns `None` for them and nothing
  here changes that.
- **It adds no permission, card or tier**, so the standing "every new feature
  gets its own audit" pass finds: bugs (the probes in
  `test_tool_profiles_chat.py`), both apps (free - chat is server-side, nothing
  one-sided, so no `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8 row), and fit (this section,
  the architecture paragraph and the two records).

Two things this section states plainly rather than hides. First, the design
report's probe expected `match("what does browser_control do")` to be `None`
before this work; measured on the merged tree it was `feature_explain` - the
feature guide answering a name it does not own - which is why the tool path must
run before it. Second, two dossier sentences read as an action already taken to
`jarvis_claims.unbacked_claim` (`set_reminder`'s title line and one `set_timer`
"gives" line are imperative). That checker runs on the MODEL's text
(`jarvis_agent._nothing_done_line`, `jarvis_agent.py:14629`), never on a
deterministic `tool_profile` result, so no chat answer is affected; it is
recorded in `test_tool_profiles_chat.py`, which fails if a third one appears, and
the wording belongs to the module's own lane.

The decision is `decisions.d/2026-11-04-capability-talk.md`.

## 188. Call recording: the phone records on the speaker path, the PC transcribes, labels who spoke and files a new note (backend, both apps, added 2026-11-04)

The owner's request, in their own words: *"add the ability of jarvis to record a
call if I tell it a keyword 'record call' where it will record all the audio,
transcribe it, put a date and identify the speakers in the transcription, and
store all of it in a new obsidian note labeled with the date and time"*. The
call is taken through the Android Jarvis app. The whole story, with the
reasoning and the honest limits, is `docs/CALL-RECORDING.md`; this section is
the wire contract the Android lane implements against.

**The platform truth, first.** The call happens on the owner's phone, and his
primary phone is a **Google Pixel 9**; this PC can neither see nor hear that
call. **Android does not let an ordinary app capture the call's own audio
stream** - `MediaRecorder.AudioSource.VOICE_CALL` is privileged and a normal app
gets silence or a `SecurityException`. So the phone records **through its
microphone with the call on speaker** and uploads that; the PC does everything
after. The far end is therefore heard through the speaker and the words are less
clear than a system recorder would give, which the note itself says.
**No real call was driven on that phone by either lane** - the Pixel was not
attached while this was built, which the Android half's own pull request states
- so how the speaker path really sounds and how good the words are afterwards
are **NOT-TESTABLE** until the owner's own field test. Importing a file from the
phone's own call recorder, if it has one, is a later addition and is **not
built**.

### 188.1 The four routes

Origin and token exactly as every other route (`X-Jarvis-Token`;
`X-Jarvis-Client: hud` from either app). One audio shape only: **16 kHz, mono,
signed 16-bit little-endian PCM**.

```
POST /api/call/recording/start
     {"started_at": "2026-11-04T13:36:05-08:00", "sample_rate": 16000,
      "channels": 1, "format": "s16le", "device": "phone"}
  -> 200 {"ok": true, "session": "call_<24 hex>", "state": "recording",
          "sample_rate": 16000, "channels": 1, "format": "s16le"}
     202 {"ok": true, "session": ..., "state": "waiting", "message": "..."}
     400 {"ok": false, "state": "refused", "error": "<one sentence>"}
     403 {"ok": false, "state": "off"|"refused", "error": "<one sentence>"}
```

`started_at` is ISO 8601; a value more than a day away from this PC's clock is
refused (400) so a wrong phone clock cannot name a note for the wrong time. A
naive timestamp is read as this PC's local time. `sample_rate` must be 16000,
`channels` 1, `format` `"s16le"` and `device` `"phone"`; anything else is
refused **naming the accepted values**, never silently converted.

```
POST /api/call/recording/chunk
     {"session": "call_...", "seq": 1, "data_b64": "<base64 PCM>"}
  -> 200 {"ok": true, "session": ..., "seq": 1, "bytes": 32000,
          "chunk_bytes": 32000}
     200 {"ok": true, ..., "chunk_bytes": 0, "already": true}
         (a seq BELOW the next one: already held, nothing written twice)
     404 {"ok": false, "error": "that recording is not on this PC..."}
     409 {"ok": false, "state": "waiting", "error": "..."}   the card is up
     409 {"ok": false, "expected": <n>, "error": "...in order..."}
     413 {"ok": false, "error": "...over the 512 KiB limit..."}
     400 (bad base64, an empty chunk, a missing seq or a seq below 1)
```

`seq` starts at **1** - the Android half's own first chunk is 1
(`CallRecordStore.nextSeq`) - and goes up by one. **A repeated `seq` is not an
error, and a gap is.** A chunk whose `seq` is BELOW the next one the recording
needs is a retry of a chunk this PC already holds - the phone died between the
PC's 200 and its own `sent.txt` append - so it answers 200 with `already: true`
and `chunk_bytes: 0`, and **writes nothing twice**. Only a `seq` ABOVE the next
one is a hole in the audio that nothing later repairs, and only a gap is a 409,
carrying the number the PC wanted in `expected`; the phone marks everything
below `expected` as sent and retries the real gap. (Refusing the repeat, which
this route did until 2026-11-05, retried the same number for ever and made the
recording permanently unsendable.) `bytes` is the **running total** the PC holds
for this recording, which is what the phone reads back to tell a PC that appends
from one that answers 0 to every chunk; `chunk_bytes` is the piece that just
landed. At most **512 KiB decoded per chunk** (16 s of 16 kHz mono; ~683 KiB
once base64 is applied, well inside the PC's 4 MiB request ceiling) and **4
hours** in all. The phone cuts 64 KiB pieces; the cap is generous so a phone
that cuts a little more is never refused mid-call. A chunk that arrives while
the start card waits is refused with 409 `state: "waiting"` - **no audio is
kept before the owner says yes** (the session's folder, its `receipt.json` and
an empty `audio.pcm` are made before the card, so a crash cannot lose the first
chunk; not one audio byte is written until it is approved), and the phone
retries the same number rather than skipping it.

```
POST /api/call/recording/finish
     {"session": "call_...", "duration_sec": 812.4,
      "title": "Talk with Sam", "consent_notice": "on"}
  -> 200 {"ok": true, "session": ..., "receipt": "<one line>",
          "note": "<vault path>" | "pending", "wav": "<path>",
          "recording": {...}}
     400 (no `consent_notice: "on"`, or no audio arrived)
     403 (the feature is off, or the start card was denied)
     409 (already finished, or not recording yet)
```

`consent_notice` must be the literal `"on"`: it is the phone saying the "this
call is being recorded" notice was shown, and neither app may finish a
recording without it. **`receipt` is a STRING** - the frozen contract's own
shape, and the only one the phone reads (`CallRecordWire.finished` takes
`receipt` when it is a string). It is one line: the session, the audio's length,
how many lines and which speakers, and the note (or `pending`). The structured
session record rides in `recording`, the same object the list route serves.

**`finish` does not wait for the words**: the WAV is assembled and the
transcription starts on a daemon thread, so the answer comes back with
`note: "pending"` when the transcription or the note's own card is still
running. **A client cannot poll for it**: the read route below is PC-only, so
the phone has no read route at all - it keeps its own copy until `finish`
answers, and the PC's own screen and the note itself are where the result is
seen. That is the frozen Android half's real behaviour, written here instead of
a poll it does not make.

```
GET /api/call/recording             -> {"ok": true, "enabled": true,
                                        "recordings": [...], "where": "<folder>"}
GET /api/call/recording?session=ID  -> {"ok": true, "recording": {...}}; 404 unknown
                                       403 from any device but this PC

POST /api/call/recording/delete
     {"session": "call_..."}
  -> 200 {"ok": true, "session": ..., "state": "deleted",
          "removed": ["audio.pcm", "audio.wav", "receipt.json", "transcript.md"],
          "message": "<one plain sentence>"}
     202 {"ok": true, "state": "waiting", "message": "..."}  its card is up
     403 {"ok": false, "state": "refused", "error": "..."}; 403 "off" is never used
     404 {"ok": false, "state": "unknown", "error": "..."}
     409 {"ok": false, "state": "recording"|"transcribing", "error": "..."}
```

Read-only: the date, duration, note path, status and speaker list. **Never the
transcript text** - the note holds the words and this route does not.
**PC-only**, through `jarvis_owner_check.from_this_pc` exactly as
`GET /api/guardian/snapshots` and the other PC surfaces do it: the list names
the owner's recordings and the note paths they went to, which is a PC surface,
and the phone has no use for it. The three audio POST routes are the phone's by
necessity - it holds the microphone - and that is the one deliberate departure,
written down in `docs/CALL-RECORDING.md` §8.

**`POST .../delete` is the ONE way a recording is removed**, and it is PC-only
for the same reason: the phone never deletes anything on this PC. It is a POST
rather than a `DELETE` because this backend wraps `do_GET` and `do_POST` for
every optional feature and has no `do_DELETE` anywhere (§112 records the same
choice for the goals store). It removes that session's whole folder -
`audio.pcm`, `audio.wav`, `transcript.md`, `receipt.json` and any
`part-*.wav` - which is also its row in the list above, and it raises **ONE
`delete_call_recording` card at tier `ask`**: deleting the audio and its
transcript cannot be undone, so it never happens without the owner's yes. The
delete itself runs on the card's worker, so a card still waiting answers 202
(the shape `start` uses) and the recording is gone from the GET once it is
approved; 200 means it is already gone. It refuses while the session is
`recording` or `transcribing` (409, in words) and it does **not** need
`[call_recording] enabled = true` - removing something is the safe direction.
**The Obsidian note is not deleted here**: it is a document of its own, written
through the notes editor's own card and undo receipt, and the answer names it so
the owner knows what is left. `docs/CALL-RECORDING.md` §7 is the retention
policy: nothing expires on a timer, and the 400-recording cap refuses a new
start rather than deleting anything.

### 188.2 The session record

`receipt.json` beside the audio, and the `recording` object on `finish` and on
the `GET`: `session`, `status` (`waiting` | `recording` | `transcribing` |
`done` | `refused` | `empty` | `failed`), `started_at`, `finished_at`,
`duration_sec`, `sample_rate`, `channels`, `format`, `device`, `bytes`, `chunks`
(the count of chunks taken), `audio`, `note`, `note_job`, `transcript`,
`speakers`, `speaker_method`, `speaker_why`, `lines`, `message`,
`consent_notice`, `english_only`, `date`. It is the session's own record of what
was recorded and where it went - **not** an action receipt with an Undo; the
note's create leaves its own undo receipt through the notes editor. `finish`'s
`receipt` string is the one-line summary of the same facts.

### 188.3 The chat command, and the `call_record` directive

The eight whole messages, matched **whole-message only** (after the repo's own
tidier, which drops a polite lead-in like "can you ..." for every command in
`jarvis_quick.py`):

- arm - "record call", "record this call", "record the call", "start recording
  the call", "start call recording";
- stop - "stop recording", "stop the call recording", "stop call recording".

The answer carries ONE new additive field in `X-Jarvis-Route`:

```json
"call_record": {"action": "arm"}      /* or {"action": "stop"} */
```

The Android app reads it and starts or stops its own recorder. The reply says
plainly what will happen (phone records on speaker; the PC transcribes and
labels who spoke; a new note named for the date and time is created when the
call ends; tell the other person), and adds one sentence when this PC's tier
makes the start raise a card. **With the feature off the reply says so and the
directive is absent** - an app must treat absence as "record nothing". Stopping
is always answered, because stopping only narrows what is happening. The
intent is `call_record`; a refusal is `call_record_refused`.

### 188.4 The switch, and the card

- **Off by default:** `[call_recording] enabled = false` in the shipped
  `jarvis-framework.toml`; a settings file with no such table is off too.
  Turning it on is a hand edit of that one line - there is **no in-app switch**,
  the same shape `github_search` and `shell_exec` use, and
  `features/features.json` says so in the row's own `where`.
- **The gate action is `record_call`**, tier `ask` in `[autonomy.tiers]`. The
  owner-initiated note actions (`append_obsidian_daily`,
  `append_logseq_journal`) ship `auto`; this one asks because it starts
  capturing **other people's** speech. The gate's `_RISK` table has a row for
  the name (added 2026-11-05): `("yes", "local", ...)` - a recording changes
  nothing on this PC, can be deleted again, and nothing leaves it. Before that
  row the gate treated the action as unclassified and its card carried the
  generic "unclassified action - treated as permanent and able to leave this
  PC" warning, whose **second half was wrong for this action**. The row does
  not loosen the tier: it stays `ask`. Deleting a recording is a second card of
  its own, `delete_call_recording`, also `ask`.

### 188.5 Transcription and speaker labels

`jarvis_media_read.read_media()` - the existing sherpa-onnx model, English only,
no network - reads the assembled WAV in **9-minute parts** (its own ceiling is
10 minutes per file), and each part's segment times are shifted by its offset.
No second speech-to-text, no model download. Segments are the reader's own
**~10-second windows**, so two people talking inside one window get one label.

Speaker labels, all on this PC: the owner's enrolled print first
(`jarvis_voice.find_profile` + `jarvis_voice.cosine`, the print's own
threshold), then clustering of the remaining segments at
`SPEAKER_MERGE_SIMILARITY` = 0.55, up to six, numbered in first-speech order.
A line too short to embed carries the previous line's label. **With no speaker
model or no trained voice print, EVERY line says "Speaker"** and the note
records which was missing - never a guessed name.

### 188.6 The note

`Calls/YYYY-MM-DD HHMM - Call.md`, a NEW file (a same-minute call gets
" (2)"), created through `jarvis_notes_edit.handle_create()` - the notes
editor's own public create path, so the vault/protected/collision checks, the
File Guardian copy, the undo receipt and the ONE `edit_vault_note` card are
unchanged. The transcript is marked `after_outside_text` provenance, because a
call's words are other people's. The frontmatter carries `date`, `started_at`,
`duration`, `duration_seconds`, `source` ("phone call, speaker recording"),
`speakers`, `audio`, `session`, `consent` ("Recorded locally; tell the other
person"), `title`, `speaker_labels`, `speaker_labels_why`, `english_only`; the
body holds one heading, the consent reminder as a visible line, and
`[HH:MM:SS] You: ...` per line in **the time of day it was said**.

**If the vault is missing or invalid**, the transcript is still written as
`transcript.md` beside the audio and that path is returned with a plain
sentence saying why. The transcript is always written there first, so a vault
problem or a refused card cannot lose a recording.

### 188.7 What the phone does (the frozen Android half's checklist)

1. Read `call_record` from `X-Jarvis-Route`; on `{"action": "arm"}` call
   `start` with the date the call began, on `{"action": "stop"}` stop the
   recorder and call `finish`. An unknown action, malformed JSON or an absent
   field is **silence, never a guess** - and never an arming.
2. Record 16 kHz mono s16le in 64 KiB pieces and POST them in order from `seq`
   1, one at a time. A failed POST is retried with the **SAME** `seq`; the
   audio is written to the phone's own files before it is posted, and a `sent`
   list is appended only after the PC acknowledges a chunk, so a dropped
   connection loses nothing. Show Android's own recording notification with the
   consent line.
3. **`start` may answer 202** while the `record_call` card waits. Keep
   recording and keep retrying the first unsent chunk: the PC refuses a chunk
   with 409 until the card is approved and then takes the queue in order. There
   is **no poll**: the read route is PC-only, so the phone has no read route at
   all, and **no audio is kept on the PC before the card is approved** (the
   session's folder, its receipt and an empty `audio.pcm` are made first; the
   audio bytes are not).
4. Stop recording if the phone's link to this PC goes stale (the repo's rule 4
   applies on the client side: never act on a stale picture of the world).
5. On stop: `finish` with the elapsed `duration_sec` and
   `consent_notice: "on"`. If it is refused, **keep the audio and the PC's
   session id and retry later** - never delete the only copy. `note` is the
   vault path, or `"pending"` while the transcription or its own
   `edit_vault_note` card is still running. A recording the PC never takes (a
   denied card, a recording that cannot be sent) is deleted **on the phone** by
   the owner's own "Delete" on the call-recording card, with a confirmation -
   the phone never sends a delete to the PC, and the PC never deletes a
   recording by itself.

### 188.8 What is not done

The Android half is its own pull request against this contract; neither lane
drove a real call on the owner's Pixel 9, so the speaker path and the quality of
the words it yields are **NOT-TESTABLE** until his field test. **A call can
raise TWO cards**: `record_call` before any audio is kept, and the notes
editor's own `edit_vault_note` card before the note is written - a transcript is
other people's words, so it is never a card-free write; deleting the recording
is a third, `delete_call_recording` (§188.1). The audio is **not encrypted at
rest** - an owner decision, not implemented here, and `docs/CALL-RECORDING.md`
§9 says so. English only, ten-second segments, and no import of the phone's own
recorder. No real phone recording, transcription, speaker model, vault write or
approval card was driven by this lane - those rows are **NOT-TESTABLE**, never
passed. `backend/test_call_notes.py` drives fake readers, fake embedders, fake
prints and a fake note creator.

## 189. Clearing old chats by date: a card, TWO yeses, a platform ticket, pinned chats kept, and the facts those chats taught erased with them (backend, routes for both apps, added 2026-11-04)

The owner's ask, in his own words: *"how long does it take for you to clear old
chats if i batched a lot of them together?"* - and the bug behind it. The live
Jarvis answered that it had **no built-in "clear old chats" action** and that it
**did not track how long it would take**. The first was false (§18.3 already
pin, archives and deletes chats; §64 already forgets a time frame), the second
was false the moment this section existed, and neither answer was what he
wanted: *"it should be able to clear conversations it does NOT have pinned when
asked to clear ones of a certain date, INCLUDING FACTS ... it must give a card
with all the details, with a DOUBLE CONFIRMATION of yes, and require a Windows
PIN or fingerprint (phone: fingerprint; Windows desktop: Windows Hello
PIN/biometric) before deleting."*

**Where it lives, and why there is no new list of screens.** `backend/
jarvis_history_purge.py` (shipped whole, in `backend/` and `jarvis-backend/`)
exports `install()`, and `history-purge.patch` is ONE added block in
`jarvis_hud.py` right after `forget-range.patch`'s own, wrapping the running
server's `do_GET`/`do_POST` for exactly its own three paths. Every rule is in
the module. It adds **no tool**: an AI may never start a bulk delete (the same
line §184 draws for `conversation_clear`).

**What it is NOT, said first because the nearest neighbour exists.** §64
"Forget a time frame" (`jarvis_forget_range.py`) already clears a date range,
and this section does not replace it:

| | §64 Forget a time frame | §187 Clear old chats by date |
|---|---|---|
| the facts it taught | **retired** - hidden, words kept | **erased** - the words are gone (`MemoryStore.erase`) |
| pinned chats | not looked at | **kept**, unless the preview asked for them |
| how it is approved | ONE approval card (`memory_forget_range`) | **two separate yeses**, the second needing a platform ticket |
| Undo | ten minutes, one tap | **none**, and the card says so |

### 189.1 The routes

All three are POST, behind the token and the origin check like every other
private route, and all three answer **423** while App lock or "Hide memory
lists and chat history" is on - a card cannot show what it would delete while
the lists are hidden, so nothing may be started.

| Route | Body | Answers | Deletes? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/api/history/purge/preview` | `{from, to, include_facts, include_pinned}` | the card (189.2) and a `preview_id` good for 10 minutes | **never** |
| `/api/history/purge/confirm` | `{preview_id, step: 1}` | `{confirmed: true, next: "second_yes_required", confirm_id, restated: {...}}` | **never** |
| `/api/history/purge/confirm` | `{preview_id, confirm_id, step: 2, auth_ticket}` | `{deleted: {conversations, messages, facts}, audit_id, elapsed_ms}` | **this is the only path that deletes** |
| `/api/history/purge/cancel` | `{preview_id}` | `{ok, cancelled: true}` and the preview is dropped | **never** |

`from` and `to` are `YYYY-MM-DD` (or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`), local time,
**inclusive both ends** - the same grammar §64 uses, imported from that module
rather than written twice. There is **ONE open preview at a time**: a new
preview invalidates the one before it, so a card on screen can never be
approved after it has been superseded. There is no bulk form, no preset list
and no "always allow" anywhere in it.

### 189.2 The card

`preview` answers 200 with:

```json
{"ok": true, "schema": "jarvis-history-purge/1",
 "preview_id": "<uuid>", "generated_at": 1790000000, "expires_at": 1790000600,
 "expires_in_seconds": 600,
 "window": {"from": "2026-10-01", "to": "2026-10-31",
            "said": "1 to 31 October 2026", "start": 1790000000, "end": 1792670400},
 "conversations": {"count": 41, "message_count": 612, "kept_pinned_count": 3,
   "per_day": [{"day": "2026-10-02", "chats": 4, "messages": 58}]},
 "facts": {"count": 7, "included": true, "names": ["..."],
           "names_shown": 7, "names_truncated": 0, "kept_due_to_pinned": 2},
 "storage": {"db_bytes": 466944, "estimated_bytes_freed": 81234, "estimate": true},
 "irreversible": true,
 "warnings": ["...", "..."],
 "card": {"title": "Clear 41 chats from 1 to 31 October 2026?",
          "details": ["Clear chats from 1 to 31 October 2026 on this PC.",
                      "  2026-10-02: 4 chats, 58 messages",
                      "And 7 facts these chats taught, erased for good:",
                      "  - <the fact's own words>",
                      "3 pinned chats in these days are kept.",
                      "This cannot be undone. There is no Undo, and no copy is kept.",
                      "This is asked twice: yes now, then your Windows Hello PIN or your phone's fingerprint."],
          "irreversible": true, "undo_seconds": 0,
          "counts": {"conversations": 41, "messages": 612, "facts": 7},
          "kept": {"pinned": 3, "facts_from_pinned": 2}},
 "next": "Read the card, then send confirm with step 1. ..."}
```

* `card.details` is EVERY line of the card, already in plain words, in reading
  order: **an app may draw it however it likes and may not add a line of its
  own** - the same rule §88 sets for a feature's own words. The counts, the days
  and the fact names come from the backend because they were measured there; an
  app that re-counted would be a second source of truth.
* `facts.names` is the first **40** facts **by their own words**, truncated at
  200 characters each. `names_truncated` is an **integer**: how many more names
  exist beyond the ones shown, `0` when none. The card never hides how many it
  is not showing.
* `storage.estimated_bytes_freed` is an **estimate** and `estimate: true` says
  so: SQLite zeroes a deleted row where it is (`secure_delete`) and the file
  only gets smaller after a VACUUM. `db_bytes` is the real size of
  `chat-history.db` plus its `-wal`.
* `warnings` always carries the irreversible sentence, the sentence that this
  is not an ordinary approval card, and the estimate caveat; then, each only
  when it applies: FACTS ARE NOT INCLUDED (with how many there would have
  been), INCLUDE_PINNED IS ON, pinned chats kept (with the count), facts kept
  because their chat was pinned, and the count of chats that also hold messages
  from outside the window and therefore go **in full**.

### 189.3 Pinned chats are never deleted by accident

The pin already exists (§18.3: `pinned`/`pinned_at` and `POST /api/history/pin`)
and this module only **reads** it.

* A pinned chat inside the window is left out of the count, out of the ids the
  preview holds, and out of `fact_ids`; it is reported as
  `conversations.kept_pinned_count` and named in the card.
* The facts **it** taught are kept too (`facts.kept_due_to_pinned`), because
  their recorded provenance is a chat that is still here.
* `include_pinned: true` is the only way past it, is never the default, and the
  card then says in words that pinned chats go too.
* A chat **pinned between the preview and the second yes** is checked again at
  execution time and **skipped**, and the skip is counted in the answer
  (`kept.pinned`) and in the audit line. A pin set after the card is a pin the
  owner meant.

### 189.4 Facts: selected by provenance, never by a guess

A fact records the conversation it was said in, in its own `meta`
(`jarvis_memory.MemoryStore.add` writes `meta["conversation_id"]`, which is what
§71's `/api/memory/conversation-facts` already reads). So:

* the facts this purge clears are exactly the facts whose **recorded
  conversation** is one of the chats being deleted - never "facts that look
  like they came from there";
* a fact that records **no** conversation, and a fact from **another** chat, are
  untouched. If a chat was deleted long ago its facts no longer point at it, so
  they are untouched too - this action never guesses at a link it cannot read;
* **forgotten facts are included** (a forgotten fact still holds its words);
  already-**erased** ones are not (there are no words left);
* `include_facts: false` clears none of them, and the card says they are kept
  and how many there would have been.

The erase is `MemoryStore.erase(fact_id)` - the same call the per-fact **"Erase
the words"** makes (§7), which replaces the text with the erased marker, strips
`message_hash` and `conversation_id` from `meta`, deletes the word-search and
vector rows, and VACUUMs `memory.db` so the words are gone from the file rather
than merely unreachable. That is deliberately stronger than §64, which
**forgets** (retires) the facts and keeps their words.

### 189.5 The auth ticket - the contract both apps build to

The second yes is signed by the app, and the backend checks the signature. The
text that is signed is exactly

```
{preview_id}|{confirm_id}|{method}|{issued_at}
```

and the ticket the app sends as `auth_ticket` is

