phone's and the plugin's door, `/api/notion/preview` and `/api/notion/import`)
has its own declared ceiling, `MAX_ZIP_UNCOMPRESSED` (500 MB before this
change), and it is not what refused this file.

**The limits now.** Two numbers moved; every other guard is unchanged and still
refuses:

| limit | before | now | what it judges |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `jarvis_documents.EXPORT_UNCOMPRESSED_MAX` | 250 MB | **4 GB** | the unpacked TOTAL an export's directory declares, before a byte is written |
| `jarvis_documents.IMPORT_MAX_BYTES` | 1 GB | **4 GB** | the bytes really written, counted as they arrive (the backstop for a header that lies) |
| `jarvis_notion_obsidian.MAX_ZIP_UNCOMPRESSED` | 500 MB | **4 GB** | the same declared total, at the vault door |
| `jarvis_notion_obsidian.MAX_BYTES` | 1 GB | **4 GB** | the same counted bytes, at the vault door |
| `IMPORT_MAX_ONE` / `MAX_ONE` | 200 MB | unchanged | one member, declared and then counted |
| `IMPORT_MAX_FILES` / `MAX_FILES` | 20,000 | unchanged | members, declared then counted |
| `IMPORT_MAX_ZIP` / `MAX_ZIP` | 2 GB | unchanged | the `.zip` file itself |
| `MAX_ZIP_RATIO` (vault door) | 100:1 | unchanged | declared unpacked against compressed (a zip bomb's shape) |
| `EXPORT_ROOM_FACTOR` (new) | - | **1.2** | free space the target drive must have, against the declared total |

The counted cap moved WITH the declared one on purpose: a backstop that is
tighter than the ceiling it backs up would refuse every honest export the
declared check lets through, and would have moved the owner's refusal from
"250 MB" to "1 GB" without fixing anything.

**Every refusal names the real numbers.** `_size_words()` writes a byte count
the way Windows shows it ("276 MB", "4 GB", "4.5 GB"), and the sentences now
carry both sides of the comparison:

```
Jarvis will not open that export: it unpacks to more than 4 GB: it declares
4.5 GB once unzipped (a zip-bomb guard)

there is not enough free space on that drive: this export declares 3.2 GB once
unzipped, so it needs 3.8 GB free (a fifth more, for the copy), and the drive
has 1.1 GB free

it unpacks to more than 4 GB: 4.0 GB has been written so far

one file in it is larger than 200 MB
```

The free-space preflight is new (`jarvis_documents.disk_space_problem`, and the
room is checked AGAIN for each Notion `Part-N.zip` inside the export, because a
part's own contents are not in the outer archive's declared total). It measures
the target drive with `shutil.disk_usage` BEFORE the first byte, and a drive
that cannot be measured is never refused on a guess. If the disk fills anyway,
the write's `ENOSPC` is its own refusal (not "a name too long") and the hidden
staging folder is removed - a refused import leaves nothing behind, on every
path.

**It can be watched while it runs.** `import_notion(..., progress=callable)`
reports `{"files", "bytes", "of_files", "of_bytes"}` as the bytes are really
written (about twice a second, never once per member), and the same counts are
readable meanwhile: `GET /api/folders` carries a new additive key,
`"importing": {"files", "bytes", "of_files", "of_bytes"}` (`null` when no
import is running; cleared on success and on every refusal). The desktop
Settings page polls that read once a second while its import is in flight and
shows the counts instead of one frozen sentence, and the window's own timeout
for this command went from 600 s to 1800 s (`folders.rs:57`) because a 4 GB
unpack is minutes. The phone needs no change for this: it reads the PC's own
sentences, and no route, control, approval card or permission changed.

**The phone sends the same export now (owner decision 2026-11-09).**
`jarvis_upload.py`'s `MAX_NOTION_BYTES` is the RAW ZIP BYTES the phone sends
over his private network; it was 250 MiB (the owner's 2026-11-05 number) and he
raised it to **4 GiB** on 2026-11-09 so a 276 MB export sent from the phone is
accepted like the PC's picker. The staging ceiling moved with it
(`STAGING_MAX` 512 MiB -> 4 GiB), because a full-size export could not otherwise
be staged at all; the unpacked check on the staged upload still follows the
4 GB constant above. The phone streams the file in 1 MiB chunks straight from
the provider, so the cap is a ceiling on the transfer, not on the phone's
memory. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8 records the numbers and their history.

**What proves it** (`backend/test_documents.py`,
`backend/test_notion_obsidian.py`; no 276 MB fixture is written): a synthetic
zip whose own directory DECLARES 276 MB - a real small export with one skipped
member's declared size rewritten - imports successfully (it is over the old
250 MB ceiling and under the new 4 GB one); a declared total over 4 GB is still
refused, with both numbers in the sentence; the ratio (100:1, a real
highly-compressible archive), the 200 MB per-file cap, the 20,000-file cap and
the 2 GB zip cap all still refuse; the free-space preflight is tested with a
drive seam (1 MB free behind an 8 MB export) AND against the real drive; the
progress callback and the live `importing` record are checked during and after
an import, including after a refusal; and the phone's relay of the PC's
sentence and its 4 GB raw-upload cap are pinned (raised 2026-11-09). `tools/gen_folders_cases.py`
regenerated the two `folders-cases.json` copies for the additive `importing`
key, and `backend/test_documents.py` checks they match the backend.

**Not tested here:** a real 276 MB Notion export was not available, so the
owner's file itself is the field test; and the desktop's progress line is
proved by the JavaScript suite against a stubbed bridge, not by watching a
real import in the packaged app.

## 208. Read out loud in Jarvis's own voice, with Pause / Resume and a real Stop (2026-11-09)

**The bug, as it stood, with the evidence.** The desktop HUD
(`jarvis-desktop/src/jarvis_hud.html`) is the one window that reads a TYPED
answer aloud. Its `voice.speak` did that with the webview's own speech engine:
`speechSynthesis.speak(new SpeechSynthesisUtterance(...))` after selecting a
voice by hand - `/en-GB/` plus a male name first, then any English voice, then
`null` (the file's own comment said *"Match the Kokoro bm_george choice:
British, male if one exists"*). That was never the voice Jarvis speaks in: the
owner's configured voice is Kokoro's (`jarvis_voices.speaker()`; the shipped
default is `af_heart`, a woman), the same voice a spoken answer and Jarvis Live
use. WebView2 cannot produce a Kokoro voice at all - its list is Windows'
SAPI voices - so the "any English voice" step was the first voice in that
list, and the owner's report of 2026-11-08 names what it was on his PC: index
0, `Microsoft David`, a man. The shell's own local-voices wrapper
(`hud_bootstrap.js` section 2e) then chose `english[0] || mine[0]` when the page
left the voice empty, which is the same first-in-list fallback a second time.
Both code paths were read in the source; the NAME of the voice that came out
is the owner's observation, not a measurement made here.

**What it does now.** A tap on an answer's speaker, or "Read out loud" in its
answer menu, plays **audio this PC made in the configured voice**, through the
SAME Rust command a spoken answer uses: `speak_reply` -> `POST /api/voice/say`
-> `jarvis_speech.say()` -> `jarvis_voices.speaker()` (or the owner's custom
voice). The page never touches `speechSynthesis`, `SpeechSynthesisUtterance` or
`getVoices`, so there is no index-0 and no male substitute to fall back to. A
long answer is cut into pieces of at most 500 characters (`speechPieces`, the
page's own pure function) and asked for one piece at a time, so it also fits the
command's 30-second fetch budget; `speak_reply` caps one request at 4,000
characters in CODE (`SAY_MAX_CHARS`), because the HUD is now a caller. Inside
the shell the command holds the token; in a plain browser (the backend still
serves this page at "/") the page asks the same route directly, so the voice is
the same one either way - and the sound arrives as a `data:audio/wav` URI, never
a blob or object URL (the HUD holds no file/blob road). **One thing had to
change in the page's own policy for that to work, and it was found by
measuring:** the page's `<meta>` CSP said `media-src 'self' blob:`, which
refused every `data:` clip with `NotSupportedError` and a `media-src data`
violation even though the shell's header CSP already allowed it; it now says
`media-src 'self' data: blob:`, and `tests/hud-live-read-aloud.mjs` drives a
real `data:` clip through both policies so this cannot silently come back.

**Pause, Resume, Stop.** `pauseSpeechPlayback()` pauses the clip playing now
where it is; `resumeSpeechPlayback()` carries on from there. Both are the page's
own functions, reached through one window object (`window.__jarvisSpeech`), and
their state is the player's (`idle | loading | playing | paused`).
`stopSpeechPlayback()` is the full reset: it bumps the token (so a request or a
clip still in flight is dropped instead of played), empties the queue, pauses
and detaches the audio element, clears the line under the answer and settles the
meter. It is called by the answer menu's **Stop reading**, by Stop everything
(the page listens for the shell's `stop-everything` event, which
`commands.rs::stop_everything_now` emits before it asks the PC to stop anything)
and by the PC's **`read_aloud {enabled: false}`** frame - so the automatic
switch's OFF is literal for a tapped read too, exactly as it is for the bar's
queue (§201). The answer menu draws **Pause / Resume and Stop reading beside
Read out loud**, only while THAT answer is the one being read, and Pause's label
says what the next tap will do.

**When the voice is unavailable, it is said - never substituted.** If the PC
cannot make the sound (no Kokoro or custom voice, a 503, the command refused),
the player stops and the page draws one fixed plain line under the answer:
"Jarvis's voice could not read this aloud, so nothing was spoken." Nothing else
is played: there is no browser-voice fallback anywhere in this path. That is the
owner's 2026-11-08 rule, and it is pinned by a test.

**The privacy rule is unchanged and still comes first.** The speaker is drawn
only for an answer `private-speech.js`'s `mayReadAloud` allows, and both tap
paths (`window.__jarvisReadAnswer` for the menu, the speaker's own click) ask
the same rule for THAT answer's route before anything is requested - failing
closed if the module cannot load. The shell's `speechSynthesis.speak` wrapper
and its "It's on your screen." line stay as the guard for any speech-synthesis
path that might return to that page.

**One new permission, as narrow as it can be.** `capabilities/hud.json` pulls
in ONE new set, `hud-speech`, which grants exactly `allow-speak-reply` - the
voice command the Jarvis bar already holds. There is no microphone command, no
recording command, no new route and no approval card in it, and
`tools/check_invoke_grants.py` holds the page's one `speak_reply` call to that
set (it fails if the grant is removed). The `voice` set stays the bar's.

**What was NOT touched.** The phone. Its tap-only Read out loud already speaks
with Android's own on-device synthesiser under its own lock rules; there is no
WebView2 voice list to fall back through, and the PC's Kokoro voice cannot be
shipped to it. In particular **the phone's voice-print / speaker-verification
path is untouched**: `jarvis_voice.py`, the enrolment routes and every
`voiceprint`-class command are exactly as they were on both apps, and no
microphone, recording or verification code was edited for this slice. ARCHITECTURE
section 8 records why this is desktop-only on purpose.

**How it is held.** `jarvis-desktop/tests/hud-read-aloud-voice.mjs` (pure node,
no browser) checks that the page has no browser-voice code left, that its one
source of sound is the PC's voice route, that Pause/Resume/Stop exist and Stop
resets everything, that the failure is said in one plain line, that Stop
everything and `read_aloud OFF` both call the reset, that the privacy rule comes
first, that the grant is the narrow set, and it lifts the real `speechPieces`
out and runs it. `tests/hud-live-read-aloud.mjs` drives the real page: a speaker
asks the PC for THAT answer's words (and never the browser engine), Pause becomes
Resume and carries on, and the PC's `read_aloud {"enabled": false}` frame stops
the clip and takes the items away. `voice.rs`'s `speech_text_tests` proves the
4,000-character bound in characters. **NOT-TESTABLE here, said plainly:** the
real WebView2 voice list, the real Kokoro audio coming out of the owner's
speakers, and how a long answer sounds in his configured voice. Those need the
owner at his PC; what is proved here is that the page cannot reach a browser
voice and that the one path it does use is the one a spoken answer uses.

## 209. A preset clicked in either app raises no card (2026-11-09)

The owner's ask, in his own words: *"if i manually click and change the preset
for jarvis, it shouldnt need a card"* and *"if i manually choose anything in the
jarvis app or deskstop program, and its something that i can easily click and
change back right away, it shouldnt need a card"*.

**The rule.** A local focus preset that is not one of the two heavy rows
(Coding and Medical), picked in either app's own preset control, applies at
once with no approval card. The preset it replaced is written into
a receipt (`preset_apply` in `jarvis_receipts.py`), and the menu it was picked
from puts the old preset one click away - that menu row is the everyday way
back. The receipt is readable through `GET /api/receipts` and undoable through
`POST /api/receipts/<receipt_id>/undo`; the apply's own answer carries its id
as `receipt_id`, and `previous_preset` names what was replaced. Undo is
registered only when the preset it replaced is itself a local one that is not
heavy: if the row it replaced was Coding, Medical or the Cloud row, the receipt
is still written, but Undo is not offered, because going back to any of those
raises its own card and that menu row is the way back. (Receipts are
routes only today - there is no separate receipts screen in either app - so the
receipt is the machine record plus the Undo the existing route can run, not a
new button.)

**Why this is the owner's click and not the model's.** Both apps' preset
controls call ONE route, `POST /api/work/apply` (`jarvis_presets.install()`,
wired by `presets.patch` onto the HUD's `Handler`), and that route already
demands the server's origin check and the pairing token before it reads the
body. The model never posts to its own HTTP API: its path is in-process -
`jarvis_model_knowledge.apply_preset` (the spoken "use the X preset" command),
`jarvis_settings_registry.set_focus_preset` ("set the focus preset to X"), and
`jarvis_quick`'s command path all call `jarvis_presets.apply_from_body`. That
function is unchanged and still carded: it raises the existing
`switch_model` card inside `jarvis_models.switch_to`. The uncarded road is a
private call, `_apply_body(..., owner_ui=True)`, made by the route wrapper
alone; there is no header, body field or query parameter that asks for it, and
`[autonomy.tiers]` still says `switch_model = "ask"`.

**The boundary - "easily click and change back right away" means all four:**
the request is a paired app's screen, the change is one model switch on a lane
that already exists, the preset it replaced is one click away in the same menu,
and nothing is downloaded, installed, deleted or spent. Under that rule:

* the ten local presets, except the two heavy ones (Coding and Medical), apply with no card;
* **Coding and Medical keep their cards.** Each needs the pooled three-card lane
  to unload the other lane models and load its own model - Coding's 14.8 GB in
  about half a minute, Medical's `medgemma:27b` at 17.31 GiB in about 47 s; that
  is not a quick click back, and the card is the warning before the first unload
  (`jarvis_model_lanes.start_pooled_lane` raises it, unchanged);
* **the Cloud row keeps its card.** It chooses where the owner's words go, and
  its card is `change_own_config` (`jarvis_presets.apply_cloud`, unchanged);
* **installs and downloads keep their cards.** `download_model` and
  `/api/models/install` are untouched: a full-model install is not this case;
* a preset asked for in chat or by voice keeps its card: that is the model's
  path, and the owner did not click it.

**What a failed apply does.** The receipt is written BEFORE the switch and
removed again if the switch does not happen, so a refused or failed apply never
leaves a receipt claiming a change. A failure after the switch rolls the model,
the chat lane and the saved preset back exactly as before, and names only the
restores it saw succeed (`restored` / `not_restored` in the answer).

**Both apps.** The desktop chip, Settings -> Focus presets and the HUD Presets
menu apply through `apply_focus_preset` (Rust) to the same route; the phone's
Focus presets plate does the same through `JarvisApi.focusPresetApply`. So the
rule is one-sided in neither app, and `tools/check_parity.py` is unaffected.
The phone's own sentence says the same thing as the desktop's: a local preset
that is not heavy switches at once, and Coding, Medical and the Cloud row still
ask.

**Proved by:** `backend/test_presets_owner_ui.py` - the route applies a local
preset with zero `jarvis_gate.check()` calls and writes one undoable receipt;
Undo puts the previous preset, model and lane back; `apply_from_body` (the
model/chat road) raises exactly one `switch_model` card and writes no receipt;
the heavy ids are exactly Coding and Medical and the uncarded decision is
`owner_ui and not heavy`; Coding still goes through its pooled lane's asking
start; Cloud still raises `change_own_config`; no request field can ask for the
uncarded road; and the shipped `jarvis_models.switch_to` still asks.
`backend/test_presets_apply.py` keeps the carded path's rollback and refusal
checks.

## 210. The manual-click rule: one allow-list, and the model path still asks (2026-11-09)

The owner's words, again: *"if i manually choose anything in the jarvis app or
deskstop program, and its something that i can easily click and change back
right away, it shouldnt need a card"*. Section 209 covers the first click that
took that road (a local focus preset). This section covers the rule itself: the
ONE allow-list every such click must be on, the ONE signal that makes a request
a screen rather than a model, the reversible choices wired today, the settings
that already needed no card, and the list that must always ask.

**The allow-list.** `backend/jarvis_reversible_ui.py` (shipped whole, twin in
the base) holds `REVERSIBLE_UI_CHOICES`, an explicit mapping of action name to
the plain-words reason it is reversible and the ONE model/chat path that still
raises a card for it. Two entries today:

* `apply_preset` - a local, non-heavy preset; the uncarded road is
  `POST /api/work/apply` -> `jarvis_presets.install()` ->
  `_apply_body(..., owner_ui=True)`; the model path (`apply_from_body`, the
  spoken and Settings setters) still raises `switch_model`. Section 209 is this
  row in full.
* `switch_model` - a model already installed on this PC, picked in either app's
  own model list. The uncarded road is `POST /api/models/switch` ->
  `jarvis_reversible_ui.install()` ->
  `jarvis_presets.switch_model_for_the_owner` (one model record and one
  tripwire, no card). The model path is `jarvis_quick` ->
  `jarvis_model_knowledge.switch_model` -> `jarvis_models.switch_to(ref,
  why="chat")`, whose `switch_model` card is unchanged; the tier table still
  says `switch_model = "ask"`.

`is_reversible_ui_choice(name)` is the only test, and it fails closed: a
non-string, an empty name or an unknown action is not reversible.

**The trusted-UI signal is the route, never a field.** `install()` wraps ONE
path on the HUD's own Handler, after the same origin check and pairing-token
check the HUD's own branch makes, and copies its answer shape exactly (`400`
with no ref, `200` on success, `409` on a refusal). Every other path is
forwarded untouched to the handler that already owned it. The model never posts
to its own HTTP routes - a chat tool call reaches the modules in-process - so a
request that arrives here came from a paired app's own control. Only `ref` and
`why` are read from the body; `owner_ui`, `ui_direct`, `no_card` or any other
invented field is not looked at, and no header or query parameter is read.

**The boundary, in one line each:** reversible means one click back, already
installed, nothing downloaded/installed/deleted, no spend, and no privacy or
security downgrade. `REVERSIBLE_UI_CHOICES` therefore never contains: deleting
or erasing a memory, `forget_range`, deleting a skill or model, reverting files;
installing or editing a skill, plugin or model (`download_model`), applying
self-code patches, running updates; turning Lockdown off, changing App Lock /
Windows Hello, revealing a private list, storing a credential, raising a spend
or safety cap; `github_create_repo`, sending email or messages, importing an
external archive. Those names are listed with their reasons in
`EXCLUDED_UI_ACTIONS`, the allow-list refuses them, and this change intercepts
no route that reaches them.

**The everyday settings, audited 2026-11-09 - most needed no change.**
Already cardless on both roads, so they are not on the allow-list (there is no
fence to claim): read-aloud; the built-in voice picker; the theme/face; to-do
carry-over; the six PC notification switches. Already cardless when turned OFF
and still carded when turned ON, deliberately, because ON gives Jarvis more
reach: the Wi-Fi auto-reconnect, the three learning switches, phone
notifications, watch notifications, and a skill turned back on (its scanner's
`modify_own_code` card). Not wired, and said so in the module: the morning
briefing's hour, whose setter lives in the live HUD this repository does not
ship.

**Both apps.** The desktop's Brain -> Model list and the phone's Brain -> Models
plate already post `/api/models/switch`; nothing in either app asks for the
uncarded road, and neither app needed a change. `tools/check_parity.py` is
unaffected.

**Proved by:** `backend/test_reversible_ui_choices.py` - for both allow-listed
actions the trusted-UI route runs with zero `jarvis_gate.check()` calls and
writes its normal record (a `preset_apply` receipt; the model state plus one
switch-log entry and the tripwire); the same actions through the model path
raise exactly one card, with `switch_model` driven through the REAL shipped
`jarvis-backend/jarvis_models.py`; the excluded set is refused and its real code
still asks (a download, `forget_range`, Lockdown off; source pins for the
live-only modules); a body naming `owner_ui`/`ui_direct` is ignored in both
directions, and no query or header is read; the tier table still says
`switch_model = "ask"`; the module is in both SHIPPED lists and the two copies
are byte-equal. `backend/test_presets_owner_ui.py` keeps section 212's own
proof.


## 211. Creator mode: one waiting folder, a scan, and ONE card a thing (added 2026-11-09, Wave 13)

The owner's ruling (2026-11-09, via the Lead): **Creator Mode's scope is "Plug-ins
and skills"** - not plug-ins only and not everything. This is the first slice: a
creator puts a skill folder or a plug-in folder in ONE fixed waiting folder on
this PC, the PC scans what is there when the Settings card is opened, and the
owner installs ONE item behind ONE approval card. Installing is not enabling.
A plug-in is a program, so this slice stages it, scans it and refuses it **in the
pack manager's own words** rather than inventing a code-install path; the exact
remaining work for that half is 211.9.

Creator mode is a new module, `jarvis-backend/jarvis_creator.py`, shipped whole
and loaded by the drop-in folder `plugins/ready/creator-mode/` - no patch. Its
two routes are answered by its own `install()`, the same way
`jarvis_skill_menu.install()` answers the Skills routes (section 178).

### 211.1 The waiting folder

ONE place, and it is a folder on this PC:

```
<config folder>/creator-incoming
```

beside `skills/`, `skills-off/`, `skills-quarantine/` and `skills-incoming/` -
the folders the rest of the skill machinery already uses. `JARVIS_CREATOR_INCOMING`
overrides it, for the suites. It is made **when it is first needed**, so the
installer carries no empty folder and no new deploy path; the only write this
module does on a read is that `mkdir`.

Every direct child folder is one item. A folder with `SKILL.md` is a skill; a
folder with `plugin.json` is a plug-in; a folder with both, or with neither, is
refused with a sentence saying so rather than guessed at. A link or a junction is
refused, because a link can point anywhere on this PC. Folder names are names,
never paths: the install request names one folder and the PC resolves it inside
the waiting folder and proves the result is still under it.

Nothing in that folder is ever run, imported, moved or copied by a read. There is
no loader, no watcher, no timer and no scheduler looking at it: the scan happens
when the owner opens the card (or presses **Look again**, or returns to the
page), and the install happens when they answer a card. Writing a file into
`creator-incoming` cannot change what Jarvis does.

### 211.2 The two routes, PC only

```http
GET  /api/creator/incoming
POST /api/creator/install
```

Both refuse every device but this PC (`jarvis_owner_check.from_this_pc`; 403 with
one plain sentence), and `tools/check_parity.py` classifies both `deliberate`
with the one-sided reason. The phone keeps reading the plain list of what is
already installed (`GET /api/skills`), which is unchanged.

`GET /api/creator/incoming` answers with the waiting folder's path, one row per
item (`name`, `kind`, `verdict`, `refused`, `can_install`, `summary`, `reason`,
the scanner's `findings`, `installed`, `where`), the counts, and one `note` in
plain words. It is a READ: it raises no card.

`POST /api/creator/install` takes **one** field, `name` - one folder - plus the
optional `accept_warnings` the owner sends after reading warnings. It answers
with the PC's own words: `installed`, `state`, `where`, `message`, and the pack
manager's scan report. A refusal is `ok: false` with `refused: true` and
`asked: false`; it is never a transport error the page has to decode.

### 211.3 The scan is the pack manager's, called not copied

A skill is handed to `jarvis_packs.scan_source()`, which is the pack manager's
own full pre-install scan (section 197.3): file list and hashes, the code and
binary refusal, the link refusal, compatibility, the existing
`jarvis_skills.vet()` verdict and findings - including the four extra checks in
`jarvis_skills._extra_findings()` (`hermes_exec`, `exfil_phrasing`,
`gate_bypass_claim`, `bare_url`; section 178) and the bundled-scripts warning
("ships N executable file(s) ... Nothing here runs them"). A folder whose
`SKILL.md` is missing, oversized or malformed is a `malformed` refusal, not a
card.

A plug-in (`plugin.json`) is a program that runs inside the backend at start-up
(`jarvis_plugins.py:57-63`), so it is **refused before any card**. The sentence
is `jarvis_packs.CODE_REFUSED`, imported from that module - never copied - with
this folder's evidence: the first file that can run when the folder holds one
(the pack manager's own scan produces that refusal word for word), or the module
its `plugin.json` names when the folder holds only its manifest. Nothing is
imported to read the manifest.

### 211.4 Install is ONE card, and installing is not enabling

A skill install calls **`jarvis_packs.install_pack()`** - the pack manager's own
door - which re-scans from scratch, refuses a refused skill without asking,
raises exactly ONE `modify_own_code` card, copies only after the yes, records the
ledger and receipt, and then **turns the skill OFF** through the existing off
path (`jarvis_skill_menu.set_state({"on": false})`). The result is the same
state a skill the owner switched off is in: not in `skills/`, not in
`jarvis_skills.cards()`, not loadable, and offered again only by the ordinary
**Turn on** control, which runs the scanner again and raises its own card.

There is **no bulk path**: the request names one folder, a body with a list is
refused before anything is scanned, and each item is its own card. There is no
"install all", no yes-to-all and no per-row loop that installs several.

### 211.5 What this deliberately does not do

- **No plug-in install.** A plug-in is code with the same trust as the backend
  itself; installing one needs the phase-2 code-trust work (197.7, 197.10), not a
  second scanner here. It is listed, scanned and refused, so the owner can see
  it and see why.
- **No network, no marketplace, no URL, no git.** A local folder only.
- **No watcher and no auto-install.** Nothing installs without a card answered
  on the PC, and nothing installs because a file appeared.
- **No phone surface.** A skill is instructions the model follows and a plug-in
  is code that runs beside it; the screen that puts one in sits where the folder
  is. ARCHITECTURE section 8 records the one-sided reason.
- **No second scanner and no second card.** `jarvis_skills.vet()`,
  `jarvis_packs.scan_source()`, `jarvis_packs.install_pack()` and
  `jarvis_skills.install()` are called; none is re-implemented.
- **No quarantine copy for a refused plug-in.** The staged folder IS the
  evidence and it stays exactly where the creator put it; nothing was ever
  handed to the installer, so there is nothing to quarantine. A refused skill
  goes through the pack manager's own path and is refused before the card, for
  the same reason.

### 211.6 The Settings card

Settings -> **Skills** gains a **Creator mode - things waiting** block
(`jarvis-desktop/src/settings.html`; `skills-menu-settings.js` over two new
actions on the existing `skills_menu` command in
`jarvis-desktop/src-tauri/src/skills_menu.rs`):

| action | what it asks the PC |
|---|---|
| `creator_read` | `GET /api/creator/incoming` - the folder and its scanned items. Read only; no card. |
| `creator_install` | `POST /api/creator/install` with ONE name - the pack manager's scanner, then its ONE card. Held while the event stream is stale. |

The block shows the folder's path, one row per item with the scanner's verdict
and findings, and an **Install it…** button ONLY on a row the PC says can be
installed. A refused skill and a plug-in show the refusal and get no button,
because the PC would not draw a card for them. The status line shows the PC's
own message - for a successful skill, the pack manager's sentence saying it was
installed and turned off.

**One-sided on purpose:** there is no phone control and no new phone screen.
The phone's existing list of what is installed is unchanged. ARCHITECTURE
section 8 carries the entry.

### 211.7 What is proved, and what needs the owner's PC

`py -3 backend/test_creator_mode.py` (130 checks, all passing): a staged skill is
seen and scanned with no card; a warning and a block are both shown, never
hidden; a plug-in is refused with `jarvis_packs.CODE_REFUSED.format(...)` word
for word; a folder that is neither shape is refused; two reads change no byte of
the staged folder, copy nothing, quarantine nothing and raise no card; a clean
install raises exactly ONE `modify_own_code` card and lands the skill in
`skills-off/` with the ledger saying `disabled`; the ordinary ON control then
raises its own card and restores it; a blocked skill and a plug-in come back
`asked: false` with the gate never called; a multi-name body is refused; names
that are paths cannot reach outside; the routes answer and fall through, are
refused from another device, and are classified `deliberate` in
`tools/check_parity.py`; and the module imports no network, process or watcher.

`node jarvis-desktop/tests/skills-menu.mjs` (25 checks) holds the page's
`creatorView()`, its missing-module sentence, the one-button-per-row rule, the
"no watcher" wiring and the `turned off` wording. `cargo test` covers the two new
actions' plan/held/answer rules. **NOT-TESTABLE here, said plainly:** the owner's
real click on the real card, on his own PC, with a real folder in
`creator-incoming` - no lane has driven that, so the field-test row stays NOT RUN
YET until he does.

### 211.8 What a creator sees, in order

1. Put the folder in `creator-incoming`. Nothing happens; nothing runs.
2. Open Settings -> Skills (the Creator mode block is in that card). The block
   scans what is there and shows the verdict, the findings, and (for a skill)
   whether it needs its warnings read first.
3. Press **Install it…** on ONE item, read the ONE card, answer it.
4. The skill lands in `skills-off/`, turned off. Turn it on in the Skills list,
   which scans it again and asks its own card.
5. A plug-in shows the pack manager's code refusal and no button. That is this
   slice's whole plug-in half.

### 211.9 What the plug-in half still needs

The staged plug-in folder is refused by `jarvis_packs.CODE_REFUSED`, so nothing
half-installs. To turn a plug-in into an installable item, the next slice needs,
in order:

1. the phase-2 code-trust design `jarvis_packs` already names (197.7/197.10):
   what a code pack may touch, where it runs (a separate process, not the HUD's
   own), and what the scan can prove about it (AST/import and obfuscation);
2. a real install path for a plug-in folder into `jarvis_plugins\` beside
   `jarvis_hud.py` (today `scripts/add-plugin.ps1` is the only door), with the
   ONE-card shape and a ledger row like the pack manager's;
3. install != enable for a plug-in too: the loader already honours a `disabled`
   marker beside `plugin.json` (`jarvis_plugins.py:159`), so landing one disabled
   and switching it on through that marker is the shape - but the restart
   sentence and the scanner's verdict for code must exist first;
4. the same tests this slice has for skills: staged, scanned, refused-never-a-
   card, one-card install, install-is-not-enable, and the phone's one-sidedness
   classified in `tools/check_parity.py`.

Until that lands, **no plug-in is installed by Creator mode, and the card says
so in the pack manager's own words** - which is the honest smaller slice rather
than a code-install path nobody has designed.

## 212. The truth about what reaches the web, and one carded `github_create_repo` (2026-11-09)

**The owner's report.** He asked why Jarvis denied web browsing while the `web_search`
switch was ON, and he asked it to create a repository called "Fitness Band". Both were
the same fault: four different things leave this PC for the internet, each with its own
switch, and the answer treated "the web" as one thing. This section records what was
added to make the answer factual without asking a language model to guess.

**The four things, kept apart on purpose.**

| What | What it really does | What decides it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (a) web search | Sends the search words to a search engine and brings back titles and snippets. | Settings, Web search (`jarvis_search.request_enabled()`), AND the `web_search` row on Settings, What asks first. |
| (b) reading one web page | Fetches the ONE address shown on its card, once, and never a link on the page. | The `read_web_page` tool row on Settings, What asks first (`jarvis_readpage.py`). |
| (c) browser control | Works a real page - clicking and typing in one tab. | Its own switch on Settings, What asks first, AND the second graphics card's "Browser control" lane or the windowless browser (Obscura). |
| (d) the GitHub integration | Reads, comments, opens an issue, re-runs a workflow and creates one new empty repository, each on its own card. | A token saved through the "connect my GitHub" card, AND each of its seven tool rows on Settings, What asks first. |

**Where the deterministic answer lives (no model, no guess).**

- `backend/jarvis_feature_guide.py`'s `SELF_FACTS["internet_access"]` - the ONE source of
  the fixed words. Its `sentence` is the owner-facing answer; its `digest` is what the
  model's `self_portrait` tool result carries, so a model turn cannot contradict the
  fixed answer. It is in `SELF_FACT_IDS`, which is what makes the portrait carry it.
- `backend/jarvis_quick.py`'s `_INTERNET_ACCESS` grammar and `_run_internet_access()` -
  whole sentences only, answered from `jarvis_reach.view()` (the same rows both apps draw
  under "What Jarvis can reach") plus `jarvis_github.connected()` and
  `jarvis_asks_first.tools_enabled_set()`. The answer says ON or OFF for each of the
  four and, for an OFF one, quotes that row's own reason and what turns it on. It is in
  `READ_ONLY_INTENTS`, so "cancel that" cannot undo a question.
- **Why only the BARE phrase is claimed.** `jarvis_quick.normalise()` strips a leading
  "can/could/would/will you" before any grammar sees the sentence, so "can you browse the
  web?" and "browse the web" arrive identically. The bare phrase is the only shape that
  is a capability question and nothing else, so it is the one claimed. A phrase with a
  task in it ("browse the web for flights to Rome") deliberately keeps its own path,
  because that one has something real to do.

- **The create-a-repository question, in the owner's own words.** `_GITHUB_CREATE_REPO`
  claims the capability forms and answers them from `_github_create_repo_words()` - the
  action's existence, its own tool switch and whether a token is saved - including the
  exact sentence the owner used, "can you create a repository?". Because `normalise()`
  removes the leading "can you", the claimed shape is the BARE `create a repository`
  (optionally `me`, `new`, `github`, `on my github`), and the match is whole-sentence: a
  request that carries the name or a description ("create a repository called Fitness
  Band") has words left over, keeps its own path to the model's `github_create_repo` tool,
  and raises its ONE card. It is never answered with a speech about the action.

**The one CREATE: `github_create_repo`.** A new model tool, `github_create_repo`, decided
under its own gate action of the same name, shipped `"ask"` in both settings copies and
listed in `jarvis_agent.NEEDS_A_PERSON`, so a loosened tier still raises the card.

- It takes a typed `name` (required) and an optional `description` and `private` flag.
  Nothing else: the request body is built field by field in `jarvis_github.plan_create_repo`,
  so a model cannot add a team, an organization or a template field, and a list of names
  is ignored rather than looped over.
- It POSTs to the fixed `https://api.github.com/user/repos` - "user" is whoever the saved
  token belongs to, so it can never create a repository in an organization or in somebody
  else's account.
- A name must be 1-100 characters of letters, numbers, dot, dash and underscore, and not
  "." or "..". A name with a space is REFUSED here with the fix in the sentence
  (`"Fitness Band"` -> `"Fitness-Band"`), never silently rewritten into a different
  repository name. A description is capped at 350 characters so the card can show it.
- ONE approval card is raised BEFORE any network call, and it prints the exact name,
  whether it is private, the description, and the one `POST` address. Nothing is sent
  until a person says yes; a denial sends nothing at all. One repository per card.
- On 201 the receipt quotes only what GitHub really answered: `full_name` and `html_url`
  (and that it is private when GitHub says so). A 201 without those fields says GitHub did
  not send the repository back rather than inventing a name or an address.
- On a refusal it quotes **GitHub's own message** (the top-level `message` and each
  `errors[].message`), scrubbed of the token, then says nothing was created. A 401 adds
  the "save a new token" sentence after GitHub's own "Bad credentials". There is no
  silent retry, and there is no HTTP code in the words the owner reads.
- The token is read from Windows Credential Manager through
  `jarvis_token_store.resolve_secret` (the same secret the connect card wrote), sent only
  in the `Authorization` header to `api.github.com`, and never printed in a card, a tool
  result, a failure sentence or a log line.

**What it still cannot do.** It cannot push anything into the new repository, upload code
or files, create a branch, delete the repository it created, merge, close or comment in
the same call. There is one create planner and one create action; nothing here is bulk.

**The phone deliberately gets no screen for it.** The tool works identically from either
app's chat, and the approval card is answerable on the phone; a name-and-private-flag form
on the phone would be a second door onto a write that cannot be undone. ARCHITECTURE
section 8 records that as one-sided on purpose.

**How it is held (hermetic, no network, no real token).**

- `python -B backend/test_github_tools.py` - the card is built and the denial sends
  nothing; the body is exactly `{name, private, description}`; extra arguments and extra
  fields are refused or ignored; the token is in no card, receipt or failure and a server
  that echoes it is scrubbed; a 201 reports GitHub's real full name and address and a 201
  with no repository in it invents neither; 401 and 422 quote GitHub's own message with no
  token and no HTTP code; every tier is `"ask"`, every table a new tool must join carries
  it, and there is exactly one create planner.
- `python -B backend/test_web_access_truth.py` - the four questions route to the fixed
  answer (not the model), the answer names all four as separate with live ON/OFF state and
  the OFF rows' own reasons, the GitHub half reads the token state and the tool count, the
  fixed words are the model's own digest, "can you create a repository?" and its other
  capability wordings ARE answered from the real action state, "create a repository called
  Fitness Band" is NOT claimed as a capability answer (it must reach the model, which calls
  the tool), and the intent is read-only.

**NOT-TESTABLE here, said plainly.** Nothing in this repository made a real GitHub call:
every test drives the module through the injected `fetch` seam with a fake transport and a
fake token. The first real `POST /user/repos` with the owner's own token, the real 201
body, GitHub's real refusal for a name that is already taken, and whether his token has
the `repo`/`public_repo` permission the create needs are only provable on his PC, with his
token, once he asks for a repository. That is a field-test row, never a pass.

## 213. A failed learning check is ONE banner, not 200 cards (2026-11-09)

**The measured finding this answers** (`.dsh-scratch`/`D:\jarvis-scratch` research of
2026-11-09; the section on "the finding I would lead with, because it is a fault and not a
decision"). When one of automatic learning's THREE batch checks fails - a damaged or
unreadable `auto-learning.json`, no local model (`OLLAMA_URL` not loopback), a cloud model
name, or a missing `jarvis_intake.py` - `after_pass` writes the SAME reason onto every
proposal in the pass. A damaged settings file reads as "off", so from then on every fact is
a card, every pass, until the file is rewritten - and the review queue holds 200. One bad
write therefore looked exactly like "Jarvis has become paranoid", and the owner's only cure
was a card. That is a fault, not a decision: it now gets one record, one banner and one
button.

**What is a fault, and what is the owner's own choice.** The two plain settings sentences -
"automatic learning is off" and "background learning is off" - are his switches, so those
proposals stay cards exactly as before. A DAMAGED settings file, a model check that fails,
and a missing intake module are machinery failing, and those are the fault. A per-fact
reason is never a fault and never hidden: a sensitive topic, a correction, a fact that
would replace a stored one, words that are not the owner's, a topic card, and "could not be
saved automatically" all keep their own cards.

**The record.** `jarvis_auto_learn.py` writes `memory-fault.json` beside
`auto-learning.json` and `learning-stats.json` in the config folder
(`~/.openjarvis`), atomically (temp file, then `os.replace`). It holds only
`{version, reason, count, at, since, tries, last_try_at, last_result}` - the check's own
fixed sentence, times, and the number of cards it parked. **No fact's words can reach it**:
the reason is one of the check functions' own strings, and nothing here reads a proposal's
text. A record that cannot be written is reported as `written: false` and **hides nothing** -
the cards are shown instead, because a suppression with no banner to explain it would be
worse than the cards.

**The two routes** (both behind the same auth as every memory route: `_origin_ok`, then
`_token_ok`; apps send `X-Jarvis-Client: hud`; no tier, no approval card, no new
permission).

- `GET /api/memory/fault` - the banner both apps read:
  `{"active": bool, "reason", "headline", "count", "since", "at", "tries",
  "last_try_at", "last_result", "recorded", "why"}`. `headline` is the PC's own sentence
  for the banner ("Jarvis could not check the facts it was about to save: ... This is the
  check failing, not your facts."). `active` is `false` when there is no fault; a record
  that cannot be READ is also `active: false` (fail visible - the cards show) with `why`
  saying so. A read changes nothing.
- `POST /api/memory/fault/retry` - the one button, body `{}`:
  `{"ok", "cleared", "fault", "outcome"}`. It re-runs ONLY the three batch checks
  (`check_settings`, `check_intake`, `check_local_model`) through the same functions and
  the same in-process `model`/`ollama` handles the learning pass uses - no new route for a
  model, no cloud call, no outside text, and none of the three checks calls a model at all.
  It approves nothing, saves nothing and decides no proposal; the cards stay exactly where
  they were. When the check passes it removes the record and `outcome` is the PC's own
  sentence ("The check works again, so the warning is cleared. Nothing was saved or
  approved by this: your facts are still waiting where they were."); if learning was
  switched OFF instead, it says that ("Learning is off on this PC, so there is no check to
  run. Nothing was saved or approved.") rather than claiming a check passed. When it still
  fails it KEEPS the record, adds one try, stores the reason in `last_result`, and
  `outcome` says "The check still fails: <reason>. Nothing was saved or approved." It
  answers 200 either way - a check that still fails is an answer, not an error. With no
  active fault it is a no-op that says so.

**The suppression boundary, exactly.** `jarvis_auto_learn.visible_pending()` is called from
`jarvis_extract.pending()`, so the one pending read every client makes (the Brain and the
phone, `/api/memory/facts`' pending count and the HUD's proposal event) stops returning the
parked cards. A row is hidden only when its `auto_learn_notes` reason is EXACTLY the
fault's reason **and** it has no sensitive label and no topic question - so a sensitive
card, a correction, a "not in your own words" card and a topic card are never hidden. The
proposal is not decided, retired or saved: it stays `pending`, and **when the fault clears
those cards come back** (fail-closed, and the banner said so). The queue cap still counts
them, because they are still in the queue. While the fault is active a per-fact card with a
different reason still appears; a new pass that fails the same check parks its cards under
the same one record, and `count` is the number the store really holds for that reason.

**What each app shows, and where.** Neither app invents a word of it - both draw the PC's
own `headline`/`reason`, and after a press the PC's own `outcome`.

- Desktop: the Brain window, Memory tab, the "Waiting for you" card - ONE warn-toned banner
  at the top with the PC's sentence and one "Retry now" button; no new screen, no new card
  in the queue. It reads `GET /api/memory/fault` through the Brain's `brain_read`
  allowlist (section "memory_fault" in `brain/routes.rs`), and the button is one Tauri
  command, `brain_memory_fault_retry` (`src-tauri/src/brain/auto_learn.rs`). It is the one
  write in that file deliberately NOT held on a stale link: it approves and saves nothing,
  it only asks the PC what its check says now.
- Phone: Mind, "Memory awaiting review" - the same ONE banner and the same one "Retry now",
  reading the PC's `/api/memory/fault` and posting `/api/memory/fault/retry`
  (`net/MemoryFault.kt`, `JarvisApi.retryMemoryFault`, `JarvisRuntime.retryMemoryFault`).
  The phone adds no local logic: it renders the PC's sentence, and after a press the PC's
  `outcome` (the banner stays, without a button, once a retry clears it).

**How it is held.** `python -B backend/test_memory_fault.py` - 51 checks: a synthetic batch
failure writes ONE record and hides exactly its cards (through the SHIPPED
`jarvis_extract.pending()`, built by applying the patch's own hunk to the published base
with `git apply`), a sensitive card and a sensitive-labelled card that happens to carry the
fault's reason still appear, the owner's own "off" is not a fault, a retry clears only when
the check passes and writes no fact and decides no proposal, a retry that still fails keeps
the record with `tries` and its reason, no fact's words are in the record (also after a
failed retry), a record that cannot be written hides nothing, and both routes answer what
they document. `node jarvis-desktop/tests/memory-fault.mjs` - the banner renders the PC's
words as text, exactly one button calls exactly one command, the PC's outcome is shown, and
a cleared retry leaves the sentence without a button. `jarvis-client`'s
`MemoryFaultTest` - the routes and words, the shapes, only an exactly-true `active` is a
banner, a retry keeps or clears with the PC's own sentence, and the failure lines. The
patch itself is proved forwards and backwards byte for byte by
`backend/test_auto_learn.py`, and the twin `jarvis-backend/jarvis_auto_learn.py` is
byte-equal (the two-file rule).

**NOT-TESTABLE here, said plainly.** No test ran on the owner's own PC against a real
damaged `auto-learning.json` or a live learning lane: every batch failure above is
synthetic (a non-loopback address, a written bad file). The route's auth is the existing
shared memory block, not a new check proved here. Both app screens were exercised against
the desktop's mock browser and the phone's JVM contract only - not driven on real hardware
with a real fault. Those are field-test rows, never a pass.

## 214. `project_read`: one bounded read of a code file inside a folder you listed (2026-11-09)

The owner approved "Jarvis takes over dev work" as a plan in four slices, the
first of which is the read half; the 2026-11-05 project decision said each
previously-unbuilt item needs its own owner decision, so this is that half's
own entry (`decisions.d/2026-11-09-project-read.md`). This section documents
the one thing that half added: a model tool called `project_read`.

**The gap it closes, measured against the two readers that already existed.**
Neither could do this job:

* `file_read` (section 35.3) opens any text file at any path, and it has **no
  check against the owner's folder list at all**. It is the unbounded read, on
  purpose, and it was left exactly as it is - adding a folder check there
  would change a shipped tool both apps and this document already describe.
* `my_files`' `read` action **is** bounded (`jarvis_documents.read` asks
  `allowed_path` before it opens anything) and it refuses code:
  `TEXT_KINDS` is `.md`, `.markdown`, `.txt`, `.csv`, so a `.py` file is
  answered with *"Jarvis reads PDF, Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx), PowerPoint
  (.pptx), Markdown, text and CSV files only."*

So "read this Python file in my project" had no bounded door. `project_read`
is a **composition of two things that already ship**, not a third boundary:

* `jarvis_documents.allowed_path()` - the ONE folder boundary the files tool
  uses - asked for the folder, and then again for the file itself;
* `jarvis_repomap._walk()` - the only `.gitignore`-aware walk in this tree,
  the same one `GET /api/projects/{id}/map` uses (section 195) - plus that
  module's own per-file cap.

**The tool.** `project_read`, declared in `jarvis_agent.TOOLS` beside
`my_files`, four fields:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `path` | a folder on "Folders Jarvis may look in", **or** a registered project's id (a `uuid4().hex`, so 32 hex characters; the map's matcher accepts 16 to 64, and a name is only taken as an id when it is not an existing folder - the same single-field convention `my_files`' `map` action uses) |
| `file` | the file's path **inside** that folder, forward or back slashes: `app/server.py` |
| `start_line` | *optional*: the first line to show, counting from 1 (default 1) |
| `lines` | *optional*: how many lines to show (default 400, hard cap 2,000) |

`start_line` and `lines` are the 2026-11-09 architecture ruling's first two
conditions (Q3). Asking for either one turns the read into a **line range**;
asking for neither is the whole-file read exactly as it shipped, so every
existing answer and every existing check stays true. Their schema is
`"integer"`, and they are not in `required` - a model that says nothing about
lines gets the whole file.

The answer is JSON: `{"ok": true, "content": "<the file's text>", "path":
"<the resolved path that was opened>", "file": "app/server.py", "folder":
{"path", "name"}, "bytes": int, "cap": int, "truncated": bool,
"outside_text": true, "what": "..."}`. A project read adds
`{"project": {"id", "name"}}`. A refusal is `{"ok": false, "error": "<ONE
plain sentence>"}` - never a stack trace, for anything a caller can cause.

**A line range, and the ONE footer.** A range read returns numbered lines in
`content`, one per line, `"{line_number}: {text}"` - the number is the REAL
file line number, so a window never restarts at 1. It adds `start_line`,
`end_line`, `total_lines`, `line_cap` (2,000) and keeps `cap` (the 512 KB
whole-file byte cap); `truncated` is `true` exactly when more follows.
`end_line` is the last line shown, or `start_line - 1` when the file ends
before that line; `total_lines` is `null` only when the file is too big to
count (below); `bytes` is how many file bytes the shown lines hold, not the
length of the numbered text. It works through a project id exactly as it does
through a folder, because `read_project` passes straight to `read_folder`.
A binary file is refused as binary for a range read too - a picture is never
numbered as if its bytes were words.

The footer is a THIRD condition from the same ruling, and it is a separate
field on purpose: **`more`, never `content`**. The model reads `content` as
source code, and a sentence appended to it is a sentence the model can quote
as if the file said it (`file_read` records the same rule). `more` is omitted
when nothing follows. Its sentence is deterministic:

* `"Showing lines A–B of N; request the next line range to read more"` - the
  exact shape the ruling asked for, with A, B and N the real numbers.
* A **second fixed sentence** when the file is over 64 MiB (`MAX_COUNT_BYTES`):
  the exact total is unknown because counting it would mean reading every byte,
  and the sentence says so and says a line range can still be asked for. The
  total is counted by STREAMING the file in binary chunks (a line ends at a
  newline, so a Windows CRLF counts once, and a last piece with no newline is
  still a line) - never by loading the file and never by guessing.
* A third fixed sentence when the 96 KiB answer limit (`MAX_SLICE_BYTES`)
  stopped the slice before the range asked for was complete - it says the limit
  was reached, so the footer never claims the file ended.
* A whole-file read cut at the 512 KB cap carries the same "request the next
  line range" footer too, using the counted total where the file is small
  enough to count; that is how a model that hits the cap learns there is a way
  to ask for the rest.

Both bound the answer: at most 2,000 lines, and at most 96 KiB of text, so an
absurd `lines` request cannot overflow the model's context. The 2,000 limit is
enforced by capping, not refusing. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or
more (`0`, `-1`, `"11"`, `1.5`, `true`) is refused with one plain sentence - a
return, never an exception. A `\r` from a Windows CRLF is dropped from the text
shown but never from the count.

**What it refuses, and why each refusal is the existing code's rather than a
second rule.**

* A folder that is not on the owner's list: refused in the map's own sentence,
  `jarvis_repomap.REFUSED`, before any walk starts. An unlisted folder is
  never walked and then filtered.
* A path that climbs out with `..`, a whole path (a drive letter, a leading
  slash, a UNC name), an empty name and a NUL byte: refused before a single
  path is built, because joining a `..` is exactly the mistake that makes a
  folder boundary meaningless.
* A link that leads out of the folder: `allowed_path()` resolves it and
  refuses it, and the check that passes is the same resolved path that is
  opened - the lesson `file_read` records, that checking one path and opening
  another lets a link swapped in between point elsewhere.
* A hidden file or folder (a name starting with `.`), a "Protected from
  Jarvis" item, a reserved Windows device name and a place file_read refuses
  (keys, saved passwords, browser data): all of them are `allowed_path()`'s
  own refusals, unchanged.
* A file the repository map would not list - ignored by the folder's own
  `.gitignore` (nested files and `!` negation included), or inside a
  build/vendor/dependency folder - is refused in one plain sentence. So the
  two readers cannot disagree about the same file.
* A binary file (a NUL byte in its first 8,192 bytes) is refused in words
  rather than returned as mojibake.
* A **credential file is refused by name**, with one plain sentence that names
  the reason: *"That is a credential file (its name says it holds a key, a
  password or a token), so Jarvis will not read it even inside a folder you
  listed."* The predicate is small and deterministic, and it is the NAME only -
  it never opens, stats or lists the file, so it cannot depend on the file
  existing or on being readable. Refused: `.env` and `.env.*` (`.env.local`),
  `.netrc`, `.git-credentials`, `.npmrc`, `credentials`, `credentials.json`,
  `id_rsa`/`id_ed25519`/`id_ecdsa`/`id_dsa` with or without a suffix
  (`id_rsa.pub`), the `.pem`, `.key`, `.pfx`, `.p12`, `.kdbx` and `.jks`
  extensions, and any path with a `.git` FOLDER in it (`.git/config`,
  `pkg/.git/HEAD`). Deliberately NOT refused: `key.py`, `keys.py`, `env.py`,
  `credentials_migration.py`, `my.env`, `credentials.md`, `my.git/config` -
  ordinary source files that merely contain the word.

**Measured before the credential sentence existed, so the record does not
overclaim.** Three of those names were genuinely readable: `id_dsa`,
`credentials` and `credentials.json`. The rest were already refused, but by
`allowed_path()`'s protected-name list, with the wrong words - a `.env` inside
a folder the owner HAD listed was answered *"Jarvis may read only files inside
the folders on the owner's list"*, which is false for that file. So this change
is both a real refusal for three names and a true reason for the rest. The
checker runs when the folder/file boundary has already refused the path and
again after the walk, before the file is opened - after the boundary/walk
checks and before any read, as the ruling required - so a name the boundary's
own list does not know is still refused, and a binary `.env` is answered as a
credential file rather than as binary, which proves it was never opened.

**The honest limit inside that last point: "`.gitignore`-aware" is NOT
"tracked files only".** `_walk` never asks git. An ignored file is skipped; an
untracked file that is not ignored **is** read, exactly as the map lists it.
Anything that needs "only what git tracks" is a different rule and is not
claimed here.

**The whole-file cap is the map's own number, not a copy of it.**
`MAX_FILE_BYTES` is `jarvis_repomap.MAX_FILE_BYTES` (512 KB). A whole-file
read past it is read to the cap and the answer says `truncated: true` and
carries the `more` footer - it is not refused, and a cut file is never
presented as the whole file. A file past the cap can be read in full a line
range at a time, which is what the footer tells the model to ask for. Bytes
that are not valid UTF-8 are decoded with replacement characters, exactly as
`file_read` and the map do. The walk carries the map's bounds too (4,000
files, 6 seconds); when it stops early the answer names the bound that stopped
it rather than reporting "no such file".

**No card, and no new gate action.** Reading is decided under `file_read`'s
own action, `read_files_readonly` - tier `auto` in the shipped
`[autonomy.tiers]` (`backend/rebuilt/jarvis-framework.toml`) - by declaring
the tool with `gate_lookup_name=lambda args: "file_read"`. There is no new
`_TOOL_ACTIONS` line, no new tier line and no `.patch`; the same shape the
repository map shipped with. Nothing is approved, written, moved or sent, so
there is nothing to approve. The tool is in
`jarvis_agent._PROTECTION_READ_ONLY_TOOLS`, so a folder the owner marked
read-only may be read and a blocked one is refused by `allowed_path()` before
anything opens.

**It is a switch row on the Tools page, and that is the repo's own law, not a
choice made here.** Since the owner's 2026-11-04 decision, every tool the
model can be offered has its own switch, and the only exceptions are the
handful whose own switch (or another tool) decides them - a closed set pinned
by `backend/test_asks_first.py`. `project_read` honours `[tools].enabled`
like every ordinary tool, so a row is real: it joins
`jarvis_asks_first.TIER_UNLISTED` (the same "Everyday helpers" group
`file_read` and `my_files` sit in), which makes the switchable count **62**,
and the desktop mirror in `jarvis-desktop/src/asks-first.js` carries the same
row. It ships **OFF** - it is not a line in the shipped `[tools].enabled`,
exactly like `file_read` - so the owner turns it on in Settings, "What asks
first", and turning it on is one card plus Windows Hello.

**Both apps: nothing new on a screen, and that is not a gap left undecided.**
This is a tool the local model calls; no app draws it, and no route was added
- the same one-sided-by-design shape section 195's repository map records in
`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8. `tools/check_parity.py` has no route to
classify here, because there is no route.

**Rule 1 holds and is unchanged.** The whole read is local: no network call,
no socket, no model call inside the module - it is `ast`-free, standard
library only, and it sends nothing anywhere. Its result carries
`outside_text: true`, and the agent's own boundary (`_TurnWatch.took_in`)
labels and scans every tool result before the model reads it, so a turn that
read code counts as having read outside text, latches private, and cannot learn
a fact from it.

**Proved by:** `backend/test_project_read.py` (178 checks, all green).
It proves: a `.py` file inside a listed folder is read and the words are the
file's own bytes; an unlisted folder is refused with the map's one sentence
and nothing is read; `..`, a bare `..`, a drive letter, a leading slash and a
UNC name are each refused before anything is joined; a real symlink that leads
outside is refused and not one word of its target comes back (SKIPPED, never
"passed", on a PC that cannot make a link); the per-file cap **is**
`jarvis_repomap.MAX_FILE_BYTES` and a 550 KB file is cut at exactly that, says
`truncated` and carries the `more` footer with the real total; an ignored
folder, an ignored `*.gen.py`, a `!` un-ignore, a build folder and a hidden
folder all behave as the map's own walk says they do, and every file that walk
lists is readable byte for byte; a project id reads that project's folder and a
folder taken off the list stops being readable even for a project that still
names it.

The ruling's four conditions have their own checks. **Line ranges:** a range
`11..15` comes back as `11: ...` through `15: ...` with the real numbers,
`start_line`/`end_line`/`total_lines` right for a 60-line file; `more` is the
exact ruling sentence and appears in no other field; a range that reaches the
end has no `more` at all; `lines` alone starts at 1, `start_line` alone shows
the default 400; `100,000` is capped at 2,000; 600 lines of 200 characters are
stopped at 96 KiB with the byte-cap sentence and `end_line` well before the
total; a file larger than a 1 MiB counting limit reports `total_lines: null`
and the unknown-total sentence while still returning the lines asked for; a
range read of a binary file is refused as binary; the same range through a
project id works; and `0`, `-1`, `"11"`, `1.5` and `true` are each refused in
the one sentence, never raised. With neither argument, the whole-file read is
byte for byte the old one and carries no range keys. **Credentials:** `.env`,
`.env.local`, `.netrc`, `.git-credentials`, `.npmrc`, `credentials`,
`credentials.json`, `id_rsa`, `id_rsa.pub`, `id_ed25519`, `id_ecdsa`,
`id_dsa`, `.pem`/`.key`/`.pfx`/`.p12`/`.kdbx`/`.jks` files,
`pkg/.git/config` and `pkg/.git/HEAD` are all refused with `PR.CREDENTIAL` and
none of their words come back, while `key.py`, `keys.py`, `env.py`,
`credentials_migration.py`, `notes.txt` and `app/server.py` still read; the
predicate is pinned on both sides (`my.env`, `server.pem.txt`,
`credentials.md`, `my.git/config` and `key` are NOT refused); a `.env` and an
`id_dsa` full of NUL bytes are answered as credential files, not as binary,
which proves they were never opened; and a hidden non-credential file keeps the
boundary's own sentence. **Zero mutation:** every file's relative path, size,
mtime_ns and SHA-256 in a temp tree is recorded before and after both a
whole-file read and a line-range read, and nothing changes, is added or is
removed. And - against the **real** `jarvis_gate` from the published base, with
the **shipped** tier table, driven through the real `_one_call` - the tool runs
at tier `auto`, the step records `"outcome": "auto"`, exactly one gate call is
made under `read_files_readonly`, and nothing is left pending: no card is
raised.

## 215. The two pre-push review gates: a review packet and a record check (2026-11-10, wave 16E)

The owner's order of 2026-11-10 was **"full parity of what DeepSeek can do on
GitHub, for Jarvis"**. Two of the DeepSeek-side abilities were read-only gates
run before a push instead of after a red CI run: a **review packet** (what
changed, by area, with the risk flags) and a **repository record check** (does
the change carry the bookkeeping CI demands). Jarvis had neither as a product.
This section documents the two model tools and the two chat sentences that add
them: `review_changes`, `check_records`, and the deterministic intents
"review my branch" and "check the records before I push".

**Both are READ-ONLY, and that is the design.** `backend/jarvis_review.py`
writes no file, keeps no log, opens no socket and reads no GitHub token. Every
command it runs is a fixed read-only git command (`rev-parse`, `merge-base`,
`diff`, `status`, `for-each-ref`, `show`) or one of this repository's own twelve
checkers from a closed allow-list. No argument a caller gives is ever spliced
into a command: a ref must match one strict pattern, the folder reaches only
`cwd`, and the checkers' argv is a constant plus an allow-listed script path.
`backend/test_github_review.py` and `backend/test_github_record.py` pin that -
including an `ast` walk for a network import and for a write call, and a real
run over a temporary repository that leaves every file's size and mtime
unchanged and creates nothing.

**The switch, and the missing card.** Each tool has its own row in
`jarvis_asks_first.TOOLS_SWITCHABLE` (tier list `TIER_UNLISTED`) and is decided
under `file_read`'s action, `read_files_readonly`, at tier `auto` - the same
line `project_read` sits on. That is why **neither raises an approval card**:
there is nothing to approve, because nothing is written, nothing is sent, and
no credential is touched. Both ship OFF (neither name is in the shipped
`[tools].enabled`), so the owner's own switch is the only way in, and the chat
answer names the switch when it is off rather than running anyway.

**The folder.** The backend runs from its installed folder, which is not the
git checkout, so the repository is named by `JARVIS_REVIEW_REPO` (documented,
one value, the PC only) or by the tool's `path` argument. A folder under a key
store, a browser profile or the Windows folder is refused by name before git is
started; that is a guard rail, not a sandbox - the review prints file NAMES and
line COUNTS, never a file's words.

**`review_changes` - the review packet** (`jarvis_review.review`). Fields:
`path`, `base`, `branch`, `pr`, `limit_files`. It measures:

| Part | What it says |
|---|---|
| the header | the folder (full path), `base <ref> <sha>` -> common ancestor -> `head <sha>`, the branch or "the local working tree", and the time it measured |
| the counts | `+N / -M` lines from `git diff --numstat`, including untracked text files' lines (bounded) and saying how many untracked files were counted |
| the groups | every changed path under one of: backend (modules and tests), jarvis-backend (the published base), desktop and HUD, Android client, docs, tools and scripts, contract and records, other |
| the risk flags | one line each, with the evidence and the next step (below) |
| the checklist | the owner's standing three-part audit (bugs, both apps, fit) and the three review rules |

The risk flags, and what each one is for: a **one-sided or mismatched twin edit**
(`backend/<file>` and `jarvis-backend/<file>` are kept equal, including the
`BESIDE` files whose base name differs and the ten `rebuilt/` modules that land
flattened); **no test changed** while a backend module did; a **new document
without the `docs/README.md` count bump** (and the size figure is never
regenerated); a **tool or route changed without `docs/JARVIS-API.md`** (this
file); **tracked scratch**; a **hand-edited `CHANGELOG.md`**; a changed
`backend/*.patch` (which needs `tools/build_patch_history.py`); the **size** of
the change (past 40 files or 3,000 lines); a **dirty working tree** (the packet
includes it, so it says so); and a note that `docs/DECISIONS.md` moved. A clean
change prints "(none of the recorded flags fired)".

A **branch** is reviewed against its `git merge-base` with the base, so another
branch's uncommitted work is not in it; this checkout includes its own. A
**pull request number** is resolved among the LOCAL branches (`fix/pr-1222` and
friends) and nothing is fetched - if no local branch carries it, the answer says
to check it out. The base defaults to `origin/main`, then `main`, then `master`,
and a base that is not there is one plain sentence, never a fetch.

**`check_records` - the record check before a push**
(`jarvis_review.record_check`). Fields: `path`, `base`, `branch`, `pr`. Six
obligations, each PRESENT / MISSING / FAIL / INFO with the exact next step:

1. **changelog** - exactly ONE `changelog.d/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md` fragment, one
   bullet with a bold title; a `CHANGELOG.md` edit is a FAIL (the rule is one
   fragment per pull request, and the roll edits `CHANGELOG.md` on a quiet
   main).
2. **docs-count** - when a document was added, `docs/README.md` must move, and
   the count it states must equal the tree's; the next step says the number and
   says NOT to touch the size.
3. **backend-twin** - every changed `backend/<file>` carried to
   `jarvis-backend/<file>` (or its `BESIDE` name), the two copies still equal
   (line endings ignored), and `backend/_where.py` re-taken rather than copied.
4. **decision** - ONE `decisions.d/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md` whose bullet is one
   dated entry and whose date agrees with its name, OR a pure tail append to
   `docs/DECISIONS.md`; a rewrite of the record is a FAIL, and the obligation
   says which form it found.
5. **claims** - every changed `docs/CLAIMS.tsv` row: 5 TAB columns, a state of
   built/open/unverifiable, and a check beginning with `file:`, `no-file:`,
   `grep:`, `absent:`, `test:` or `number:` (or an unverifiable reason).
6. **defect-register** - every changed register row: 7 columns and an
   open/closed status, with the `.md` twin still agreeing.

Then the repository's own **twelve checkers**, each a fixed command, bounded in
time and output: `tools/roll_changelog.py --check`, `tools/check_docs_map.py`,
`tools/roll_decisions.py --check`, `tools/check_claims.py` (the slow one - it
re-runs the suites its rows name), `tools/check_defect_register.py`,
`tools/check_stale_twins.py`, `backend/test_base_matches_repo.py`,
`backend/test_base_regeneration.py`, `tools/check_no_source_pins.py`,
`tools/check_parity.py`, `tools/check_plugins.py` and
`tools/check_no_scratch_in_the_tree.py`. Each is selected by the change set (a
checker nothing it checks touched is named as "not needed", which is neither a
failure nor a pass), and each is run with the Python that runs the backend,
`PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` (so no `__pycache__` appears in the tree it just
measured) and `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` (so not even `git status` may refresh the
index).

**Nothing that did not run is a pass.** A checker that will not start, runs out
of time, exits non-zero, or whose own output says SKIPPED is **NOT-RUN**,
**TIMEOUT** or **FAIL** with the reason - and the verdict says so:

| Verdict | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `READY` | no obligation is MISSING or FAIL, and every checker that was supposed to run really passed |
| `NEEDS-RECORDS` | every checker passed, but a record obligation is missing or wrong |
| `CHECKER-FAILED` | a checker failed, timed out or could not start |
| `INCOMPLETE` | an obligation is fine and no checker failed, but a checker did not run |

The answer is bounded at 7,000 characters (900 when Live speaks it), says which
folder and head it measured, and never writes a log: the failure excerpt rides
in the answer and the full output is dropped.

**Where the owner reaches it.** In chat or Live, "review my branch" and "check
the records before I push" are answered **deterministically** by
`jarvis_quick.py` - not by the model, because a review the model narrates is a
description of a review. Those two answers are in `READ_ONLY_INTENTS`, so they
cannot take away what "cancel that" would undo, and a private chat hands them to
its own gate like every other read. The model also has the two tools, in the
`github` group, and both ship off until their own switch is turned on under
Settings, What asks first, "Jarvis's own tools".

## 216. GitHub full parity, Step 2: nine more actions, card-free reads, and a carded issue close/reopen (added 2026-11-10, the owner's 22:30 and 23:00 PT decisions)

The owner's ruling of 2026-11-10 22:30, "GitHub full integration, full parity
with DeepSeek", named a Step 2 of GitHub actions to build on top of the merge
and the fix-and-push of §190.9-§190.10 (wave 16B). The same evening, at 23:00,
the owner answered two questions that changed two standing rules: **GitHub reads
are card-free**, and **closing one issue is allowed, carded**. This section is
the record of both, and of every action the Step 2 list added.

### 216.1 What was added, and what each one does

| Tool | Kind | What it does | The request(s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `github_pr_detail` | read (shares `github_inspect`) | reads ONE pull request in full: title, body, state/draft/mergeable, head commit and base branch, then its changed files, commits, comments and reviews. At most 10 of each shown, the real count always printed, every text bounded | five fixed GETs: the pull request, `.../files`, `.../commits`, `.../issues/{n}/comments`, `.../pulls/{n}/reviews` |
| `github_open_pr` | write (own action) | two stages. "prepare" copies the repository at a base branch into the scratch root and makes a NEW branch there; "open" shows every commit, every changed file, the exact push command, the title and the WHOLE body on ONE card, then pushes that ONE new branch and opens the pull request, pinned to the HEAD commit the card showed | `GET /repos/{r}` then `git clone`/`checkout -b`; on open: local git reads, `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<new branch>`, then `POST /repos/{r}/pulls` with exactly `{title, body, head, base}` |
| `github_workflow` | write (own action) | "cancel" ONE in-progress workflow run, or "rerun_failed" to run only the FAILED jobs of ONE finished run. It re-reads the run first and refuses, changing nothing, if it is not in the state the card named. It never dispatches a workflow | `GET .../actions/runs/{id}`, then `POST .../cancel` or `POST .../rerun-failed-jobs` |
| `github_issue_labels` | write (own action) | adds and/or removes labels on ONE issue or pull request. It reads the current labels first, refuses if a label it would remove is not there, and sends the whole final set in ONE request | `GET .../issues/{n}`, then `PUT .../issues/{n}/labels` with the whole set |
| `github_edit_pr` | write (own action) | edits ONE pull request's title and/or body. The card shows the exact before and after; the run re-reads the pull request and refuses, changing nothing, if either text is no longer the one on the card. No other field is editable | `GET .../pulls/{n}`, then `PATCH .../pulls/{n}` with only `title` and/or `body` |
| `github_pr_review` | write (own action) | posts ONE review with verdict `COMMENT` or `REQUEST_CHANGES` and shows the whole review text first. The `APPROVE` verdict is **refused by name** before any card exists - a formal approval would hand the owner's own sign-off to the assistant | `POST .../pulls/{n}/reviews` with exactly `{event, body}` |
| `github_issue_state` | write (own action) | **the owner's 23:00 decision**: closes ONE issue, or reopens ONE closed issue, on its own card. The card shows the repository, the issue number and title, the direction and an optional reason (at most 400 characters, shown on the card and in the answer; GitHub's state change has no free-text reason field, so it is not sent as one). It cannot delete, transfer or edit the issue, never touches a pull request, and never bulk | `GET .../issues/{n}` (the title is the pin - a changed title refuses with nothing sent), then `PATCH .../issues/{n}` with exactly `{"state": "closed"|"open"}` |

The other two of the nine are not new tools: `github_pr_detail` is a read, and
the owner's 23:00 answer also means `github_open_issue` is unchanged (it still
cannot close what it opens - the close/reopen is the separate action above).

### 216.2 Decision A: GitHub READS are card-free (owner, 2026-11-10 23:00 PT)

A read is a GET on `api.github.com` and changes nothing, so the owner chose
"make GitHub reads card-free". Concretely:

* `github_inspect` ships **`"auto"`** in both shipped settings files
  (`backend/rebuilt/jarvis-framework.toml` and `jarvis-backend/jarvis-framework.toml`).
* The five read tools (`github_list`, `github_read_file`, `github_ci_status`,
  `github_pr_scan`, `github_pr_detail`) are **not** in
  `jarvis_agent.NEEDS_A_PERSON`; a read no longer raises a card.
* The read TOOLS are still switched off until the owner switches them on (the
  owner's 2026-11-04 rule: every offered tool is switchable). It is the read
  ACTION that never asks.
* **Every WRITE still asks its own card**, is its own `"ask"` tier line, and is
  still in `NEEDS_A_PERSON`; a loosened line still raises its card.
